italian: Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita mi ritrovai per una selva oscura ché la diritta via era smarrita.
english: When I had journeyed half of our life’s way, I found myself within a shadowed forest, for I had lost the path that does not stray.

italian: Ahi quanto a dir qual era è cosa dura esta selva selvaggia e aspra e forte che nel pensier rinova la paura!
english: Ah, it is hard to speak of what it was, that savage forest, dense and difficult, which even in recall renews my fear:

italian: Tant’ è amara che poco è più morte; ma per trattar del ben ch’i’ vi trovai, dirò de l’altre cose ch’i’ v’ho scorte.
english: so bitter — death is hardly more severe! But to retell the good discovered there, I’ll also tell the other things I saw.

italian: Io non so ben ridir com’ i’ v’intrai, tant’ era pien di sonno a quel punto che la verace via abbandonai.
english: I cannot clearly say how I had entered the wood; I was so full of sleep just at the point where I abandoned the true path.

italian: Ma poi ch’i’ fui al piè d’un colle giunto, là dove terminava quella valle che m’avea di paura il cor compunto,
english: But when I’d reached the bottom of a hill — it rose along the boundary of the valley that had harassed my heart with so much fear —

italian: guardai in alto, e vidi le sue spalle vestite già de’ raggi del pianeta che mena dritto altrui per ogne calle.
english: I looked on high and saw its shoulders clothed already by the rays of that same planet which serves to lead men straight along all roads.

italian: Allor fu la paura un poco queta che nel lago del cor m’era durata la notte ch’i’ passai con tanta pieta.
english: At this my fear was somewhat quieted; for through the night of sorrow I had spent, the lake within my heart felt terror present.

italian: E come quei che con lena affannata uscito fuor del pelago a la riva si volge a l’acqua perigliosa e guata,
english: And just as he who, with exhausted breath, having escaped from sea to shore, turns back to watch the dangerous waters he has quit,

italian: così l’animo mio, ch’ancor fuggiva, si volse a retro a rimirar lo passo che non lasciò già mai persona viva.
english: so did my spirit, still a fugitive, turn back to look intently at the pass that never has let any man survive.

italian: Poi ch’èi posato un poco il corpo lasso, ripresi via per la piaggia diserta, sì che ’l piè fermo sempre era ’l più basso.
english: I let my tired body rest awhile. Moving again, I tried the lonely slope — my firm foot always was the one below.

italian: Ed ecco, quasi al cominciar de l’erta, una lonza leggera e presta molto, che di pel macolato era coverta;
english: And almost where the hillside starts to rise — look there! — a leopard, very quick and lithe, a leopard covered with a spotted hide.

italian: e non mi si partia dinanzi al volto, anzi ’mpediva tanto il mio cammino, ch’i’ fui per ritornar più volte vòlto.
english: He did not disappear from sight, but stayed; indeed, he so impeded my ascent that I had often to turn back again.

italian: Temp’ era dal principio del mattino, e ’l sol montava ’n sù con quelle stelle ch’eran con lui quando l’amor divino
english: The time was the beginning of the morning; the sun was rising now in fellowship with the same stars that had escorted it

italian: mosse di prima quelle cose belle; sì ch’a bene sperar m’era cagione di quella fiera a la gaetta pelle
english: when Divine Love first moved those things of beauty; so that the hour and the gentle season gave me good cause for hopefulness on seeing

italian: l’ora del tempo e la dolce stagione; ma non sì che paura non mi desse la vista che m’apparve d’un leone.
english: that beast before me with his speckled skin; but hope was hardly able to prevent the fear I felt when I beheld a lion.

italian: Questi parea che contra me venisse con la test’ alta e con rabbiosa fame, sì che parea che l’aere ne tremesse.
english: His head held high and ravenous with hunger — even the air around him seemed to shudder — this lion seemed to make his way against me.

italian: Ed una lupa, che di tutte brame sembiava carca ne la sua magrezza, e molte genti fé già viver grame,
english: And then a she-wolf showed herself; she seemed to carry every craving in her leanness; she had already brought despair to many.

italian: questa mi porse tanto di gravezza con la paura ch’uscia di sua vista, ch’io perdei la speranza de l’altezza.
english: The very sight of her so weighted me with fearfulness that I abandoned hope of ever climbing up that mountain slope.

italian: E qual è quei che volontieri acquista, e giugne ’l tempo che perder lo face, che ’n tutti suoi pensier piange e s’attrista;
english: Even as he who glories while he gains will, when the time has come to tally loss, lament with every thought and turn despondent,

italian: tal mi fece la bestia sanza pace, che, venendomi ’ncontro, a poco a poco mi ripigneva là dove ’l sol tace.
english: so was I when I faced that restless beast which, even as she stalked me, step by step had thrust me back to where the sun is speechless.

italian: Mentre ch’i’ rovinava in basso loco, dinanzi a li occhi mi si fu offerto chi per lungo silenzio parea fioco.
english: While I retreated down to lower ground, before my eyes there suddenly appeared one who seemed faint because of the long silence.

italian: Quando vidi costui nel gran diserto, « Miserere di me», gridai a lui, «qual che tu sii, od ombra od omo certo!».
english: When I saw him in that vast wilderness, “Have pity on me,” were the words I cried, “whatever you may be — a shade, a man.”

italian: Rispuosemi: «Non omo, omo già fui, e li parenti miei furon lombardi, mantoani per patrïa ambedui.
english: He answered me: “Not man; I once was man. Both of my parents came from Lombardy, and both claimed Mantua as native city.

italian: Nacqui sub Iulio , ancor che fosse tardi, e vissi a Roma sotto ’l buono Augusto nel tempo de li dèi falsi e bugiardi.
english: And I was born, though late, sub Julio, and lived in Rome under the good Augustus — the season of the false and lying gods.

italian: Poeta fui, e cantai di quel giusto figliuol d’Anchise che venne di Troia, poi che ’l superbo Ilión fu combusto.
english: I was a poet, and I sang the righteous son of Anchises who had come from Troy when flames destroyed the pride of Ilium.

italian: Ma tu perché ritorni a tanta noia? perché non sali il dilettoso monte ch’è principio e cagion di tutta gioia?».
english: But why do you return to wretchedness? Why not climb up the mountain of delight, the origin and cause of every joy?”

italian: «Or se’ tu quel Virgilio e quella fonte che spandi di parlar sì largo fiume?», rispuos’ io lui con vergognosa fronte.
english: “And are you then that Virgil, you the fountain that freely pours so rich a stream of speech?” I answered him with shame upon my brow.

italian: «O de li altri poeti onore e lume vagliami ’l lungo studio e ’l grande amore che m’ha fatto cercar lo tuo volume.
english: “O light and honor of all other poets, may my long study and the intense love that made me search your volume serve me now.

italian: Tu se’ lo mio maestro e ’l mio autore; tu se’ solo colui da cu’ io tolsi lo bello stilo che m’ha fatto onore.
english: You are my master and my author, you — the only one from whom my writing drew the noble style for which I have been honored.

italian: Vedi la bestia per cu’ io mi volsi: aiutami da lei, famoso saggio, ch’ella mi fa tremar le vene e i polsi».
english: You see the beast that made me turn aside; help me, o famous sage, to stand against her, for she has made my blood and pulses shudder,”

italian: «A te convien tenere altro vïaggio», rispuose poi che lagrimar mi vide, «se vuo’ campar d’esto loco selvaggio;
english: “It is another path that you must take,” he answered when he saw my tearfulness, “if you would leave this savage wilderness;

italian: ché questa bestia, per la qual tu gride, non lascia altrui passar per la sua via, ma tanto lo ’mpedisce che l’uccide;
english: the beast that is the cause of your outcry allows no man to pass along her track, but blocks him even to the point of death;

italian: e ha natura sì malvagia e ria, che mai non empie la bramosa voglia, e dopo ’l pasto ha più fame che pria.
english: her nature is so squalid, so malicious that she can never sate her greedy will; when she has fed, she’s hungrier than ever.

italian: Molti son li animali a cui s’ammoglia, e più saranno ancora, infin che ’l veltro verrà, che la farà morir con doglia.
english: She mates with many living souls and shall yet mate with many more, until the Greyhound arrives, inflicting painful death on her.

italian: Questi non ciberà terra né peltro, ma sapïenza, amore e virtute, e sua nazion sarà tra feltro e feltro.
english: That Hound will never feed on land or pewter, but find his fare in wisdom, love, and virtue; his place of birth shall be between two felts.

italian: Di quella umile Italia fia salute per cui morì la vergine Cammilla, Eurialo e Turno e Niso di ferute.
english: He will restore low-lying Italy for which the maid Camilla died of wounds, and Nisus, Turnus, and Euryalus.

italian: Questi la caccerà per ogne villa, fin che l’avrà rimessa ne lo ’nferno, là onde ’nvidia prima dipartilla.
english: And he will hunt that beast through every city until he thrusts her back again to Hell, for which she was first sent above by envy.

italian: Ond’ io per lo tuo me’ penso e discerno che tu mi segui, e io sarò tua guida, e trarrotti di qui per loco etterno,
english: Therefore, I think and judge it best for you to follow me, and I shall guide you, taking you from this place through an eternal place,

italian: ove udirai le disperate strida, vedrai li antichi spiriti dolenti, ch’a la seconda morte ciascun grida;
english: where you shall hear the howls of desperation and see the ancient spirits in their pain, as each of them laments his second death;

italian: e vederai color che son contenti nel foco, perché speran di venire quando che sia a le beate genti.
english: and you shall see those souls who are content within the fire, for they hope to reach — whenever that may be — the blessed people.

italian: A le quai poi se tu vorrai salire, anima fia a ciò più di me degna: con lei ti lascerò nel mio partire;
english: If you would then ascend as high as these, a soul more worthy than I am will guide you; I’ll leave you in her care when I depart,

italian: ché quello imperador che là sù regna, perch’ i’ fu’ ribellante a la sua legge, non vuol che ’n sua città per me si vegna.
english: because that Emperor who reigns above, since I have been rebellious to His law, will not allow me entry to His city.

italian: In tutte parti impera e quivi regge; quivi è la sua città e l’alto seggio: oh felice colui cu’ ivi elegge!».
english: He governs everywhere, but rules from there; there is His city, His high capital: o happy those He chooses to be there!”

italian: E io a lui: «Poeta, io ti richeggio per quello Dio che tu non conoscesti, acciò ch’io fugga questo male e peggio,
english: And I replied: “O poet — by that God whom you had never come to know — I beg you, that I may flee this evil and worse evils,

italian: che tu mi meni là dov’or dicesti, sì ch’io veggia la porta di san Pietro e color cui tu fai cotanto mesti».
english: to lead me to the place of which you spoke, that I may see the gateway of Saint Peter and those whom you describe as sorrowful.”

italian: Allor si mosse, e io li tenni dietro.
english: Then he set out, and I moved on behind him.

italian: Lo giorno se n’andava, e l’aere bruno toglieva li animai che sono in terra da le fatiche loro; e io sol uno
english: The day was now departing; the dark air released the living beings of the earth from work and weariness; and I myself

italian: m’apparecchiava a sostener la guerra sì del cammino e sì de la pietate, che ritrarrà la mente che non erra.
english: alone prepared to undergo the battle both of the journeying and of the pity, which memory, mistaking not, shall show.

italian: O muse, o alto ingegno, or m’aiutate; o mente che scrivesti ciò ch’io vidi, qui si parrà la tua nobilitate.
english: O Muses, o high genius, help me now; o memory that set down what I saw, here shall your excellence reveal itself!

italian: Io cominciai: «Poeta che mi guidi, guarda la mia virtù s’ell’ è possente, prima ch’a l’alto passo tu mi fidi.
english: I started: “Poet, you who are my guide, see if the force in me is strong enough before you let me face that rugged pass.

italian: Tu dici che di Silvïo il parente, corruttibile ancora, ad immortale secolo andò, e fu sensibilmente.
english: You say that he who fathered Sylvius, while he was still corruptible, had journeyed into the deathless world with his live body.

italian: Però, se l’avversario d’ogne male cortese i fu, pensando l’alto effetto ch’uscir dovea di lui e ’l chi e ’l quale
english: For, if the Enemy of every evil was courteous to him, considering all he would cause and who and what he was,

italian: non pare indegno ad omo d’intelletto; ch’e’ fu de l’alma Roma e di suo impero ne l’empireo ciel per padre eletto:
english: that does not seem incomprehensible, since in the empyrean heaven he was chosen to father honored Rome and her empire;

italian: la quale e ’l quale, a voler dir lo vero, fu stabilita per lo loco santo u’ siede il successor del maggior Piero.
english: and if the truth be told, Rome and her realm were destined to become the sacred place, the seat of the successor of great Peter.

italian: Per quest’ andata onde li dai tu vanto, intese cose che furon cagione di sua vittoria e del papale ammanto.
english: And through the journey you ascribe to him, he came to learn of things that were to bring his victory and, too, the papal mantle.

italian: Andovvi poi lo Vas d’elezïone, per recarne conforto a quella fede ch’è principio a la via di salvazione.
english: Later the Chosen Vessel travelled there, to bring us back assurance of that faith with which the way to our salvation starts.

italian: Ma io, perché venirvi? o chi ’l concede? Io non Enëa, io non Paulo sono; me degno a ciò né io né altri ’l crede.
english: But why should I go there? Who sanctions it? For I am not Aeneas, am not Paul; nor I nor others think myself so worthy.

italian: Per che, se del venire io m’abbandono, temo che la venuta non sia folle. Se’ savio; intendi me’ ch’i’ non ragiono».
english: Therefore, if I consent to start this journey, I fear my venture may be wild and empty. You’re wise; you know far more than what I say.”

italian: E qual è quei che disvuol ciò che volle e per novi pensier cangia proposta, sì che dal cominciar tutto si tolle,
english: And just as he who unwills what he wills and shifts what he intends to seek new ends so that he’s drawn from what he had begun,

italian: tal mi fec’ ïo ’n quella oscura costa, perché, pensando, consumai la ’mpresa che fu nel cominciar cotanto tosta.
english: so was I in the midst of that dark land, because, with all my thinking, I annulled the task I had so quickly undertaken.

italian: «S’i’ ho ben la parola tua intesa», rispuose del magnanimo quell’ ombra; «l’anima tua è da viltade offesa;
english: “If I have understood what you have said,” replied the shade of that great-hearted one, “your soul has been assailed by cowardice,

italian: la qual molte fïate l’ omo ingombra sì che d’onrata impresa lo rivolve, come falso veder bestia quand’ ombra.
english: which often weighs so heavily on a man— distracting him from honorable trials— as phantoms frighten beasts when shadows fall.

italian: Da questa tema acciò che tu ti solve, dirotti perch’ io venni e quel ch’io ’ntesi nel primo punto che di te mi dolve.
english: That you may be delivered from this fear, I’ll tell you why I came and what I heard when I first felt compassion for your pain.

italian: Io era tra color che son sospesi, e donna mi chiamò beata e bella, tal che di comandare io la richiesi.
english: I was among those souls who are suspended; a lady called to me, so blessed, so lovely that I implored to serve at her command.

italian: Lucevan li occhi suoi più che la stella; e cominciommi a dir soave e piana, con angelica voce, in sua favella:
english: Her eyes surpassed the splendor of the star’s; and she began to speak to me—so gently and softly—with angelic voice. She said:

italian: “O anima cortese mantoana, di cui la fama ancor nel mondo dura, e durerà quanto ’l mondo lontana,
english: ‘O spirit of the courteous Mantuan, whose fame is still a presence in the world and shall endure as long as the world lasts,

italian: l’amico mio, e non de la ventura, ne la diserta piaggia è impedito sì nel cammin, che volt’ è per paura;
english: my friend, who has not been the friend of fortune, is hindered in his path along that lonely hillside; he has been turned aside by terror.

italian: e temo che non sia già sì smarrito, ch’io mi sia tardi al soccorso levata, per quel ch’i’ ho di lui nel cielo udito.
english: From all that I have heard of him in Heaven, he is, I fear, already so astray that I have come to help him much too late.

italian: Or movi, e con la tua parola ornata e con ciò c’ha mestieri al suo campare, l’aiuta, sì ch’i’ ne sia consolata.
english: Go now; with your persuasive word, with all that is required to see that he escapes, bring help to him, that I may be consoled.

italian: I’ son Beatrice che ti faccio andare; vegno del loco ove tornar disio; amor mi mosse, che mi fa parlare.
english: For I am Beatrice who send you on; I come from where I most long to return; Love prompted me, that Love which makes me speak.

italian: Quando sarò dinanzi al segnor mio, di te mi loderò sovente a lui”. Tacette allora, e poi comincia’ io:
english: When once again I stand before my Lord, then I shall often let Him hear your praises.’ Now Beatrice was silent. I began:

italian: “O donna di virtù, sola per cui l’umana spezie eccede ogne contento di quel ciel c’ha minor li cerchi sui,
english: ‘O Lady of virtue, the sole reason why the human race surpasses all that lies beneath the heaven with the smallest spheres,

italian: tanto m’aggrada il tuo comandamento, che l’ubidir, se già fosse, m’è tardi; più non t’è uo’ ch’aprirmi il tuo talento.
english: so welcome is your wish, that even if it were already done, it would seem tardy; all you need do is let me know your will.

italian: Ma dimmi la cagion che non ti guardi de lo scender qua giuso in questo centro de l’ampio loco ove tornar tu ardi”.
english: But tell me why you have not been more prudent— descending to this center, moving from that spacious place where you long to return?’

italian: “Da che tu vuo’ saver cotanto a dentro, dirotti brievemente”, mi rispuose, “perch’ i’ non temo di venir qua entro.
english: ‘Because you want to fathom things so deeply, I now shall tell you promptly,’ she replied, ‘why I am not afraid to enter here.

italian: Temer si dee di sole quelle cose c’hanno potenza di fare altrui male; de l’altre no, ché non son paurose.
english: One ought to be afraid of nothing other than things possessed of power to do us harm, but things innocuous need not be feared.

italian: I’ son fatta da Dio, sua mercé, tale, che la vostra miseria non mi tange, né fiamma d’esto ’ncendio non m’assale.
english: God, in His graciousness, has made me so that this, your misery, cannot touch me; I can withstand the fires flaming here.

italian: Donna è gentil nel ciel che si compiange di questo ’mpedimento ov’ io ti mando, sì che duro giudicio là sù frange.
english: In Heaven there’s a gentle lady—one who weeps for the distress toward which I send you, so that stern judgment up above is shattered.

italian: Questa chiese Lucia in suo dimando e disse: – Or ha bisogno il tuo fedele di te, e io a te lo raccomando -.
english: And it was she who called upon Lucia, requesting of her: “Now your faithful one has need of you, and I commend him to you.”

italian: Lucia, nimica di ciascun crudele, si mosse, e venne al loco dov’ i’ era, che mi sedea con l’antica Rachele.
english: Lucia, enemy of every cruelty, arose and made her way to where I was, sitting beside the venerable Rachel.

italian: Disse: – Beatrice, loda di Dio vera, ché non soccorri quei che t’amò tanto, ch’uscì per te de la volgare schiera?
english: She said: “You, Beatrice, true praise of God, why have you not helped him who loves you so that—for your sake—he’s left the vulgar crowd?

italian: Non odi tu la pieta del suo pianto, non vedi tu la morte che ’l combatte su la fiumana ove ’l mar non ha vanto? -.
english: Do you not hear the anguish in his cry? Do you not see the death he wars against upon that river ruthless as the sea?”

italian: Al mondo non fur mai persone ratte a far lor pro o a fuggir lor danno, com’ io, dopo cotai parole fatte,
english: No one within this world has ever been so quick to seek his good or flee his harm as I—when she had finished speaking thus—

italian: venni qua giù del mio beato scanno, fidandomi del tuo parlare onesto, ch’onora te e quei ch’udito l’hanno”.
english: to come below, down from my blessed station; I trusted in your honest utterance, which honors you and those who’ve listened to you.’

italian: Poscia che m’ebbe ragionato questo, li occhi lucenti lacrimando volse, per che mi fece del venir più presto.
english: When she had finished with her words to me, she turned aside her gleaming, tearful eyes, which only made me hurry all the more.

italian: E venni a te così com’ ella volse; d’inanzi a quella fiera ti levai che del bel monte il corto andar ti tolse.
english: And, just as she had wished, I came to you: I snatched you from the path of the fierce beast that barred the shortest way up the fair mountain.

italian: Dunque: che è? perché, perché restai, perché tanta viltà nel core allette, perché ardire e franchezza non hai,
english: What is it then? Why, why do you resist? Why does your heart host so much cowardice? Where are your daring and your openness

italian: poscia che tai tre donne benedette curan di te ne la corte del cielo, e ‘l mio parlar tanto ben ti promette?».
english: as long as there are three such blessed women concerned for you within the court of Heaven and my words promise you so great a good?”

italian: Quali fioretti dal notturno gelo chinati e chiusi, poi che ’l sol li ’mbianca si drizzan tutti aperti in loro stelo,
english: As little flowers, which the chill of night has bent and huddled, when the white sun strikes grow straight and open fully on their stems,

italian: tal mi fec’ io di mia virtude stanca, e tanto buono ardire al cor mi corse, ch’i’ cominciai come persona franca:
english: so did I, too, with my exhausted force; and such warm daring rushed into my heart that I—as one who has been freed—began:

italian: «Oh pietosa colei che mi soccorse! e te cortese ch’ubidisti tosto a le vere parole che ti porse!
english: “O she, compassionate, who has helped me! And you who, courteous, obeyed so quickly the true words that she had addressed to you!

italian: Tu m’hai con disiderio il cor disposto sì al venir con le parole tue, ch’i’ son tornato nel primo proposto.
english: You, with your words, have so disposed my heart to longing for this journey—I return to what I was at first prepared to do.

italian: Or va, ch’un sol volere è d’ambedue: tu duca, tu segnore, e tu maestro». Così li dissi; e poi che mosso fue,
english: Now go; a single will fills both of us: you are my guide, my governor, my master.” These were my words to him; when he advanced

italian: intrai per lo cammino alto e silvestro.
english: I entered on the steep and savage path.

italian: ‘Per me si va ne la città dolente, per me si va ne l’etterno dolore, per me si va tra la perduta gente.
english: THROUGH ME THE WAY INTO THE SUFFERING CITY, THROUGH ME THE WAY TO THE ETERNAL PAIN, THROUGH ME THE WAY THAT RUNS AMONG THE LOST.

italian: Giustizia mosse il mio alto fattore; fecemi la divina podestate, la somma sapïenza e ’l primo amore.
english: JUSTICE URGED ON MY HIGH ARTIFICER; MY MAKER WAS DIVINE AUTHORITY, THE HIGHEST WISDOM, AND THE PRIMAL LOVE.

italian: Dinanzi a me non fuor cose create se non etterne, e io etterno duro. Lasciate ogne speranza, voi ch’intrate’.
english: BEFORE ME NOTHING BUT ETERNAL THINGS WERE MADE, AND I ENDURE ETERNALLY. ABANDON EVERY HOPE, WHO ENTER HERE.

italian: Queste parole di colore oscuro vid’ ïo scritte al sommo d’una porta; per ch’io: «Maestro, il senso lor m’è duro».
english: These words—their aspect was obscure—I read inscribed above a gateway, and I said: “Master, their meaning is difficult for me.”

italian: Ed elli a me, come persona accorta: «Qui si convien lasciare ogne sospetto; ogne viltà convien che qui sia morta.
english: And he to me, as one who comprehends: “Here one must leave behind all hesitation; here every cowardice must meet its death.

italian: Noi siam venuti al loco ov’ i’ t’ho detto che tu vedrai le genti dolorose c’hanno perduto il ben de l’intelletto».
english: For we have reached the place of which I spoke, where you will see the miserable people, those who have lost the good of the intellect.”

italian: E poi che la sua mano a la mia puose con lieto volto, ond’ io mi confortai, mi mise dentro a le segrete cose.
english: And when, with gladness in his face, he placed his hand upon my own, to comfort me, he drew me in among the hidden things.

italian: Quivi sospiri, pianti e alti guai risonavan per l’aere sanza stelle, per ch’io al cominciar ne lagrimai.
english: Here sighs and lamentations and loud cries were echoing across the starless air, so that, as soon as I set out, I wept.

italian: Diverse lingue, orribili favelle, parole di dolore, accenti d’ira, voci alte e fioche, e suon di man con elle
english: Strange utterances, horrible pronouncements, accents of anger, words of suffering, and voices shrill and faint, and beating hands—

italian: facevano un tumulto, il qual s’aggira sempre in quell’ aura sanza tempo tinta, come la rena quando turbo spira.
english: all went to make a tumult that will whirl forever through that turbid, timeless air, like sand that eddies when a whirlwind swirls.

italian: E io ch’avea d’error la testa cinta, dissi: «Maestro, che è quel ch’i’ odo? e che gent’ è che par nel duol sì vinta?».
english: And I—my head oppressed by horror—said: “Master, what is it that I hear? Who are those people so defeated by their pain?”

italian: Ed elli a me: «Questo misero modo tegnon l’anime triste di coloro che visser sanza ’nfamia e sanza lodo.
english: And he to me: “This miserable way is taken by the sorry souls of those who lived without disgrace and without praise.

italian: Mischiate sono a quel cattivo coro de li angeli che non furon ribelli né fur fedeli a Dio, ma per sé fuoro.
english: They now commingle with the coward angels, the company of those who were not rebels nor faithful to their God, but stood apart.

italian: Caccianli i ciel per non esser men belli, né lo profondo inferno li riceve, ch’alcuna gloria i rei avrebber d’elli».
english: The heavens, that their beauty not be lessened, have cast them out, nor will deep Hell receive them— even the wicked cannot glory in them.”

italian: E io: «Maestro, che è tanto greve a lor che lamentar li fa sì forte?». Rispuose: «Dicerolti molto breve.
english: And I: “What is it, master, that oppresses these souls, compelling them to wail so loud?” He answered: “I shall tell you in few words.

italian: Questi non hanno speranza di morte, e la lor cieca vita è tanto bassa, che ’nvidïosi son d’ogne altra sorte.
english: Those who are here can place no hope in death, and their blind life is so abject that they are envious of every other fate.

italian: Fama di loro il mondo esser non lassa; misericordia e giustizia li sdegna: non ragioniam di lor, ma guarda e passa».
english: The world will let no fame of theirs endure; both justice and compassion must disdain them; let us not talk of them, but look and pass.”

italian: E io, che riguardai, vidi una ’nsegna che girando correva tanto ratta, che d’ogne posa mi parea indegna;
english: And I, looking more closely, saw a banner that, as it wheeled about, raced on—so quick that any respite seemed unsuited to it.

italian: e dietro le venìa sì lunga tratta di gente, ch’i’ non averei creduto che morte tanta n’avesse disfatta.
english: Behind that banner trailed so long a file of people—I should never have believed that death could have unmade so many souls.

italian: Poscia ch’io v’ebbi alcun riconosciuto, vidi e conobbi l’ombra di colui che fece per viltade il gran rifiuto.
english: After I had identified a few, I saw and recognized the shade of him who made, through cowardice, the great refusal.

italian: Incontanente intesi e certo fui che questa era la setta d’i cattivi, a Dio spiacenti e a’ nemici sui.
english: At once I understood with certainty: this company contained the cowardly, hateful to God and to His enemies.

italian: Questi sciaurati, che mai non fur vivi, erano ignudi e stimolati molto da mosconi e da vespe ch’eran ivi.
english: These wretched ones, who never were alive, went naked and were stung again, again by horseflies and by wasps that circled them.

italian: Elle rigavan lor di sangue il volto, che, mischiato di lagrime, a’ lor piedi da fastidiosi vermi era ricolto.
english: The insects streaked their faces with their blood, which, mingled with their tears, fell at their feet, where it was gathered up by sickening worms.

italian: E poi ch’a riguardar oltre mi diedi, vidi genti a la riva d’un gran fiume; per ch’io dissi: «Maestro, or mi concedi
english: And then, looking beyond them, I could see a crowd along the bank of a great river; at which I said: “Allow me now to know

italian: ch’i’ sappia quali sono, e qual costume le fa di trapassar parer sì pronte, com’ i’ discerno per lo fioco lume».
english: who are these people—master—and what law has made them seem so eager for the crossing, as I can see despite the feeble light.”

italian: Ed elli a me: «Le cose ti fier conte quando noi fermerem li nostri passi su la trista riviera d’Acheronte».
english: And he to me: “When we have stopped along the melancholy shore of Acheron, then all these matters will be plain to you.”

italian: Allor con li occhi vergognosi e bassi, temendo no ’l mio dir li fosse grave, infino al fiume del parlar mi trassi.
english: At that, with eyes ashamed, downcast, and fearing that what I said had given him offense, I did not speak until we reached the river.

italian: Ed ecco verso noi venir per nave un vecchio, bianco per antico pelo, gridando: «Guai a voi, anime prave!
english: And here, advancing toward us, in a boat, an aged man—his hair was white with years — was shouting: “Woe to you, corrupted souls!

italian: Non isperate mai veder lo cielo: i’ vegno per menarvi a l’altra riva ne le tenebre etterne, in caldo e ’n gelo.
english: Forget your hope of ever seeing Heaven: I come to lead you to the other shore, to the eternal dark, to fire and frost.

italian: E tu che se’ costì, anima viva, pàrtiti da cotesti che son morti». Ma poi che vide ch’io non mi partiva,
english: And you approaching there, you living soul, keep well away from these—they are the dead.” But when he saw I made no move to go,

italian: disse: «Per altra via, per altri porti verrai a piaggia, non qui, per passare: più lieve legno convien che ti porti».
english: he said: “Another way and other harbors— not here—will bring you passage to your shore: a lighter craft will have to carry you.”

italian: E ’l duca lui: «Caron, non ti crucciare: vuolsi così colà dove si puote ciò che si vuole, e più non dimandare».
english: My guide then: “Charon, don’t torment yourself: our passage has been willed above, where One can do what He has willed; and ask no more.”

italian: Quinci fuor quete le lanose gote al nocchier de la livida palude, che ’ntorno a li occhi avea di fiamme rote.
english: Now silence fell upon the wooly cheeks of Charon, pilot of the livid marsh, whose eyes were ringed about with wheels of flame.

italian: Ma quell’ anime, ch’eran lasse e nude, cangiar colore e dibattero i denti, ratto che ’nteser le parole crude.
english: But all those spirits, naked and exhausted, had lost their color, and they gnashed their teeth as soon as they heard Charon’s cruel words;

italian: Bestemmiavano Dio e lor parenti, l’umana spezie e ’l loco e ’l tempo e ’l seme di lor semenza e di lor nascimenti.
english: they execrated God and their own parents and humankind, and then the place and time of their conception’s seed and of their birth.

italian: Poi si ritrasser tutte quante insieme, forte piangendo, a la riva malvagia ch’attende ciascun uom che Dio non teme.
english: Then they forgathered, huddled in one throng, weeping aloud along that wretched shore which waits for all who have no fear of God.

italian: Caron dimonio, con occhi di bragia loro accennando, tutte le raccoglie; batte col remo qualunque s’adagia.
english: The demon Charon, with his eyes like embers, by signaling to them, has all embark; his oar strikes anyone who stretches out.

italian: Come d’autunno si levan le foglie l’una appresso de l’altra, fin che ’l ramo vede a la terra tutte le sue spoglie,
english: As, in the autumn, leaves detach themselves, first one and then the other, till the bough sees all its fallen garments on the ground,

italian: similemente il mal seme d’Adamo gittansi di quel lito ad una ad una, per cenni come augel per suo richiamo.
english: similarly, the evil seed of Adam descended from the shoreline one by one, when signaled, as a falcon—called—will come.

italian: Così sen vanno su per l’onda bruna, e avanti che sien di là discese, anche di qua nuova schiera s’auna.
english: So do they move across the darkened waters; even before they reach the farther shore, new ranks already gather on this bank.

italian: «Figliuol mio», disse ’l maestro cortese, «quelli che muoion ne l’ira di Dio tutti convegnon qui d’ogne paese;
english: “My son,” the gracious master said to me, “those who have died beneath the wrath of God, all these assemble here from every country;

italian: e pronti sono a trapassar lo rio, ché la divina giustizia li sprona, sì che la tema si volve in disio.
english: and they are eager for the river crossing because celestial justice spurs them on, so that their fear is turned into desire.

italian: Quinci non passa mai anima buona; e però, se Caron di te si lagna, ben puoi sapere omai che ’l suo dir suona».
english: No good soul ever takes its passage here; therefore, if Charon has complained of you, by now you can be sure what his words mean.”

italian: Finito questo, la buia campagna tremò sì forte, che de lo spavento la mente di sudore ancor mi bagna.
english: And after this was said, the darkened plain quaked so tremendously—the memory of terror then, bathes me in sweat again.

italian: La terra lagrimosa diede vento, che balenò una luce vermiglia la qual mi vinse ciascun sentimento;
english: A whirlwind burst out of the tear-drenched earth, a wind that crackled with a bloodred light, a light that overcame all of my senses;

italian: e caddi come l’uom cui sonno piglia.
english: and like a man whom sleep has seized, I fell.

italian: Ruppemi l’alto sonno ne la testa un greve truono, sì ch’io mi riscossi come persona ch’è per forza desta;
english: The heavy sleep within my head was smashed by an enormous thunderclap, so that I started up as one whom force awakens;

italian: e l’occhio riposato intorno mossi, dritto levato, e fiso riguardai per conoscer lo loco dov’ io fossi.
english: I stood erect and turned my rested eyes from side to side, and I stared steadily to learn what place it was surrounding me.

italian: Vero è che ’n su la proda mi trovai de la valle d’abisso dolorosa che ’ntrono accoglie d’infiniti guai.
english: In truth I found myself upon the brink of an abyss, the melancholy valley containing thundering, unending wailings.

italian: Oscura e profonda era e nebulosa tanto che, per ficcar lo viso a fondo, io non vi discernea alcuna cosa.
english: That valley, dark and deep and filled with mist, is such that, though I gazed into its pit, I was unable to discern a thing.

italian: «Or discendiam qua giù nel cieco mondo», cominciò il poeta tutto smorto. «Io sarò primo, e tu sarai secondo».
english: “Let us descend into the blind world now,” the poet, who was deathly pale, began; “I shall go first and you will follow me.”

italian: E io, che del color mi fui accorto, dissi: «Come verrò, se tu paventi che suoli al mio dubbiare esser conforto?».
english: But I, who’d seen the change in his complexion, said: “How shall I go on if you are frightened, you who have always helped dispel my doubts?”

italian: Ed elli a me: «L’angoscia de le genti che son qua giù, nel viso mi dipigne quella pietà che tu per tema senti.
english: And he to me: “The anguish of the people whose place is here below, has touched my face with the compassion you mistake for fear.

italian: Andiam, ché la via lunga ne sospigne». Così si mise e così mi fé intrare nel primo cerchio che l’abisso cigne.
english: Let us go on, the way that waits is long.” So he set out, and so he had me enter on that first circle girdling the abyss.

italian: Quivi, secondo che per ascoltare, non avea pianto mai che di sospiri, che l’aura etterna facevan tremare;
english: Here, for as much as hearing could discover, there was no outcry louder than the sighs that caused the everlasting air to tremble.

italian: ciò avvenia di duol senza martìri, ch’avean le turbe, ch’eran molte e grandi, d’infanti e di femmine e di viri.
english: The sighs arose from sorrow without torments, out of the crowds—the many multitudes— of infants and of women and of men.

italian: Lo buon maestro a me: «Tu non dimandi che spiriti son questi che tu vedi? Or vo’ che sappi, innanzi che più andi,
english: The kindly master said: “Do you not ask who are these spirits whom you see before you? I’d have you know, before you go ahead,

italian: ch’ei non peccaro; e s’elli hanno mercedi, non basta, perché non ebber battesmo, ch’è porta de la fede che tu credi;
english: they did not sin; and yet, though they have merits, that’s not enough, because they lacked baptism, the portal of the faith that you embrace.

italian: e s’e’ furon dinanzi al cristianesmo, non adorar debitamente a Dio: e di questi cotai son io medesmo.
english: And if they lived before Christianity, they did not worship God in fitting ways; and of such spirits I myself am one.

italian: Per tai difetti, non per altro rio, semo perduti, e sol di tanto offesi, che sanza speme vivemo in disio».
english: For these defects, and for no other evil, we now are lost and punished just with this: we have no hope and yet we live in longing.”

italian: Gran duol mi prese al cor quando lo ’ntesi, però che gente di molto valore conobbi che ’n quel limbo eran sospesi.
english: Great sorrow seized my heart on hearing him, for I had seen some estimable men among the souls suspended in that limbo.

italian: «Dimmi, maestro mio, dimmi, segnore», comincia’ io per voler esser certo di quella fede che vince ogne errore:
english: “Tell me, my master, tell me, lord.” I then began because I wanted to be certain of that belief which vanquishes all errors,

italian: «uscicci mai alcuno, o per suo merto o per altrui, che poi fosse beato?». E quei che ’ntese il mio parlar coverto,
english: “did any ever go—by his own merit or others’—from this place toward blessedness?” And he, who understood my covert speech,

italian: rispuose: «Io era nuovo in questo stato, quando ci vidi venire un possente, con segno di vittoria coronato.
english: replied: “I was new—entered on this state when I beheld a Great Lord enter here; the crown he wore, a sign of victory.

italian: Trasseci l’ombra del primo parente, d’Abèl suo figlio e quella di Noè, di Moïsè legista e ubidente;
english: He carried off the shade of our first father, of his son Abel, and the shade of Noah, of Moses, the obedient legislator,

italian: Abraàm patrïarca e Davìd re, Israèl con lo padre e co’ suoi nati e con Rachele, per cui tanto fé;
english: of father Abraham, David the king, of Israel, his father, and his sons, and Rachel, she for whom he worked so long,

italian: e altri molti, e feceli beati. E vo’ che sappi che, dinanzi ad essi, spiriti umani non eran salvati».
english: and many others—and He made them blessed; and I should have you know that, before them, there were no human souls that had been saved.”

italian: Non lasciavam l’andar perch’ ei dicessi, ma passavam la selva tuttavia, la selva, dico, di spiriti spessi.
english: We did not stay our steps although he spoke; we still continued onward through the wood— the wood, I say, where many spirits thronged.

italian: Non era lunga ancor la nostra via di qua dal sonno, quand’ io vidi un foco ch’emisperio di tenebre vincia.
english: Our path had not gone far beyond the point where I had slept, when I beheld a fire win out against a hemisphere of shadows.

italian: Di lungi n’eravamo ancora un poco, ma non sì ch’io non discernessi in parte ch’orrevol gente possedea quel loco.
english: We still were at a little distance from it, but not so far I could not see in part that honorable men possessed that place.

italian: «O tu ch’onori scïenzïa e arte, questi chi son c’hanno cotanta onranza, che dal modo de li altri li diparte?».
english: “O you who honor art and science both, who are these souls whose dignity has kept their way of being, separate from the rest?”

italian: E quelli a me: «L’onrata nominanza che di lor suona sù ne la tua vita, grazïa acquista in ciel che sì li avanza».
english: And he to me: “The honor of their name, which echoes up above within your life, gains Heaven’s grace, and that advances them.”

italian: Intanto voce fu per me udita: «Onorate l’altissimo poeta; l’ombra sua torna, ch’era dipartita».
english: Meanwhile there was a voice that I could hear: “Pay honor to the estimable poet; his shadow, which had left us, now returns.”

italian: Poi che la voce fu restata e queta, vidi quattro grand’ ombre a noi venire: sembianz’ avevan né trista né lieta.
english: After that voice was done, when there was silence, I saw four giant shades approaching us; in aspect, they were neither sad nor joyous.

italian: Lo buon maestro cominciò a dire: «Mira colui con quella spada in mano, che vien dinanzi ai tre sì come sire:
english: My kindly master then began by saying: “Look well at him who holds that sword in hand who moves before the other three as lord.

italian: quelli è Omero poeta sovrano; l’altro è Orazio satiro che vene; Ovidio è ’l terzo, e l’ultimo Lucano.
english: That shade is Homer, the consummate poet; the other one is Horace, satirist; the third is Ovid, and the last is Lucan.

italian: Però che ciascun meco si convene nel nome che sonò la voce sola, fannomi onore, e di ciò fanno bene».
english: Because each of these spirits shares with me the name called out before by the lone voice, they welcome me—and, doing that, do well.”

italian: Così vid’ i’ adunar la bella scola di quel segnor de l’altissimo canto che sovra li altri com’ aquila vola.
english: And so I saw that splendid school assembled led by the lord of song incomparable, who like an eagle soars above the rest.

italian: Da ch’ebber ragionato insieme alquanto, volsersi a me con salutevol cenno, e ’l mio maestro sorrise di tanto;
english: Soon after they had talked a while together, they turned to me, saluting cordially; and having witnessed this, my master smiled;

italian: e più d’onore ancora assai mi fenno, ch’e’ sì mi fecer de la loro schiera, sì ch’io fui sesto tra cotanto senno.
english: and even greater honor then was mine, for they invited me to join their ranks— I was the sixth among such intellects.

italian: Così andammo infino a la lumera, parlando cose che ’l tacere è bello, sì com’ era ’l parlar colà dov’ era.
english: So did we move along and toward the light, talking of things about which silence here is just as seemly as our speech was there.

italian: Venimmo al piè d’un nobile castello, sette volte cerchiato d’alte mura, difeso intorno d’un bel fiumicello.
english: We reached the base of an exalted castle, encircled seven times by towering walls, defended all around by a fair stream.

italian: Questo passammo come terra dura; per sette porte intrai con questi savi: giugnemmo in prato di fresca verdura.
english: We forded this as if upon hard ground; I entered seven portals with these sages; we reached a meadow of green flowering plants.

italian: Genti v’eran con occhi tardi e gravi, di grande autorità ne’ lor sembianti: parlavan rado, con voci soavi.
english: The people here had eyes both grave and slow; their features carried great authority; they spoke infrequently, with gentle voices.

italian: Traemmoci così da l’un de’ canti, in loco aperto, luminoso e alto, sì che veder si potien tutti quanti.
english: We drew aside to one part of the meadow, an open place both high and filled with light, and we could see all those who were assembled.

italian: Colà diritto, sovra ’l verde smalto, mi fuor mostrati li spiriti magni, che del vedere in me stesso m’essalto.
english: Facing me there, on the enameled green, great—hearted souls were shown to me and I still glory in my having witnessed them.

italian: I’ vidi Eletra con molti compagni, tra ’ quai conobbi Ettòr ed Enea, Cesare armato con li occhi grifagni.
english: I saw Electra with her many comrades, among whom I knew Hector and Aeneas, and Caesar, in his armor, falcon-eyed.

italian: Vidi Cammilla e la Pantasilea; da l’altra parte vidi ’l re Latino che con Lavina sua figlia sedea.
english: I saw Camilla and Penthesilea and, on the other side, saw King Latinus, who sat beside Lavinia, his daughter.

italian: Vidi quel Bruto che cacciò Tarquino, Lucrezia, Iulia, Marzïa e Corniglia; e solo, in parte, vidi ’l Saladino.
english: I saw that Brutus who drove Tarquin out, Lucretia, Julia, Marcia, and Cornelia, and, solitary, set apart, Saladin.

italian: Poi ch’innalzai un poco più le ciglia, vidi ’l maestro di color che sanno seder tra filosofica famiglia.
english: When I had raised my eyes a little higher, I saw the master of the men who know seated in philosophic family.

italian: Tutti lo miran, tutti onor li fanno: quivi vid’ ïo Socrate e Platone, che ’nnanzi a li altri più presso li stanno;
english: There all look up to him, all do him honor: there I beheld both Socrates and Plato, closest to him, in front of all the rest;

italian: Democrito, che ’l mondo a caso pone, Dïogenès, Anassagora e Tale, Empedoclès, Eraclito e Zenone;
english: Democritus, who ascribes the world to chance, Diogenes, Empedocles, and Zeno, and Thales, Anaxagoras, Heraclitus;

italian: e vidi il buono accoglitor del quale, Dïascoride dico; e vidi Orfeo, Tulïo e Lino e Seneca morale;
english: I saw the good collector of medicinals, I mean Dioscorides; and I saw Orpheus, and Tully, Linus, moral Seneca;

italian: Euclide geomètra e Tolomeo, Ipocràte, Avicenna e Galïeno, Averoìs, che ’l gran comento feo.
english: and Euclid the geometer, and Ptolemy, Hippocrates and Galen, Avicenna, Averroes, of the great Commentary.

italian: Io non posso ritrar di tutti a pieno, però che sì mi caccia il lungo tema, che molte volte al fatto il dir vien meno.
english: I cannot here describe them all in full; my ample theme impels me onward so: what’s told is often less than the event.

italian: La sesta compagnia in due si scema: per altra via mi mena il savio duca, fuor de la queta, ne l’ aura che trema.
english: The company of six divides in two; my knowing guide leads me another way, beyond the quiet, into trembling air.

italian: E vegno in parte ove non è che luca.
english: And I have reached a part where no thing gleams.

italian: Così discesi del cerchio primaio giù nel secondo, che men loco cinghia e tanto più dolor, che punge a guaio.
english: So I descended from the first enclosure down to the second circle, that which girdles less space but grief more great, that goads to weeping.

italian: Stavvi Minòs orribilmente, e ringhia: essamina le colpe ne l’intrata; giudica e manda secondo ch’avvinghia.
english: There dreadful Minos stands, gnashing his teeth: examining the sins of those who enter, he judges and assigns as his tail twines.

italian: Dico che quando l’anima mal nata li vien dinanzi, tutta si confessa; e quel conoscitor de le peccata
english: I mean that when the spirit born to evil appears before him, it confesses all; and he, the connoisseur of sin, can tell

italian: vede qual loco d’inferno è da essa; cignesi con la coda tante volte quantunque gradi vuol che giù sia messa.
english: the depth in Hell appropriate to it; as many times as Minos wraps his tail around himself, that marks the sinner’s level.

italian: Sempre dinanzi a lui ne stanno molte: vanno a vicenda ciascuna al giudizio, dicono e odono e poi son giù volte.
english: Always there is a crowd that stands before him: each soul in turn advances toward that judgment; they speak and hear, then they are cast below.

italian: «O tu che vieni al doloroso ospizio», disse Minòs a me quando mi vide, lasciando l’atto di cotanto offizio,
english: Arresting his extraordinary task, Minos, as soon as he had seen me, said: “O you who reach this house of suffering,

italian: «guarda com’ entri e di cui tu ti fide; non t’inganni l’ampiezza de l’intrare!». E ’l duca mio a lui: «Perché pur gride?
english: be careful how you enter, whom you trust; the gate is wide, but do not be deceived!” To which my guide replied: “But why protest?

italian: Non impedir lo suo fatale andare: vuolsi così colà dove si puote ciò che si vuole, e più non dimandare».
english: Do not attempt to block his fated path: our passage has been willed above, where One can do what He has willed; and ask no more.”

italian: Or incomincian le dolenti note a farmisi sentire; or son venuto là dove molto pianto mi percuote.
english: Now notes of desperation have begun to overtake my hearing; now I come where mighty lamentation beats against me.

italian: Io venni in loco d’ogne luce muto, che mugghia come fa mar per tempesta, se da contrari venti è combattuto.
english: I reached a place where every light is muted, which bellows like the sea beneath a tempest, when it is battered by opposing winds.

italian: La bufera infernal, che mai non resta, mena li spirti con la sua rapina; voltando e percotendo li molesta.
english: The hellish hurricane, which never rests, drives on the spirits with its violence: wheeling and pounding, it harasses them.

italian: Quando giungon davanti a la ruina, quivi le strida, il compianto, il lamento; bestemmian quivi la virtù divina.
english: When they come up against the ruined slope, then there are cries and wailing and lament, and there they curse the force of the divine.

italian: Intesi ch’a così fatto tormento enno dannati i peccator carnali, che la ragion sommettono al talento.
english: I learned that those who undergo this torment are damned because they sinned within the flesh, subjecting reason to the rule of lust.

italian: E come li stornei ne portan l’ali nel freddo tempo, a schiera larga e piena, così quel fiato li spiriti mali
english: And as, in the cold season, starlings’ wings bear them along in broad and crowded ranks so does that blast bear on the guilty spirits:

italian: di qua, di là, di giù, di sù li mena; nulla speranza li conforta mai, non che di posa, ma di minor pena.
english: now here, now there, now down, now up, it drives them. There is no hope that ever comforts them— no hope for rest and none for lesser pain.

italian: E come i gru van cantando lor lai, faccendo in aere di sé lunga riga, così vid’ io venir, traendo guai,
english: And just as cranes in flight will chant their lays, arraying their long file across the air, so did the shades I saw approaching, borne

italian: ombre portate da la detta briga; per ch’i’ dissi: «Maestro, chi son quelle genti che l’aura nera sì gastiga?».
english: by that assailing wind, lament and moan; so that I asked him: “Master, who are those who suffer punishment in this dark air?”

italian: «La prima di color di cui novelle tu vuo’ saper», mi disse quelli allotta, «fu imperadrice di molte favelle.
english: “The first of those about whose history you want to know,” my master then told me “once ruled as empress over many nations.

italian: A vizio di lussuria fu sì rotta, che libito fé licito in sua legge, per tòrre il biasmo in che era condotta.
english: Her vice of lust became so customary that she made license licit in her laws to free her from the scandal she had caused.

italian: Ell’ è Semiramìs, di cui si legge che succedette a Nino e fu sua sposa: tenne la terra che ’l Soldan corregge.
english: She is Semiramis, of whom we read that she was Ninus’ wife and his successor: she held the land the Sultan now commands.

italian: L’altra è colei che s’ancise amorosa, e ruppe fede al cener di Sicheo; poi è Cleopatràs lussurïosa.
english: That other spirit killed herself for love, and she betrayed the ashes of Sychaeus; the wanton Cleopatra follows next.

italian: Elena vedi, per cui tanto reo tempo si volse, e vedi ’l grande Achille, che con amore al fine combatteo.
english: See Helen, for whose sake so many years of evil had to pass; see great Achilles, who finally met love-in his last battle.

italian: Vedi Parìs, Tristano»; e più di mille ombre mostrommi e nominommi a dito, ch’amor di nostra vita dipartille.
english: See Paris, Tristan . . .”—and he pointed out and named to me more than a thousand shades departed from our life because of love.

italian: Poscia ch’io ebbi ’l mio dottore udito nomar le donne antiche e ’ cavalieri, pietà mi giunse, e fui quasi smarrito.
english: No sooner had I heard my teacher name the ancient ladies and the knights, than pity seized me, and I was like a man astray.

italian: I’ cominciai: «Poeta, volontieri parlerei a quei due che ’nsieme vanno, e paion sì al vento esser leggeri».
english: My first words: “Poet, I should willingly speak with those two who go together there and seem so lightly carried by the wind.”

italian: Ed elli a me: «Vedrai quando saranno più presso a noi; e tu allor li priega per quello amor che i mena, ed ei verranno».
english: And he to me: “You’ll see when they draw closer to us, and then you may appeal to them by that love which impels them. They will come.”

italian: Sì tosto come il vento a noi li piega, mossi la voce: «O anime affannate, venite a noi parlar, s’altri nol niega!».
english: No sooner had the wind bent them toward us than I urged on my voice: “O battered souls if One does not forbid it, speak with us.”

italian: Quali colombe dal disio chiamate con l’ali alzate e ferme al dolce nido vegnon per l’aere, dal voler portate;
english: Even as doves when summoned by desire, borne forward by their will, move through the air with wings uplifted, still, to their sweet nest,

italian: cotali uscir de la schiera ov’ è Dido, a noi venendo per l’aere maligno, sì forte fu l’affettüoso grido.
english: those spirits left the ranks where Dido suffers approaching us through the malignant air; so powerful had been my loving cry.

italian: «O animal grazïoso e benigno che visitando vai per l’aere perso noi che tignemmo il mondo di sanguigno,
english: “O living being, gracious and benign, who through the darkened air have come to visit our souls that stained the world with blood, if He

italian: se fosse amico il re de l’universo, noi pregheremmo lui de la tua pace, poi c’hai pietà del nostro mal perverso.
english: who rules the universe were friend to us then we should pray to Him to give you peace for you have pitied our atrocious state.

italian: Di quel che udire e che parlar vi piace, noi udiremo e parleremo a voi, mentre che ’l vento, come fa, ci tace.
english: Whatever pleases you to hear and speak will please us, too, to hear and speak with you, now while the wind is silent, in this place.

italian: Siede la terra dove nata fui su la marina dove ’l Po discende per aver pace co’ seguaci sui.
english: The land where I was born lies on that shore to which the Po together with the waters that follow it descends to final rest.

italian: Amor, ch’al cor gentil ratto s’apprende, prese costui de la bella persona che mi fu tolta; e ’l modo ancor m’offende.
english: Love, that can quickly seize the gentle heart, took hold of him because of the fair body taken from me—how that was done still wounds me.

italian: Amor, ch’a nullo amato amar perdona, mi prese del costui piacer sì forte, che, come vedi, ancor non m’abbandona.
english: Love, that releases no beloved from loving, took hold of me so strongly through his beauty that, as you see, it has not left me yet.

italian: Amor condusse noi ad una morte. Caina attende chi a vita ci spense». Queste parole da lor ci fuor porte.
english: Love led the two of us unto one death. Caina waits for him who took our life.” These words were borne across from them to us.

italian: Quand’ io intesi quell’ anime offense, china’ il viso, e tanto il tenni basso, fin che ’l poeta mi disse: «Che pense?».
english: When I had listened to those injured souls, I bent my head and held it low until the poet asked of me: “What are you thinking?”

italian: Quando rispuosi, cominciai: «Oh lasso, quanti dolci pensier, quanto disio menò costoro al doloroso passo!».
english: When I replied, my words began: “Alas, how many gentle thoughts, how deep a longing, had led them to the agonizing pass!”

italian: Poi mi rivolsi a loro e parla’ io, e cominciai: «Francesca, i tuoi martìri a lagrimar mi fanno tristo e pio.
english: Then I addressed my speech again to them, and I began: “Francesca, your afflictions move me to tears of sorrow and of pity.

italian: Ma dimmi: al tempo d’i dolci sospiri, a che e come concedette amore che conosceste i dubbiosi disiri?».
english: But tell me, in the time of gentle sighs, with what and in what way did Love allow you to recognize your still uncertain longings?”

italian: E quella a me: «Nessun maggior dolore che ricordarsi del tempo felice ne la miseria; e ciò sa ’l tuo dottore.
english: And she to me: “There is no greater sorrow than thinking back upon a happy time in misery—and this your teacher knows.

italian: Ma s’a conoscer la prima radice del nostro amor tu hai cotanto affetto, dirò come colui che piange e dice.
english: Yet if you long so much to understand the first root of our love, then I shall tell my tale to you as one who weeps and speaks.

italian: Noi leggiavamo un giorno per diletto di Lancialotto come amor lo strinse; soli eravamo e sanza alcun sospetto.
english: One day, to pass the time away, we read of Lancelot—how love had overcome him. We were alone, and we suspected nothing.

italian: Per più fïate li occhi ci sospinse quella lettura, e scolorocci il viso; ma solo un punto fu quel che ci vinse.
english: And time and time again that reading led our eyes to meet, and made our faces pale, and yet one point alone defeated us.

italian: Quando leggemmo il disïato riso esser basciato da cotanto amante, questi, che mai da me non fia diviso,
english: When we had read how the desired smile was kissed by one who was so true a lover, this one, who never shall be parted from me,

italian: la bocca mi basciò tutto tremante. Galeotto fu ’l libro e chi lo scrisse: quel giorno più non vi leggemmo avante».
english: while all his body trembled, kissed my mouth. A Gallehault indeed, that book and he who wrote it, too; that day we read no more.”

italian: Mentre che l’uno spirto questo disse, l’altro piangëa; sì che di pietade io venni men così com’ io morisse.
english: And while one spirit said these words to me, the other wept, so that—because of pity— I fainted, as if I had met my death.

italian: E caddi come corpo morto cade.
english: And then I fell as a dead body falls.

italian: ﻿Al tornar de la mente, che si chiuse dinanzi a la pietà d’i due cognati, che di trestizia tutto mi confuse,
english: Upon my mind’s reviving—it had closed on hearing the lament of those two kindred, since sorrow had confounded me completely—

italian: novi tormenti e novi tormentati mi veggio intorno, come ch’io mi mova e ch’io mi volga, e come che io guati.
english: I see new sufferings, new sufferers surrounding me on every side, wherever I move or turn about or set my eyes.

italian: Io sono al terzo cerchio, de la piova etterna, maladetta, fredda e greve; regola e qualità mai non l’è nova.
english: I am in the third circle, filled with cold, unending, heavy, and accursed rain; its measure and its kind are never changed.

italian: Grandine grossa, acqua tinta e neve per l’aere tenebroso si riversa; pute la terra che questo riceve.
english: Gross hailstones, water gray with filth, and snow come streaking down across the shadowed air; the earth, as it receives that shower, stinks.

italian: Cerbero, fiera crudele e diversa, con tre gole caninamente latra sovra la gente che quivi è sommersa.
english: Over the souls of those submerged beneath that mess, is an outlandish, vicious beast, his three throats barking, doglike: Cerberus.

italian: Li occhi ha vermigli, la barba unta e atra, e ’l ventre largo, e unghiate le mani; graffia li spirti ed iscoia ed isquatra.
english: His eyes are bloodred; greasy, black, his beard; his belly bulges, and his hands are claws; his talons tear and flay and rend the shades.

italian: Urlar li fa la pioggia come cani; de l’un de’ lati fanno a l’altro schermo; volgonsi spesso i miseri profani.
english: That downpour makes the sinners howl like dogs; they use one of their sides to screen the other— those miserable wretches turn and turn.

italian: Quando ci scorse Cerbero, il gran vermo, le bocche aperse e mostrocci le sanne; non avea membro che tenesse fermo.
english: When Cerberus, the great worm, noticed us, he opened wide his mouths, showed us his fangs; there was no part of him that did not twitch.

italian: E ’l duca mio distese le sue spanne, prese la terra, e con piene le pugna la gittò dentro a le bramose canne.
english: My guide opened his hands to their full span, plucked up some earth, and with his fists filled full he hurled it straight into those famished jaws.

italian: Qual è quel cane ch’abbaiando agogna, e si racqueta poi che ’l pasto morde, ché solo a divorarlo intende e pugna,
english: Just as a dog that barks with greedy hunger will then fall quiet when he gnaws his food, intent and straining hard to cram it in,

italian: cotai si fecer quelle facce lorde de lo demonio Cerbero, che ’ntrona l’anime sì, ch’esser vorrebber sorde.
english: so were the filthy faces of the demon Cerberus transformed—after he’d stunned the spirits so, they wished that they were deaf.

italian: Noi passavam su per l’ombre che adona la greve pioggia, e ponavam le piante sovra lor vanità che par persona.
english: We walked across the shades on whom there thuds that heavy rain, and set our soles upon their empty images that seem like persons.

italian: Elle giacean per terra tutte quante, fuor d’una ch’a seder si levò, ratto ch’ella ci vide passarsi davante.
english: And all those spirits lay upon the ground, except for one who sat erect as soon as he caught sight of us in front of him.

italian: «O tu che se’ per questo ’nferno tratto», mi disse, «riconoscimi, se sai: tu fosti, prima ch’io disfatto, fatto».
english: “O you who are conducted through this Hell,” he said to me, “recall me, if you can; for you, before I was unmade, were made.”

italian: E io a lui: «L’angoscia che tu hai forse ti tira fuor de la mia mente, sì che non par ch’i’ ti vedessi mai.
english: And I to him: “It is perhaps your anguish that snatches you out of my memory, so that it seems that I have never seen you.

italian: Ma dimmi chi tu se’ che ’n sì dolente loco se’ messo, e hai sì fatta pena, che, s’altra è maggio, nulla è sì spiacente».
english: But tell me who you are, you who are set in such a dismal place, such punishment— if other pains are more, none’s more disgusting.”

italian: Ed elli a me: «La tua città, ch’è piena d’invidia sì che già trabocca il sacco, seco mi tenne in la vita serena.
english: And he to me: “Your city—one so full of envy that its sack has always spilled— that city held me in the sunlit life.

italian: Voi cittadini mi chiamaste Ciacco: per la dannosa colpa de la gola, come tu vedi, a la pioggia mi fiacco.
english: The name you citizens gave me was Ciacco; and for the damning sin of gluttony, as you can see, I languish in the rain.

italian: E io anima trista non son sola, ché tutte queste a simil pena stanno per simil colpa». E più non fé parola.
english: And I, a wretched soul, am not alone, for all of these have this same penalty for this same sin.” And he said nothing more.

italian: Io li rispuosi: «Ciacco, il tuo affanno mi pesa sì, ch’a lagrimar mi ’nvita; ma dimmi, se tu sai, a che verranno
english: I answered him: “Ciacco, your suffering so weights on me that I am forced to weep; but tell me, if you know, what end awaits

italian: li cittadin de la città partita; s’alcun v’è giusto; e dimmi la cagione per che l’ha tanta discordia assalita».
english: the citizens of that divided city; is any just man there? Tell me the reason why it has been assailed by so much schism.”

italian: E quelli a me: «Dopo lunga tencione verranno al sangue, e la parte selvaggia caccerà l’altra con molta offensione.
english: And he to me: “After long controversy, they’ll come to blood; the party of the woods will chase the other out with much offense.

italian: Poi appresso convien che questa caggia infra tre soli, e che l’altra sormonti con la forza di tal che testé piaggia.
english: But then, within three suns, they too must fall; at which the other party will prevail, using the power of one who tacks his sails.

italian: Alte terrà lungo tempo le fronti, tenendo l’altra sotto gravi pesi, come che di ciò pianga o che n’aonti.
english: This party will hold high its head for long and heap great weights upon its enemies, however much they weep indignantly.

italian: Giusti son due, e non vi sono intesi; superbia, invidia e avarizia sono le tre faville c’hanno i cuori accesi».
english: Two men are just, but no one listens to them. Three sparks that set on fire every heart are envy, pride, and avariciousness.”

italian: Qui puose fine al lagrimabil suono. E io a lui: «Ancor vo’ che mi ’nsegni e che di più parlar mi facci dono.
english: With this, his words, inciting tears, were done; and I to him: “I would learn more from you; I ask you for a gift of further speech:

italian: Farinata e ’l Tegghiaio, che fuor sì degni, Iacopo Rusticucci, Arrigo e ’l Mosca e li altri ch’a ben far puoser li ’ngegni,
english: Tegghiaio, Farinata, men so worthy, Arrigo, Mosca, Jacopo Rusticucci, and all the rest whose minds bent toward the good,

italian: dimmi ove sono e fa ch’io li conosca; ché gran disio mi stringe di savere se ’l ciel li addolcia o lo ’nferno li attosca».
english: do tell me where they are and let me meet them; for my great longing drives me on to learn if Heaven sweetens or Hell poisons them.”

italian: E quelli: «Ei son tra l’anime più nere; diverse colpe giù li grava al fondo: se tanto scendi, là i potrai vedere.
english: And he: “They are among the blackest souls; a different sin has dragged them to the bottom; if you descend so low, there you can see them.

italian: Ma quando tu sarai nel dolce mondo, priegoti ch’a la mente altrui mi rechi: più non ti dico e più non ti rispondo».
english: But when you have returned to the sweet world, I pray, recall me to men’s memory: I say no more to you, answer no more.”

italian: Li diritti occhi torse allora in biechi; guardommi un poco e poi chinò la testa: cadde con essa a par de li altri ciechi.
english: Then his straight gaze grew twisted and awry; he looked at me awhile, then bent his head; he fell as low as all his blind companions.

italian: E ’l duca disse a me: «Più non si desta di qua dal suon de l’angelica tromba, quando verrà la nimica podesta:
english: And my guide said to me: “He’ll rise no more until the blast of the angelic trumpet upon the coming of the hostile Judge:

italian: ciascun rivederà la trista tomba, ripiglierà sua carne e sua figura, udirà quel ch’in etterno rimbomba».
english: each one shall see his sorry tomb again and once again take on his flesh and form, and hear what shall resound eternally.”

italian: Sì trapassammo per sozza mistura de l’ombre e de la pioggia, a passi lenti, toccando un poco la vita futura;
english: So did we pass across that squalid mixture of shadows and of rain, our steps slowed down, talking awhile about the life to come.

italian: per ch’io dissi: «Maestro, esti tormenti crescerann’ ei dopo la gran sentenza, o fier minori, o saran sì cocenti?».
english: At which I said: “And after the great sentence- o master—will these torments grow, or else be less, or will they be just as intense?”

italian: Ed elli a me: «Ritorna a tua scïenza, che vuol, quanto la cosa è più perfetta, più senta il bene, e così la doglienza.
english: And he to me: “Remember now your science, which says that when a thing has more perfection, so much the greater is its pain or pleasure.

italian: Tutto che questa gente maladetta in vera perfezion già mai non vada, di là più che di qua essere aspetta».
english: Though these accursed sinners never shall attain the true perfection, yet they can expect to be more perfect then than now.”

italian: Noi aggirammo a tondo quella strada, parlando più assai ch’i’ non ridico; venimmo al punto dove si digrada:
english: We took the circling way traced by that road; we said much more than I can here recount; we reached the point that marks the downward slope.

italian: quivi trovammo Pluto, il gran nemico.
english: Here we found Plutus, the great enemy.

italian: « Pape Satàn, pape Satàn aleppe! », cominciò Pluto con la voce chioccia; e quel savio gentil, che tutto seppe,
english: “Pape Satan, Pape Satan aleppe!” so Plutus, with his grating voice, began. The gentle sage, aware of everything,

italian: disse per confortarmi: «Non ti noccia la tua paura; ché, poder ch’elli abbia, non ci torrà lo scender questa roccia».
english: said reassuringly, “Don’t let your fear defeat you; for whatever power he has, he cannot stop our climbing down this crag.”

italian: Poi si rivolse a quella ’nfiata labbia, e disse: «Taci, maladetto lupo! consuma dentro te con la tua rabbia.
english: Then he turned back to Plutus’ swollen face and said to him: “Be quiet, cursed wolf! Let your vindictiveness feed on yourself.

italian: Non è sanza cagion l’andare al cupo: vuolsi ne l’alto, là dove Michele fé la vendetta del superbo strupo».
english: His is no random journey to the deep: it has been willed on high, where Michael took revenge upon the arrogant rebellion.”

italian: Quali dal vento le gonfiate vele caggiono avvolte, poi che l’alber fiacca, tal cadde a terra la fiera crudele.
english: As sails inflated by the wind collapse, entangled in a heap, when the mast cracks, so that ferocious beast fell to the ground.

italian: Così scendemmo ne la quarta lacca, pigliando più de la dolente ripa che ’l mal de l’universo tutto insacca.
english: Thus we made our way down to the fourth ditch, to take in more of that despondent shore where all the universe’s ill is stored.

italian: Ahi giustizia di Dio! tante chi stipa nove travaglie e pene quant’ io viddi? e perché nostra colpa sì ne scipa?
english: Justice of God! Who has amassed as many strange tortures and travails as I have seen? Why do we let our guilt consume us so?

italian: Come fa l’onda là sovra Cariddi, che si frange con quella in cui s’intoppa, così convien che qui la gente riddi.
english: Even as waves that break above Charybdis, each shattering the other when they meet, so must the spirits here dance their round dance.

italian: Qui vid’ i’ gente più ch’altrove troppa, e d’una parte e d’altra, con grand’ urli, voltando pesi per forza di poppa.
english: Here, more than elsewhere, I saw multitudes to every side of me; their howls were loud while, wheeling weights, they used their chests to push.

italian: Percotëansi ’ncontro; e poscia pur lì si rivolgea ciascun, voltando a retro, gridando: «Perché tieni?» e «Perché burli?».
english: They struck against each other; at that point, each turned around and, wheeling back those weights, cried out: “Why do you hoard?” “Why do you squander?”

italian: Così tornavan per lo cerchio tetro da ogne mano a l’opposito punto, gridandosi anche loro ontoso metro;
english: So did they move around the sorry circle from left and right to the opposing point; again, again they cried their chant of scorn;

italian: poi si volgea ciascun, quand’ era giunto, per lo suo mezzo cerchio a l’altra giostra. E io, ch’avea lo cor quasi compunto,
english: and so, when each of them had changed positions, he circled halfway back to his next joust. And I, who felt my heart almost pierced through,

italian: dissi: «Maestro mio, or mi dimostra che gente è questa, e se tutti fuor cherci questi chercuti a la sinistra nostra».
english: requested: “Master, show me now what shades are these and tell me if they all were clerics— those tonsured ones who circle on our left.”

italian: Ed elli a me: «Tutti quanti fuor guerci sì de la mente in la vita primaia, che con misura nullo spendio ferci.
english: And he to me: “All these, to left and right were so squint-eyed of mind in the first life— no spending that they did was done with measure.

italian: Assai la voce lor chiaro l’abbaia, quando vegnono a’ due punti del cerchio dove colpa contraria li dispaia.
english: Their voices bark this out with clarity when they have reached the two points of the circle where their opposing guilts divide their ranks.

italian: Questi fuor cherci, che non han coperchio piloso al capo, e papi e cardinali, in cui usa avarizia il suo soperchio».
english: These to the left—their heads bereft of hair— were clergymen, and popes and cardinals, within whom avarice works its excess.”

italian: E io: «Maestro, tra questi cotali dovre’ io ben riconoscere alcuni che furo immondi di cotesti mali».
english: And I to him: “Master, among this kind I certainly might hope to recognize some who have been bespattered by these crimes.”

italian: Ed elli a me: «Vano pensiero aduni: la sconoscente vita che i fé sozzi, ad ogne conoscenza or li fa bruni.
english: And he to me: “That thought of yours is empty: the undiscerning life that made them filthy now renders them unrecognizable.

italian: In etterno verranno a li due cozzi: questi resurgeranno del sepulcro col pugno chiuso, e questi coi crin mozzi.
english: For all eternity they’ll come to blows: these here will rise up from their sepulchers with fists clenched tight; and these, with hair cropped close.

italian: Mal dare e mal tener lo mondo pulcro ha tolto loro, e posti a questa zuffa: qual ella sia, parole non ci appulcro.
english: Ill giving and ill keeping have robbed both of the fair world and set them to this fracas— what that is like, my words need not embellish.

italian: Or puoi, figliuol, veder la corta buffa d’i ben che son commessi a la fortuna, per che l’umana gente si rabbuffa;
english: Now you can see, my son, how brief’s the sport of all those goods that are in Fortune’s care, for which the tribe of men contend and brawl;

italian: ché tutto l’oro ch’è sotto la luna e che già fu, di quest’ anime stanche non poterebbe farne posare una».
english: for all the gold that is or ever was beneath the moon could never offer rest to even one of these exhausted spirits.”

italian: «Maestro mio», diss’ io, «or mi dì anche: questa fortuna di che tu mi tocche, che è, che i ben del mondo ha sì tra branche?».
english: “Master,” I asked of him, “now tell me too: this Fortune whom you’ve touched upon just now— what’s she, who clutches so all the world’s goods?”

italian: E quelli a me: «Oh creature sciocche, quanta ignoranza è quella che v’offende! Or vo’ che tu mia sentenza ne ’mbocche.
english: And he to me: “O unenlightened creatures, how deep—the ignorance that hampers you! I want you to digest my word on this.

italian: Colui lo cui saver tutto trascende, fece li cieli e diè lor chi conduce sì, ch’ogne parte ad ogne parte splende,
english: Who made the heavens and who gave them guides was He whose wisdom transcends everything; that every part may shine unto the other,

italian: distribuendo igualmente la luce. Similemente a li splendor mondani ordinò general ministra e duce
english: He had the light apportioned equally; similarly, for wordly splendors, He ordained a general minister and guide

italian: che permutasse a tempo li ben vani di gente in gente e d’uno in altro sangue, oltre la difension d’i senni umani;
english: to shift, from time to time, those empty goods from nation unto nation, clan to clan, in ways that human reason can’t prevent;

italian: per ch’una gente impera e l’altra langue, seguendo lo giudicio di costei, che è occulto come in erba l’angue.
english: just so, one people rules, one languishes, obeying the decision she has given, which, like a serpent in the grass, is hidden.
