english: the sepulchers make all the plain uneven, so they did here on every side, except that here the sepulchers were much more harsh;

italian: ché tra li avelli fiamme erano sparte, per le quali eran sì del tutto accesi, che ferro più non chiede verun’ arte.
english: for flames were scattered through the tombs, and these had kindled all of them to glowing heat; no artisan could ask for hotter iron.

italian: Tutti li lor coperchi eran sospesi, e fuor n’uscivan sì duri lamenti, che ben parean di miseri e d’offesi.
english: The lid of every tomb was lifted up, and from each tomb such sorry cries arose as could come only from the sad and hurt.

italian: E io: «Maestro, quai son quelle genti che, seppellite dentro da quell’ arche, si fan sentir coi sospiri dolenti?».
english: And I: “Master, who can these people be who, buried in great chests of stone like these, must speak by way of sighs in agony?”

italian: E quelli a me: «Qui son li eresïarche con lor seguaci, d’ogne setta, e molto più che non credi son le tombe carche.
english: And he to me: “Here are arch—heretics and those who followed them, from every sect; those tombs are much more crowded than you think.

italian: Simile qui con simile è sepolto, e i monimenti son più e men caldi». E poi ch’a la man destra si fu vòlto,
english: Here, like has been ensepulchered with like; some monuments are heated more, some less.” And then he turned around and to his right;

italian: passammo tra i martìri e li alti spaldi.
english: we passed between the torments and high walls.

italian: Ora sen va per un secreto calle, tra ’l muro de la terra e li martìri, lo mio maestro, e io dopo le spalle.
english: Now, by a narrow path that ran between those torments and the ramparts of the city, my master moves ahead, I following.

italian: «O virtù somma, che per li empi giri mi volvi», cominciai, «com’ a te piace, parlami, e sodisfammi a’ miei disiri.
english: “O highest virtue, you who lead me through these circles of transgression, at your will, do speak to me, and satisfy my longings.

italian: La gente che per li sepolcri giace potrebbesi veder? già son levati tutt’ i coperchi, e nessun guardia face».
english: Can those who lie within the sepulchers be seen? The lids—in fact—have all been lifted; no guardian is watching over them.”

italian: E quelli a me: «Tutti saran serrati quando di Iosafàt qui torneranno coi corpi che là sù hanno lasciati.
english: And he to me: “They’ll all be shuttered up when they return here from Jehosaphat together with the flesh they left above.

italian: Suo cimitero da questa parte hanno con Epicuro tutti suoi seguaci, che l’anima col corpo morta fanno.
english: Within this region is the cemetery of Epicurus and his followers, all those who say the soul dies with the body.

italian: Però a la dimanda che mi faci quinc’ entro satisfatto sarà tosto, e al disio ancor che tu mi taci».
english: And so the question you have asked of me will soon find satisfaction while we’re here, as will the longing you have hid from me.”

italian: E io: «Buon duca, non tegno riposto a te mio cuor se non per dicer poco, e tu m’hai non pur mo a ciò disposto».
english: And I: “Good guide, the only reason I have hid my heart was that I might speak briefly, and you, long since, encouraged me in this.”

italian: «O Tosco che per la città del foco vivo ten vai così parlando onesto, piacciati di restare in questo loco.
english: “O Tuscan, you who pass alive across the fiery city with such seemly words, be kind enough to stay your journey here.

italian: La tua loquela ti fa manifesto di quella nobil patrïa natio a la qual forse fui troppo molesto».
english: Your accent makes it clear that you belong among the natives of the noble city I may have dealt with too vindictively.”

italian: Subitamente questo suono uscìo d’una de l’arche; però m’accostai, temendo, un poco più al duca mio.
english: This sound had burst so unexpectedly out of one sepulcher that, trembling, I then drew a little closer to my guide.

italian: Ed el mi disse: «Volgiti! Che fai? Vedi là Farinata che s’è dritto: da la cintola in sù tutto ’l vedrai».
english: But he told me: “Turn round! What are you doing? That’s Farinata who has risen there— you will see all of him from the waist up.”

italian: Io avea già il mio viso nel suo fitto; ed el s’ergea col petto e con la fronte com’ avesse l’inferno a gran dispitto.
english: My eyes already were intent on his; and up he rose—his forehead and his chest- as if he had tremendous scorn for Hell.

italian: E l’animose man del duca e pronte mi pinser tra le sepulture a lui, dicendo: «Le parole tue sien conte».
english: My guide—his hands encouraging and quick- thrust me between the sepulchers toward him, saying: “Your words must be appropriate.”

italian: Com’ io al piè de la sua tomba fui, guardommi un poco, e poi, quasi sdegnoso, mi dimandò: «Chi fuor li maggior tui?».
english: When I’d drawn closer to his sepulcher, he glanced at me, and as if in disdain, he asked of me: “Who were your ancestors?”

italian: Io ch’era d’ubidir disideroso, non gliel celai, ma tutto gliel’ apersi; ond’ ei levò le ciglia un poco in suso;
english: Because I wanted so to be compliant, I hid no thing from him: I told him all. At this he lifted up his brows a bit,

italian: poi disse: «Fieramente furo avversi a me e a miei primi e a mia parte, sì che per due fïate li dispersi».
english: then said: “They were ferocious enemies of mine and of my parents and my party, so that I had to scatter them twice over.”

italian: «S’ei fur cacciati, ei tornar d’ogne parte», rispuos’ io lui, «l’una e l’altra fïata; ma i vostri non appreser ben quell’arte».
english: “If they were driven out,” I answered him, “they still returned, both times, from every quarter; but yours were never quick to learn that art.”

italian: Allor surse a la vista scoperchiata un’ombra, lungo questa, infino al mento: credo che s’era in ginocchie levata.
english: At this there rose another shade alongside, uncovered to my sight down to his chin; I think that he had risen on his knees.

italian: Dintorno mi guardò, come talento avesse di veder s’altri era meco; e poi che ’l sospecciar fu tutto spento,
english: He looked around me, just as if he longed to see if I had come with someone else; but then, his expectation spent, he said

italian: piangendo disse: «Se per questo cieco carcere vai per altezza d’ ingegno, mio figlio ov’ è? e perché non è teco?».
english: in tears: “If it is your high intellect that lets you journey here, through this blind prison, where is my son? Why is he not with you?”

italian: E io a lui: «Da me stesso non vegno: colui ch’attende là, per qui mi mena forse cui Guido vostro ebbe a disdegno».
english: I answered: “My own powers have not brought me; he who awaits me there, leads me through here perhaps to one your Guido did disdain.”

italian: Le sue parole e ’l modo de la pena m’avean di costui già letto il nome; però fu la risposta così piena.
english: His words, the nature of his punishment— these had already let me read his name; therefore, my answer was so fully made.

italian: Di sùbito drizzato gridò: «Come dicesti “elli ebbe”? non viv’ elli ancora? non fiere li occhi suoi lo dolce lume?».
english: Then suddenly erect, he cried: “What’s that: He ‘did disdain’? He is not still alive? The sweet light does not strike against his eyes?”

italian: Quando s’accorse d’alcuna dimora ch’io facëa dinanzi a la risposta, supin ricadde e più non parve fora.
english: And when he noticed how I hesitated a moment in my answer, he fell back— supine—and did not show himself again.

italian: Ma quell’ altro magnanimo, a cui posta restato m’era, non mutò aspetto, né mosse collo, né piegò sua costa;
english: But that great—hearted one, the other shade at whose request I’d stayed, did not change aspect or turn aside his head or lean or bend;

italian: e sé continüando al primo detto, «S’elli han quell’ arte», disse, «male appresa, ciò mi tormenta più che questo letto.
english: and taking up his words where—he’d left off, “If they were slow,” he said, “to learn that art, that is more torment to me than this bed.

italian: Ma non cinquanta volte fia raccesa la faccia de la donna che qui regge, che tu saprai quanto quell’ arte pesa.
english: And yet the Lady who is ruler here will not have her face kindled fifty times before you learn how heavy is that art.

italian: E se tu mai nel dolce mondo regge, dimmi: perché quel popolo è sì empio incontr’ a’ miei in ciascuna sua legge?».
english: And so may you return to the sweet world, tell me: why are those citizens so cruel against my kin in all of their decrees?”

italian: Ond’ io a lui: «Lo strazio e ’l grande scempio che fece l’Arbia colorata in rosso, tal orazion fa far nel nostro tempio».
english: To which I said: “The carnage, the great bloodshed that stained the waters of the Arbia red have led us to such prayers in our temple.”

italian: Poi ch’ebbe sospirando il capo mosso, «A ciò non fu’ io sol», disse, «né certo sanza cagion con li altri sarei mosso.
english: He sighed and shook his head, then said: “In that, I did not act alone, but certainly I’d not have joined the others without cause.

italian: Ma fu’ io solo, là dove sofferto fu per ciascun di tòrre via Fiorenza, colui che la difesi a viso aperto».
english: But where I was alone was there where all the rest would have annihilated Florence, had I not interceded forcefully.”

italian: «Deh, se riposi mai vostra semenza», prega’ io lui, «solvetemi quel nodo che qui ha ’nviluppata mia sentenza.
english: “Ah, as I hope your seed may yet find peace,” I asked, “so may you help me to undo the knot that here has snarled my course of thought.

italian: El par che voi veggiate, se ben odo, dinanzi quel che ’l tempo seco adduce, e nel presente tenete altro modo».
english: It seems, if I hear right, that you can see beforehand that which time is carrying, but you’re denied the sight of present things.”

italian: «Noi veggiam, come quei c’ha mala luce, le cose», disse, «che ne son lontano; cotanto ancor ne splende il sommo duce.
english: “We see, even as men who are farsighted, those things,” he said, “that are remote from us; the Highest Lord allots us that much light.

italian: Quando s’appressano o son, tutto è vano nostro intelletto; e s’altri non ci apporta, nulla sapem di vostro stato umano.
english: But when events draw near or are, our minds are useless; were we not informed by others, we should know nothing of your human state.

italian: Però comprender puoi che tutta morta fia nostra conoscenza da quel punto che del futuro fia chiusa la porta».
english: So you can understand how our awareness will die completely at the moment when the portal of the future has been shut.”

italian: Allor, come di mia colpa compunto, dissi: «Or direte dunque a quel caduto che ’l suo nato è co’ vivi ancor congiunto;
english: Then, as if penitent for my omission, I said: “Will you now tell that fallen man his son is still among the living ones;

italian: e s’i’ fui, dianzi, a la risposta muto, fate i saper che ’l fei perché pensava già ne l’error che m’avete soluto».
english: and if, a while ago, I held my tongue before his question, let him know it was because I had in mind the doubt you’ve answered.”

italian: E già ’l maestro mio mi richiamava; per ch’i’ pregai lo spirto più avaccio che mi dicesse chi con lu’ istava.
english: And now my master was recalling me; so that, more hurriedly, I asked the spirit to name the others who were there with him.

italian: Dissemi: «Qui con più di mille giaccio: qua dentro è ’l secondo Federico, e ’l Cardinale; e de li altri mi taccio».
english: He said: “More than a thousand lie with me: the second Frederick is but one among them, as is the Cardinal; I name no others.”

italian: Indi s’ascose; e io inver’ l’antico poeta volsi i passi, ripensando a quel parlar che mi parea nemico.
english: With that, he hid himself; and pondering the speech that seemed to me so menacing, I turned my steps to meet the ancient poet.

italian: Elli si mosse; e poi, così andando, mi disse: «Perché se’ tu sì smarrito?». E io li sodisfeci al suo dimando.
english: He moved ahead, and as we made our way, he said to me: “Why are you so dismayed?” I satisfied him, answering him fully.

italian: «La mente tua conservi quel ch’udito hai contra te», mi comandò quel saggio; «e ora attendi qui», e drizzò ’l dito:
english: And then that sage exhorted me: “Remember the words that have been spoken here against you. Now pay attention,” and he raised his finger;

italian: «quando sarai dinanzi al dolce raggio di quella il cui bell’ occhio tutto vede, da lei saprai di tua vita il vïaggio».
english: “when you shall stand before the gentle splendor of one whose gracious eyes see everything, then you shall learn—from her—your lifetime’s journey.”

italian: Appresso mosse a man sinistra il piede: lasciammo il muro e gimmo inver’ lo mezzo per un sentier ch’a una valle fiede,
english: Following that, his steps turned to the left, leaving the wall and moving toward the middle along a path that strikes into a valley

italian: che ’nfin là sù facea spiacer suo lezzo.
english: whose stench, as it rose up, disgusted us.

italian: In su l’estremità d’un’alta ripa che facevan gran pietre rotte in cerchio, venimmo sopra più crudele stipa;
english: Along the upper rim of a high bank formed by a ring of massive broken boulders, we came above a crowd more cruelly pent.

italian: e quivi, per l’orribile soperchio del puzzo che ’l profondo abisso gitta, ci raccostammo, in dietro, ad un coperchio
english: And here, because of the outrageous stench thrown up in excess by that deep abyss, we drew back till we were behind the lid

italian: d’un grand’ avello, ov’ io vidi una scritta che dicea: ‘Anastasio papa guardo, lo qual trasse Fotin de la via dritta’.
english: of a great tomb, on which I made out this, inscribed: “I hold Pope Anastasius, enticed to leave the true path by Photinus.”

italian: «Lo nostro scender conviene esser tardo, sì che s’ausi un poco in prima il senso al tristo fiato; e poi no i fia riguardo».
english: “It would be better to delay descent so that our senses may grow somewhat used to this foul stench; and then we can ignore it.”

italian: Così ’l maestro; e io «Alcun compenso», dissi lui, «trova che ’l tempo non passi perduto». Ed elli: «Vedi ch’a ciò penso».
english: So said my master, and I answered him: “Do find some compensation, lest this time be lost.” And he: “You see, I’ve thought of that.”

italian: «Figliuol mio, dentro da cotesti sassi», cominciò poi a dir, «son tre cerchietti di grado in grado, come que’ che lassi.
english: “My son, within this ring of broken rocks,” he then began, “there are three smaller circles; like those that you are leaving, they range down.

italian: Tutti son pien di spirti maladetti; ma perché poi ti basti pur la vista, intendi come e perché son costretti.
english: Those circles are all full of cursed spirits; so that your seeing of them may suffice, learn now the how and why of their confinement.

italian: D’ogne malizia, ch’odio in cielo acquista, ingiuria è ’l fine, ed ogne fin cotale o con forza o con frode altrui contrista.
english: Of every malice that earns hate in Heaven, injustice is the end; and each such end by force or fraud brings harm to other men.

italian: Ma perché frode è de l’uom proprio male, più spiace a Dio; e però stan di sotto li frodolenti, e più dolor li assale.
english: However, fraud is man’s peculiar vice; God finds it more displeasing — and therefore, the fraudulent are lower, suffering more.

italian: Di vïolenti il primo cerchio è tutto; ma perché si fa forza a tre persone, in tre gironi è distinto e costrutto.
english: The violent take all of the first circle; but since one uses force against three persons, that circle’s built of three divided rings.

italian: A Dio, a sé, al prossimo si pòne far forza, dico in loro e in lor cose, come udirai con aperta ragione.
english: To God and to one’s self and to one’s neighbor — I mean, to them or what is theirs — one can do violence, as you shall now hear clearly.

italian: Morte per forza e ferute dogliose nel prossimo si danno, e nel suo avere ruine, incendi e tollette dannose;
english: Violent death and painful wounds may be inflicted on one’s neighbor; his possessions may suffer ruin, fire, and extortion;

italian: onde omicide e ciascun che mal fiere, guastatori e predon, tutti tormenta lo giron primo per diverse schiere.
english: thus, murderers and those who strike in malice, as well as plunderers and robbers — these, in separated ranks, the first ring racks.

italian: Puote omo avere in sé man vïolenta e ne’ suoi beni; e però nel secondo giron convien che sanza pro si penta
english: A man can set violent hands against himself or his belongings; so within the second ring repents, though uselessly,

italian: qualunque priva sé del vostro mondo, biscazza e fonde la sua facultade, e piange là dov’ esser de’ giocondo.
english: whoever would deny himself your world, gambling away, wasting his patrimony, and weeping where he should instead be happy.

italian: Puossi far forza nella deïtade, col cor negando e bestemmiando quella, e spregiando natura e sua bontade;
english: One can be violent against the Godhead, one’s heart denying and blaspheming Him and scorning nature and the good in her;

italian: e però lo minor giron suggella del segno suo e Soddoma e Caorsa e chi, spregiando Dio col cor, favella.
english: so, with its sign, the smallest ring has sealed both Sodom and Cahors and all of those who speak in passionate contempt of God.

italian: La frode, ond’ ogne coscïenza è morsa, può l’omo usare in colui che ’n lui fida e in quel che fidanza non imborsa.
english: Now fraud, that eats away at every conscience, is practiced by a man against another who trusts in him, or one who has no trust.

italian: Questo modo di retro par ch’incida pur lo vinco d’amor che fa natura; onde nel cerchio secondo s’annida
english: This latter way seems only to cut off the bond of love that nature forges; thus, nestled within the second circle are:

italian: ipocresia, lusinghe e chi affattura, falsità, ladroneccio e simonia, ruffian, baratti e simile lordura.
english: hypocrisy and flattery, sorcerers, and falsifiers, simony, and theft, and barrators and panders and like trash.

italian: Per l’altro modo quell’ amor s’oblia che fa natura, e quel ch’è poi aggiunto, di che la fede spezïal si cria;
english: But in the former way of fraud, not only the love that nature forges is forgotten, but added love that builds a special trust;

italian: onde nel cerchio minore, ov’ è ’l punto de l’universo in su che Dite siede, qualunque trade in etterno è consunto».
english: thus, in the tightest circle, where there is the universe’s center, seat of Dis, all traitors are consumed eternally.”

italian: E io: «Maestro, assai chiara procede la tua ragione, e assai ben distingue questo baràtro e ’l popol ch’e’ possiede.
english: “Master, your reasoning is clear indeed,” I said; “it has made plain for me the nature of this pit and the population in it.

italian: Ma dimmi: quei de la palude pingue, che mena il vento, e che batte la pioggia, e che s’incontran con sì aspre lingue,
english: But tell me: those the dense marsh holds, or those driven before the wind, or those on whom rain falls, or those who clash with such harsh tongues,

italian: perché non dentro da la città roggia sono ei puniti, se Dio li ha in ira? e se non li ha, perché sono a tal foggia?».
english: why are they not all punished in the city of flaming red if God is angry with them? And if He’s not, why then are they tormented?”

italian: Ed elli a me «Perché tanto delira», disse, «lo ’ngegno tuo da quel che sòle? o ver la mente dove altrove mira?
english: And then to me, “Why does your reason wander so far from its accustomed course?” he said. “Or of what other things are you now thinking?

italian: Non ti rimembra di quelle parole con le quai la tua Etica pertratta le tre disposizion che ’l ciel non vole,
english: Have you forgotten, then, the words with which your Ethics treats of those three dispositions that strike at Heaven’s will: incontinence

italian: incontenenza, malizia e la matta bestialitade? e come incontenenza men Dio offende e men biasimo accatta?
english: and malice and mad bestiality? And how the fault that is the least condemned and least offends God is incontinence?

italian: Se tu riguardi ben questa sentenza, e rechiti a la mente chi son quelli che sù di fuor sostegnon penitenza,
english: If you consider carefully this judgment and call to mind the souls of upper Hell, who bear their penalties outside this city,

italian: tu vedrai ben perché da questi felli sien dipartiti, e perché men crucciata la divina vendetta li martelli».
english: you’ll see why they have been set off from these unrighteous ones, and why, when heaven’s vengeance hammers at them, it carries lesser anger.”

italian: «O sol che sani ogni vista turbata, tu mi contenti sì quando tu solvi, che, non men che saver, dubbiar m’aggrata.
english: “O sun that heals all sight that is perplexed, when I ask you, your answer so contents that doubting pleases me as much as knowing.

italian: Ancora in dietro un poco ti rivolvi», diss’ io, «là dove di’ ch’usura offende la divina bontade, e ’l groppo solvi».
english: Go back a little to that point,” I said, “where you told me that usury offends divine goodness; unravel now that knot.”

italian: «Filosofia», mi disse, «a chi la ’ntende, nota, non pure in una sola parte, come natura lo suo corso prende
english: “Philosophy, for one who understands, points out, and not in just one place,” he said, “how nature follows — as she takes her course —

italian: dal divino ’ntelletto e da sua arte; e se tu ben la tua Fisica note, tu troverai, non dopo molte carte,
english: the Divine Intellect and Divine Art; and if you read your Physics carefully, not many pages from the start, you’ll see

italian: che l’arte vostra quella, quanto pote, segue, come ’l maestro fa ’l discente; sì che vostr’ arte a Dio quasi è nepote.
english: that when it can, your art would follow nature, just as a pupil imitates his master; so that your art is almost God’s grandchild.

italian: Da queste due, se tu ti rechi a mente lo Genesì dal principio, convene prender sua vita e avanzar la gente;
english: From these two, art and nature, it is fitting, if you recall how Genesis begins, for men to make their way, to gain their living;

italian: e perché l’usuriere altra via tene, per sé natura e per la sua seguace dispregia, poi ch’in altro pon la spene.
english: and since the usurer prefers another pathway, he scorns both nature in herself and art, her follower; his hope is elsewhere.

italian: Ma seguimi oramai, che ’l gir mi piace; ché i Pesci guizzan su per l’orizzonta, e ’l Carro tutto sovra ’l Coro giace,
english: But follow me, for it is time to move; the Fishes glitter now on the horizon all the Wain is spread out over Caurus;

italian: e ’l balzo via là oltra si dismonta».
english: only beyond, can one climb down the cliff.”

italian: Era lo loco ov’ a scender la riva venimmo, alpestro e, per quel che v’er’ anco, tal, ch’ogne vista ne sarebbe schiva.
english: The place that we had reached for our descent along the bank was alpine; what reclined upon that bank would, too, repel all eyes.

italian: Qual è quella ruina che nel fianco di qua da Trento l’Adice percosse, o per tremoto o per sostegno manco,
english: Just like the toppled mass of rock that struck— because of earthquake or eroded props— the Adige on its flank, this side of Trent,

italian: che da cima del monte, onde si mosse, al piano è sì la roccia discoscesa, ch’alcuna via darebbe a chi sù fosse:
english: where from the mountain top from which it thrust down to the plain, the rock is shattered so that it permits a path for those above:

italian: cotal di quel burrato era la scesa; e ’n su la punta de la rotta lacca l’infamïa di Creti era distesa
english: such was the passage down to that ravine. And at the edge above the cracked abyss, there lay outstretched the infamy of Crete,

italian: che fu concetta ne la falsa vacca; e quando vide noi, sé stesso morse, sì come quei cui l’ira dentro fiacca.
english: conceived within the counterfeited cow; and, catching sight of us, he bit himself like one whom fury devastates within.

italian: Lo savio mio inver’ lui gridò: «Forse tu credi che qui sia ’l duca d’Atene, che sù nel mondo la morte ti porse?
english: Turning to him, my sage cried out: “Perhaps you think this is the Duke of Athens here, who, in the world above, brought you your death.

italian: Pàrtiti, bestia, ché questi non vene ammaestrato da la tua sorella, ma vassi per veder le vostre pene».
english: Be off, you beast; this man who comes has not been tutored by your sister; all he wants in coming here is to observe your torments.”

italian: Qual è quel toro che si slaccia in quella c’ha ricevuto già ’l colpo mortale, che gir non sa, ma qua e là saltella,
english: Just as the bull that breaks loose from its halter the moment it receives the fatal stroke, and cannot run but plunges back and forth,

italian: vid’io lo Minotauro far cotale; e quello accorto gridò; «Corri al varco: mentre ch’e’ ’nfuria, è buon che tu ti cale».
english: so did I see the Minotaur respond; and my alert guide cried: “Run toward the pass; it’s better to descend while he’s berserk.”

italian: Così prendemmo via giù per lo scarco di quelle pietre, che spesso moviensi sotto i miei piedi per lo novo carco.
english: And so we made our way across that heap of stones, which often moved beneath my feet because my weight was somewhat strange for them.

english: And my good master, though I had not asked, urged me: “Look at that mighty one who comes and does not seem to shed a tear of pain:

italian: quanto aspetto reale ancor ritene! Quelli è Iasón, che per cuore e per senno li Colchi del monton privati féne.
english: how he still keeps the image of a king! That shade is Jason, who with heart and head deprived the men of Colchis of their ram.

italian: Ello passò per l’isola di Lenno, poi che l’ardite femmine spietate tutti li maschi loro a morte dienno.
english: He made a landfall on the isle of Lemnos after its women, bold and pitiless, had given all their island males to death.

italian: Ivi con segni e con parole ornate Isifile ingannò, la giovinetta che prima avea tutte l’ altre ingannate.
english: With polished words and love signs he took in Hypsipyle, the girl whose own deception had earlier deceived the other women.

italian: Lasciolla quivi, gravida, soletta; tal colpa a tal martiro lui condanna; e anche di Medea si fa vendetta.
english: And he abandoned her, alone and pregnant; such guilt condemns him to such punishment; and for Medea, too, revenge is taken.

italian: Con lui sen va chi da tal parte inganna: e questo basti de la prima valle sapere e di color che ’n sé assanna».
english: With him go those who cheated so: this is enough for you to know of that first valley and of the souls it clamps within its jaws.”

italian: Già eravam là ’ve lo stretto calle con l’ argine secondo s’incrocicchia, e fa di quello ad un altr’ arco spalle.
english: We were already where the narrow path reaches and intersects the second bank and serves as shoulder for another bridge.

italian: Quindi sentimmo gente che si nicchia ne l’altra bolgia e che col muso scuffa, e sé medesma con le palme picchia.
english: We heard the people whine in the next pouch and heard them as they snorted with their snouts; we heard them use their palms to beat themselves.

italian: Le ripe eran grommate d’una muffa, per l’alito di giù che vi s’appasta, che con li occhi e col naso facea zuffa.
english: And exhalations, rising from below, stuck to the banks, encrusting them with mold, and so waged war against both eyes and nose.

italian: Lo fondo è cupo sì, che non ci basta loco a veder sanza montare al dosso de l’arco, ove lo scoglio più sovrasta.
english: The bottom is so deep, we found no spot to see it from, except by climbing up the arch until the bridge’s highest point.

italian: Quivi venimmo; e quindi giù nel fosso vidi gente attuffata in uno sterco che da li uman privadi parea mosso.
english: This was the place we reached; the ditch beneath held people plunged in excrement that seemed as if it had been poured from human privies.

italian: E mentre ch’io là giù con l’occhio cerco, vidi un col capo sì di merda lordo, che non parëa s’era laico o cherco.
english: And while my eyes searched that abysmal sight, I saw one with a head so smeared with shit, one could not see if he were lay or cleric.

italian: Quei mi sgridò: «Perché se’ tu sì gordo di riguardar più me che li altri brutti?». E io a lui: «Perché, se ben ricordo,
english: He howled: “Why do you stare more greedily at me than at the others who are filthy?” And I: “Because, if I remember right,

italian: già t’ho veduto coi capelli asciutti, e se’ Alessio Interminei da Lucca: però t’adocchio più che li altri tutti».
english: I have seen you before, with your hair dry; and so I eye you more than all: you are Alessio Interminei of Lucca.”‘

italian: Ed elli allor, battendosi la zucca: «Qua giù m’hanno sommerso le lusinghe ond’io non ebbi mai la lingua stucca».
english: Then he continued, pounding on his pate: “I am plunged here because of flatteries— of which my tongue had such sufficiency.”

italian: Appresso ciò lo duca «Fa che pinghe», mi disse «il viso un poco più avante, sì che la faccia ben con l’occhio attinghe
english: At which my guide advised me: “See you thrust your head a little farther to the front, so that your eyes can clearly glimpse the face

italian: di quella sozza e scapigliata fante che là si graffia con l’unghie merdose, e or s’accoscia e ora è in piedi stante.
english: of that besmirched, bedraggled harridan who scratches at herself with shit—filled nails, and now she crouches, now she stands upright.

italian: Taïde è, la puttana che rispuose al drudo suo quando disse “Ho io grazie grandi apo te?”: “Anzi maravigliose!”.
english: That is Thais, the harlot who returned her lover’s question, ‘Are you very grateful to me?’ by saying, ‘Yes, enormously.'”

italian: E quinci sien le nostre viste sazie».
english: And now our sight has had its fill of this.”

italian: O Simon mago, o miseri seguaci che le cose di Dio, che di bontate deon essere spose, e voi rapaci
english: O Simon Magus! O his sad disciples! Rapacious ones, who take the things of God, that ought to be the brides of Righteousness,

italian: per oro e per argento avolterate, or convien che per voi suoni la tromba, però che ne la terza bolgia state.
english: and make them fornicate for gold and silver! The time has come to let the trumpet sound for you; your place is here in this third pouch.

italian: Già eravamo, a la seguente tomba, montati de lo scoglio in quella parte ch’a punto sovra mezzo ’l fosso piomba.
english: We had already reached the tomb beyond and climbed onto the ridge, where its high point hangs just above the middle of the ditch.

italian: O somma sapïenza, quanta è l’arte che mostri in cielo, in terra e nel mal mondo, e quanto giusto tua virtù comparte!
english: O Highest Wisdom, how much art you show in heaven, earth, and this sad world below, how just your power is when it allots!

italian: Io vidi per le coste e per lo fondo piena la pietra livida di fóri, d’un largo tutti e ciascun era tondo.
english: Along the sides and down along the bottom, I saw that livid rock was perforated: the openings were all one width and round.

italian: Non mi parean men ampi né maggiori che que’ che son nel mio bel San Giovanni, fatti per loco d’i battezzatori;
english: They did not seem to me less broad or more than those that in my handsome San Giovanni were made to serve as basins for baptizing;

italian: l’un de li quali, ancor non è molt’ anni, rupp’ io per un che dentro v’annegava: e questo sia suggel ch’ogn’omo sganni.
english: and one of these, not many years ago, I broke for someone who was drowning in it: and let this be my seal to set men straight.

italian: Fuor de la bocca a ciascun soperchiava d’un peccator li piedi e de le gambe infino al grosso, e l’altro dentro stava.
english: Out from the mouth of each hole there emerged a sinner’s feet and so much of his legs up to the thigh; the rest remained within.

italian: Le piante erano a tutti accese intrambe; per che sì forte guizzavan le giunte, che spezzate averien ritorte e strambe.
english: Both soles of every sinner were on fire; their joints were writhing with such violence, they would have severed withes and ropes of grass.

italian: Qual suole il fiammeggiar de le cose unte muoversi pur su per la strema buccia, tal era lì dai calcagni a le punte.
english: As flame on oily things will only stir along the outer surface, so there, too, that fire made its way from heels to toes.

italian: «Chi è colui, maestro, che si cruccia guizzando più che li altri suoi consorti», diss’ io, «e cui più roggia fiamma succia?».
english: “Master,” I said, “who is that shade who suffers and quivers more than all his other comrades, that sinner who is licked by redder flames?”

italian: Ed elli a me: «Se tu vuo’ ch’i’ ti porti là giù per quella ripa che più giace, da lui saprai di sé e de’ suoi torti».
english: And he to me: “If you would have me lead you down along the steepest of the banks, from him you’ll learn about his self and sins.”

italian: E io: «Tanto m’è bel, quanto a te piace: tu se’ segnore, e sai ch’i’ non mi parto dal tuo volere, e sai quel che si tace».
english: And I: “What pleases you will please me too: you are my lord; you know I do not swerve from what you will, you know what is unspoken.”

italian: Allor venimmo in su l’argine quarto; volgemmo e discendemmo a mano stanca là giù nel fondo foracchiato e arto.
english: At this we came upon the fourth embankment; we turned and, keeping to the left, descended into the narrow, perforated bottom.

italian: Lo buon maestro ancor de la sua anca non mi dipuose, sì mi giunse al rotto di quel che si piangeva con la zanca.
english: My good lord did not let me leave his side until he’d brought me to the hole that held that sinner who lamented with his legs.

italian: «O qual che se’ che ’l di sù tien di sotto, anima trista come pal commessa», comincia’ io a dir, «se puoi, fa motto».
english: “Whoever you may be, dejected soul, whose head is downward, planted like a pole,” my words began, “do speak if you are able.”

italian: Io stava come ’l frate che confessa lo perfido assessin, che, poi ch’è fitto, richiama lui per che la morte cessa.
english: I stood as does the friar who confesses the foul assassin who, fixed fast, head down, calls back the friar, and so delays his death;

italian: Ed el gridò: «Se’ tu già costì ritto, se’ tu già costì ritto, Bonifazio? Di parecchi anni mi mentì lo scritto.
english: and he cried out: “Are you already standing, already standing there, o Boniface? The book has lied to me by several years.

italian: Se’ tu sì tosto di quell’ aver sazio per lo qual non temesti tòrre a ’nganno la bella donna, e poi di farne strazio?».
english: Are you so quickly sated with the riches for which you did not fear to take by guile the Lovely Lady, then to violate her?”

italian: Tal mi fec’ io, quai son color che stanno, per non intender ciò ch’è lor risposto, quasi scornati, e risponder non sanno.
english: And I became like those who stand as if they have been mocked, who cannot understand what has been said to them and can’t respond.

italian: Allor Virgilio disse: «Dilli tosto: “Non son colui, non son colui che credi”»; e io rispuosi come a me fu imposto.
english: But Virgil said: “Tell this to him at once: ‘I am not he—not who you think I am.'” And I replied as I was told to do.

italian: Per che lo spirto tutti storse i piedi; poi, sospirando e con voce di pianto, mi disse: «Dunque che a me richiedi?
english: At this the spirit twisted both his feet, and sighing and with a despairing voice, he said: “What is it, then, you want of me?

italian: Se di saper ch’i’ sia ti cal cotanto, che tu abbi però la ripa corsa, sappi ch’i’ fui vestito del gran manto;
english: If you have crossed the bank and climbed so far to find out who I am, then know that I was one of those who wore the mighty mantle,

italian: e veramente fui figliuol de l’orsa, cupido sì per avanzar li orsatti, che sù l’avere e qui me misi in borsa.
english: and surely was a son of the she—bear, so eager to advance the cubs that I pursed wealth above while here I purse myself.

italian: Di sotto al capo mio son li altri tratti che precedetter me simoneggiando, per le fessure de la pietra piatti.
english: Below my head there is the place of those who took the way of simony before me; and they are stuffed within the clefts of stone.

italian: Là giù cascherò io altresì quando verrà colui ch’i’ credea che tu fossi, allor ch’i’ feci ’l sùbito dimando.
english: I, too, shall yield my place and fall below when he arrives, the one for whom I had mistaken you when I was quick to question.

italian: Ma più è ’l tempo già che i piè mi cossi e ch’i’ son stato così sottosopra, ch’el non starà piantato coi piè rossi:
english: But I have baked my feet a longer time, have stood like this, upon my head, than he is to stand planted here with scarlet feet:

italian: ché dopo lui verrà di più laida opra, di ver’ ponente, un pastor sanza legge, tal che convien che lui e me ricuopra.
english: for after him, one uglier in deeds will come, a lawless shepherd from the west, worthy to cover him and cover me.

italian: Nuovo Iasón sarà, di cui si legge ne’ Maccabei; e come a quel fu molle suo re, così fia lui chi Francia regge».
english: He’ll be a second Jason, of whom we read in Maccabees; and just as Jason’s king was soft to him, so shall the king of France

italian: Io non so s’i’ mi fui qui troppo folle, ch’i’ pur rispuosi lui a questo metro: «Deh, or mi dì: quanto tesoro volle
english: be soft to this one.” And I do not know if I was too rash here—I answered so: “Then tell me now, how much gold did our Lord

italian: Nostro Segnore in prima da san Pietro ch’ei ponesse le chiavi in sua balìa? Certo non chiese se non “Viemmi retro”.
english: ask that Saint Peter give to him before he placed the keys within his care? Surely the only thing he said was: ‘Follow me.’

italian: Né Pier né li altri tolsero a Matia oro od argento, quando fu sortito al loco che perdé l’anima ria.
english: And Peter and the others never asked for gold or silver when they chose Matthias to take the place of the transgressing soul.

italian: Però ti sta, ché tu se’ ben punito; e guarda ben la mal tolta moneta ch’esser ti fece contra Carlo ardito.
english: Stay as you are, for you are rightly punished; and guard with care the money got by evil that made you so audacious against Charles.

italian: E se non fosse ch’ancor lo mi vieta la reverenza de le somme chiavi che tu tenesti ne la vita lieta,
english: And were it not that I am still prevented by reverence for those exalted keys that you had held within the happy life,

italian: io userei parole ancor più gravi; ché la vostra avarizia il mondo attrista, calcando i buoni e sollevando i pravi.
english: I’d utter words much heavier than these, because your avarice afflicts the world: it tramples on the good, lifts up the wicked.

italian: Di voi pastor s’accorse il Vangelista, quando colei che siede sopra l’acque puttaneggiar coi regi a lui fu vista;
english: You, shepherds, the Evangelist had noticed when he saw her who sits upon the waters and realized she fornicates with kings,

italian: quella che con le sette teste nacque, e da le diece corna ebbe argomento, fin che virtute al suo marito piacque.
english: she who was born with seven heads and had the power and support of the ten horns, as long as virtue was her husband’s pleasure.

italian: Fatto v’avete dio d’oro e d’argento; e che altro è da voi a l’idolatre, se non ch’elli uno, e voi ne orate cento?
english: You’ve made yourselves a god of gold and silver; how are you different from idolaters, save that they worship one and you a hundred?

italian: Ahi, Costantin, di quanto mal fu matre, non la tua conversion, ma quella dote che da te prese il primo ricco patre!».
english: Ah, Constantine, what wickedness was born— and not from your conversion—from the dower that you bestowed upon the first rich father!”

italian: E mentr’ io li cantava cotai note, o ira o coscïenza che ’l mordesse, forte spingava con ambo le piote.
english: And while I sang such notes to him—whether it was his indignation or his conscience that bit him—he kicked hard with both his soles.

italian: I’ credo ben ch’al mio duca piacesse, con sì contenta labbia sempre attese lo suon de le parole vere espresse.
english: I do indeed believe it pleased my guide: he listened always with such satisfied expression to the sound of those true words.

italian: Però con ambo le braccia mi prese; e poi che tutto su mi s’ebbe al petto, rimontò per la via onde discese.
english: And then he gathered me in both his arms and, when he had me fast against his chest, where he climbed down before, climbed upward now;

italian: Né si stancò d’avermi a sé distretto, sì men portò sovra ’l colmo de l’arco che dal quarto al quinto argine è tragetto.
english: nor did he tire of clasping me until he brought me to the summit of the arch that crosses from the fourth to the fifth rampart.

italian: Quivi soavemente spuose il carco, soave per lo scoglio sconcio ed erto che sarebbe a le capre duro varco.
english: And here he gently set his burden down— gently because the ridge was rough and steep, and would have been a rugged pass for goats.

italian: Indi un altro vallon mi fu scoperto.
english: From there another valley lay before me.

italian: Di nova pena mi conven far versi e dar matera al ventesimo canto de la prima canzon ch’è d’i sommersi.
english: I must make verses of new punishment and offer matter now for Canto Twenty of this first canticle—of the submerged.

italian: Io era già disposto tutto quanto a riguardar ne lo scoperto fondo, che si bagnava d’angoscioso pianto;
english: I was already well prepared to stare below, into the depth that was disclosed, where tears of anguished sorrow bathed the ground;

italian: e vidi gente per lo vallon tondo venir, tacendo e lagrimando, al passo che fanno le letane in questo mondo.
english: and in the valley’s circle I saw souls advancing, mute and weeping, at the pace that, in our world, holy processions take.

italian: Come ’l viso mi scese in lor più basso, mirabilmente apparve esser travolto ciascun tra ’l mento e ’l principio del casso;
english: As I inclined my head still more, I saw that each, amazingly, appeared contorted between the chin and where the chest begins;

italian: ché da le reni era tornato ’l volto, e in dietro venir li convenia, perché ’l veder dinanzi era lor tolto.
english: they had their faces twisted toward their haunches and found it necessary to walk backward, because they could not see ahead of them.

italian: Forse per forza già di parlasia si travolse così alcun del tutto; ma io nol vidi, né credo che sia.
english: Perhaps the force of palsy has so fully distorted some, but that I’ve yet to see, and I do not believe that that can be.

italian: Se Dio ti lasci, lettor, prender frutto di tua lezione, or pensa per te stesso com’ io potea tener lo viso asciutto,
english: May God so let you, reader, gather fruit from what you read; and now think for yourself how I could ever keep my own face dry

italian: quando la nostra imagine di presso vidi sì torta, che ’l pianto de li occhi le natiche bagnava per lo fesso.
english: when I beheld our image so nearby and so awry that tears, down from the eyes, bathed the buttocks, running down the cleft.

italian: Certo io piangea, poggiato a un de’ rocchi del duro scoglio, sì che la mia scorta mi disse: «Ancor se’ tu de li altri sciocchi?
english: Of course I wept, leaning against a rock along that rugged ridge, so that my guide told me: “Are you as foolish as the rest?

italian: Qui vive la pietà quand’ è ben morta; chi è più scellerato che colui che al giudicio divin passion comporta?
english: Here pity only lives when it is dead: for who can be more impious than he who links God’s judgment to passivity?

italian: Drizza la testa, drizza, e vedi a cui s’aperse a li occhi d’i Teban la terra; per ch’ei gridavan tutti: “Dove rui,
english: Lift, lift your head and see the one for whom the earth was opened while the Thebans watched, so that they all cried: ‘Amphiaraus,

italian: Anfïarao? perché lasci la guerra?”. E non restò di ruinare a valle fino a Minòs che ciascheduno afferra.
english: where are you rushing? Have you quit the fight?’ Nor did he interrupt his downward plunge to Minos, who lays hands on every sinner.

italian: Mira c’ha fatto petto de le spalle: perché volle veder troppo davante, di retro guarda e fa retroso calle.
english: See how he’s made a chest out of his shoulders; and since he wanted so to see ahead, he looks behind and walks a backward path.

italian: Vedi Tiresia, che mutò sembiante quando di maschio femmina divenne cangiandosi le membra tutte quante;
english: And see Tiresias, who changed his mien when from a man he turned into a woman, so totally transforming all his limbs

italian: e prima, poi, ribatter li convenne li duo serpenti avvolti, con la verga, che riavesse le maschili penne.
english: that then he had to strike once more upon the two entwining serpents with his wand before he had his manly plumes again.

italian: Aronta è quel ch’al ventre li s’atterga, che ne’ monti di Luni, dove ronca lo Carrarese che di sotto alberga,
english: And Aruns is the one who backs against the belly of Tiresias—Aruns who, in Luni’s hills, tilled by the Carrarese,

italian: ebbe tra ’ bianchi marmi la spelonca per sua dimora; onde a guardar le stelle e ’l mar no li era la veduta tronca.
english: who live below, had as his home, a cave among white marbles, from which he could gaze at stars and sea with unimpeded view.

italian: E quella che ricuopre le mammelle, che tu non vedi, con le trecce sciolte, e ha di là ogne pilosa pelle,
english: And she who covers up her breasts—which you can’t see—with her disheveled locks, who keeps all of her hairy parts to the far side,

italian: Manto fu, che cercò per terre molte; poscia si puose là dove nacqu’ io; onde un poco mi piace che m’ascolte.
english: was Manto, who had searched through many lands, then settled in the place where I was born; on this, I’d have you hear me now a while.

italian: Poscia che ’l padre suo di vita uscìo e venne serva la città di Baco, questa gran tempo per lo mondo gio.
english: When Manto’s father took his leave of life, and Bacchus’ city found itself enslaved, she wandered through the world for many years.

italian: Suso in Italia bella giace un laco, a piè de l’Alpe che serra Lamagna sovra Tiralli, c’ha nome Benaco.
english: High up, in lovely Italy, beneath the Alps that shut in Germany above Tirolo, lies a lake known as Benaco.

italian: Per mille fonti, credo, e più si bagna tra Garda e Val Camonica e Pennino de l’acqua che nel detto laco stagna.
english: A thousand springs and more, I think, must flow out of the waters of that lake to bathe Pennino, Garda, Val Camonica.

italian: Loco è nel mezzo là dove ’l trentino pastore e quel di Brescia e ’l veronese segnar poria, s’e’ fesse quel cammino.
english: And at its middle is a place where three— the bishops of Verona, Brescia, Trento— may bless if they should chance to come that way.

italian: Siede Peschiera, bello e forte arnese da fronteggiar Bresciani e Bergamaschi, ove la riva ’ntorno più discese.
english: Peschiera, strong and handsome fortress, built to face the Brescians and the Bergamasques stands where the circling shore is at its lowest.

italian: Ivi convien che tutto quanto caschi ciò che ’n grembo a Benaco star non può, e fassi fiume giù per verdi paschi.
english: There, all the waters that cannot be held within the bosom of Benaco fall, to form a river running through green meadows.

italian: Tosto che l’acqua a correr mette co, non più Benaco, ma Mencio si chiama fino a Governol, dove cade in Po.
english: No sooner has that stream begun to flow than it is called the Mincio, not Benaco— until Governolo, where it joins the Po.

italian: Non molto ha corso, ch’el trova una lama, ne la qual si distende e la ’mpaluda; e suol di state talor essere grama.
english: It’s not flowed far before it finds flat land; and there it stretches out to form a fen that in the summer can at times be fetid.

italian: Quindi passando la vergine cruda vide terra, nel mezzo del pantano, sanza coltura e d’abitanti nuda.
english: And when she passed that way, the savage virgin saw land along the middle of the swamp, untilled and stripped of its inhabitants.

italian: Lì, per fuggire ogne consorzio umano, ristette con suoi servi a far sue arti, e visse, e vi lasciò suo corpo vano.
english: And there, to flee all human intercourse, she halted with her slaves to ply her arts; and there she lived, there left her empty body.

italian: Li uomini poi che ’ntorno erano sparti s’accolsero a quel loco, ch’era forte per lo pantan ch’avea da tutte parti.
english: And afterward, the people of those parts collected at that place, because the marsh— surrounding it on all sides—made it strong.

italian: Fer la città sovra quell’ ossa morte; e per colei che ’l loco prima elesse, Mantüa l’appellar sanz’ altra sorte.
english: They built a city over her dead bones; and after her who first had picked that spot, they called it Mantua—they cast no lots.

italian: Già fuor le genti sue dentro più spesse, prima che la mattia da Casalodi da Pinamonte inganno ricevesse.
english: There once were far more people in its walls, before the foolishness of Casalodi was tricked by the deceit of Pinamonte.

italian: Però t’assenno che, se tu mai odi originar la mia terra altrimenti, la verità nulla menzogna frodi».
english: Therefore, I charge you, if you ever hear a different tale of my town’s origin, do not let any falsehood gull the truth.”

italian: E io: «Maestro, i tuoi ragionamenti mi son sì certi e prendon sì mia fede, che li altri mi sarien carboni spenti.
english: And I: “O master, that which you have spoken convinces me and so compels my trust that others’ words would only be spent coals.

italian: Ma dimmi, de la gente che procede, se tu ne vedi alcun degno di nota; ché solo a ciò la mia mente rifiede».
english: But tell me if among the passing souls you see some spirits worthy of our notice, because my mind is bent on that alone.”

italian: Allor mi disse: «Quel che da la gota porge la barba in su le spalle brune, fu – quando Grecia fu di maschi vòta,
english: Then he to me: “That shade who spreads his beard down from his cheeks across his swarthy shoulders— when Greece had been so emptied of its males

italian: sì ch’a pena rimaser per le cune – augure, e diede ’l punto con Calcanta in Aulide a tagliar la prima fune.
english: that hardly any cradle held a son, he was an augur; and at Aulis, he and Calchas set the time to cut the cables.

italian: Euripilo ebbe nome, e così ’l canta l’alta mia tragedìa in alcun loco: ben lo sai tu che la sai tutta quanta.
english: His name’s Eurypylus; a certain passage of my high tragedy has sung it so; you know that well enough, who know the whole.

italian: Quell’ altro che ne’ fianchi è così poco, Michele Scotto fu, che veramente de le magiche frode seppe ’l gioco.
english: That other there, his flanks extremely spare, was Michael Scot, a man who certainly knew how the game of magic fraud was played.

italian: Vedi Guido Bonatti; vedi Asdente, ch’avere inteso al cuoio e a lo spago ora vorrebbe, ma tardi si pente.
english: See there Guido Bonatti; see Asdente, who now would wish he had attended to his cord and leather, but repents too late.

italian: Vedi le triste che lasciaron l’ago, la spuola e ’l fuso, e fecersi ’ndivine; fecer malie con erbe e con imago.
english: See those sad women who had left their needle, shuttle, and spindle to become diviners; they cast their spells with herbs and effigies

italian: Ma vienne omai, ché già tiene ’l confine d’amendue li emisperi e tocca l’onda sotto Sobilia Caino e le spine;
english: But let us go; Cain with his thorns already is at the border of both hemispheres and there, below Seville, touches the sea.

italian: e già iernotte fu la luna tonda: ben ten de’ ricordar, ché non ti nocque alcuna volta per la selva fonda».
english: Last night the moon was at its full; you should be well aware of this, for there were times when it did you no harm in the deep wood.”

italian: Sì mi parlava, e andavamo introcque.
english: These were his words to me; meanwhile we journeyed.

italian: Così di ponte in ponte, altro parlando che la mia comedìa cantar non cura, venimmo; e tenavamo ’l colmo, quando
english: We came along from one bridge to another, talking of things my Comedy is not concerned to sing. We held fast to the summit,

italian: restammo per veder l’altra fessura di Malebolge e li altri pianti vani; e vidila mirabilmente oscura.
english: then stayed our steps to spy the other cleft of Malebolge and other vain laments. I saw that it was wonderfully dark.

italian: Quale ne l’arzanà de’ Viniziani bolle l’inverno la tenace pece a rimpalmare i legni lor non sani,
english: As in the arsenal of the Venetians, all winter long a stew of sticky pitch boils up to patch their sick and tattered ships

italian: ché navicar non ponno – in quella vece chi fa suo legno novo e chi ristoppa le coste a quel che più vïaggi fece;
english: that cannot sail (instead of voyaging, some build new keels, some tow and tar the ribs of hulls worn out by too much journeying;

italian: chi ribatte da proda e chi da poppa; altri fa remi e altri volge sarte; chi terzeruolo e artimon rintoppa -:
english: some hammer at the prow, some at the stern, and some make oars, and some braid ropes and cords; one mends the jib, another, the mainsail);

italian: tal, non per foco, ma per divin’ arte, bollia là giuso una pegola spessa, che ’nviscava la ripa d’ogne parte.
english: so, not by fire but by the art of God, below there boiled a thick and tarry mass that covered all the banks with clamminess.

italian: I’ vedea lei, ma non vedëa in essa mai che le bolle che ’l bollor levava, e gonfiar tutta, e riseder compressa.
english: I saw it, but I could not see within it; no thing was visible but boiling bubbles, the swelling of the pitch; and then it settled.

italian: Mentr’ io là giù fisamente mirava, lo duca mio, dicendo «Guarda, guarda!», mi trasse a sé del loco dov’ io stava.
english: And while I watched below attentively, my guide called out to me: “Take care! Take care!” And then, from where I stood, he drew me near.

italian: Allor mi volsi come l’uom cui tarda di veder quel che li convien fuggire e cui paura sùbita sgagliarda,
english: I turned around as one who is impatient to see what he should shun but is dashed down beneath the terror he has undergone,

italian: che, per veder, non indugia ’l partire: e vidi dietro a noi un diavol nero correndo su per lo scoglio venire.
english: who does not stop his flight and yet would look. And then in back of us I saw a black demon as he came racing up the crags.

italian: Ahi quant’ elli era ne l’aspetto fero! e quanto mi parea ne l’atto acerbo, con l’ali aperte e sovra i piè leggero!
english: Ah, he was surely barbarous to see! And how relentless seemed to me his acts! His wings were open and his feet were lithe;

italian: L’omero suo, ch’era aguto e superbo, carcava un peccator con ambo l’anche, e quei tenea de’ piè ghermito ’l nerbo.
english: across his shoulder, which was sharp and high, he had slung a sinner, upward from the thighs; in front, the demon gripped him by the ankles.

italian: Del nostro ponte disse: «O Malebranche, ecco un de li anzïan di Santa Zita! Mettetel sotto, ch’i’ torno per anche
english: Then from our bridge, he called: “O Malebranche, I’ve got an elder of Saint Zita for you! Shove this one under—I’ll go back for more—

italian: a quella terra che n’è ben fornita: ogn’ uom v’è barattier, fuor che Bonturo; del no, per li denar vi si fa ita ».
english: his city is well furnished with such stores; there, everyone’s a grafter but Bonturo; and there—for cash—they’ll change a no to yes.”

italian: Là giù ’l buttò, e per lo scoglio duro si volse; e mai non fu mastino sciolto con tanta fretta a seguitar lo furo.
english: He threw the sinner down, then wheeled along The stony cliff: no mastiff’s ever been unleashed with so much haste to chase a thief.

italian: Quel s’attuffò, e tornò sù convolto; ma i demon che del ponte avean coperchio, gridar: «Qui non ha loco il Santo Volto:
english: The sinner plunged, then surfaced, black with pitch; but now the demons, from beneath the bridge, shouted: “The Sacred Face has no place here;

italian: qui si nuota altrimenti che nel Serchio! Però, se tu non vuo’ di nostri graffi, non far sopra la pegola soverchio».
english: here we swim differently than in the Serchio; if you don’t want to feel our grappling hooks, don’t try to lift yourself above that ditch.”

italian: Poi l’addentar con più di cento raffi, disser: «Coverto convien che qui balli, sì che, se puoi, nascosamente accaffi».
english: They pricked him with a hundred prongs and more, then taunted: “Here one dances under cover, so try to grab your secret graft below.”

italian: Non altrimenti i cuoci a’ lor vassalli fanno attuffare in mezzo la caldaia la carne con li uncin, perché non galli.
english: The demons did the same as any cook who has his urchins force the meat with hooks deep down into the pot, that it not float.

italian: Lo buon maestro «Acciò che non si paia che tu ci sia», mi disse, «giù t’acquatta dopo uno scheggio, ch’alcun schermo t’aia;
english: Then my good master said to me: “Don’t let those demons see that you are here; take care to crouch behind the cover of a crag.

italian: e per nulla offension che mi sia fatta, non temer tu, ch’i’ ho le cose conte, perch’ altra volta fui a tal baratta».
english: No matter what offense they offer me, don’t be afraid; I know how these things go— I’ve had to face such fracases before.”

italian: Poscia passò di là dal co del ponte; e com’ el giunse in su la ripa sesta, mestier li fu d’aver sicura fronte.
english: When this was said, he moved beyond the bridgehead. And on the sixth embankment, he had need to show his imperturbability.

italian: Con quel furore e con quella tempesta ch’escono i cani a dosso al poverello che di sùbito chiede ove s’arresta,
english: With the same frenzy, with the brouhaha of dogs, when they beset a poor wretch who then stops dead in his tracks as if to beg,

italian: usciron quei di sotto al ponticello, e volser contra lui tutt’ i runcigli; ma el gridò: «Nessun di voi sia fello!
english: so, from beneath the bridge, the demons rushed against my guide with all their prongs, but he called out: “Can’t you forget your savagery!

italian: Innanzi che l’uncin vostro mi pigli, traggasi avante l’un di voi che m’oda, e poi d’arruncigliarmi si consigli».
english: Before you try to maul me, just let one of all your troop step forward. Hear me out, and then decide if I am to be hooked.”

italian: Tutti gridaron: «Vada Malacoda!»; per ch’un si mosse – e li altri stetter fermi – e venne a lui dicendo: «Che li approda?».
english: At this they howled, “Let Malacoda go!” And one of them moved up—the others stayed— and as he came, he asked: “How can he win?”

italian: «Credi tu, Malacoda, qui vedermi esser venuto», disse ’l mio maestro, «sicuro già da tutti vostri schermi,
english: “O Malacoda, do you think I’ve come,” my master answered him, “already armed— as you can see—against your obstacles,

italian: sanza voler divino e fato destro? Lascian’ andar, ché nel cielo è voluto ch’i’ mostri altrui questo cammin silvestro».
english: without the will of God and helpful fate? Let us move on; it is the will of Heaven for me to show this wild way to another.”

italian: Allor li fu l’orgoglio sì caduto, ch’e’ si lasciò cascar l’uncino a’ piedi, e disse a li altri: «Omai non sia feruto».
english: At this the pride of Malacoda fell; his prong dropped to his feet. He told his fellows: “Since that’s the way things stand, let us not wound him.”

italian: E ’l duca mio a me: «O tu che siedi tra li scheggion del ponte quatto quatto, sicuramente omai a me ti riedi».
english: My guide then spoke to me: “O you, who crouch, bent low among the bridge’s splintered rocks, you can feel safe—and now return to me.”

italian: Per ch’io mi mossi, e a lui venni ratto; e i diavoli si fecer tutti avanti, sì ch’io temetti ch’ei tenesser patto;
english: At this I moved and quickly came to him. The devils had edged forward, all of them; I feared that they might fail to keep their word:

italian: così vid’ ïo già temer li fanti ch’uscivan patteggiati di Caprona, veggendo sé tra nemici cotanti.
english: just so, I saw the infantry when they marched out, under safe conduct, from Caprona; they trembled when they passed their enemies.

italian: I’ m’accostai con tutta la persona lungo ’l mio duca, e non torceva li occhi da la sembianza lor ch’era non buona.
english: My body huddled closer to my guide; I did not let the demons out of sight; the looks they cast at us were less than kind.

italian: Ei chinavan li raffi e «Vuo’ che ’l tocchi», diceva l’un con l’altro, «in sul groppone?». E rispondien: «Sì, fa che gliel’ accocchi».
english: They bent their hooks and shouted to each other: “And shall I give it to him on the rump?” And all of them replied, “Yes, let him have it!”

italian: Ma quel demonio che tenea sermone col duca mio, si volse tutto presto e disse: «Posa, posa, Scarmiglione!».
english: But Malacoda, still in conversation with my good guide, turned quickly to his squadron and said: “Be still, Scarmiglione, still!”

italian: Poi disse a noi: «Più oltre andar per questo iscoglio non si può, però che giace tutto spezzato al fondo l’arco sesto.
english: To us he said: “There is no use in going much farther on this ridge, because the sixth bridge—at the bottom there—is smashed to bits.

italian: E se l’andare avante pur vi piace, andatevene su per questa grotta; presso è un altro scoglio che via face.
english: Yet if you two still want to go ahead, move up and walk along this rocky edge; nearby, another ridge will form a path.

italian: Ier, più oltre cinqu’ ore che quest’ otta, mille dugento con sessanta sei anni compié che qui la via fu rotta.
english: Five hours from this hour yesterday, one thousand and two hundred sixty—six years passed since that roadway was shattered here.

italian: Io mando verso là di questi miei a riguardar s’alcun se ne sciorina; gite con lor, che non saranno rei».
english: I’m sending ten of mine out there to see if any sinner lifts his head for air; go with my men—there is no malice in them.”

italian: «Tra’ti avante, Alichino, e Calcabrina», cominciò elli a dire, «e tu, Cagnazzo; e Barbariccia guidi la decina.
english: “Step forward, Alichino and Calcabrina,” he then began to say, “and you, Cagnazzo; and Barbariccia, who can lead the ten.

italian: Libicocco vegn’ oltre e Draghignazzo, Cirïatto sannuto e Graffiacane e Farfarello e Rubicante pazzo.
english: Let Libicocco go, and Draghignazzo and tusky Ciriatto and Graffiacane and Farfarello and mad Rubicante.

italian: Cercate ’ntorno le boglienti pane; costor sian salvi infino a l’altro scheggio che tutto intero va sovra le tane».
english: Search all around the clammy stew of pitch; keep these two safe and sound till the next ridge that rises without break across the dens.”

italian: «Omè, maestro, che è quel ch’i’ veggio?», diss’ io, «deh, sanza scorta andianci soli, se tu sa’ ir; ch’i’ per me non la cheggio.
english: “Ah me! What is this, master, that I see?” I said. “Can’t we do without company? If you know how to go, I want no escort.

italian: Se tu se’ sì accorto come suoli, non vedi tu ch’e’ digrignan li denti, e con le ciglia ne minaccian duoli?».
english: If you are just as keen as usual, can’t you see how those demons grind their teeth? Their brows are menacing, they promise trouble.”

italian: Ed elli a me: «Non vo’ che tu paventi; lasciali digrignar pur a lor senno, ch’e’ fanno ciò per li lessi dolenti».
english: And he to me: “I do not want you frightened: just let them gnash away as they may wish; they do it for the wretches boiled in pitch.”

italian: Per l’argine sinistro volta dienno; ma prima avea ciascun la lingua stretta coi denti, verso lor duca, per cenno;
english: They turned around along the left hand bank: but first each pressed his tongue between his teeth as signal for their leader, Barbariccia.

italian: ed elli avea del cul fatto trombetta.
english: And he had made a trumpet of his ass.

italian: Io vidi già cavalier muover campo, e cominciare stormo e far lor mostra, e talvolta partir per loro scampo;
english: Before this I’ve seen horsemen start to march and open the assault and muster ranks and seen them, too, at times beat their retreat;

italian: corridor vidi per la terra vostra, o Aretini, e vidi gir gualdane, fedir torneamenti e correr giostra;
english: and on your land, o Aretines, I’ve seen rangers and raiding parties galloping, the clash of tournaments, the rush of jousts,

italian: quando con trombe, e quando con campane, con tamburi e con cenni di castella, e con cose nostrali e con istrane;
english: now done with trumpets, now with bells, and now with drums, and now with signs from castle walls, with native things and with imported ware;

italian: né già con sì diversa cennamella cavalier vidi muover né pedoni, né nave a segno di terra o di stella.
english: but never yet have I seen horsemen or seen infantry or ship that sails by signal of land or star move to so strange a bugle!

italian: Noi andavam con li diece demoni. Ahi fiera compagnia! ma ne la chiesa coi santi, e in taverna coi ghiottoni.
english: We made our way together with ten demons: ah, what ferocious company! And yet “in church with saints, with rotters in the tavern.”

italian: Pur a la pegola era la mia ’ntesa, per veder de la bolgia ogne contegno e de la gente ch’entro v’era incesa.
english: But I was all intent upon the pitch, to seek out every feature of the pouch and of the people who were burning in it.

italian: Come i dalfini, quando fanno segno a’ marinar con l’arco de la schiena che s’argomentin di campar lor legno,
english: Just as the dolphins do, when with arched back, they signal to the seamen to prepare for tempest, that their vessel may be spared,

italian: talor così, ad alleggiar la pena, mostrav’ alcun de’ peccatori ’l dosso e nascondea in men che non balena.
english: so here from time to time, to ease his torment, some sinner showed his back above the surface, then hid more quickly than a lightning flash.

italian: E come a l’orlo de l’acqua d’un fosso stanno i ranocchi pur col muso fuori, sì che celano i piedi e l’altro grosso,
english: And just as on the margin of a ditch, frogs crouch, their snouts alone above the water, so as to hide their feet and their plump flesh,

italian: sì stavan d’ogne parte i peccatori; ma come s’appressava Barbariccia, così si ritraén sotto i bollori.
english: so here on every side these sinners crouched; but faster than a flash, when Barbariccia drew near, they plunged beneath the boiling pitch.

italian: I’ vidi, e anco il cor me n’accapriccia, uno aspettar così, com’ elli ’ncontra ch’una rana rimane e l’altra spiccia;
english: I saw-my heart still shudders in recall— one who delayed, just as at times a frog is left behind while others dive below;

italian: e Graffiacan, che li era più di contra, li arruncigliò le ’mpegolate chiome e trassel sù, che mi parve una lontra.
english: and Graffiacane, who was closest to him, then hooked him by his pitch—entangled locks and hauled him up; he seemed to me an otter.

italian: I’ sapea già di tutti quanti ’l nome, sì li notai quando fuorono eletti, e poi ch’e’ si chiamaro, attesi come.
english: By now I knew the names of all those demons— I’d paid attention when the fiends were chosen; I’d watched as they stepped forward one by one.

italian: «O Rubicante, fa che tu li metti li unghioni a dosso, sì che tu lo scuoi!», gridavan tutti insieme i maladetti.
english: “O Rubicante, see you set your talons right into him, so you can flay his flesh!” So did those cursed ones cry out together.

italian: E io: «Maestro mio, fa, se tu puoi, che tu sappi chi è lo sciagurato venuto a man de li avversari suoi».
english: And I: “My master, if you can, find out what is the name of that unfortunate who’s fallen victim to his enemies.”

italian: Lo duca mio li s’accostò allato; domandollo ond’ ei fosse, e quei rispuose: «I’ fui del regno di Navarra nato.
english: My guide, who then drew near that sinner’s side, asked him to tell his birthplace. He replied: “My homeland was the kingdom of Navarre.

italian: Mia madre a servo d’un segnor mi puose, che m’avea generato d’un ribaldo, distruggitor di sé e di sue cose.
english: My mother, who had had me by a wastrel, destroyer of himself and his possessions, had placed me in the service of a lord.

italian: Poi fui famiglia del buon re Tebaldo; quivi mi misi a far baratteria, di ch’io rendo ragione in questo caldo».
english: Then I was in the household of the worthy King Thibault; there I started taking graft; with this heat I pay reckoning for that.”

italian: E Cirïatto, a cui di bocca uscia d’ogne parte una sanna come a porco, li fé sentir come l’una sdruscia.
english: And Ciriatto, from whose mouth there bulged to right and left two tusks like a wild hog’s, then let him feel how one of them could mangle.

italian: Tra male gatte era venuto ’l sorco; ma Barbariccia il chiuse con le braccia e disse: «State in là, mentr’ io lo ’nforco».
english: The mouse had fallen in with evil cats; but Barbariccia clasped him in his arms and said: “Stand off there, while I fork him fast.”

italian: E al maestro mio volse la faccia; «Domanda», disse, «ancor, se più disii saper da lui, prima ch’altri ’l disfaccia».
english: And turning toward my master then, he said: “Ask on, if you would learn some more from him before one of the others does him in.”

italian: Lo duca dunque: «Or dì: de li altri rii conosci tu alcun che sia latino sotto la pece?». E quelli: «I’ mi partii,
english: At which my guide: “Now tell: among the sinners who hide beneath the pitch, are any others Italian?” And he: “I have just left

italian: poco è, da un che fu di là vicino. Così foss’ io ancor con lui coperto, ch’i’ non temerei unghia né uncino!».
english: one who was nearby there; and would I were still covered by the pitch as he is hidden, for then I’d have no fear of hook or talon.”

italian: E Libicocco «Troppo avem sofferto», disse; e preseli ’l braccio col runciglio, sì che, stracciando, ne portò un lacerto.

italian: Draghignazzo anco i volle dar di piglio giuso a le gambe; onde ’l decurio loro si volse intorno intorno con mal piglio.

italian: «Chi fu colui da cui mala partita di’ che facesti per venire a proda?». Ed ei rispuose: «Fu frate Gomita,
english: “Who was the one you left to come ashore— unluckily—as you just said before?” He answered: “Fra Gomita of Gallura,

italian: quel di Gallura, vasel d’ogne froda, ch’ebbe i nemici di suo donno in mano, e fé sì lor, che ciascun se ne loda.
english: who was a vessel fit for every fraud; he had his master’s enemies in hand, but handled them in ways that pleased them all.

italian: Danar si tolse, e lasciolli di piano, sì com’ e’ dice; e ne li altri offici anche barattier fu non picciol, ma sovrano.
english: He took their gold and smoothly let them off, as he himself says; and in other matters, he was a sovereign, not a petty, swindler.

italian: Usa con esso donno Michel Zanche di Logodoro; e a dir di Sardigna le lingue lor non si sentono stanche.
english: His comrade there is Don Michele Zanche of Logodoro; and their tongues are never too tired to talk of their Sardinia.

italian: Omè, vedete l’altro che digrigna; i’ direi anche, ma i’ temo ch’ello non s’apparecchi a grattarmi la tigna».
english: Ah me, see that one there who grinds his teeth! If I were not afraid, I’d speak some more, but he is getting set to scratch my scurf.”

italian: E ’l gran proposto, vòlto a Farfarello che stralunava li occhi per fedire, disse: «Fatti ’n costà, malvagio uccello!».
english: And their great marshal, facing Farfarello— who was so hot to strike he rolled his eyes, said: “Get away from there, you filthy bird!”

italian: «Se voi volete vedere o udire», ricominciò lo spaürato appresso «Toschi o Lombardi, io ne farò venire;
english: “If you perhaps would like to see or hear,” that sinner, terrified, began again, “Lombards or Tuscans, I can fetch you some;

italian: ma stieno i Malebranche un poco in cesso, sì ch’ei non teman de le lor vendette; e io, seggendo in questo loco stesso,
english: but let the Malebranche stand aside so that my comrades need not fear their vengeance. Remaining in this very spot, I shall,

italian: per un ch’io son, ne farò venir sette quand’ io suffolerò, com’ è nostro uso di fare allor che fori alcun si mette».
english: although alone, make seven more appear when I have whistled, as has been our custom when one of us has managed to get out.”

italian: Cagnazzo a cotal motto levò ’l muso, crollando ’l capo, e disse: «Odi malizia ch’elli ha pensata per gittarsi giuso!».
english: At that, Cagnazzo lifted up his snout and shook his head, and said: “Just listen to that trick by which he thinks he can dive back!”

italian: Ond’ ei, ch’avea lacciuoli a gran divizia, rispuose: «Malizioso son io troppo, quand’ io procuro a’ mia maggior trestizia».
english: To this, he who was rich in artifice replied: “Then I must have too many tricks, if I bring greater torment to my friends.”

italian: Alichin non si tenne e, di rintoppo a li altri, disse a lui: «Se tu ti cali, io non ti verrò dietro di gualoppo,
english: This was too much for Alichino and, despite the others, he cried out: “If you dive back, I shall not gallop after you

italian: ma batterò sovra la pece l’ali. Lascisi ’l collo, e sia la ripa scudo, a veder se tu sol più di noi vali».
english: but beat my wings above the pitch; we’ll leave this height; with the embankment as a screen, we’ll see if you—alone—can handle us.”

italian: O tu che leggi, udirai nuovo ludo: ciascun da l’altra costa li occhi volse, quel prima, ch’a ciò fare era più crudo.
english: O you who read, hear now of this new sport: each turned his eyes upon the other shore, he first who’d been most hesitant before.

italian: Lo Navarrese ben suo tempo colse; fermò le piante a terra, e in un punto saltò e dal proposto lor si sciolse.
english: The Navarrese, in nick of time, had planted his feet upon the ground; then in an instant he jumped and freed himself from their commander.

italian: Di che ciascun di colpa fu compunto, ma quei più che cagion fu del difetto; però si mosse e gridò: «Tu se’ giunto!».
english: At this each demon felt the prick of guilt, and most, he who had led his band to blunder; so he took off and shouted: “You are caught!”

italian: Ma poco i valse: ché l’ali al sospetto non potevo avanzar; quelli andò sotto, e quei drizzò volando suso il petto:

english: My guide then asked that sinner who he was; to this he answered: “Not long since, I rained from Tuscany into this savage maw.
