english: Mule that I was, the bestial life pleased me and not the human; I am Vanni Fucci, beast; and the den that suited me—Pistoia.”

italian: E ïo al duca: «Dilli che non mucci, e domanda che colpa qua giù ’l pinse; ch’io ’l vidi uomo di sangue e di crucci».
english: And I to Virgil: “Tell him not to slip away, and ask what sin has thrust him here; I knew him as a man of blood and anger.”

italian: E ’l peccator, che ’ntese, non s’infinse, ma drizzò verso me l’animo e ’l volto, e di trista vergogna si dipinse;
english: The sinner heard and did not try to feign but turned his mind and face, intent, toward me; and coloring with miserable shame,

italian: poi disse: «Più mi duol che tu m’hai colto ne la miseria dove tu mi vedi, che quando fui de l’altra vita tolto.
english: he said: “I suffer more because you’ve caught me in this, the misery you see, than I suffered when taken from the other life.

italian: Io non posso negar quel che tu chiedi; in giù son messo tanto perch’ io fui ladro a la sagrestia d’i belli arredi,
english: I can’t refuse to answer what you ask: I am set down so far because I robbed the sacristy of its fair ornaments,

italian: e falsamente già fu apposto altrui. Ma perché di tal vista tu non godi, se mai sarai di fuor da’ luoghi bui,
english: and someone else was falsely blamed for that. But lest this sight give you too much delight, if you can ever leave these lands of darkness,

italian: apri li orecchi al mio annunzio, e odi. Pistoia in pria d’i Neri si dimagra; poi Fiorenza rinova gente e modi.
english: open your ears to my announcement, hear: Pistoia first will strip herself of Blacks, then Florence will renew her men and manners.

italian: Tragge Marte vapor di Val di Magra ch’è di torbidi nuvoli involuto; e con tempesta impetüosa e agra
english: From Val di Magra, Mars will draw a vapor which turbid clouds will try to wrap; the clash between them will be fierce, impetuous,

italian: sovra Campo Picen fia combattuto; ond’ ei repente spezzerà la nebbia, sì ch’ogne Bianco ne sarà feruto.
english: a tempest, fought upon Campo Piceno, until that vapor, vigorous, shall crack the mist, and every White be struck by it.

italian: E detto l’ho perché doler ti debbia!».
english: And I have told you this to make you grieve.”

italian: ﻿Al fine de le sue parole il ladro le mani alzò con amendue le fiche, gridando: «Togli, Dio, ch’a te le squadro!».
english: When he had finished with his words, the thief raised high his fists with both figs cocked and cried: “Take that, o God; I square them off for you!”

italian: Da indi in qua mi fuor le serpi amiche, perch’ una li s’avvolse allora al collo, come dicesse ‘Non vo’ che più diche’;
english: From that time on, those serpents were my friends, for one of them coiled then around his neck, as if to say, “I’ll have you speak no more”;

italian: e un’altra a le braccia, e rilegollo, ribadendo sé stessa sì dinanzi, che non potea con esse dare un crollo.
english: another wound about his arms and bound him again and wrapped itself in front so firmly, he could not even make them budge an inch.

italian: Ahi Pistoia, Pistoia, ché non stanzi d’incenerarti sì che più non duri, poi che ’n mal fare il seme tuo avanzi?
english: Pistoia, ah, Pistoia, must you last: why not decree your self-incineration, since you surpass your seed in wickedness?

italian: Per tutt’ i cerchi de lo ’nferno scuri non vidi spirto in Dio tanto superbo, non quel che cadde a Tebe giù da’ muri.
english: Throughout the shadowed circles of deep Hell, I saw no soul against God so rebel, not even he who fell from Theban walls.

italian: El si fuggì che non parlò più verbo; e io vidi un centauro pien di rabbia venir chiamando: «Ov’ è, ov’ è l’acerbo?».
english: He fled and could not say another word; and then I saw a Centaur full of anger, shouting: “Where is he, where’s that bitter one?”

italian: Maremma non cred’ io che tante n’abbia, quante bisce elli avea su per la groppa infin ove comincia nostra labbia.
english: I do not think Maremma has the number of snakes that Centaur carried on his haunch until the part that takes our human form.

italian: Sovra le spalle, dietro da la coppa, con l’ali aperte li giacea un draco; e quello affuoca qualunque s’intoppa.
english: Upon his shoulders and behind his nape there lay a dragon with its wings outstretched; it sets ablaze all those it intercepts.

italian: Lo mio maestro disse: «Questi è Caco, che, sotto ’l sasso di monte Aventino, di sangue fece spesse volte laco.
english: My master said: “That Centaur there is Cacus, who often made a lake of blood within a grotto underneath Mount Aventine.

italian: Non va co’ suoi fratei per un cammino, per lo furto che frodolente fece del grande armento ch’elli ebbe a vicino;
english: He does not ride the same road as his brothers because he stole—and most deceitfully— from the great herd nearby; his crooked deeds

italian: onde cessar le sue opere biece sotto la mazza d’Ercule, che forse gliene diè cento, e non sentì le diece».
english: ended beneath the club of Hercules, who may have given him a hundred blows— but he was not alive to feel the tenth.”

italian: Mentre che sì parlava, ed el trascorse, e tre spiriti venner sotto noi, de’ quai né io né ’l duca mio s’accorse,
english: While he was talking so, Cacus ran by and, just beneath our ledge, three souls arrived; but neither I nor my guide noticed them

italian: se non quando gridar: «Chi siete voi?»; per che nostra novella si ristette, e intendemmo pur ad essi poi.
english: until they had cried out: “And who are you?” At this the words we shared were interrupted, and we attended only to those spirits.

italian: Io non li conoscea; ma ei seguette, come suol seguitar per alcun caso, che l’un nomar un altro convenette,
english: I did not recognize them, but it happened, as chance will usually bring about, that one of them called out the other’s name,

italian: dicendo: «Cianfa dove fia rimaso?»; per ch’io, acciò che ’l duca stesse attento, mi puosi ’l dito su dal mento al naso.
english: exclaiming: “Where was Cianfa left behind?” At this, so that my guide might be alert, I raised my finger up from chin to nose.

italian: Se tu se’ or, lettore, a creder lento ciò ch’io dirò, non sarà maraviglia, ché io che ’l vidi, a pena il mi consento.
english: If, reader, you are slow now to believe what I shall tell, that is no cause for wonder, for I who saw it hardly can accept it.

italian: Com’ io tenea levate in lor le ciglia, e un serpente con sei piè si lancia dinanzi a l’uno, e tutto a lui s’appiglia.
english: As I kept my eyes fixed upon those sinners, a serpent with six feet springs out against one of the three, and clutches him completely.

italian: Co’ piè di mezzo li avvinse la pancia e con li anterïor le braccia prese; poi li addentò e l’una e l’altra guancia;
english: It gripped his belly with its middle feet, and with its forefeet grappled his two arms; and then it sank its teeth in both his cheeks;

italian: li diretani a le cosce distese, e miseli la coda tra ’mbedue e dietro per le ren sù la ritese.
english: it stretched its rear feet out along his thighs and ran its tail along between the two, then straightened it again behind his loins.

italian: Ellera abbarbicata mai non fue ad alber sì, come l’orribil fiera per l’altrui membra avviticchiò le sue.
english: No ivy ever gripped a tree so fast as when that horrifying monster clasped and intertwined the other’s limbs with its.

italian: Poi s’appiccar, come di calda cera fossero stati, e mischiar lor colore, né l’un né l’altro già parea quel ch’era:
english: Then just as if their substance were warm wax, they stuck together and they mixed their colors, so neither seemed what he had been before;

italian: come procede innanzi da l’ardore, per lo papiro suso, un color bruno che non è nero ancora e ’l bianco more.
english: just as, when paper’s kindled, where it still has not caught flame in full, its color’s dark though not yet black, while white is dying off.

italian: Li altri due ’l riguardavano, e ciascuno gridava: «Omè, Agnel, come ti muti! Vedi che già non se’ né due né uno».
english: The other two souls stared, and each one cried: “Ah me, Agnello, how you change! Just see, you are already neither two nor one!”

italian: Già eran li due capi un divenuti, quando n’apparver due figure miste in una faccia, ov’ eran due perduti.
english: Then two heads were already joined in one, when in one face where two had been dissolved, two intermingled shapes appeared to us.

italian: Fersi le braccia due di quattro liste; le cosce con le gambe e ’l ventre e ’l casso divenner membra che non fuor mai viste.
english: Two arms came into being from four lengths; the thighs and legs, the belly and the chest became such limbs as never had been seen.

italian: Ogne primaio aspetto ivi era casso: due e nessun l’imagine perversa parea; e tal sen gio con lento passo.
english: And every former shape was canceled there: that perverse image seemed to share in both— and none; and so, and slowly, it moved on.

italian: Come ’l ramarro sotto la gran fersa dei dì canicular, cangiando sepe, folgore par se la via attraversa,
english: Just as the lizard, when it darts from hedge to hedge, beneath the dog days’ giant lash, seems, if it cross one’s path, a lightning flash,

italian: sì pareva, venendo verso l’epe de li altri due, un serpentello acceso, livido e nero come gran di pepe;
english: so seemed a blazing little serpent moving against the bellies of the other two, as black and livid as a peppercorn.

italian: e quella parte onde prima è preso nostro alimento, a l’un di lor trafisse; poi cadde giuso innanzi lui disteso.
english: Attacking one of therm, it pierced right through the part where we first take our nourishment; and then it fell before him at full length.

italian: Lo trafitto ’l mirò, ma nulla disse; anzi, co’ piè fermati, sbadigliava pur come sonno o febbre l’assalisse.
english: The one it had transfixed stared but said nothing; in fact he only stood his ground and yawned as one whom sleep or fever has undone.

italian: Elli ’l serpente e quei lui riguardava; l’un per la piaga e l’altro per la bocca fummavan forte, e ’l fummo si scontrava.
english: The serpent stared at him, he at the serpent; one through his wound, the other through his mouth were smoking violently; their smoke met.

italian: Taccia Lucano ormai là dov’ e’ tocca del misero Sabello e di Nasidio, e attenda a udir quel ch’or si scocca.
english: Let Lucan now be silent, where he sings of sad Sabellus and Nasidius, and wait to hear what flies off from my bow.

italian: Taccia di Cadmo e d’Aretusa Ovidio, ché se quello in serpente e quella in fonte converte poetando, io non lo ’nvidio;
english: Let Ovid now be silent, where he tells of Cadmus, Arethusa; if his verse has made of one a serpent, one a fountain,

italian: ché due nature mai a fronte a fronte non trasmutò sì ch’amendue le forme a cambiar lor matera fosser pronte.
english: I do not envy him; he never did transmute two natures, face to face, so that both forms were ready to exchange their matter.

italian: Insieme si rispuosero a tai norme, che ’l serpente la coda in forca fesse, e ’l feruto ristrinse insieme l’orme.
english: These were the ways they answered to each other: the serpent split its tail into a fork; the wounded sinner drew his steps together.

italian: Le gambe con le cosce seco stesse s’appiccar sì, che ’n poco la giuntura non facea segno alcun che si paresse.
english: The legs and then the thighs along with them so fastened to each other that the juncture soon left no sign that was discernible.

italian: Togliea la coda fessa la figura che si perdeva là, e la sua pelle si facea molle, e quella di là dura.
english: Meanwhile the cleft tail took upon itself the form the other gradually lost; its skin grew soft, the other’s skin grew hard.

italian: Io vidi intrar le braccia per l’ascelle, e i due piè de la fiera, ch’eran corti, tanto allungar quanto accorciavan quelle.
english: I saw the arms that drew in at his armpits and also saw the monster’s two short feet grow long for just as much as those were shortened.

italian: Poscia li piè di rietro, insieme attorti, diventaron lo membro che l’uom cela, e ’l misero del suo n’avea due porti.
english: The serpent’s hind feet, twisted up together, became the member that man hides; just as the wretch put out two hind paws from his member.

italian: Mentre che ’l fummo l’uno e l’altro vela di color novo, e genera ’l pel suso per l’una parte e da l’altra il dipela,
english: And while the smoke veils each with a new color, and now breeds hair upon the skin of one, just as it strips the hair from off the other,

italian: l’un si levò e l’altro cadde giuso, non torcendo però le lucerne empie, sotto le quai ciascun cambiava muso.
english: the one rose up, the other fell; and yet they never turned aside their impious eyelamps, beneath which each of them transformed his snout:

italian: Quel ch’era dritto, il trasse ver’ le tempie, e di troppa matera ch’in là venne uscir li orecchi de le gote scempie;
english: he who stood up drew his back toward the temples, and from the excess matter growing there came ears upon the cheeks that had been bare;

italian: ciò che non corse in dietro e si ritenne di quel soverchio, fé naso a la faccia e le labbra ingrossò quanto convenne.
english: whatever had not been pulled back but kept, superfluous, then made his face a nose and thickened out his lips appropriately.

italian: Quel che giacëa, il muso innanzi caccia, e li orecchi ritira per la testa come face le corna la lumaccia;
english: He who was lying down thrust out his snout; and even as the snail hauls in its horns, he drew his ears straight back into his head;

italian: e la lingua, ch’avëa unita e presta prima a parlar, si fende, e la forcuta ne l’altro si richiude; e ’l fummo resta.
english: his tongue, which had before been whole and fit for speech, now cleaves; the other’s tongue, which had been forked, now closes up; and the smoke stops.

italian: L’anima ch’era fiera divenuta, suffolando si fugge per la valle, e l’altro dietro a lui parlando sputa.
english: The soul that had become an animal, now hissing, hurried off along the valley; the other one, behind him, speaks and spits.

italian: Poscia li volse le novelle spalle, e disse a l’altro: «I’ vo’ che Buoso corra, com’ ho fatt’ io, carpon per questo calle».
english: And then he turned aside his new-made shoulders and told the third soul: “I’d have Buoso run on all fours down this road, as I have done.”

italian: Così vid’ io la settima zavorra mutare e trasmutare; e qui mi scusi la novità se fior la penna abborra.
english: And so I saw the seventh ballast change and rechange; may the strangeness plead for me if there’s been some confusion in my pen.

italian: E avvegna che li occhi miei confusi fossero alquanto e l’animo smagato, non poter quei fuggirsi tanto chiusi,
english: And though my eyes were somewhat blurred, my mind bewildered, those three sinners did not flee so secretly that I could not perceive

italian: ch’i’ non scorgessi ben Puccio Sciancato; ed era quel che sol, di tre compagni che venner prima, non era mutato;
english: Puccio Sciancato clearly, he who was the only soul who’d not been changed among the three companions we had met at first;

italian: l’altr’ era quel che tu, Gaville, piagni.
english: the other one made you, Gaville, grieve.

italian: Godi, Fiorenza, poi che se’ sì grande che per mare e per terra batti l’ali, e per lo ’nferno tuo nome si spande!
english: Be joyous, Florence, you are great indeed, for over sea and land you beat your wings; through every part of Hell your name extends!

italian: Tra li ladron trovai cinque cotali tuoi cittadini onde mi ven vergogna, e tu in grande orranza non ne sali.
english: Among the thieves I found five citizens of yours—and such, that shame has taken me; with them, you can ascend to no high honor.

italian: Ma se presso al mattin del ver si sogna, tu sentirai, di qua da picciol tempo, di quel che Prato, non ch’altri, t’agogna.
english: But if the dreams dreamt close to dawn are true, then little time will pass before you feel what Prato and the others crave for you.

italian: E se già fosse, non saria per tempo. Così foss’ ei, da che pur esser dee! ché più mi graverà, com’ più m’attempo.
english: Were that already come, it would not be too soon—and let it come, since it must be! As I grow older, it will be more heavy.

italian: Noi ci partimmo, e su per le scalee che n’avean fatto iborni a scender pria, rimontò ’l duca mio e trasse mee;
english: We left that deep and, by protruding stones that served as stairs for our descent before, my guide climbed up again and drew me forward;

italian: e proseguendo la solinga via, tra le schegge e tra ’ rocchi de lo scoglio lo piè sanza la man non si spedia.
english: and as we took our solitary path among the ridge’s jagged spurs and rocks, our feet could not make way without our hands.

italian: Allor mi dolsi, e ora mi ridoglio quando drizzo la mente a ciò ch’io vidi, e più lo ’ngegno affreno ch’i’ non soglio,
english: It grieved me then and now grieves me again when I direct my mind to what I saw; and more than usual, I curb my talent,

italian: perché non corra che virtù nol guidi; sì che, se stella bona o miglior cosa m’ha dato ’l ben, ch’io stessi nol m’invidi.
english: that it not run where virtue does not guide; so that, if my kind star or something better has given me that gift, I not abuse it.

italian: Quante ’l villan ch’al poggio si riposa, nel tempo che colui che ’l mondo schiara la faccia sua a noi tien meno ascosa,
english: As many as the fireflies the peasant (while resting on a hillside in the season when he who lights the world least hides his face),

italian: come la mosca cede a la zanzara, vede lucciole giù per la vallea, forse colà dov’ e’ vendemmia e ara:
english: just when the fly gives way to the mosquito, sees glimmering below, down in the valley, there where perhaps he gathers grapes and tills—

italian: di tante fiamme tutta risplendea l’ottava bolgia, sì com’ io m’accorsi tosto che fui là ’ve ’l fondo parea.
english: so many were the flames that glittered in the eighth abyss; I made this out as soon as I had come to where one sees the bottom.

italian: E qual colui che si vengiò con li orsi vide ’l carro d’Elia al dipartire, quando i cavalli al cielo erti levorsi,
english: Even as he who was avenged by bears saw, as it left, Elijah’s chariot— its horses rearing, rising right to heaven—

italian: che nol potea sì con li occhi seguire, ch’el vedesse altro che la fiamma sola, sì come nuvoletta, in sù salire:
english: when he could not keep track of it except by watching one lone flame in its ascent, just like a little cloud that climbs on high:

italian: tal si move ciascuna per la gola del fosso, ché nessuna mostra ’l furto, e ogne fiamma un peccatore invola.
english: so, through the gullet of that ditch, each flame must make its way; no flame displays its prey, though every flame has carried off a sinner.

italian: Io stava sovra ’l ponte a veder surto, sì che s’io non avessi un ronchion preso, caduto sarei giù sanz’ esser urto.
english: I stood upon the bridge and leaned straight out to see; and if I had not gripped a rock, I should have fallen off—without a push.

italian: E ’l duca che mi vide tanto atteso, disse: «Dentro dai fuochi son li spirti; catun si fascia di quel ch’elli è inceso».
english: My guide, who noted how intent I was, told me: “Within those fires there are souls; each one is swathed in that which scorches him.”

italian: «Maestro mio», rispuos’ io, «per udirti son io più certo; ma già m’era avviso che così fosse, e già voleva dirti:
english: “My master,” I replied, “on hearing you, I am more sure; but I’d already thought that it was so, and I had meant to ask:

italian: chi è ’n quel foco che vien sì diviso di sopra, che par surger de la pira dov’ Eteòcle col fratel fu miso?».
english: Who is within the flame that comes so twinned above that it would seem to rise out of the pyre Eteocles shared with his brother?”

italian: Rispuose a me: «Là dentro si martira Ulisse e Dïomede, e così insieme a la vendetta vanno come a l’ira;
english: He answered me: “Within that flame, Ulysses and Diomedes suffer; they, who went as one to rage, now share one punishment.

italian: e dentro da la lor fiamma si geme l’agguato del caval che fé la porta onde uscì de’ Romani il gentil seme.
english: And there, together in their flame, they grieve over the horse’s fraud that caused a breach— the gate that let Rome’s noble seed escape.

italian: Piangevisi entro l’arte per che, morta, Deïdamìa ancor si duol d’Achille, e del Palladio pena vi si porta».
english: There they regret the guile that makes the dead Deidamia still lament Achilles; and there, for the Palladium, they pay.”

italian: «S’ei posson dentro da quelle faville parlar», diss’ io, «maestro, assai ten priego e ripriego, che ’l priego vaglia mille,
english: “If they can speak within those sparks,” I said, “I pray you and repray and, master, may my prayer be worth a thousand pleas, do not

italian: che non mi facci de l’attender niego fin che la fiamma cornuta qua vegna; vedi che del disio ver’ lei mi piego!».
english: forbid my waiting here until the flame with horns approaches us; for you can see how, out of my desire, I bend toward it.”

italian: Ed elli a me: «La tua preghiera è degna di molta loda, e io però l’accetto; ma fa che la tua lingua si sostegna.
english: And he to me: “What you have asked is worthy of every praise; therefore, I favor it. I only ask you this: refrain from talking.

italian: Lascia parlare a me, ch’i’ ho concetto ciò che tu vuoi; ch’ei sarebbero schivi, perch’ e’ fuor greci, forse del tuo detto».
english: Let me address them—I have understood what you desire of them. Since they were Greek, perhaps they’d be disdainful of your speech.”

italian: Poi che la fiamma fu venuta quivi dove parve al mio duca tempo e loco, in questa forma lui parlare audivi:
english: And when my guide adjudged the flame had reached a point where time and place were opportune, this was the form I heard his words assume:

italian: «O voi che siete due dentro ad un foco, s’io meritai di voi mentre ch’io vissi, s’io meritai di voi assai o poco
english: “You two who move as one within the flame, if I deserved of you while I still lived, if I deserved of you much or a little

italian: quando nel mondo li alti versi scrissi, non vi movete; ma l’un di voi dica dove, per lui, perduto a morir gissi».
english: when in the world I wrote my noble lines, do not move on; let one of you retell where, having gone astray, he found his death.”

italian: Lo maggior corno de la fiamma antica cominciò a crollarsi mormorando, pur come quella cui vento affatica;
english: The greater horn within that ancient flame began to sway and tremble, murmuring just like a fire that struggles in the wind;

italian: indi la cima qua e là menando, come fosse la lingua che parlasse, gittò voce di fuori e disse: «Quando
english: and then he waved his flame—tip back and forth as if it were a tongue that tried to speak, and flung toward us a voice that answered: “When

italian: mi diparti’ da Circe, che sottrasse me più d’un anno là presso a Gaeta, prima che sì Enëa la nomasse,
english: I sailed away from Circe, who’d beguiled me to stay more than a year there, near Gaeta— before Aeneas gave that place a name—

italian: né dolcezza di figlio, né la pieta del vecchio padre, né ’l debito amore lo qual dovea Penelopè far lieta,
english: neither my fondness for my son nor pity for my old father nor the love I owed Penelope, which would have gladdened her,

italian: vincer potero dentro a me l’ardore ch’i’ ebbi a divenir del mondo esperto e de li vizi umani e del valore;
english: was able to defeat in me the longing I had to gain experience of the world and of the vices and the worth of men.

italian: ma misi me per l’alto mare aperto sol con un legno e con quella compagna picciola da la qual non fui diserto.
english: Therefore, I set out on the open sea with but one ship and that small company of those who never had deserted me.

italian: L’un lito e l’altro vidi infin la Spagna, fin nel Morrocco, e l’isola d’i Sardi, e l’altre che quel mare intorno bagna.
english: I saw as far as Spain, far as Morocco, along both shores; I saw Sardinia and saw the other islands that sea bathes.

italian: Io e ’ compagni eravam vecchi e tardi quando venimmo a quella foce stretta dov’ Ercule segnò li suoi riguardi
english: And I and my companions were already old and slow, when we approached the narrows where Hercules set up his boundary stones

italian: acciò che l’uom più oltre non si metta; da la man destra mi lasciai Sibilia, da l’altra già m’avea lasciata Setta.
english: that men might heed and never reach beyond: upon my right, I had gone past Seville, and on the left, already passed Ceuta.

italian: “O frati”, dissi, “che per cento milia perigli siete giunti a l’occidente, a questa tanto picciola vigilia
english: ‘Brothers,’ I said, ‘o you, who having crossed a hundred thousand dangers, reach the west, to this brief waking—time that still is left

italian: d’i nostri sensi ch’è del rimanente non vogliate negar l’esperïenza, di retro al sol, del mondo sanza gente.
english: unto your senses, you must not deny experience of that which lies beyond the sun, and of the world that is unpeopled.

italian: Considerate la vostra semenza: fatti non foste a viver come bruti, ma per seguir virtute e canoscenza”.
english: Consider well the seed that gave you birth: you were not made to live your lives as brutes, but to be followers of worth and knowledge.’

italian: Li miei compagni fec’ io sì aguti, con questa orazion picciola, al cammino, che a pena poscia li avrei ritenuti;
english: I spurred my comrades with this brief address to meet the journey with such eagerness that I could hardly, then, have held them back;

italian: e volta nostra poppa nel mattino, de’ remi facemmo ali al folle volo, sempre acquistando dal lato mancino.
english: and having turned our stern toward morning, we made wings out of our oars in a wild flight and always gained upon our left—hand side.

italian: Tutte le stelle già de l’altro polo vedea la notte, e ’l nostro tanto basso, che non surgëa fuor del marin suolo.
english: At night I now could see the other pole and all its stars; the star of ours had fallen and never rose above the plain of the ocean.

italian: Cinque volte racceso e tante casso lo lume era di sotto da la luna, poi che ’ntrati eravam ne l’alto passo,
english: Five times the light beneath the moon had been rekindled, and, as many times, was spent, since that hard passage faced our first attempt,

italian: quando n’apparve una montagna, bruna per la distanza, e parvemi alta tanto quanto veduta non avëa alcuna.
english: when there before us rose a mountain, dark because of distance, and it seemed to me the highest mountain I had ever seen.

italian: Noi ci allegrammo, e tosto tornò in pianto; ché de la nova terra un turbo nacque e percosse del legno il primo canto.
english: And we were glad, but this soon turned to sorrow, for out of that new land a whirlwind rose and hammered at our ship, against her bow.

italian: Tre volte il fé girar con tutte l’acque; a la quarta levar la poppa in suso e la prora ire in giù, com’ altrui piacque,
english: Three times it turned her round with all the waters; and at the fourth, it lifted up the stern so that our prow plunged deep, as pleased an Other,

italian: infin che ’l mar fu sovra noi richiuso».
english: until the sea again closed—over us.”

italian: Già era dritta in sù la fiamma e queta per non dir più, e già da noi sen gia con la licenza del dolce poeta,
english: The flame already was erect and silent — it had no more to say. Now it had left us with the permission of the gentle poet,

italian: quand’ un’altra, che dietro a lei venìa, ne fece volger li occhi a la sua cima per un confuso suon che fuor n’uscia.
english: when, just behind it, came another flame that drew our eyes to watch its tip because of the perplexing sound that it sent forth.

italian: Come ’l bue cicilian che mugghiò prima col pianto di colui, e ciò fu dritto, che l’avea temperato con sua lima,
english: Even as the Sicilian bull (that first had bellowed with the cry — and this was just — of him who shaped it with his instruments)

italian: mugghiava con la voce de l’afflitto, sì che, con tutto che fosse di rame, pur el pareva dal dolor trafitto;
english: would always bellow with its victim’s voice, so that, although that bull was only brass, it seemed as if it were pierced through by pain;

italian: così, per non aver via né forame dal principio nel foco, in suo linguaggio si convertïan le parole grame.
english: so were the helpless words that, from the first, had found no path or exit from the flame, transformed into the language of the fire.

italian: Ma poscia ch’ebber colto lor vïaggio su per la punta, dandole quel guizzo che dato avea la lingua in lor passaggio,
english: But after they had found their way up toward the tip, and given it that movement which the tongue had given them along their passage,

italian: udimmo dire: «O tu a cu’ io drizzo la voce e che parlavi mo lombardo, dicendo “Istra ten va, più non t’adizzo”,
english: we heard: “O you to whom I turn my voice, who only now were talking Lombard, saying, ‘Now you may leave — I’ll not provoke more speech,’

italian: perch’ io sia giunto forse alquanto tardo, non t’incresca restare a parlar meco; vedi che non incresce a me, e ardo!
english: though I have come perhaps a little late, may it not trouble you to stop and speak with me; see how I stay — and I am burning!

italian: Se tu pur mo in questo mondo cieco caduto se’ di quella dolce terra latina ond’ io mia colpa tutta reco,
english: If you have fallen into this blind world but recently, out of the sweet Italian country from which I carry all my guilt,

italian: dimmi se Romagnuoli han pace o guerra; ch’io fui d’i monti là intra Orbino e ’l giogo di che Tever si diserra».
english: do tell me if the Romagnoles have peace or war; I was from there — the hills between Urbino and the ridge where Tiber springs.”

italian: Io era in giuso ancora attento e chino, quando il mio duca mi tentò di costa, dicendo: «Parla tu; questi è latino».
english: I still was bent, attentive, over him, when my guide nudged me lightly at the side and said: “You speak; he is Italian.”

italian: E io, ch’avea già pronta la risposta, sanza indugio a parlare incominciai: «O anima che se’ là giù nascosta,
english: And I, who had my answer set already, without delay began to speak to him: “O soul that is concealed below in flame,

italian: Romagna tua non è, e non fu mai, sanza guerra ne’ cuor de’ suoi tiranni; ma ’n palese nessuna or vi lasciai.
english: Romagna is not now and never was quite free of war inside its tyrants’ hearts; but when I left her, none had broken out.

italian: Ravenna sta come stata è molt’ anni: l’aguglia da Polenta la si cova, sì che Cervia ricuopre co’ suoi vanni.
english: Ravenna stands as it has stood for years; the eagle of Polenta shelters it and also covers Cervia with his wings.

italian: La terra che fé già la lunga prova e di Franceschi sanguinoso mucchio, sotto le branche verdi si ritrova.
english: The city that already stood long trial and made a bloody heap out of the French, now finds itself again beneath green paws.

italian: E ’l mastin vecchio e ’l nuovo da Verrucchio, che fecer di Montagna il mal governo, là dove soglion fan d’i denti succhio.
english: Both mastiffs of Verruchio, old and new, who dealt so badly with Montagna, use their teeth to bore where they have always gnawed.

italian: Le città di Lamone e di Santerno conduce il lïoncel dal nido bianco, che muta parte da la state al verno.
english: The cities on Lamone and Santerno are led by the young lion of the white lair; from summer unto winter, he shifts factions.

italian: E quella cu’ il Savio bagna il fianco, così com’ ella sie’ tra ’l piano e ’l monte tra tirannia si vive e stato franco.
english: That city with its side bathed by the Savio, just as it lies between the plain and mountain, lives somewhere between tyranny and freedom.

italian: Ora chi se’, ti priego che ne conte; non esser duro più ch’altri sia stato, se ’l nome tuo nel mondo tegna fronte».
english: And now, I pray you, tell me who you are: do not be harder than I’ve been with you, that in the world your name may still endure.”

italian: Poscia che ’l foco alquanto ebbe rugghiato al modo suo, l’aguta punta mosse di qua, di là, e poi diè cotal fiato:
english: After the flame, in customary fashion, had roared awhile, it moved its pointed tip this side and that and then set free this breath:

italian: «S’i’ credesse che mia risposta fosse a persona che mai tornasse al mondo, questa fiamma staria sanza più scosse;
english: “If I thought my reply were meant for one who ever could return into the world, this flame would stir no more; and yet, since none —

italian: ma però che già mai di questo fondo non tornò vivo alcun, s’i’ odo il vero, sanza tema d’infamia ti rispondo.
english: if what I hear is true — ever returned alive from this abyss, then without fear of facing infamy, I answer you.

italian: Io fui uom d’arme, e poi fui cordigliero, credendomi, sì cinto, fare ammenda; e certo il creder mio venìa intero,
english: I was a man of arms, then wore the cord, believing that, so girt, I made amends; and surely what I thought would have been true

italian: se non fosse il gran prete, a cui mal prenda!, che mi rimise ne le prime colpe; e come e quare , voglio che m’intenda.
english: had not the Highest Priest — may he be damned! — made me fall back into my former sins; and how and why, I’d have you hear from me.

italian: Mentre ch’io forma fui d’ossa e di polpe che la madre mi diè, l’opere mie non furon leonine, ma di volpe.
english: While I still had the form of bones and flesh my mother gave to me, my deeds were not those of the lion but those of the fox.

italian: Li accorgimenti e le coperte vie io seppi tutte, e sì menai lor arte, ch’al fine de la terra il suono uscie.
english: The wiles and secret ways — I knew them all and so employed their arts that my renown had reached the very boundaries of earth.

italian: Quando mi vidi giunto in quella parte di mia etade ove ciascun dovrebbe calar le vele e raccoglier le sarte,
english: But when I saw myself come to that part of life when it is fitting for all men to lower sails and gather in their ropes,

italian: ciò che pria mi piacëa, allor m’increbbe, e pentuto e confesso mi rendei; ahi miser lasso! e giovato sarebbe.
english: what once had been my joy was now dejection; repenting and confessing, I became a friar; and — poor me — it would have helped.

italian: Lo principe d’i novi Farisei, avendo guerra presso a Laterano, e non con Saracin né con Giudei,
english: The prince of the new Pharisees, who then was waging war so near the Lateran — and not against the Jews or Saracens,

italian: ché ciascun suo nimico era cristiano, e nessun era stato a vincer Acri né mercatante in terra di Soldano,
english: for every enemy of his was Christian, and none of them had gone to conquer Acre or been a trader in the Sultan’s lands —

italian: né sommo officio né ordini sacri guardò in sé, né in me quel capestro che solea fare i suoi cinti più macri.
english: took no care for the highest office or the holy orders that were his, or for my cord, which used to make its wearers leaner.

italian: Ma come Costantin chiese Silvestro d’entro Siratti a guerir de la lebbre, così mi chiese questi per maestro
english: But just as Constantine, on Mount Soracte, to cure his leprosy, sought out Sylvester, so this one sought me out as his instructor,

italian: a guerir de la sua superba febbre; domandommi consiglio, e io tacetti perché le sue parole parver ebbre.
english: to ease the fever of his arrogance. He asked me to give counsel. I was silent — his words had seemed to me delirious.

italian: E’ poi ridisse: “Tuo cuor non sospetti; finor t’assolvo, e tu m’insegna fare sì come Penestrino in terra getti.
english: And then he said: ‘Your heart must not mistrust: I now absolve you in advance — teach me to batter Penestrino to the ground.

italian: Lo ciel poss’ io serrare e diserrare, come tu sai; però son due le chiavi che ’l mio antecessor non ebbe care”.
english: You surely know that I possess the power to lock and unlock Heaven; for the keys my predecessor did not prize are two.’

italian: Allor mi pinser li argomenti gravi là ’ ve ’l tacer mi fu avviso ’l peggio, e dissi: “Padre, da che tu mi lavi
english: Then his grave arguments compelled me so, my silence seemed a worse offense than speech, and I said: ‘Since you cleanse me of the sin

italian: di quel peccato ov’io mo cader deggio, lunga promessa con l’attender corto ti farà trïunfar ne l’alto seggio”.
english: that I must now fall into, Father, know: long promises and very brief fulfillments will bring a victory to your high throne.’

italian: Francesco venne poi com’ io fu’ morto, per me; ma un d’i neri cherubini li disse: “Non portar: non mi far torto.
english: Then Francis came, as soon as I was dead, for me; but one of the black cherubim told him: ‘Don’t bear him off; do not cheat me.

italian: Venir se ne dee giù tra ’ miei meschini perché diede ’l consiglio frodolente, dal quale in qua stato li sono a’ crini;
english: He must come down among my menials; the counsel that he gave was fraudulent; since then, I’ve kept close track, to snatch his scalp;

italian: ch’assolver non si può chi non si pente, né pentere e volere insieme puossi per la contradizion che nol consente”.
english: one can’t absolve a man who’s not repented, and no one can repent and will at once; the law of contradiction won’t allow it.’

italian: Oh me dolente! come mi riscossi quando mi prese dicendomi: “Forse tu non pensavi ch’io löico fossi!”.
english: O miserable me, for how I started when he took hold of me and said: ‘Perhaps you did not think that I was a logician!’

italian: A Minòs mi portò; e quelli attorse otto volte la coda al dosso duro; e poi che per gran rabbia la si morse,
english: He carried me to Minos; and that monster twisted his tail eight times around his hide and then, when he had bit it in great anger,

italian: disse: “Questi è d’i rei del foco furo”; per ch’io là dove vedi son perduto, e sì vestito, andando, mi rancuro».
english: announced: ‘This one is for the thieving fire’; for which — and where, you see — I now am lost, and in this garb I move in bitterness.”

italian: Quand’ elli ebbe ’l suo dir così compiuto, la fiamma dolorando si partio, torcendo e dibattendo ’l corno aguto.
english: And when, with this, his words were at an end, the flame departed, sorrowing and writhing and tossing its sharp horn. We moved beyond;

italian: Noi passamm’ oltre, e io e ’l duca mio, su per lo scoglio infino in su l’altr’ arco che cuopre ’l fosso in che si paga il fio
english: I went together with my guide, along the ridge until the other arch that bridges the ditch where payment is imposed on those

italian: a quei che scommettendo acquistan carco.
english: who, since they brought such discord, bear such loads.

italian: ﻿Chi poria mai pur con parole sciolte dicer del sangue e de le piaghe a pieno ch’i’ ora vidi, per narrar più volte?
english: Who, even with untrammeled words and many attempts at telling, ever could recount in full the blood and wounds that I now saw?

italian: Ogne lingua per certo verria meno per lo nostro sermone e per la mente c’hanno a tanto comprender poco seno.
english: Each tongue that tried would certainly fall short because the shallowness of both our speech and intellect cannot contain so much.

italian: S’el s’aunasse ancor tutta la gente che già, in su la fortunata terra di Puglia, fu del suo sangue dolente
english: Were you to reassemble all the men who once, within Apulia’s fateful land, had mourned their blood, shed at the Trojans’ hands,

italian: per li Troiani e per la lunga guerra che de l’anella fé sì alte spoglie, come Livïo scrive, che non erra,
english: as well as those who fell in the long war where massive mounds of rings were battle spoils— even as Livy writes, who does not err—

italian: con quella che sentio di colpi doglie per contastare a Ruberto Guiscardo; e l’altra il cui ossame ancor s’accoglie
english: and those who felt the thrust of painful blows when they fought hard against Robert Guiscard; with all the rest whose bones are still piled up

italian: a Ceperan, là dove fu bugiardo ciascun Pugliese, e là da Tagliacozzo, dove sanz’ arme vinse il vecchio Alardo;
english: at Ceperano—each Apulian was a traitor there—and, too, at Tagliacozzo, where old Alardo conquered without weapons;

italian: e qual forato suo membro e qual mozzo mostrasse, d’aequar sarebbe nulla il modo de la nona bolgia sozzo.
english: and then, were one to show his limb pierced through and one his limb hacked off, that would not match the hideousness of the ninth abyss.

italian: Già veggia, per mezzul perdere o lulla, com’ io vidi un, così non si pertugia, rotto dal mento infin dove si trulla.
english: No barrel, even though it’s lost a hoop or end— piece, ever gapes as one whom I saw ripped right from his chin to where we fart:

italian: Tra le gambe pendevan le minugia; la corata pareva e ’l tristo sacco che merda fa di quel che si trangugia.
english: his bowels hung between his legs, one saw his vitals and the miserable sack that makes of what we swallow excrement.

italian: Mentre che tutto in lui veder m’attacco, guardommi e con le man s’aperse il petto, dicendo: «Or vedi com’ io mi dilacco!
english: While I was all intent on watching him, he looked at me, and with his hands he spread his chest and said: “See how I split myself!

italian: vedi come storpiato è Mäometto! Dinanzi a me sen va piangendo Alì, fesso nel volto dal mento al ciuffetto.
english: See now how maimed Mohammed is! And he who walks and weeps before me is Ali, whose face is opened wide from chin to forelock.

italian: E tutti li altri che tu vedi qui, seminator di scandalo e di scisma fuor vivi, e però son fessi così.
english: And all the others here whom you can see were, when alive, the sowers of dissension and scandal, and for this they now are split.

italian: Un diavolo è qua dietro che n’accisma sì crudelmente, al taglio de la spada rimettendo ciascun di questa risma,
english: Behind us here, a devil decks us out so cruelly, re—placing every one of this throng underneath the sword edge when

italian: quand’ avem volta la dolente strada; però che le ferite son richiuse prima ch’altri dinanzi li rivada.
english: we’ve made our way around the road of pain, because our wounds have closed again before we have returned to meet his blade once more.

italian: Ma tu chi se’ che ’n su lo scoglio muse, forse per indugiar d’ire a la pena ch’è giudicata in su le tue accuse?».
english: But who are you who dawdle on this ridge, perhaps to slow your going to the verdict that was pronounced on your self—accusations?

italian: «Né morte ’l giunse ancor, né colpa ’l mena», rispuose ’l mio maestro, «a tormentarlo; ma per dar lui esperïenza piena,
english: “Death has not reached him yet,” my master answered, “nor is it guilt that summons him to torment; but that he may gain full experience,

italian: a me, che morto son, convien menarlo per lo ’nferno qua giù di giro in giro; e quest’ è ver così com’ io ti parlo».
english: I, who am dead, must guide him here below, to circle after circle, throughout Hell: this is as true as that I speak to you.”

italian: Più fuor di cento che, quando l’udiro, s’arrestaron nel fosso a riguardarmi per maraviglia, oblïando il martiro.
english: More than a hundred, when they heard him, stopped within the ditch and turned to look at me, forgetful of their torture, wondering.

italian: «Or dì a fra Dolcin dunque che s’armi, tu che forse vedra’ il sole in breve, s’ello non vuol qui tosto seguitarmi,
english: “Then you, who will perhaps soon see the sun, tell Fra Dolcino to provide himself with food, if he has no desire to join me

italian: sì di vivanda, che stretta di neve non rechi la vittoria al Noarese, ch’altrimenti acquistar non saria leve».
english: here quickly, lest when snow besieges him, it bring the Novarese the victory that otherwise they would not find too easy.”

italian: Poi che l’un piè per girsene sospese, Mäometto mi disse esta parola; indi a partirsi in terra lo distese.
english: When he had raised his heel, as if to go, Mohammed said these words to me, and then he set it on the ground and off he went.

italian: Un altro, che forata avea la gola e tronco ’l naso infin sotto le ciglia, e non avea mai ch’una orecchia sola,
english: Another sinner, with his throat slit through and with his nose hacked off up to his eyebrows, and no more than a single ear remaining,

italian: ristato a riguardar per maraviglia con li altri, innanzi a li altri aprì la canna, ch’era di fuor d’ogne parte vermiglia,
english: had—with the others—stayed his steps in wonder; he was the first, before the rest, to open his windpipe—on the outside, all bloodred—

italian: e disse: «O tu cui colpa non condanna e cu’ io vidi su in terra latina, se troppa simiglianza non m’inganna,
english: and said: “O you whom guilt does not condemn, and whom, unless too close resemblance cheats me, I’ve seen above upon Italian soil,

italian: rimembriti di Pier da Medicina, se mai torni a veder lo dolce piano che da Vercelli a Marcabò dichina.
english: remember Pier da Medicina if you ever see again the gentle plain that from Vercelli slopes to Marcabo.

italian: E fa saper a’ due miglior da Fano, a messer Guido e anco ad Angiolello, che, se l’antiveder qui non è vano,
english: And let the two best men of Fano know— I mean both Messer Guido and Angiolello— that, if the foresight we have here’s not vain,

italian: gittati saran fuor di lor vasello e mazzerati presso a la Cattolica per tradimento d’un tiranno fello.
english: they will be cast out of their ship and drowned, weighed down with stones, near La Cattolica, because of a foul tyrant’s treachery.

italian: Tra l’isola di Cipri e di Maiolica non vide mai sì gran fallo Nettuno, non da pirate, non da gente argolica.
english: Between the isles of Cyprus and Majorca, Neptune has never seen so cruel a crime committed by the pirates or the Argives.

italian: Quel traditor che vede pur con l’uno, e tien la terra che tale qui meco vorrebbe di vedere esser digiuno,
english: That traitor who sees only with one eye and rules the land which one who’s here with me would wish his sight had never seen, will call

italian: farà venirli a parlamento seco; poi farà sì, ch’al vento di Focara non sarà lor mestier voto né preco».
english: Guido and Angiolello to a parley, and then will so arrange it that they’ll need no vow or prayer to Focara’s wind!”

italian: E io a lui: «Dimostrami e dichiara, se vuo’ ch’i’ porti sù di te novella, chi è colui da la veduta amara».
english: And I to him: “If you would have me carry some news of you above, then tell and show me who so detests the sight of Rimini.”

italian: Allor puose la mano a la mascella d’un suo compagno e la bocca li aperse, gridando: «Questi è desso, e non favella.
english: And then he set his hand upon the jaw of a companion, opening his mouth and shouting: “This is he, and he speaks not.

italian: Questi, scacciato, il dubitar sommerse in Cesare, affermando che ’l fornito sempre con danno l’attender sofferse».
english: A man cast out, he quenched the doubt in Caesar, insisting that the one who is prepared can only suffer harm if he delays.”

italian: Oh quanto mi pareva sbigottito con la lingua tagliata ne la strozza Curïo, ch’a dir fu così ardito!
english: Oh, how dismayed and pained he seemed to me, his tongue slit in his gullet: Curio, who once was so audacious in his talk!

italian: E un ch’avea l’una e l’altra man mozza, levando i moncherin per l’aura fosca, sì che ’l sangue facea la faccia sozza,
english: And one who walked with both his hands hacked off, while lifting up his stumps through the dark air, so that his face was hideous with blood,

italian: gridò: «Ricordera’ti anche del Mosca, che disse, lasso!, “Capo ha cosa fatta”, che fu mal seme per la gente tosca».
english: cried out: “You will remember Mosca, too, who said—alas—’What’s done is at an end,’ which was the seed of evil for the Tuscans.”

italian: E io li aggiunsi: «E morte di tua schiatta»; per ch’elli, accumulando duol con duolo, sen gio come persona trista e matta.
english: I added: “—and brought death to your own kinsmen”; then having heard me speak, grief heaped on grief, he went his way as one gone mad with sadness.

italian: Ma io rimasi a riguardar lo stuolo, e vidi cosa ch’io avrei paura, sanza più prova, di contarla solo;
english: But I stayed there to watch that company and saw a thing that I should be afraid to tell with no more proof than my own self—

italian: se non che coscïenza m’assicura, la buona compagnia che l’uom francheggia sotto l’asbergo del sentirsi pura.
english: except that I am reassured by conscience, that good companion, heartening a man beneath the breastplate of its purity.

italian: Io vidi certo, e ancor par ch’io ’l veggia, un busto sanza capo andar sì come andavan li altri de la trista greggia;
english: I surely saw, and it still seems I see, a trunk without a head that walked just like the others in that melancholy herd;

italian: e ’l capo tronco tenea per le chiome, pesol con mano a guisa di lanterna: e quel mirava noi e dicea: «Oh me!».
english: it carried by the hair its severed head, which swayed within its hand just like a lantern; and that head looked at us and said: “Ah me!”

italian: Di sé facea a sé stesso lucerna, ed eran due in uno e uno in due; com’ esser può, quei sa che sì governa.
english: Out of itself it made itself a lamp, and they were two in one and one in two; how that can be, He knows who so decrees.

italian: Quando diritto al piè del ponte fue, levò ’l braccio alto con tutta la testa per appressarne le parole sue,
english: When it was just below the bridge, it lifted its arm together with its head, so that its words might be more near us, words that said:

italian: che fuoro: «Or vedi la pena molesta, tu che, spirando, vai veggendo i morti: vedi s’alcuna è grande come questa.
english: “Now you can see atrocious punishment, you who, still breathing, go to view the dead: see if there’s any pain as great as this.

english: My guide and I came on that hidden road to make our way back into the bright world; and with no care for any rest, we climbed—

italian: salimmo sù, el primo e io secondo, tanto ch’i’ vidi de le cose belle che porta ’l ciel, per un pertugio tondo.
english: he first, I following—until I saw, through a round opening, some of those things of beauty Heaven bears. It was from there

italian: E quindi uscimmo a riveder le stelle.
english: that we emerged, to see—once more—the stars.

italian: Per correr miglior acque alza le vele omai la navicella del mio ingegno, che lascia dietro a sé mar sì crudele;
english: To course across more kindly waters now my talent’s little vessel lifts her sails, leaving behind herself a sea so cruel;

italian: e canterò di quel secondo regno dove l’umano spirito si purga e di salire al ciel diventa degno.
english: and what I sing will be that second kingdom, in which the human soul is cleansed of sin, becoming worthy of ascent to Heaven.

italian: Ma qui la morta poesì resurga, o sante Muse, poi che vostro sono; e qui Calïopè alquanto surga,
english: But here, since I am yours, o holy Muses, may this poem rise again from Hell’s dead realm; and may Calliope rise somewhat here,

italian: seguitando il mio canto con quel suono di cui le Piche misere sentiro lo colpo tal, che disperar perdono.
english: accompanying my singing with that music whose power struck the poor Pierides so forcefully that they despaired of pardon.

italian: Dolce color d’orïental zaffiro, che s’accoglieva nel sereno aspetto del mezzo, puro infino al primo giro,
english: The gentle hue of oriental sapphire in which the sky’s serenity was steeped— its aspect pure as far as the horizon—

italian: a li occhi miei ricominciò diletto, tosto ch’io usci’ fuor de l’aura morta che m’avea contristati li occhi e ’l petto.
english: brought back my joy in seeing just as soon as I had left behind the air of death that had afflicted both my sight and breast.

italian: Lo bel pianeto che d’amar conforta faceva tutto rider l’orïente, velando i Pesci ch’erano in sua scorta.
english: The lovely planet that is patroness of love made all the eastern heavens glad, veiling the Pisces in the train she led.

italian: I’ mi volsi a man destra, e puosi mente a l’altro polo, e vidi quattro stelle non viste mai fuor ch’a la prima gente.
english: Then I turned to the right, setting my mind upon the other pole, and saw four stars not seen before except by the first people.

italian: Goder pareva ’l ciel di lor fiammelle: oh settentrïonal vedovo sito, poi che privato se’ di mirar quelle!
english: Heaven appeared to revel in their flames: o northern hemisphere, because you were denied that sight, you are a widower!

italian: Com’ io da loro sguardo fui partito, un poco me volgendo a l’altro polo, là onde ’l Carro già era sparito,
english: After my eyes took leave of those four stars, turning a little toward the other pole, from which the Wain had disappeared by now,

italian: vidi presso di me un veglio solo, degno di tanta reverenza in vista, che più non dee a padre alcun figliuolo.
english: I saw a solitary patriarch near me—his aspect worthy of such reverence that even son to father owes no more.

italian: Lunga la barba e di pel bianco mista portava, a’ suoi capelli simigliante, de’ quai cadeva al petto doppia lista.
english: His beard was long and mixed with white, as were the hairs upon his head; and his hair spread down to his chest in a divided tress.

italian: Li raggi de le quattro luci sante fregiavan sì la sua faccia di lume, ch’i’ ’l vedea come ’l sol fosse davante.
english: The rays of the four holy stars so framed his face with light that in my sight he seemed like one who is confronted by the sun.

italian: «Chi siete voi che contro al cieco fiume fuggita avete la pregione etterna?», diss’ el, movendo quelle oneste piume.
english: “Who are you—who, against the hidden river, were able to escape the eternal prison?” he said, moving those venerable plumes.

italian: «Chi v’ha guidati, o che vi fu lucerna, uscendo fuor de la profonda notte che sempre nera fa la valle inferna?
english: “Who was your guide? What served you both as lantern when, from the deep night that will always keep the hellish valley dark, you were set free?

italian: Son le leggi d’abisso così rotte? o è mutato in ciel novo consiglio, che, dannati, venite a le mie grotte?».
english: The laws of the abyss—have they been broken? Or has a new, a changed decree in Heaven let you, though damned, approach my rocky slopes?”

italian: Lo duca mio allor mi diè di piglio, e con parole e con mani e con cenni reverenti mi fé le gambe e ’l ciglio.
english: My guide took hold of me decisively; by way of words and hands and other signs, he made my knees and brow show reverence.

italian: Poscia rispuose lui: «Da me non venni: donna scese del ciel, per li cui prieghi de la mia compagnia costui sovvenni.
english: Then he replied: “I do not come through my own self. There was a lady sent from Heaven; her pleas led me to help and guide this man.

italian: Ma da ch’è tuo voler che più si spieghi di nostra condizion com’ ell’ è vera, esser non puote il mio che a te si nieghi.
english: But since your will would have a far more full and accurate account of our condition, my will cannot withhold what you request.

italian: Questi non vide mai l’ultima sera; ma per la sua follia le fu sì presso, che molto poco tempo a volger era.
english: This man had yet to see his final evening; but, through his folly, little time was left before he did—he was so close to it.

italian: Sì com’ io dissi, fui mandato ad esso per lui campare; e non lì era altra via che questa per la quale i’ mi son messo.
english: As I have told you, I was sent to him for his deliverance; the only road I could have taken was the road I took.

italian: Mostrata ho lui tutta la gente ria; e ora intendo mostrar quelli spirti che purgan sé sotto la tua balìa.
english: I showed him all the people of perdition; now I intend to show to him those spirits who, in your care, are bent on expiation.

italian: Com’ io l’ho tratto, saria lungo a dirti; de l’alto scende virtù che m’aiuta conducerlo a vederti e a udirti.
english: To tell you how I led him would take long; it is a power descending from above that helps me guide him here, to see and hear you.

italian: Or ti piaccia gradir la sua venuta: libertà va cercando, ch’è sì cara, come sa chi per lei vita rifiuta.
english: Now may it please you to approve his coming; he goes in search of liberty—so precious, as he who gives his life for it must know.

italian: Tu ’l sai, ché non ti fu per lei amara in Utica la morte, ove lasciasti la vesta ch’al gran dì sarà sì chiara.
english: You know it—who, in Utica, found death for freedom was not bitter, when you left the garb that will be bright on the great day.

italian: Non son li editti etterni per noi guasti, ché questi vive e Minòs me non lega; ma son del cerchio ove son li occhi casti
english: Eternal edicts are not broken for us; this man’s alive, and I’m not bound by Minos; but I am from the circle where the chaste

italian: di Marzia tua, che ’n vista ancor ti priega, o santo petto, che per tua la tegni: per lo suo amore adunque a noi ti piega.
english: eyes of your Marcia are; and she still prays to you, o holy breast, to keep her as your own: for her love, then, incline to us.

italian: Lasciane andar per li tuoi sette regni; grazie riporterò di te a lei, se d’ esser mentovato là giù degni».
english: Allow our journey through your seven realms. I shall thank her for kindness you bestow— if you would let your name be named below.”

italian: «Marzïa piacque tanto a li occhi miei mentre ch’i’ fu’ di là», diss’ elli allora, «che quante grazie volse da me, fei.
english: “While I was there, within the other world, Marcia so pleased my eyes,” he then replied, “each kindness she required, I satisfied.

italian: Or che di là dal mal fiume dimora, più muover non mi può, per quella legge che fatta fu quando me n’usci’ fora.
english: Now that she dwells beyond the evil river, she has no power to move me any longer, such was the law decreed when I was freed.

italian: Ma se donna del ciel ti muove e regge, come tu di’ , non c’è mestier lusinghe: bastisi ben che per lei mi richegge.
english: But if a lady come from Heaven speeds and helps you, as you say, there is no need of flattery; it is enough, indeed,

italian: Va dunque, e fa che tu costui ricinghe d’un giunco schietto e che li lavi ’l viso, sì ch’ogne sucidume quindi stinghe;
english: to ask me for her sake. Go then; but first wind a smooth rush around his waist and bathe his face, to wash away all of Hell’s stains;

italian: ché non si converria, l’occhio sorpriso d’alcuna nebbia, andar dinanzi al primo ministro, ch’è di quei di paradiso.
english: for it would not be seemly to approach with eyes still dimmed by any mists, the first custodian angel, one from Paradise.

italian: Questa isoletta intorno ad imo ad imo, là giù colà dove la batte l’onda, porta di giunchi sovra ’l molle limo;
english: This solitary island, all around its very base, there where the breakers pound, bears rushes on its soft and muddy ground.

italian: null’ altra pianta che facesse fronda o indurasse, vi puote aver vita, però ch’a le percosse non seconda.
english: There is no other plant that lives below: no plant with leaves or plant that, as it grows, hardens—and breaks beneath the waves’ harsh blows.

italian: Poscia non sia di qua vostra reddita; lo sol vi mosterrà, che surge omai, prendere il monte a più lieve salita».
english: That done, do not return by this same pass; the sun, which rises now, will show you how this hillside can be climbed more easily.”

italian: Così sparì; e io sù mi levai sanza parlare, e tutto mi ritrassi al duca mio, e li occhi a lui drizzai.
english: With that he vanished; and without a word, I rose and drew in closer to my guide, and it was on him that I set my eyes.

italian: El cominciò: «Figliuol, segui i miei passi: volgianci in dietro, ché di qua dichina questa pianura a’ suoi termini bassi».
english: And he began: “Son, follow in my steps; let us go back; this is the point at which the plain slopes down to reach its lowest bounds.”

italian: L’alba vinceva l’ora mattutina che fuggia innanzi, sì che di lontano conobbi il tremolar de la marina.
english: Daybreak was vanquishing the dark’s last hour, which fled before it; in the distance, I could recognize the trembling of the sea.

italian: Noi andavam per lo solingo piano com’ om che torna a la perduta strada, che ’nfino ad essa li pare ire in vano.
english: We made our way across the lonely plain, like one returning to a lost pathway, who, till he finds it, seems to move in vain.

italian: Quando noi fummo là ’ve la rugiada pugna col sole, per essere in parte dove, ad orezza, poco si dirada,
english: When we had reached the point where dew contends with sun and, under sea winds, in the shade, wins out because it won’t evaporate,

italian: ambo le mani in su l’erbetta sparte soavemente ’l mio maestro pose: ond’ io, che fui accorto di sua arte,
english: my master gently placed both of his hands— outspread—upon the grass; therefore, aware of what his gesture and intention were,

italian: porsi ver’ lui le guance lacrimose; ivi mi fece tutto discoverto quel color che l’ inferno mi nascose.
english: I reached and offered him my tear—stained cheeks; and on my cheeks, he totally revealed the color that Inferno had concealed.

italian: Venimmo poi in sul lito diserto, che mai non vide navicar sue acque omo, che di tornar sia poscia esperto.
english: Then we arrived at the deserted shore, which never yet had seen its waters coursed by any man who journeyed back again.

italian: Quivi mi cinse sì com’ altrui piacque: oh maraviglia! ché qual elli scelse l’umile pianta, cotal si rinacque
english: There, just as pleased another, he girt me. O wonder! Where he plucked the humble plant that he had chosen, there that plant sprang up

italian: subitamente là onde l’avelse.
english: again, identical, immediately.

italian: Già era ’l sole a l’orizzonte giunto lo cui meridïan cerchio coverchia Ierusalèm col suo più alto punto;
english: By now the sun was crossing the horizon of the meridian whose highest point covers Jerusalem; and from the Ganges,

italian: e la notte, che opposita a lui cerchia, uscia di Gange fuor con le Bilance, che le caggion di man quando soverchia;
english: night, circling opposite the sun, was moving together with the Scales that, when the length of dark defeats the day, desert night’s hands;

italian: sì che le bianche e le vermiglie guance, là dov’ i’ era, de la bella Aurora per troppa etate divenivan rance.
english: so that, above the shore that I had reached, the fair Aurora’s white and scarlet cheeks were, as Aurora aged, becoming orange.

italian: Noi eravam lunghesso mare ancora, come gente che pensa a suo cammino, che va col cuore e col corpo dimora.
english: We still were by the sea, like those who think about the journey they will undertake, who go in heart but in the body stay.

italian: Ed ecco, qual, sorpreso dal mattino, per li grossi vapor Marte rosseggia giù nel ponente sovra ’l suol marino,
english: And just as Mars, when it is overcome by the invading mists of dawn, glows red above the waters’ plain, low in the west,

italian: cotal m’apparve, s’ io ancor lo veggia, un lume per lo mar venir sì ratto, che ’l muover suo nessun volar pareggia.
english: so there appeared to me—and may I see it again—a light that crossed the sea: so swift, there is no flight of bird to equal it.

italian: Dal qual com’ io un poco ebbi ritratto l’occhio per domandar lo duca mio, rividil più lucente e maggior fatto.
english: When, for a moment, I’d withdrawn my eyes that I might ask a question of my guide, I saw that light again, larger, more bright.

italian: Poi d’ogne lato ad esso m’appario un non sapeva che bianco, e di sotto a poco a poco un altro a lui uscìo.
english: Then, to each side of it, I saw a whiteness, though I did not know what that whiteness was; below, another whiteness slowly showed.

italian: Lo mio maestro ancor non facea motto, mentre che i primi bianchi apparver ali; allor che ben conobbe il galeotto,
english: My master did not say a word before the whitenesses first seen appeared as wings; but then, when he had recognized the helmsman,

italian: gridò: «Fa, fa che le ginocchia cali. Ecco l’angel di Dio: piega le mani; omai vedrai di sì fatti officiali.
english: he cried: “Bend, bend your knees: behold the angel of God, and join your hands; from this point on, this is the kind of minister you’ll meet.

italian: Vedi che sdegna li argomenti umani, sì che remo non vuol, né altro velo che l’ali sue, tra liti sì lontani.
english: See how much scorn he has for human means; he’d have no other sail than his own wings and use no oar between such distant shores.

italian: Vedi come l’ha dritte verso ’l cielo, trattando l’aere con l’etterne penne, che non si mutan come mortal pelo».
english: See how he holds his wings, pointing to Heaven, piercing the air with his eternal pinions, which do not change as mortal plumage does.”

italian: Poi, come più e più verso noi venne l’uccel divino, più chiaro appariva: per che l’occhio da presso nol sostenne,
english: Then he—that bird divine—as he drew closer and closer to us, seemed to gain in brightness, so that my eyes could not endure his nearness,

italian: ma chinail giuso; e quei sen venne a riva tanto che l’acqua nulla ne ‘nghiottiva.
english: and I was forced to lower them; and he came on to shore with boat so light, so quick that nowhere did the water swallow it.

italian: Da poppa stava il celestial nocchiero, tal che faria beato pur descripto; e più di cento spirti entro sediero.
english: The helmsman sent from Heaven, at the stern, seemed to have blessedness inscribed upon him; more than a hundred spirits sat within.

italian: ‘In exitu Isräel de Aegypto’ cantavan tutti insieme ad una voce con quanto di quel salmo è poscia scripto.
english: “In exitu Israel de Aegypto,” with what is written after of that psalm, all of those spirits sang as with one voice.

italian: Poi fece il segno lor di santa croce; ond’ ei si gittar tutti in su la piaggia: ed el sen gì, come venne, veloce.
english: Then over them he made the holy cross as sign; they flung themselves down on the shore, and he moved off as he had come—swiftly.

italian: La turba che rimase lì, selvaggia parea del loco, rimirando intorno come colui che nove cose assaggia.
english: The crowd that he had left along the beach seemed not to know the place; they looked about like those whose eyes try out things new to them.

italian: Da tutte parti saettava il giorno lo sol, ch’avea con le saette conte di mezzo ’l ciel cacciato Capricorno,
english: Upon all sides the sun shot forth the day; and from mid—heaven its incisive arrows already had chased Capricorn away,

italian: quando la nova gente alzò la fronte ver’ noi, dicendo a noi: «Se voi sapete, mostratene la via di gire al monte».
english: when those who’d just arrived lifted their heads toward us and said: “Do show us, if you know, the way by which we can ascend this slope.”

italian: E Virgilio rispuose: «Voi credete forse che siamo esperti d’esto loco; ma noi siam peregrin come voi siete.
english: And Virgil answered: “You may be convinced that we are quite familiar with this shore; but we are strangers here, just as you are;

italian: Dianzi venimmo, innanzi a voi un poco, per altra via, che fu sì aspra e forte, che lo salire omai ne parrà gioco».
english: we came but now, a little while before you, though by another path, so difficult and dense that this ascent seems sport to us.”

italian: L’anime, che si fuor di me accorte, per lo spirare, ch’i’ era ancor vivo, maravigliando diventaro smorte.
english: The souls who, noticing my breathing, sensed that I was still a living being, then, out of astonishment, turned pale; and just

italian: E come a messagger che porta ulivo tragge la gente per udir novelle, e di calcar nessun si mostra schivo,
english: as people crowd around a messenger who bears an olive branch, to hear his news, and no one hesitates to join that crush,

italian: così al viso mio s’affisar quelle anime fortunate tutte quante, quasi oblïando d’ire a farsi belle.
english: so here those happy spirits—all of them— stared hard at my face, just as if they had forgotten to proceed to their perfection.

italian: Io vidi una di lor trarresi avante per abbracciarmi con sì grande affetto, che mosse me a far lo somigliante.
english: I saw one of those spirits moving forward in order to embrace me—his affection so great that I was moved to mime his welcome.

italian: Ohi ombre vane, fuor che ne l’aspetto! tre volte dietro a lei le mani avvinsi, e tante mi tornai con esse al petto.
english: O shades—in all except appearance—empty! Three times I clasped my hands behind him and as often brought them back against my chest.

italian: Di maraviglia, credo, mi dipinsi; per che l’ombra sorrise e si ritrasse, e io, seguendo lei, oltre mi pinsi.
english: Dismay, I think, was painted on my face; at this, that shadow smiled as he withdrew; and I, still seeking him, again advanced.

italian: Soavemente disse ch’io posasse; allor conobbi chi era, e pregai che, per parlarmi, un poco s’arrestasse.
english: Gently, he said that I could now stand back; then I knew who he was, and I beseeched him to remain awhile and talk with me.

italian: Rispuosemi: «Così com’ io t’amai nel mortal corpo, così t’amo sciolta: però m’arresto; ma tu perché vai?».
english: He answered: “As I loved you when I was within my mortal flesh, so, freed, I love you: therefore I stay. But you, why do you journey?”

italian: «Casella mio, per tornar altra volta là dov’ io son, fo io questo vïaggio», diss’ io; «ma a te com’ è tanta ora tolta?».
english: “My own Casella, to return again to where I am, I journey thus; but why,” I said, “were you deprived of so much time?”

italian: Ed elli a me: «Nessun m’è fatto oltraggio, se quei che leva quando e cui li piace, più volte m’ ha negato esto passaggio;
english: And he: “No injury is done to me if he who takes up whom—and when—he pleases has kept me from this crossing many times,

italian: ché di giusto voler lo suo si face: veramente da tre mesi elli ha tolto chi ha voluto intrar, con tutta pace.
english: for his own will derives from a just will. And yet, for three months now, he has accepted, most tranquilly, all those who would embark.

italian: Ond’ io, ch’era ora a la marina vòlto dove l’acqua di Tevero s’insala, benignamente fu’ da lui ricolto.
english: Therefore, I, who had turned then to the shore at which the Tiber’s waters mix with salt, was gathered in by his benevolence.

italian: A quella foce ha elli or dritta l’ala, però che sempre quivi si ricoglie qual verso Acheronte non si cala».
english: Straight to that river mouth, he set his wings: that always is the place of gathering for those who do not sink to Acheron.”

italian: E io: «Se nuova legge non ti toglie memoria o uso a l’amoroso canto che mi solea quetar tutte mie doglie,
english: And I: “If there’s no new law that denies you memory or practice of the songs of love that used to quiet all my longings,

italian: di ciò ti piaccia consolare alquanto l’anima mia, che, con la sua persona venendo qui, è affannata tanto!».
english: then may it please you with those songs to solace my soul somewhat; for—having journeyed here together with my body—it is weary.”

italian: ‘ Amor che ne la mente mi ragiona’ cominciò elli allor sì dolcemente, che la dolcezza ancor dentro mi suona.
english: “Love that discourses to me in my mind” he then began to sing—and sang so sweetly that I still hear that sweetness sound in me.

italian: Lo mio maestro e io e quella gente ch’eran con lui parevan sì contenti, come a nessun toccasse altro la mente.
english: My master, I, and all that company around the singer seemed so satisfied, as if no other thing might touch our minds.

italian: Noi eravam tutti fissi e attenti a le sue note; ed ecco il veglio onesto gridando: «Che è ciò, spiriti lenti?
english: We all were motionless and fixed upon the notes, when all at once the grave old man cried out: “What have we here, you laggard spirits?

italian: qual negligenza, quale stare è questo? Correte al monte a spogliarvi lo scoglio ch’esser non lascia a voi Dio manifesto».
english: What negligence, what lingering is this? Quick, to the mountain to cast off the slough that will not let you see God show Himself!”

italian: Come quando, cogliendo biado o loglio, li colombi adunati a la pastura, queti, sanza mostrar l’usato orgoglio,
english: Even as doves, assembled where they feed, quietly gathering their grain or weeds, forgetful of their customary strut,

italian: se cosa appare ond’ elli abbian paura, subitamente lasciano star l’esca, perch’ assaliti son da maggior cura;
english: will, if some thing appears that makes them fear, immediately leave their food behind because they are assailed by greater care;

italian: così vid’ io quella masnada fresca lasciar lo canto, e fuggir ver’ la costa, com’ om che va, né sa dove rïesca;
english: so did I see that new—come company— they left the song behind, turned toward the slope, like those who go and yet do not know where.

italian: né la nostra partita fu men tosta.
english: And we were no less hasty in departure.

italian: Avvegna che la subitana fuga dispergesse color per la campagna, rivolti al monte ove ragion ne fruga,
english: But while their sudden flight was scattering those souls across the plain and toward the mountain where we are racked by rightful punishments,

italian: i’ mi ristrinsi a la fida compagna: e come sare’ io sanza lui corso? chi m’avria tratto su per la montagna?
english: I drew in closer to my true companion. For how could I have run ahead without him? Who could have helped me as I climbed the mountain?

italian: El mi parea da sé stesso rimorso: o dignitosa coscïenza e netta, come t’è picciol fallo amaro morso!
english: He seemed like one who’s stung by self—reproof; o pure and noble conscience, you in whom each petty fault becomes a harsh rebuke!

italian: Quando li piedi suoi lasciar la fretta, che l’onestade ad ogn’ atto dismaga, la mente mia, che prima era ristretta,
english: And when his feet had left off hurrying— for haste denies all acts their dignity— my mind, which was—before—too focused, grew

italian: lo ’ntento rallargò, sì come vaga, e diedi ’l viso mio incontr’ al poggio che ’nverso ’l ciel più alto si dislaga.
english: more curious and widened its attention; I set my vision toward the slope that rises most steeply, up to heaven from the sea.

italian: Lo sol, che dietro fiammeggiava roggio, rotto m’era dinanzi a la figura, ch’avëa in me de’ suoi raggi l’appoggio.
english: Behind my back the sun was flaming red; but there, ahead of me, its light was shattered because its rays were resting on my body.

italian: Io mi volsi dallato con paura d’ essere abbandonato, quand’ io vidi solo dinanzi a me la terra oscura;
english: And when I saw the ground was dark in front of me and me alone, afraid that I had been abandoned, I turned to my side;

italian: e ’l mio conforto: «Perché pur diffidi?», a dir mi cominciò tutto rivolto; «non credi tu me teco e ch’io ti guidi?
english: and he, my only comfort, as he turned around, began: “Why must you still mistrust? Don’t you believe that I am with—and guide—you?

italian: Vespero è già colà dov’ è sepolto lo corpo dentro al quale io facea ombra: Napoli l’ha, e da Brandizio è tolto.
english: The body from within which I cast shadows is buried where it now is evening: taken from Brindisi, it now belongs to Naples.

italian: Ora, se innanzi a me nulla s’aombra, non ti maravigliar più che d’i cieli che l’uno a l’altro raggio non ingombra.

italian: e come ai rivi grandi si convenne, ver’ lo fiume real tanto veloce si ruinò, che nulla la ritenne.

english: and then, as nuptial ring, his gem, knows that.”

english: When dicing’s done and players separate, the loser’s left alone, disconsolate— rehearsing what he’d thrown, he sadly learns;

english: all of the crowd surrounds the one who won— one goes in front, and one tugs at his back, and at his side one asks to be remembered;

italian: el non s’arresta, e questo e quello intende; a cui porge la man, più non fa pressa; e così da la calca si difende.
english: he does not halt but listens to them all; and when he gives them something, they desist; and so he can fend off the pressing throng.

english: There, with his outstretched hands, was Federigo Novello, praying, and the Pisan who made good Marzucco show his fortitude.

english: My Florence, you indeed may be content that this digression would leave you exempt: your people’s strivings spare you this lament.

english: Others have justice in their hearts, and thought is slow to let it fly off from their bow; but your folk keep it ready—on their lips.

english: I am Virgil, and I am deprived of Heaven for no fault other than my lack of faith.” This was the answer given by my guide.

english: what merit or what grace shows you to me? If I deserve to hear your word, then answer: tell me if you’re from Hell and from what cloister.”

english: “Through every circle of the sorry kingdom,” he answered him, “I journeyed here; a power from Heaven moved me, and with that, I come.

italian: Non per far, ma per non fare ho perduto a veder l’alto Sol che tu disiri e che fu tardi per me conosciuto.
english: Not for the having—but not having—done, I lost the sight that you desire, the Sun— that high Sun I was late in recognizing.

italian: Luogo è là giù non tristo di martìri, ma di tenebre solo, ove i lamenti non suonan come guai, ma son sospiri.
english: There is a place below that only shadows— not torments—have assigned to sadness; there, lament is not an outcry, but a sigh.

italian: Quivi sto io coi pargoli innocenti dai denti morsi de la morte avante che fosser da l’umana colpa essenti;
english: There I am with the infant innocents, those whom the teeth of death had seized before they were set free from human sinfulness;

english: “Brother,” he said, “the pages painted by the brush of Franco Bolognese smile more brightly: all the glory now is his;

italian: Ben non sare’ io stato sì cortese mentre ch’io vissi, per lo gran disio de l’eccellenza ove mio core intese.
english: mine, but a part. In truth I would have been less gracious when I lived-so great was that desire for eminence which drove my heart.
