english: For such pride, here one pays the penalty; and I’d not be here yet, had it not been that, while I still could sin, I turned to Him.

italian: Oh vana gloria de l’umane posse! com’ poco verde in su la cima dura, se non è giunta da l’etati grosse!
english: O empty glory of the powers of humans! How briefly green endures upon the peak- unless an age of dullness follows it.

italian: Credette Cimabue ne la pittura tener lo campo, e ora ha Giotto il grido, sì che la fama di colui è scura:
english: In painting Cimabue thought he held the field, and now it’s Giotto they acclaim- the former only keeps a shadowed fame.

italian: così ha tolto l’uno a l’altro Guido la gloria de la lingua; e forse è nato chi l’uno e l’altro caccerà del nido.
english: So did one Guido, from the other, wrest the glory of our tongue-and he perhaps is born who will chase both out of the nest.

italian: Non è il mondan romore altro ch’un fiato di vento, ch’or vien quinci e or vien quindi, e muta nome perché muta lato.
english: Worldly renown is nothing other than a breath of wind that blows now here, now there, and changes name when it has changed its course.

italian: Che voce avrai tu più, se vecchia scindi da te la carne, che se fossi morto anzi che tu lasciassi il ‘pappo’ e ’l ’dindi’ ,
english: Before a thousand years have passed-a span that, for eternity, is less space than an eyeblink for the slowest sphere in heaven-

italian: pria che passin mill’ anni? ch’ è più corto spazio a l’etterno, ch’un muover di ciglia al cerchio che più tardi in cielo è torto.
english: would you find greater glory if you left your flesh when it was old than if your death had come before your infant words were spent?

italian: Colui che del cammin sì poco piglia dinanzi a me, Toscana sonò tutta; e ora a pena in Siena sen pispiglia,
english: All Tuscany acclaimed his name-the man who moves so slowly on the path before me, and now they scarcely whisper of him even

italian: ond’ era sire quando fu distrutta la rabbia fiorentina, che superba fu a quel tempo sì com’ ora è putta.
english: in Siena, where he lorded it when they destroyed the raging mob of Florence-then as arrogant as now it’s prostitute.

italian: La vostra nominanza è color d’erba, che viene e va, e quei la discolora per cui ella esce de la terra acerba».
english: Your glory wears the color of the grass that comes and goes; the sun that makes it wither first drew it from the ground, still green and tender.”

italian: E io a lui: «Tuo vero dir m’incora bona umiltà, e gran tumor m’appiani; ma chi è quei di cui tu parlavi ora?».
english: And I to him: “Your truthful speech has filled my soul with sound humility, abating my overswollen pride; but who is he

italian: «Quelli è», rispuose, «Provenzan Salvani; ed è qui perché fu presuntüoso a recar Siena tutta a le sue mani.
english: of whom you spoke now?” “Provenzan Salvani, he answered, “here because-presumptuously-” he thought his grip could master all Siena.

italian: Ito è così e va, sanza riposo, poi che morì; cotal moneta rende a sodisfar chi è di là troppo oso».
english: So he has gone, and so he goes, with no rest since his death; this is the penalty exacted from those who-there-overreached.”

italian: E io: «Se quello spirito ch’attende, pria che si penta, l’orlo de la vita, qua giù dimora e qua sù non ascende,
english: And I: “But if a spirit who awaits the edge of life before repenting must- unless good prayers help him-stay below

italian: se buona orazïon lui non aita, prima che passi tempo quanto visse, come fu la venuta lui largita?».
english: and not ascend here for as long a time as he had spent alive, do tell me how Salvani’s entry here has been allowed.”

italian: «Quando vivea più glorïoso», disse, «liberamente nel Campo di Siena, ogne vergogna diposta, s’affisse;
english: “When he was living in his greatest glory” said he, “then of his own free will he set aside all shame and took his place upon

italian: e lì, per trar l’amico suo di pena ch’e’ sostenea ne la prigion di Carlo, si condusse a tremar per ogne vena.
english: the Campo of Siena; there, to free his friend from suffering in Charles’s prison, humbling himself, he trembled in each vein.

italian: Più non dirò, e scuro so che parlo; ma poco tempo andrà, che ’ tuoi vicini faranno sì che tu potrai chiosarlo.
english: I say no more; I know I speak obscurely; but soon enough you’ll find your neighbor’s acts are such that what I say can be explained.

italian: Quest’ opera li tolse quei confini».
english: This deed delivered him from those confines.”

italian: Di pari, come buoi che vanno a giogo, m’andava io con quell’ anima carca, fin che ’l sofferse il dolce pedagogo.
english: As oxen, yoked, proceed abreast, so I moved with that burdened soul as long as my kind pedagogue allowed me to; but when

italian: Ma quando disse: «Lascia lui e varca; ché qui è buono con l’ali e coi remi, quantunque può, ciascun pinger sua barca»;
english: he said: “Leave him behind, and go ahead; for here it’s fitting that with wings and oars each urge his boat along with all his force,”

italian: dritto sì come andar vuolsi rife’mi con la persona, avvegna che i pensieri mi rimanessero e chinati e scemi.
english: I drew my body up again, erect— the stance most suitable to man—and yet the thoughts I thought were still submissive, bent.

italian: Io m’era mosso, e seguia volontieri del mio maestro i passi, e amendue già mostravam com’ eravam leggeri;
english: Now I was on my way, and willingly I followed in my teacher’s steps, and we together showed what speed we could command.

italian: ed el mi disse: «Volgi li occhi in giùe: buon ti sarà, per tranquillar la via, veder lo letto de le piante tue».
english: He said to me: “Look downward, for the way will offer you some solace if you pay attention to the pavement at your feet.”

italian: Come, perché di lor memoria sia, sovra i sepolti le tombe terragne portan segnato quel ch’elli eran pria,
english: As, on the lids of pavement tombs, there are stone effigies of what the buried were before, so that the dead may be remembered;

italian: onde lì molte volte si ripiagne per la puntura de la rimembranza, che solo a’ pïi dà de le calcagne;
english: and there, when memory—inciting only the pious—has renewed their mourning, men are often led to shed their tears again;

italian: sì vid’ io lì, ma di miglior sembianza secondo l’artificio, figurato quanto per via di fuor del monte avanza.
english: so did I see, but carved more skillfully, with greater sense of likeness, effigies on all the path protruding from the mountain.

italian: Vedea colui che fu nobil creato più ch’altra creatura, giù dal cielo folgoreggiando scender, da l’un lato.
english: I saw, to one side of the path, one who had been created nobler than all other beings, falling lightning—like from Heaven.

italian: Vedëa Brïareo, fitto dal telo celestïal giacer, da l’altra parte, grave a la terra per lo mortal gelo.
english: I saw, upon the other side, Briareus transfixed by the celestial shaft: he lay, ponderous, on the ground, in fatal cold.

italian: Vedea Timbreo, vedea Pallade e Marte, armati ancora, intorno al padre loro, mirar le membra d’i Giganti sparte.
english: I saw Thymbraeus, I saw Mars and Pallas, still armed, as they surrounded Jove, their father, gazing upon the Giants’ scattered limbs.

italian: Vedea Nembròt a piè del gran lavoro quasi smarrito, e riguardar le genti che ‘n Sennaàr con lui superbi fuoro.
english: I saw bewildered Nimrod at the foot of his great labor; watching him were those of Shinar who had shared his arrogance.

italian: O Nïobè, con che occhi dolenti vedea io te segnata in su la strada, tra sette e sette tuoi figliuoli spenti!
english: O Niobe, what tears afflicted me when, on that path, I saw your effigy among your slaughtered children, seven and seven!

italian: O Saùl, come in su la propria spada quivi parevi morto in Gelboè, che poi non sentì pioggia né rugiada!
english: O Saul, you were portrayed there as one who had died on his own sword, upon Gilboa, which never after knew the rain, the dew!

italian: O folle Aragne, sì vedea io te già mezza ragna, trista in su li stracci de l’opera che mal per te si fé.
english: O mad Arachne, I saw you already half spider, wretched on the ragged remnants of work that you had wrought to your own hurt!

italian: O Roboàm, già non par che minacci quivi ’l tuo segno; ma pien di spavento nel porta un carro, sanza ch’altri il cacci.
english: O Rehoboam, you whose effigy seems not to menace there, and yet you flee by chariot, terrified, though none pursues!

italian: Mostrava ancor lo duro pavimento come Almeon a sua madre fé caro parer lo sventurato addornamento.
english: It also showed-that pavement of hard stone— how much Alcmaeon made his mother pay: the cost of the ill-omened ornament.

italian: Mostrava come i figli si gittaro sovra Sennacherìb dentro dal tempio, e come, morto lui, quivi il lasciaro.
english: It showed the children of Sennacherib as they assailed their father in the temple, then left him, dead, behind them as they fled.

italian: Mostrava la ruina e ’l crudo scempio che fé Tamiri, quando disse a Ciro: «Sangue sitisti, e io di sangue t’empio».
english: It showed the slaughter and the devastation wrought by Tomyris when she taunted Cyrus: “You thirsted after blood; with blood I fill you.”

italian: Mostrava come in rotta si fuggiro li Assiri, poi che fu morto Oloferne, e anche le reliquie del martiro.
english: It showed the rout of the Assyrians, sent reeling after Holofernes’ death, and also showed his body—what was left.

italian: Vedeva Troia in cenere e in caverne; o Ilión, come te basso e vile mostrava il segno che lì si discerne!
english: I saw Troy turned to caverns and to ashes; O Ilium, your effigy in stone— it showed you there so squalid, so cast down!

italian: Qual di pennel fu maestro o di stile che ritraesse l’ombre e ’ tratti ch’ivi mirar farieno uno ingegno sottile?
english: What master of the brush or of the stylus had there portrayed such masses, such outlines as would astonish all discerning minds?

italian: Morti li morti e i vivi parean vivi: non vide mei di me chi vide il vero, quant’ io calcai, fin che chinato givi.
english: The dead seemed dead and the alive, alive: I saw, head bent, treading those effigies, as well as those who’d seen those scenes directly.

italian: Or superbite, e via col viso altero, figliuoli d’Eva, e non chinate il volto sì che veggiate il vostro mal sentero!
english: Now, sons of Eve, persist in arrogance, in haughty stance, do not let your eyes bend, lest you be forced to see your evil path!

italian: Più era già per noi del monte vòlto e del cammin del sole assai più speso che non stimava l’animo non sciolto,
english: We now had circled round more of the mountain and much more of the sun’s course had been crossed than I, my mind absorbed, had gauged, when he

italian: quando colui che sempre innanzi atteso andava, cominciò: «Drizza la testa; non è più tempo di gir sì sospeso.
english: who always looked ahead insistently, as he advanced, began: “Lift up your eyes; it’s time to set these images aside.

italian: Vedi colà un angel che s’appresta per venir verso noi; vedi che torna dal servigio del dì l’ancella sesta.
english: See there an angel hurrying to meet us, and also see the sixth of the handmaidens returning from her service to the day.

italian: Di reverenza il viso e li atti addorna, sì che i diletti lo ’nvïarci in suso; pensa che questo dì mai non raggiorna!».
english: Adorn your face and acts with reverence, that he be pleased to send us higher. Remember— today will never know another dawn.”

italian: Io era ben del suo ammonir uso pur di non perder tempo, sì che ’n quella materia non potea parlarmi chiuso.
english: I was so used to his insistent warnings against the loss of time; concerning that, his words to me could hardly be obscure.

italian: A noi venìa la creatura bella, biancovestito e ne la faccia quale par tremolando mattutina stella.
english: That handsome creature came toward us; his clothes were white, and in his aspect he seemed like the trembling star that rises in the morning.

italian: Le braccia aperse, e indi aperse l’ale; disse: «Venite: qui son presso i gradi, e agevolemente omai si sale.
english: He opened wide his arms, then spread his wings; he said: “Approach: the steps are close at hand; from this point on one can climb easily.

italian: A questo invito vegnon molto radi: o gente umana, per volar sù nata, perché a poco vento così cadi?».
english: This invitation’s answered by so few: o humankind, born for the upward flight, why are you driven back by wind so slight?”

italian: Menocci ove la roccia era tagliata; quivi mi batté l’ali per la fronte; poi mi promise sicura l’andata.
english: He led us to a cleft within the rock, and then he struck my forehead with his wing; that done, he promised me safe journeying.

italian: Come a man destra, per salire al monte dove siede la chiesa che soggioga la ben guidata sopra Rubaconte,

english: the daring slope of the ascent is broken by steps that were constructed in an age when record books and measures could be trusted,

italian: così s’allenta la ripa che cade quivi ben ratta da l’ altro girone; ma quinci e quindi l’alta pietra rade.
english: so was the slope that plummets there so steeply down from the other ring made easier; but on this side and that, high rock encroaches.

english: While we began to move in that direction, “Beati pauperes spiritu” was sung so sweetly—it can not be told in words.

italian: Ahi quanto son diverse quelle foci da l’infernali! ché quivi per canti s’entra, e là giù per lamenti feroci.
english: How different were these entryways from those of Hell! For here it is with song one enters; down there, it is with savage lamentations.

italian: Già montavam su per li scaglion santi, ed esser mi parea troppo più lieve che per lo pian non mi parea davanti.
english: Now we ascended by the sacred stairs, but I seemed to be much more light than I had been, before, along the level terrace.

italian: Ond’ io: «Maestro, dì, qual cosa greve levata s’è da me, che nulla quasi per me fatica, andando, si riceve?».
english: At this I asked: “Master, tell me, what heavy weight has been lifted from me, so that I, in going, notice almost no fatigue?”

italian: Rispuose: «Quando i P che son rimasi ancor nel volto tuo presso che stinti, saranno, com’ è l’un, del tutto rasi,
english: He answered: “When the P’s that still remain upon your brow—now almost all are faint— have been completely, like this P. erased,

italian: fier li tuoi piè dal buon voler sì vinti, che non pur non fatica sentiranno, ma fia diletto loro esser sù pinti».
english: your feet will be so mastered by good will that they not only will not feel travail but will delight when they are urged uphill.”

italian: Allor fec’ io come color che vanno con cosa in capo non da lor saputa, se non che ’ cenni altrui sospecciar fanno;
english: Then I behaved like those who make their way with something on their head of which they’re not aware, till others’ signs make them suspicious,

italian: per che la mano ad accertar s’aiuta, e cerca e truova e quello officio adempie che non si può fornir per la veduta;
english: at which, the hand helps them to ascertain; it seeks and finds and touches and provides the services that sight cannot supply;

italian: e con le dita de la destra scempie trovai pur sei le lettere che ’ncise quel da le chiavi a me sovra le tempie:
english: so, with my right hand’s outspread fingers, I found just six of the letters once inscribed by him who holds the keys, upon my forehead;

italian: a che guardando, il mio duca sorrise.
english: and as he watched me do this, my guide smiled.

italian: ﻿Noi eravamo al sommo de la scala, dove secondamente si risega lo monte che salendo altrui dismala.
english: We now had reached the summit of the stairs where once again the mountain whose ascent delivers man from sin has been indented.

italian: Ivi così una cornice lega dintorno il poggio, come la primaia; se non che l’arco suo più tosto piega.
english: There, just as in the case of the first terrace, a second terrace runs around the slope, except that it describes a sharper arc.

english: No effigy is there and no outline: the bank is visible, the naked path— only the livid color of raw rock.

english: “If we wait here in order to inquire of those who pass,” the poet said, “I fear our choice of path may be delayed too long.”

english: You warm the world and you illumine it; unless a higher Power urge us elsewhere, your rays must always be the guides that lead.”

italian: Quanto di qua per un migliaio si conta, tanto di là eravam noi già iti, con poco tempo, per la voglia pronta;
english: We had already journeyed there as far as we should reckon here to be a mile, and done it in brief time—our will was eager—

italian: e verso noi volar furon sentiti, non però visti, spiriti parlando a la mensa d’amor cortesi inviti.
english: when we heard spirits as they flew toward us, though they could not be seen—spirits pronouncing courteous invitations to love’s table.

italian: La prima voce che passò volando ‘Vinum non habent’ altamente disse, e dietro a noi l’andò reïterando.
english: The first voice that flew by called out aloud: “Vinum non habent,” and behind us that same voice reiterated its example.

italian: E prima che del tutto non si udisse per allungarsi, un’altra ‘I’ sono Oreste’ passò gridando, e anco non s’affisse.
english: And as that voice drew farther off, before it faded finally, another cried: “I am Orestes.” It, too, did not stop.

italian: «Oh!», diss’ io, «padre, che voci son queste?». E com’ io domandai, ecco la terza dicendo: ‘Amate da cui male aveste’.
english: “What voices are these, father?” were my words; and as I asked him this, I heard a third voice say: “Love those by whom you have been hurt.”

italian: E ’l buon maestro: «Questo cinghio sferza la colpa de la invidia, e però sono tratte d’amor le corde de la ferza.
english: And my good master said: “The sin of envy is scourged within this circle; thus, the cords that form the scourging lash are plied by love.

italian: Lo fren vuol esser del contrario suono; credo che l’udirai, per mio avviso, prima che giunghi al passo del perdono.
english: The sounds of punished envy, envy curbed, are different; if I judge right, you’ll hear those sounds before we reach the pass of pardon.

english: But let your eyes be fixed attentively and, through the air, you will see people seated before us, all of them on the stone terrace.”

italian: Allora più che prima li occhi apersi; guarda’mi innanzi, e vidi ombre con manti al color de la pietra non diversi.
english: I opened—wider than before—my eyes; I looked ahead of me, and I saw shades with cloaks that shared their color with the rocks.

italian: E poi che fummo un poco più avanti, udia gridar: ‘Maria, òra per noi’: gridar ‘Michele’ e ‘Pietro’ e ‘Tutti santi’.
english: And once we’d moved a little farther on, I heard the cry of, “Mary, pray for us,” and then heard, “Michael,” “Peter,” and “All saints.”

italian: Non credo che per terra vada ancoi omo sì duro, che non fosse punto per compassion di quel ch’i’ vidi poi;
english: I think no man now walks upon the earth who is so hard that he would not have been pierced by compassion for what I saw next;

italian: ché, quando fui sì presso di lor giunto, che li atti loro a me venivan certi, per li occhi fui di grave dolor munto.
english: for when I had drawn close enough to see clearly the way they paid their penalty, the force of grief pressed tears out of my eyes.

italian: Di vil ciliccio mi parean coperti, e l’un sofferia l’altro con la spalla, e tutti da la ripa eran sofferti.
english: Those souls—it seemed—were cloaked in coarse haircloth; another’s shoulder served each shade as prop, and all of them were bolstered by the rocks:

italian: Così li ciechi a cui la roba falla, stanno a’ perdoni a chieder lor bisogna, e l’uno il capo sopra l’altro avvalla,
english: so do the blind who have to beg appear on pardon days to plead for what they need, each bending his head back and toward the other,

italian: perché ’n altrui pietà tosto si pogna, non pur per lo sonar de le parole, ma per la vista che non meno agogna.
english: that all who watch feel—quickly—pity’s touch not only through the words that would entreat but through the sight, which can—no less—beseech.

italian: E come a li orbi non approda il sole, così a l’ombre quivi, ond’ io parlo ora, luce del ciel di sé largir non vole;
english: And just as, to the blind, no sun appears, so to the shades—of whom I now speak—here, the light of heaven would not give itself;

italian: ché a tutti un fil di ferro i cigli fóra e cusce sì, come a sparvier selvaggio si fa però che queto non dimora.
english: for iron wire pierces and sews up the lids of all those shades, as untamed hawks are handled, lest, too restless, they fly off.

italian: A me pareva, andando, fare oltraggio, veggendo altrui, non essendo veduto: per ch’io mi volsi al mio consiglio saggio.
english: It seemed to me a gross discourtesy for me, going, to see and not be seen; therefore, I turned to my wise counselor.

italian: Ben sapev’ ei che volea dir lo muto; e però non attese mia dimanda, ma disse: «Parla, e sie breve e arguto».
english: He knew quite well what I, though mute, had meant; and thus he did not wait for my request, but said: “Speak, and be brief and to the point.”

italian: Virgilio mi venìa da quella banda de la cornice onde cader si puote, perché da nulla sponda s’inghirlanda;
english: Virgil was to my right, along the outside, nearer the terrace—edge—no parapet was there to keep a man from falling off;

italian: da l’altra parte m’eran le divote ombre, che per l’orribile costura premevan sì, che bagnavan le gote.
english: and to my other side were the devout shades; through their eyes, sewn so atrociously, those spirits forced the tears that bathed their cheeks.

italian: Volsimi a loro e: «O gente sicura», incominciai, «di veder l’alto lume che ’l disio vostro solo ha in sua cura,
english: I turned to them; and “You who can be certain,” I then began, “of seeing that high light which is the only object of your longing,

italian: se tosto grazia resolva le schiume di vostra coscïenza sì che chiaro per essa scenda de la mente il fiume,
english: may, in your conscience, all impurity soon be dissolved by grace, so that the stream of memory flow through it limpidly;

italian: ditemi, ché mi fia grazioso e caro, s’anima è qui tra voi che sia latina; e forse lei sarà buon s’i’ l’apparo».
english: tell me, for I shall welcome such dear words, if any soul among you is Italian; if I know that, then I—perhaps—can help him.”

italian: «O frate mio, ciascuna è cittadina d’una vera città; ma tu vuo’ dire che vivesse in Italia peregrina».
english: “My brother, each of us is citizen of one true city: what you meant to say was ‘one who lived in Italy as pilgrim.'”

italian: Questo mi parve per risposta udire più innanzi alquanto che là dov’ io stava, ond’ io mi feci ancor più là sentire.
english: My hearing placed the point from which this answer had come somewhat ahead of me; therefore, I made myself heard farther on; moving,

italian: Tra l’altre vidi un’ombra ch’aspettava in vista; e se volesse alcun dir ‘Come?’, lo mento a guisa d’orbo in sù levava.
english: I saw one shade among the rest who looked expectant; and if any should ask how— its chin was lifted as a blind man’s is.

italian: «Spirto», diss’ io, «che per salir ti dome, se tu se’ quelli che mi rispondesti, fammiti conto o per luogo o per nome».
english: “Spirit,” I said, “who have subdued yourself that you may climb, if it is you who answered, then let me know you by your place or name.”

italian: «Io fui sanese», rispuose, «e con questi altri rimendo qui la vita ria, lagrimando a colui che sé ne presti.
english: “I was a Sienese,” she answered, “and with others here I mend my wicked life, weeping to Him that He grant us Himself.

italian: Savia non fui, avvegna che Sapìa fossi chiamata, e fui de li altrui danni più lieta assai che di ventura mia.
english: I was not sapient, though I was called Sapia; and I rejoiced far more at others’ hurts than at my own good fortune. And lest you

italian: E perché tu non creda ch’io t’inganni, odi s’i’ fui, com’ io ti dico, folle, già discendendo l’arco d’i miei anni.
english: should think I have deceived you, hear and judge if I was not, as I have told you, mad when my years’ arc had reached its downward part.

italian: Eran li cittadin miei presso a Colle in campo giunti co’ loro avversari, e io pregava Iddio di quel ch’e’ volle.
english: My fellow citizens were close to Colle, where they’d joined battle with their enemies, and I prayed God for that which He had willed.

italian: Rotti fuor quivi e vòlti ne li amari passi di fuga; e veggendo la caccia, letizia presi a tutte altre dispari,
english: There they were routed, beaten; they were reeling along the bitter paths of flight; and seeing that chase, I felt incomparable joy,

italian: tanto ch’io volsi in sù l’ardita faccia, gridando a Dio: “Omai più non ti temo!”, come fé ’l merlo per poca bonaccia.
english: so that I lifted up my daring face and cried to God: ‘Now I fear you no more!’— as did the blackbird after brief fair weather.

italian: Pace volli con Dio in su lo stremo de la mia vita; e ancor non sarebbe lo mio dover per penitenza scemo,
english: I looked for peace with God at my life’s end; the penalty I owe for sin would not be lessened now by penitence had not

italian: se ciò non fosse, ch’a memoria m’ebbe Pier Pettinaio in sue sante orazioni, a cui di me per caritate increbbe.
english: one who was sorrowing for me because of charity in him—Pier Pettinaio— remembered me in his devout petitions.

italian: Ma tu chi se’, che nostre condizioni vai dimandando, e porti li occhi sciolti, sì com’ io credo, e spirando ragioni?».
english: But who are you, who question our condition as you move on, whose eyes—if I judge right— have not been sewn, who uses breath to speak?”

italian: «Li occhi», diss’ io, «mi fieno ancor qui tolti, ma picciol tempo, ché poca è l’offesa fatta per esser con invidia vòlti.
english: “My eyes,” I said, “will be denied me here, but only briefly; the offense of envy was not committed often by their gaze.

italian: Troppa è più la paura ond’ è sospesa l’anima mia del tormento di sotto, che già lo ’ncarco di là giù mi pesa».
english: I fear much more the punishment below; my soul is anxious, in suspense; already I feel the heavy weights of the first terrace.”

italian: Ed ella a me: «Chi t’ha dunque condotto qua sù tra noi, se giù ritornar credi?». E io: «Costui ch’è meco e non fa motto.
english: And she: “Who, then, led you up here among us, if you believe you will return below?” And I: “He who is with me and is silent.

italian: E vivo sono; e però mi richiedi, spirito eletto, se tu vuo’ ch’i’ mova di là per te ancor li mortai piedi».
english: I am alive; and therefore, chosen spirit, if you would have me move my mortal steps on your behalf, beyond, ask me for that.”

italian: «Oh, questa è a udir sì cosa nuova», rispuose, «che gran segno è che Dio t’ami; però col priego tuo talor mi giova.
english: “Oh, this,” she answered, “is so strange a thing to hear: the sign is clear—you have God’s love. Thus, help me sometimes with your prayers. I ask

italian: E cheggioti, per quel che tu più brami, se mai calchi la terra di Toscana, che a’ miei propinqui tu ben mi rinfami.
english: of you, by that which you desire most, if you should ever tread the Tuscan earth, to see my name restored among my kin.

italian: Tu li vedrai tra quella gente vana che spera in Talamone, e perderagli più di speranza ch’a trovar la Diana;
english: You will see them among those vain ones who have put their trust in Talamone (their loss in hope will be more than Diana cost);

italian: ma più vi perderanno li ammiragli».
english: but there the admirals will lose the most.”

italian: ﻿«Chi è costui che ’l nostro monte cerchia prima che morte li abbia dato il volo, e apre li occhi a sua voglia e coverchia?».
english: “Who is this man who, although death has yet to grant him flight, can circle round our mountain, and can, at will, open and shut his eyes?”

italian: «Non so chi sia, ma so ch’e’ non è solo; domandal tu che più li t’avvicini, e dolcemente, sì che parli, acco’lo».
english: “I don’t know who he is, but I do know he’s not alone; you’re closer; question him and greet him gently, so that he replies.”

italian: Così due spirti, l’uno a l’altro chini, ragionavan di me ivi a man dritta; poi fer li visi, per dirmi, supini;
english: So were two spirits, leaning toward each other, discussing me, along my right—hand side; then they bent back their heads to speak to me,

italian: e disse l’uno: «O anima che fitta nel corpo ancora inver’ lo ciel ten vai, per carità ne consola e ne ditta
english: and one began: “O soul who—still enclosed within the body—make your way toward Heaven, may you, through love, console us; tell us who

italian: onde vieni e chi se’; ché tu ne fai tanto maravigliar de la tua grazia, quanto vuol cosa che non fu più mai».
english: you are, from where you come; the grace that you’ve received—a thing that’s never come to pass before—has caused us much astonishment.”

italian: E io: «Per mezza Toscana si spazia un fiumicel che nasce in Falterona, e cento miglia di corso nol sazia.
english: And I: “Through central Tuscany there spreads a little stream first born in Falterona; one hundred miles can’t fill the course it needs.

italian: Di sovr’ esso rech’ io questa persona: dirvi ch’i’ sia, saria parlare indarno, ché ’l nome mio ancor molto non suona».
english: I bring this body from that river’s banks; to tell you who I am would be to speak in vain—my name has not yet gained much fame.”

italian: «Se ben lo ’ntendimento tuo accarno con lo ’ntelletto», allora mi rispuose quei che diceva pria, «tu parli d’Arno».
english: “If, with my understanding, I have seized your meaning properly,” replied to me the one who’d spoken first, “you mean the Arno.”

italian: E l’altro disse lui: «Perché nascose questi il vocabol di quella riviera, pur com’ om fa de l’orribili cose?».
english: The other said to him: “Why did he hide that river’s name, even as one would do in hiding something horrible from view?”

italian: E l’ombra che di ciò domandata era, si sdebitò così: «Non so; ma degno ben è che ’l nome di tal valle pèra;
english: The shade to whom this question was addressed repaid with this: “I do not know; but it is right for such a valley’s name to perish,

italian: ché dal principio suo, ov’ è sì pregno l’alpestro monte ond’ è tronco Peloro, che ’n pochi luoghi passa oltra quel segno,
english: for from its source (at which the rugged chain— from which Pelorus was cut off—surpasses most other places with its mass of mountains)

italian: infin là ’ve si rende per ristoro di quel che ’l ciel de la marina asciuga, ond’ hanno i fiumi ciò che va con loro,
english: until its end point (where it offers back those waters that evaporating skies drew from the sea, that streams may be supplied),

italian: vertù così per nimica si fuga da tutti come biscia, o per sventura del luogo, o per mal uso che li fruga:
english: virtue is seen as serpent, and all flee from it as if it were an enemy, either because the site is ill—starred or

italian: ond’ hanno sì mutata lor natura li abitator de la misera valle, che par che Circe li avesse in pastura.
english: their evil custom goads them so; therefore, the nature of that squalid valley’s people has changed, as if they were in Circe’s pasture.

italian: Tra brutti porci, più degni di galle che d’altro cibo fatto in uman uso, dirizza prima il suo povero calle.
english: That river starts its miserable course among foul hogs, more fit for acorns than for food devised to serve the needs of man.

italian: Botoli trova poi, venendo giuso, ringhiosi più che non chiede lor possa, e da lor disdegnosa torce il muso.
english: Then, as that stream descends, it comes on curs that, though their force is feeble, snap and snarl; scornful of them, it swerves its snout away.

italian: Vassi caggendo; e quant’ ella più ’ngrossa, tanto più trova di can farsi lupi la maladetta e sventurata fossa.
english: And, downward, it flows on; and when that ditch, ill-fated and accursed, grows wider, it finds, more and more, the dogs becoming wolves.

italian: Discesa poi per più pelaghi cupi, trova le volpi sì piene di froda, che non temono ingegno che le occùpi.
english: Descending then through many dark ravines, it comes on foxes so full of deceit— there is no trap that they cannot defeat.

italian: Né lascerò di dir perch’ altri m’oda; e buon sarà costui, s’ancor s’ammenta di ciò che vero spirto mi disnoda.
english: Nor will I keep from speech because my comrade hears me (and it will serve you, too, to keep in mind what prophecy reveals to me).

italian: Io veggio tuo nepote che diventa cacciator di quei lupi in su la riva del fiero fiume, e tutti li sgomenta.
english: I see your grandson: he’s become a hunter of wolves along the banks of the fierce river, and he strikes every one of them with terror.

italian: Vende la carne loro essendo viva; poscia li ancide come antica belva; molti di vita e sé di pregio priva.
english: He sells their flesh while they are still alive; then, like an ancient beast, he turns to slaughter, depriving many of life, himself of honor.

italian: Sanguinoso esce de la trista selva; lasciala tal, che di qui a mille anni ne lo stato primaio non si rinselva».
english: Bloody, he comes out from the wood he’s plundered, leaving it such that in a thousand years it will not be the forest that it was.”

italian: Com’ a l’annunzio di dogliosi danni si turba il viso di colui ch’ascolta, da qual che parte il periglio l’assanni,
english: Just as the face of one who has heard word of pain and injury becomes perturbed, no matter from what side that menace stirs,

italian: così vid’ io l’altr’ anima, che volta stava a udir, turbarsi e farsi trista, poi ch’ebbe la parola a sé raccolta.
english: so did I see that other soul, who’d turned to listen, growing anxious and dejected when he had taken in his comrade’s words.

italian: Lo dir de l’una e de l’altra la vista mi fer voglioso di saper lor nomi, e dimanda ne fei con prieghi mista;
english: The speech of one, the aspect of the other had made me need to know their names, and I both queried and beseeched at the same time,

italian: per che lo spirto che di pria parlòmi ricominciò: «Tu vuo’ ch’io mi deduca nel fare a te ciò che tu far non vuo’mi.
english: at which the spirit who had spoken first to me began again: “You’d have me do for you that which, to me, you have refused.

italian: Ma da che Dio in te vuol che traluca tanto sua grazia, non ti sarò scarso; però sappi ch’io fui Guido del Duca.
english: But since God would, in you, have His grace glow so brightly, I shall not be miserly; know, therefore, that I was Guido del Duca.

italian: Fu il sangue mio d’invidia sì rïarso, che se veduto avesse uom farsi lieto, visto m’avresti di livore sparso.
english: My blood was so afire with envy that, when I had seen a man becoming happy, the lividness in me was plain to see.

italian: Di mia semente cotal paglia mieto; o gente umana, perché poni ’l core là ’v’ è mestier di consorte divieto?
english: From what I’ve sown, this is the straw I reap: o humankind, why do you set your hearts there where our sharing cannot have a part?

italian: Questi è Rinier; questi è ’l pregio e l’onore de la casa da Calboli, ove nullo fatto s’è reda poi del suo valore.
english: This is Rinieri, this is he—the glory, the honor of the house of Calboli; but no one has inherited his worth.

italian: E non pur lo suo sangue è fatto brullo, tra ’l Po e ’l monte e la marina e ’l Reno, del ben richesto al vero e al trastullo;
english: It’s not his kin alone, between the Po and mountains, and the Reno and the coast, who’ve lost the truth’s grave good and lost the good

italian: ché dentro a questi termini è ripieno di venenosi sterpi, sì che tardi per coltivare omai verrebber meno.
english: of gentle living, too; those lands are full of poisoned stumps; by now, however much one were to cultivate, it is too late.

italian: Ov’ è ’l buon Lizio e Arrigo Mainardi? Pier Traversaro e Guido di Carpigna? Oh Romagnuoli tornati in bastardi!
english: Where is good Lizio? Arrigo Mainardi? Pier Traversaro? Guido di Carpigna? O Romagnoles returned to bastardy!

italian: Quando in Bologna un Fabbro si ralligna? quando in Faenza un Bernardin di Fosco, verga gentil di picciola gramigna?
english: When will a Fabbro flourish in Bologna? When, in Faenza, a Bernadin di Fosco, the noble offshoot of a humble plant?

italian: Non ti maravigliar s’io piango, Tosco, quando rimembro, con Guido da Prata, Ugolin d’Azzo che vivette nosco,
english: Don’t wonder, Tuscan, if I weep when I remember Ugolino d’Azzo, one who lived among us, and Guido da Prata,

italian: Federigo Tignoso e sua brigata, la casa Traversara e li Anastagi (e l’una gente e l’altra è diretata),
english: the house of Traversara, of Anastagi (both houses without heirs), and Federigo Tignoso and his gracious company,

italian: le donne e ’ cavalier, li affanni e li agi che ne ’nvogliava amore e cortesia là dove i cuor son fatti sì malvagi.
english: the ladies and the knights, labors and leisure to which we once were urged by courtesy and love, where hearts now host perversity.

italian: O Bretinoro, ché non fuggi via, poi che gita se n’è la tua famiglia e molta gente per non esser ria?
english: O Bretinoro, why do you not flee— when you’ve already lost your family and many men who’ve fled iniquity?

italian: Ben fa Bagnacaval, che non rifiglia; e mal fa Castrocaro, e peggio Conio, che di figliar tai conti più s’impiglia.
english: Bagnacaval does well: it breeds no more— and Castrocuro ill, and Conio worse, for it insists on breeding counts so cursed.

italian: Ben faranno i Pagan, da che ’l demonio lor sen girà; ma non però che puro già mai rimagna d’essi testimonio.
english: Once freed of their own demon, the Pagani will do quite well, but not so well that any will testify that they are pure and worthy.

italian: O Ugolin de’ Fantolin, sicuro è ’l nome tuo, da che più non s’aspetta chi far lo possa, tralignando, scuro.
english: Your name, o Ugolin de’ Fantolini, is safe, since one no longer waits for heirs to blacken it with their degeneracy.

italian: Ma va via, Tosco, omai; ch’or mi diletta troppo di pianger più che di parlare, sì m’ha nostra ragion la mente stretta».
english: But, Tuscan, go your way; I am more pleased to weep now than to speak: for that which we have spoken presses heavily on me!”

italian: Noi sapavam che quell’ anime care ci sentivano andar; però, tacendo, facëan noi del cammin confidare.
english: We knew those gentle souls had heard us move away; therefore, their silence made us feel more confident about the path we took.

italian: Poi fummo fatti soli procedendo, folgore parve quando l’aere fende, voce che giunse di contra dicendo:
english: When we, who’d gone ahead, were left alone, a voice that seemed like lightning as it splits the air encountered us, a voice that said:

italian: ‘Anciderammi qualunque m’apprende’; e fuggì come tuon che si dilegua, se sùbito la nuvola scoscende.
english: “Whoever captures me will slaughter me”; and then it fled like thunder when it fades after the cloud is suddenly ripped through.

italian: Come da lei l’udir nostro ebbe triegua, ed ecco l’altra con sì gran fracasso, che somigliò tonar che tosto segua:
english: As soon as that first voice had granted us a truce, another voice cried out with such uproar—like thunder quick to follow thunder:

italian: «Io sono Aglauro che divenni sasso»; e allor, per ristrignermi al poeta, in destro feci, e non innanzi, il passo.
english: “I am Aglauros, who was turned to stone”; and then, to draw more near the poet, I moved to my right instead of moving forward.

italian: Già era l’aura d’ogne parte queta; ed el mi disse: «Quel fu ’l duro camo che dovria l’uom tener dentro a sua meta.
english: By now the air on every side was quiet; and he told me: “That is the sturdy bit that should hold every man within his limits.

italian: Ma voi prendete l’esca, sì che l’amo de l’antico avversaro a sé vi tira; e però poco val freno o richiamo.
english: But you would take the bait, so that the hook of the old adversary draws you to him; thus, neither spur nor curb can serve to save you.

italian: Chiamavi ’l cielo e ’ntorno vi si gira, mostrandovi le sue bellezze etterne, e l’occhio vostro pur a terra mira;
english: Heaven would call—and it encircles—you; it lets you see its never—ending beauties; and yet your eyes would only see the ground;

italian: onde vi batte chi tutto discerne».
english: thus, He who sees all things would strike you down.”

italian: ﻿Quanto tra l’ultimar de l’ora terza e ’l principio del dì par de la spera che sempre a guisa di fanciullo scherza,
english: As many as the hours in which the sphere that’s always playing like a child appears from daybreak to the end of the third hour,

italian: tanto pareva già inver’ la sera essere al sol del suo corso rimaso; vespero là, e qui mezza notte era.
english: so many were the hours of light still left before the course of day had reached sunset; vespers was there; and where we are, midnight.

italian: E i raggi ne ferien per mezzo ’l naso, perché per noi girato era sì ’l monte, che già dritti andavamo inver’ l’occaso,
english: When sunlight struck directly at our faces, for we had circled so much of the mountain that now we headed straight into the west,

italian: quand’ io senti’ a me gravar la fronte a lo splendore assai più che di prima, e stupor m’eran le cose non conte;
english: then I could feel my vision overcome by radiance greater than I’d sensed before, and unaccounted things left me amazed;

italian: ond’ io levai le mani inver’ la cima de le mie ciglia, e fecimi ’l solecchio, che del soverchio visibile lima.
english: at which, that they might serve me as a shade, I lifted up my hands above my brow, to limit some of that excessive splendor.

italian: Come quando da l’acqua o da lo specchio salta lo raggio a l’opposita parte, salendo su per lo modo parecchio
english: As when a ray of light, from water or a mirror, leaps in the opposed direction and rises at an angle equal to

italian: a quel che scende, e tanto si diparte dal cader de la pietra in igual tratta, sì come mostra esperïenza e arte;
english: its angle of descent, and to each side the distance from the vertical is equal, as science and experiment have shown;

italian: così mi parve da luce rifratta quivi dinanzi a me esser percosso; per che a fuggir la mia vista fu ratta.
english: so did it seem to me that I had been struck there by light reflected, facing me, at which my eyes turned elsewhere rapidly.

italian: «Che è quel, dolce padre, a che non posso schermar lo viso tanto che mi vaglia», diss’ io, «e pare inver’ noi esser mosso?».
english: “Kind father, what is that against which I have tried in vain,” I said, “to screen my eyes? It seems to move toward us.” And he replied:

italian: «Non ti maravigliar s’ancor t’abbaglia la famiglia del cielo», a me rispuose: «messo è che viene ad invitar ch’om saglia.
english: “Don’t wonder if you are still dazzled by the family of Heaven: a messenger has come, and he invites us to ascend.

italian: Tosto sarà ch’a veder queste cose non ti fia grave, ma fieti diletto quanto natura a sentir ti dispuose».
english: Soon, in the sight of such things, there will be no difficulty for you, but delight— as much as nature fashioned you to feel.”

italian: Poi giunti fummo a l’angel benedetto, con lieta voce disse: «Intrate quinci ad un scaleo vie men che li altri eretto».
english: No sooner had we reached the blessed angel than with glad voice he told us: “Enter here; these are less steep than were the other stairs.”

italian: Noi montavam, già partiti di linci, e ‘Beati misericordes!’ fue cantato retro, e ‘Godi tu che vinci!’.
english: We climbed, already past that point; behind us, we heard “Beati misericordes” sung and then “Rejoice, you who have overcome.”

italian: Lo mio maestro e io soli amendue suso andavamo; e io pensai, andando, prode acquistar ne le parole sue;
english: I and my master journeyed on alone, we two together, upward; as we walked, I thought I’d gather profit from his words;

italian: e dirizza’mi a lui sì dimandando: «Che volse dir lo spirto di Romagna, e ‘divieto’ e ‘consorte’ menzionando?».
english: and even as I turned toward him, I asked: “What did the spirit of Romagna mean when he said, ‘Sharing cannot have a part’?”

italian: Per ch’elli a me: «Di sua maggior magagna conosce il danno; e però non s’ammiri se ne riprende perché men si piagna.
english: And his reply: “He knows the harm that lies in his worst vice; if he chastises it, to ease its expiation—do not wonder.

italian: Perché s’appuntano i vostri disiri dove per compagnia parte si scema, invidia move il mantaco a’ sospiri.
english: For when your longings center on things such that sharing them apportions less to each, then envy stirs the bellows of your sighs.

italian: Ma se l’amor de la spera supprema torcesse in suso il disiderio vostro, non vi sarebbe al petto quella tema;
english: But if the love within the Highest Sphere should turn your longings heavenward, the fear inhabiting your breast would disappear;

italian: ché, per quanti si dice più lì ‘nostro’, tanto possiede più di ben ciascuno, e più di caritate arde in quel chiostro».
english: for there, the more there are who would say ‘ours,’ so much the greater is the good possessed by each—so much more love burns in that cloister.”

italian: «Io son d’esser contento più digiuno», diss’ io, «che se mi fosse pria taciuto, e più di dubbio ne la mente aduno.
english: “I am more hungry now for satisfaction” I said, “than if I’d held my tongue before; I host a deeper doubt within my mind.

italian: Com’ esser puote ch’un ben, distributo in più posseditor, faccia più ricchi di sé che se da pochi è posseduto?».
english: How can a good that’s shared by more possessors enable each to be more rich in it than if that good had been possessed by few?”

italian: Ed elli a me: «Però che tu rificchi la mente pur a le cose terrene, di vera luce tenebre dispicchi.
english: And he to me: “But if you still persist in letting your mind fix on earthly things, then even from true light you gather darkness.

italian: Quello infinito e ineffabil bene che là sù è, così corre ad amore com’ a lucido corpo raggio vene.
english: That Good, ineffable and infinite, which is above, directs Itself toward love as light directs itself to polished bodies.

italian: Tanto si dà quanto trova d’ardore; sì che, quantunque carità si stende, cresce sovr’ essa l’etterno valore.
english: Where ardor is, that Good gives of Itself; and where more love is, there that Good confers a greater measure of eternal worth.

italian: E quanta gente più là sù s’intende, più v’è da bene amare, e più vi s’ama, e come specchio l’uno a l’altro rende.
english: And when there are more souls above who love, there’s more to love well there, and they love more, and, mirror—like, each soul reflects the other.

italian: E se la mia ragion non ti disfama, vedrai Beatrice, ed ella pienamente ti torrà questa e ciascun’ altra brama.
english: And if my speech has not appeased your hunger, you will see Beatrice—she will fulfill this and all other longings that you feel.

italian: Procaccia pur che tosto sieno spente, come son già le due, le cinque piaghe, che si richiudon per esser dolente».
english: Now only strive, so that the other five wounds may be canceled quickly, as the two already are—the wounds contrition heals.”

italian: Com’ io voleva dicer ‘Tu m’appaghe’, vidimi giunto in su l’altro girone, sì che tacer mi fer le luci vaghe.
english: But wanting then to say, “You have appeased me,” I saw that I had reached another circle, and my desiring eyes made me keep still.

italian: Ivi mi parve in una visïone estatica di sùbito esser tratto, e vedere in un tempio più persone;
english: There I seemed, suddenly, to be caught up in an ecstatic vision and to see some people in a temple; and a woman

italian: e una donna, in su l’entrar, con atto dolce di madre dicer: «Figliuol mio, perché hai tu così verso noi fatto?
english: just at the threshold, in the gentle manner that mothers use, was saying: “O my son, why have you done this to us? You can see

italian: Ecco, dolenti, lo tuo padre e io ti cercavamo». E come qui si tacque, ciò che pareva prima, dispario.
english: how we have sought you—sorrowing, your father and I.” And at this point, as she fell still, what had appeared at first now disappeared.

italian: Indi m’apparve un’altra con quell’ acque giù per le gote che ’l dolor distilla quando di gran dispetto in altrui nacque,
english: Then there appeared to me another woman: upon her cheeks—the tears that grief distills when it is born of much scorn for another.

italian: e dir: «Se tu se’ sire de la villa del cui nome ne’ dèi fu tanta lite, e onde ogne scïenza disfavilla,
english: She said: “If you are ruler of that city to name which even goddesses once vied— where every science had its source of light—

italian: vendica te di quelle braccia ardite ch’abbracciar nostra figlia, o Pisistràto». E ’l segnor mi parea, benigno e mite,
english: revenge yourself on the presumptuous arms that embraced our daughter, o Pisistratus.” And her lord seemed to me benign and mild,

italian: risponder lei con viso temperato: «Che farem noi a chi mal ne disira, se quei che ci ama è per noi condannato?»,
english: his aspect temperate, as he replied: “What shall we do to one who’d injure us if one who loves us earns our condemnation?”

italian: Poi vidi genti accese in foco d’ira con pietre un giovinetto ancider, forte gridando a sé pur: «Martira, martira!».
english: Next I saw people whom the fire of wrath had kindled, as they stoned a youth and kept on shouting loudly to each other: “Kill!”

italian: E lui vedea chinarsi, per la morte che l’aggravava già, inver’ la terra, ma de li occhi facea sempre al ciel porte,
english: “Kill!” “Kill!” I saw him now, weighed down by death, sink to the ground, although his eyes were bent always on Heaven—they were Heaven’s gates—

italian: orando a l’alto Sire, in tanta guerra, che perdonasse a’ suoi persecutori, con quello aspetto che pietà diserra.
english: praying to his high Lord, despite the torture, to pardon those who were his persecutors; his look was such that it unlocked compassion.

italian: Quando l’anima mia tornò di fori a le cose che son fuor di lei vere, io riconobbi i miei non falsi errori.
english: And when my soul returned outside itself and met the things outside it that are real, I then could recognize my not false errors.

italian: Lo duca mio, che mi potea vedere far sì com’ om che dal sonno si slega, disse: «Che hai che non ti puoi tenere,
english: My guide, on seeing me behave as if I were a man who’s freed himself from sleep, said: “What is wrong with you? You can’t walk straight;

italian: ma se’ venuto più che mezza lega velando li occhi e con le gambe avvolte, a guisa di cui vino o sonno piega?».
english: for more than half a league now you have moved with clouded eyes and lurching legs, as if you were a man whom wine or sleep has gripped!”

italian: «O dolce padre mio, se tu m’ascolte, io ti dirò», diss’ io, «ciò che m’apparve quando le gambe mi furon sì tolte».
english: “Oh, my kind father, if you hear me out, I’ll tell you what appeared to me,” I said, “when I had lost the right use of my legs.”

italian: Ed ei: «Se tu avessi cento larve sovra la faccia, non mi sarian chiuse le tue cogitazion, quantunque parve.
english: And he: “Although you had a hundred masks upon your face, that still would not conceal from me the thoughts you thought, however slight.

italian: Ciò che vedesti fu perché non scuse d’aprir lo core a l’acque de la pace che da l’etterno fonte son diffuse.
english: What you have seen was shown lest you refuse to open up your heart unto the waters of peace that pour from the eternal fountain.

italian: Non dimandai “Che hai?” per quel che face chi guarda pur con l’occhio che non vede, quando disanimato il corpo giace;
english: I did not ask ‘What’s wrong with you?’ as one who only sees with earthly eyes, which—once the body, stripped of soul, lies dead—can’t see;

italian: ma dimandai per darti forza al piede: così frugar conviensi i pigri, lenti ad usar lor vigilia quando riede».
english: I asked so that your feet might find more force: so must one urge the indolent, too slow to use their waking time when it returns.”

italian: Noi andavam per lo vespero, attenti oltre quanto potean li occhi allungarsi contra i raggi serotini e lucenti.
english: We made our way until the end of vespers, peering, as far ahead as sight could stretch, at rays of light that, although late, were bright.

italian: Ed ecco a poco a poco un fummo farsi verso di noi come la notte oscuro; né da quello era loco da cansarsi.
english: But, gradually, smoke as black as night began to overtake us; and there was no place where we could have avoided it.

italian: Questo ne tolse li occhi e l’aere puro.
english: This smoke deprived us of pure air and sight.

italian: ﻿Buio d’inferno e di notte privata d’ogne pianeto, sotto pover cielo, quant’ esser può di nuvol tenebrata,
english: Darkness of Hell and of a night deprived of every planet, under meager skies, as overcast by clouds as sky can be,

italian: non fece al viso mio sì grosso velo come quel fummo ch’ivi ci coperse, né a sentir di così aspro pelo,
english: had never served to veil my eyes so thickly nor covered them with such rough—textured stuff as smoke that wrapped us there in Purgatory;

italian: che l’occhio stare aperto non sofferse; onde la scorta mia saputa e fida mi s’accostò e l’omero m’offerse.
english: my eyes could not endure remaining open; so that my faithful, knowledgeable escort drew closer as he offered me his shoulder.

italian: Sì come cieco va dietro a sua guida per non smarrirsi e per non dar di cozzo in cosa che ’l molesti, o forse ancida,
english: Just as a blind man moves behind his guide, that he not stray or strike against some thing that may do damage to—or even kill—him,

italian: m’andava io per l’aere amaro e sozzo, ascoltando il mio duca che diceva pur: «Guarda che da me tu non sia mozzo».
english: so I moved through the bitter, filthy air, while listening to my guide, who kept repeating: “Take care that you are not cut off from me.”

italian: Io sentia voci, e ciascuna pareva pregar per pace e per misericordia l’Agnel di Dio che le peccata leva.
english: But I heard voices, and each seemed to pray unto the Lamb of God, who takes away our sins, for peace and mercy. “Agnus Dei”

italian: Pur ‘Agnus Dei’ eran le loro essordia; una parola in tutte era e un modo, sì che parea tra esse ogne concordia.
english: was sung repeatedly as their exordium, words sung in such a way—in unison— that fullest concord seemed to be among them.

italian: «Quei sono spirti, maestro, ch’i’ odo?», diss’ io. Ed elli a me: «Tu vero apprendi, e d’iracundia van solvendo il nodo».
english: “Master, are those whom I hear, spirits?” I asked him. “You have grasped rightly,” he replied, “and as they go they loose the knot of anger.”

italian: «Or tu chi se’ che ’l nostro fummo fendi, e di noi parli pur come se tue partissi ancor lo tempo per calendi?».
english: “Then who are you whose body pierces through our smoke, who speak of us exactly like a man who uses months to measure time?”

italian: Così per una voce detto fue; onde ’l maestro mio disse: «Rispondi, e domanda se quinci si va sùe».
english: A voice said this. On hearing it, my master turned round to me: “Reply to him, then ask if this way leads us to the upward path.”

italian: E io: «O creatura che ti mondi per tornar bella a colui che ti fece, maraviglia udirai, se mi secondi».
english: And I: “O creature who—that you return fair unto Him who made you—cleanse yourself, you shall hear wonders if you follow me.”

italian: «Io ti seguiterò quanto mi lece», rispuose; «e se veder fummo non lascia, l’udir ci terrà giunti in quella vece».
english: “I’ll follow you as far as I’m allowed,” he answered, “and if smoke won’t let us see, hearing will serve instead to keep us linked.”

italian: Allora incominciai: «Con quella fascia che la morte dissolve men vo suso, e venni qui per l’infernale ambascia.
english: Then I began: “With those same swaddling—bands that death unwinds I take my upward path: I have come here by way of Hell’s exactions;

italian: E se Dio m’ha in sua grazia rinchiuso, tanto che vuol ch’i’ veggia la sua corte per modo tutto fuor del moderno uso,
english: since God’s so gathered me into His grace that He would have me, in a manner most unusual for moderns, see His court,

italian: non mi celar chi fosti anzi la morte, ma dilmi, e dimmi s’i’ vo bene al varco; e tue parole fier le nostre scorte».
english: do not conceal from me who you once were, before your death, and tell me if I go straight to the pass; your words will be our escort.”

italian: «Lombardo fui, e fu’ chiamato Marco; del mondo seppi, e quel valore amai al quale ha or ciascun disteso l’arco.
english: “I was a Lombard and I was called Marco; I knew the world’s ways, and I loved those goods for which the bows of all men now grow slack.

italian: Per montar sù dirittamente vai». Così rispuose, e soggiunse: «I’ ti prego che per me prieghi quando sù sarai».
english: The way you’ve taken leads directly upward.” So he replied, and then he added: “I pray you to pray for me when you’re above.”

italian: E io a lui: «Per fede mi ti lego di far ciò che mi chiedi; ma io scoppio dentro ad un dubbio, s’io non me ne spiego.
english: And I to him: “I pledge my faith to you to do what you have asked; and yet a doubt will burst in me if it finds no way out.

italian: Prima era scempio, e ora è fatto doppio ne la sentenza tua, che mi fa certo qui, e altrove, quello ov’ io l’accoppio.
english: Before, my doubt was simple; but your statement has doubled it and made me sure that I am right to couple your words with another’s.

italian: Lo mondo è ben così tutto diserto d’ogne virtute, come tu mi sone, e di malizia gravido e coverto;
english: The world indeed has been stripped utterly of every virtue; as you said to me, it cloaks-and is cloaked by—perversity.

italian: ma priego che m’addite la cagione, sì ch’i’ la veggia e ch’i’ la mostri altrui; ché nel cielo uno, e un qua giù la pone».
english: Some place the cause in heaven, some, below; but I beseech you to define the cause, that, seeing it, I may show it to others.”

italian: Alto sospir, che duolo strinse in «uhi!», mise fuor prima; e poi cominciò: «Frate, lo mondo è cieco, e tu vien ben da lui.
english: A sigh, from which his sorrow formed an “Oh,” was his beginning; then he answered: “Brother, the world is blind, and you come from the world.

italian: Voi che vivete ogne cagion recate pur suso al cielo, pur come se tutto movesse seco di necessitate.
english: You living ones continue to assign to heaven every cause, as if it were the necessary source of every motion.

italian: Se così fosse, in voi fora distrutto libero arbitrio, e non fora giustizia per ben letizia, e per male aver lutto.
english: If this were so, then your free will would be destroyed, and there would be no equity in joy for doing good, in grief for evil.

italian: Lo cielo i vostri movimenti inizia; non dico tutti, ma, posto ch’i’ ’l dica, lume v’è dato a bene e a malizia,
english: The heavens set your appetites in motion— not all your appetites, but even if that were the case, you have received both light

italian: e libero voler; che, se fatica ne le prime battaglie col ciel dura, poi vince tutto, se ben si notrica.
english: on good and evil, and free will, which though it struggle in its first wars with the heavens, then conquers all, if it has been well nurtured.

italian: A maggior forza e a miglior natura liberi soggiacete; e quella cria la mente in voi, che ’l ciel non ha in sua cura.
english: On greater power and a better nature you, who are free, depend; that Force engenders the mind in you, outside the heavens’ sway.

italian: Però, se ’l mondo presente disvia, in voi è la cagione, in voi si cheggia; e io te ne sarò or vera spia.
english: Thus, if the present world has gone astray, in you is the cause, in you it’s to be sought; and now I’ll serve as your true exegete.

italian: Esce di mano a lui che la vagheggia prima che sia, a guisa di fanciulla che piangendo e ridendo pargoleggia,
english: Issuing from His hands, the soul—on which He thought with love before creating it— is like a child who weeps and laughs in sport;

italian: l’anima semplicetta che sa nulla, salvo che, mossa da lieto fattore, volontier torna a ciò che la trastulla.
english: that soul is simple, unaware; but since a joyful Maker gave it motion, it turns willingly to things that bring delight.

italian: Di picciol bene in pria sente sapore; quivi s’inganna, e dietro ad esso corre, se guida o fren non torce suo amore.
english: At first it savors trivial goods; these would beguile the soul, and it runs after them, unless there’s guide or rein to rule its love.

italian: Onde convenne legge per fren porre; convenne rege aver, che discernesse de la vera cittade almen la torre.
english: Therefore, one needed law to serve as curb; a ruler, too, was needed, one who could discern at least the tower of the true city.

italian: Le leggi son, ma chi pon mano ad esse? Nullo, però che ’l pastor che procede, rugumar può, ma non ha l’unghie fesse;
english: The laws exist, but who applies them now? No one—the shepherd who precedes his flock can chew the cud but does not have cleft hooves;

italian: per che la gente, che sua guida vede pur a quel ben fedire ond’ ella è ghiotta, di quel si pasce, e più oltre non chiede.
english: and thus the people, who can see their guide snatch only at that good for which they feel some greed, would feed on that and seek no further.

italian: Ben puoi veder che la mala condotta è la cagion che ’l mondo ha fatto reo, e non natura che ’n voi sia corrotta.
english: Misrule, you see, has caused the world to be malevolent; the cause is clearly not celestial forces—they do not corrupt.

italian: Soleva Roma, che ’l buon mondo feo, due soli aver, che l’una e l’altra strada facean vedere, e del mondo e di Deo.
english: For Rome, which made the world good, used to have two suns; and they made visible two paths— the world’s path and the pathway that is God’s.

italian: L’un l’altro ha spento; ed è giunta la spada col pasturale, e l’un con l’altro insieme per viva forza mal convien che vada;
english: Each has eclipsed the other; now the sword has joined the shepherd’s crook; the two together must of necessity result in evil,

italian: però che, giunti, l’un l’altro non teme: se non mi credi, pon mente a la spiga, ch’ogn’ erba si conosce per lo seme.
english: because, so joined, one need not fear the other: and if you doubt me, watch the fruit and flower, for every plant is known by what it seeds.

italian: In sul paese ch’Adice e Po riga, solea valore e cortesia trovarsi, prima che Federigo avesse briga;
english: Within the territory watered by the Adige and Po, one used to find valor and courtesy—that is, before

italian: or può sicuramente indi passarsi per qualunque lasciasse, per vergogna di ragionar coi buoni o d’appressarsi.
english: Frederick was met by strife; now anyone ashamed of talking with the righteous or of meeting them can journey there, secure.

italian: Ben v’èn tre vecchi ancora in cui rampogna l’antica età la nova, e par lor tardo che Dio a miglior vita li ripogna:
english: True, three old men are there, in whom old times reprove the new; and they find God is slow in summoning them to a better life:

italian: Currado da Palazzo e ’l buon Gherardo e Guido da Castel, che mei si noma, francescamente, il semplice Lombardo.
english: Currado da Palazzo, good Gherardo, and Guido da Castel, whom it is better to call, as do the French, the candid Lombard.

italian: Dì oggimai che la Chiesa di Roma, per confondere in sé due reggimenti, cade nel fango, e sé brutta e la soma».
english: You can conclude: the Church of Rome confounds two powers in itself; into the filth, it falls and fouls itself and its new burden.”

italian: «O Marco mio», diss’ io, «bene argomenti; e or discerno perché dal retaggio li figli di Levì furono essenti.
english: “Good Marco,” I replied, “you reason well; and now I understand why Levi’s sons were not allowed to share in legacies.

italian: Ma qual Gherardo è quel che tu per saggio di’ ch’è rimaso de la gente spenta, in rimprovèro del secol selvaggio?».
english: But what Gherardo is this whom you mention as an example of the vanished people whose presence would reproach this savage age?”

italian: «O tuo parlar m’inganna, o el mi tenta», rispuose a me; «ché, parlandomi tosco, par che del buon Gherardo nulla senta.
english: “Either your speech deceives me or would tempt me,” he answered then, “for you, whose speech is Tuscan, seem to know nothing of the good Gherardo.

italian: Per altro sopranome io nol conosco, s’io nol togliessi da sua figlia Gaia. Dio sia con voi, ché più non vegno vosco.
english: There is no other name by which I know him, unless I speak of him as Gaia’s father. God be with you; I come with you no farther.

italian: Vedi l’albor che per lo fummo raia già biancheggiare, e me convien partirmi (l’angelo è ivi) prima ch’io li paia».
english: You see the rays that penetrate the smoke already whitening; I must take leave— the angel has arrived—before he sees me.”

italian: Così tornò, e più non volle udirmi.
english: So he turned back and would not hear me more.

italian: ﻿Ricorditi, lettor, se mai ne l’alpe ti colse nebbia per la qual vedessi non altrimenti che per pelle talpe,
english: Remember, reader, if you’ve ever been caught in the mountains by a mist through which you only saw as moles see through their skin,

italian: come, quando i vapori umidi e spessi a diradar cominciansi, la spera del sol debilemente entra per essi;
english: how, when the thick, damp vapors once begin to thin, the sun’s sphere passes feebly through them, then your imagination will be quick

italian: e fia la tua imagine leggera in giugnere a veder com’ io rividi lo sole in pria, che già nel corcar era.
english: to reach the point where it can see how I first came to see the sun again—when it was almost at the point at which it sets.

italian: Sì, pareggiando i miei co’ passi fidi del mio maestro, usci’ fuor di tal nube ai raggi morti già ne’ bassi lidi.
english: So, my steps matched my master’s trusty steps; out of that cloud I came, reaching the rays that, on the shores below, by now were spent.

italian: O imaginativa che ne rube talvolta sì di fuor, ch’om non s’accorge perché dintorno suonin mille tube,
english: O fantasy, you that at times would snatch us so from outward things—we notice nothing although a thousand trumpets sound around us—

italian: chi move te, se ’l senso non ti porge? Moveti lume che nel ciel s’informa, per sé o per voler che giù lo scorge.
english: who moves you when the senses do not spur you? A light that finds its form in Heaven moves you— directly or led downward by God’s will.

italian: De l’empiezza di lei che mutò forma ne l’uccel ch’a cantar più si diletta, ne l’imagine mia apparve l’orma;
english: Within my fantasy I saw impressed the savagery of one who then, transformed, became the bird that most delights in song;

italian: e qui fu la mia mente sì ristretta dentro da sé, che di fuor non venìa cosa che fosse allor da lei ricetta.
english: at this, my mind withdrew to the within, to what imagining might bring; no thing that came from the without could enter in.

italian: Poi piovve dentro a l’alta fantasia un crucifisso, dispettoso e fero ne la sua vista, e cotal si moria;
english: Then into my deep fantasy there rained one who was crucified; and as he died, he showed his savagery and his disdain.

italian: intorno ad esso era il grande Assüero, Estèr sua sposa e ’l giusto Mardoceo, che fu al dire e al far così intero.
english: Around him were great Ahasuerus and Esther his wife, and the just Mordecai, whose saying and whose doing were so upright.

italian: E come questa imagine rompeo sé per sé stessa, a guisa d’una bulla cui manca l’acqua sotto qual si feo,
english: And when this image shattered of itself, just like a bubble that has lost the water beneath which it was formed, there then rose up

italian: surse in mia visïone una fanciulla piangendo forte, e dicea: «O regina, perché per ira hai voluto esser nulla?
english: in my envisioning a girl who wept most bitterly and said: “O queen, why did you, in your wrath, desire to be no more?

italian: Ancisa t’hai per non perder Lavina; or m’hai perduta! Io son essa che lutto, madre, a la tua pria ch’a l’altrui ruina».
english: So as to keep Lavinia, you killed yourself; now you have lost me! I am she, mother, who mourns your fall before another’s.”

italian: Come si frange il sonno ove di butto nova luce percuote il viso chiuso, che fratto guizza pria che muoia tutto;
english: Even as sleep is shattered when new light strikes suddenly against closed eyes and, once it’s shattered, gleams before it dies completely,

italian: così l’imaginar mio cadde giuso tosto che lume il volto mi percosse, maggior assai che quel ch’è in nostro uso.
english: so my imagination fell away as soon as light—more powerful than light we are accustomed to—beat on my eyes.

italian: I’ mi volgea per veder ov’ io fosse, quando una voce disse «Qui si monta», che da ogne altro intento mi rimosse;
english: I looked about to see where I might be; but when a voice said: “Here one can ascend,” then I abandoned every other intent.

italian: e fece la mia voglia tanto pronta di riguardar chi era che parlava, che mai non posa, se non si raffronta.
english: That voice made my will keen to see the one who’d spoken—with the eagerness that cannot be still until it faces what it wants.

italian: Ma come al sol che nostra vista grava e per soverchio sua figura vela, così la mia virtù quivi mancava.
english: But even as the sun, become too strong, defeats our vision, veiling its own form, so there my power of sight was overcome.

italian: «Questo è divino spirito, che ne la via da ir sù ne drizza sanza prego, e col suo lume sé medesmo cela.
english: “This spirit is divine; and though unasked, he would conduct us to the upward path; he hides himself with that same light he sheds.

italian: Sì fa con noi, come l’uom si fa sego; ché quale aspetta prego e l’uopo vede, malignamente già si mette al nego.
english: He does with us as men do with themselves; for he who sees a need but waits to be asked is already set on cruel refusal.

italian: Or accordiamo a tanto invito il piede; procacciam di salir pria che s’abbui, ché poi non si poria, se ’l dì non riede».
english: Now let our steps accept his invitation, and let us try to climb before dark falls— then, until day returns, we’ll have to halt.”

italian: Così disse il mio duca, e io con lui volgemmo i nostri passi ad una scala; e tosto ch’io al primo grado fui,
english: So said my guide; and toward a stairway, he and I, together, turned; and just as soon as I was at the first step, I sensed something

italian: senti’mi presso quasi un muover d’ala e ventarmi nel viso e dir: ‘Beati pacifici, che son sanz’ ira mala!’.
english: much like the motion of a wing, and wind that beat against my face, and words: “Beati pacifici, those free of evil anger!”

italian: Già eran sovra noi tanto levati li ultimi raggi che la notte segue, che le stelle apparivan da più lati.
english: Above us now the final rays before; the fall of night were raised to such a height that we could see the stars on every side.

italian: ‘O virtù mia, perché sì ti dilegue?’, fra me stesso dicea, ché mi sentiva la possa de le gambe posta in triegue.
english: “O why, my strength, do you so melt away?” I said within myself, because I felt the force within my legs compelled to halt.

italian: Noi eravam dove più non saliva la scala sù, ed eravamo affissi, pur come nave ch’a la piaggia arriva.
english: We’d reached a point at which the upward stairs no longer climbed, and we were halted there just like a ship when it has touched the shore.

italian: E io attesi un poco, s’io udissi alcuna cosa nel novo girone; poi mi volsi al maestro mio, e dissi:
english: I listened for a while, hoping to hear whatever there might be in this new circle; then I turned toward my master, asking him:

italian: «Dolce mio padre, dì, quale offensione si purga qui nel giro dove semo? Se i piè si stanno, non stea tuo sermone».
english: “Tell me, my gentle father: what offense is purged within the circle we have reached? Although our feet must stop, your words need not.”

italian: Ed elli a me: «L’amor del bene, scemo del suo dover, quiritta si ristora; qui si ribatte il mal tardato remo.
english: And he to me: “Precisely here, the love of good that is too tepidly pursued is mended; here the lazy oar plies harder.

italian: Ma perché più aperto intendi ancora, volgi la mente a me, e prenderai alcun buon frutto di nostra dimora».
english: But so that you may understand more clearly, now turn your mind to me, and you will gather some useful fruit from our delaying here.

italian: «Né creator né creatura mai», cominciò el, «figliuol, fu sanza amore, o naturale o d’animo; e tu ’l sai.
english: My son, there’s no Creator and no creature who ever was without love—natural or mental; and you know that,” he began.

italian: Lo naturale è sempre sanza errore, ma l’altro puote errar per malo obietto o per troppo o per poco di vigore.
english: “The natural is always without error, but mental love may choose an evil object or err through too much or too little vigor.

italian: Mentre ch’elli è nel primo ben diretto, e ne’ secondi sé stesso misura, esser non può cagion di mal diletto;
english: As long as it’s directed toward the First Good and tends toward secondary goods with measure, it cannot be the cause of evil pleasure;

italian: ma quando al mal si torce, o con più cura o con men che non dee corre nel bene, contra ’l fattore adovra sua fattura.
english: but when it twists toward evil, or attends to good with more or less care than it should, those whom He made have worked against their Maker.

italian: Quinci comprender puoi ch’esser convene amor sementa in voi d’ogne virtute e d’ogne operazion che merta pene.
english: From this you see that—of necessity— love is the seed in you of every virtue and of all acts deserving punishment.

italian: Or, perché mai non può da la salute amor del suo subietto volger viso, da l’odio proprio son le cose tute;
english: Now, since love never turns aside its eyes from the well-being of its subject, things are surely free from hatred of themselves;

italian: e perché intender non si può diviso, e per sé stante, alcuno esser dal primo, da quello odiare ogne effetto è deciso.
english: and since no being can be seen as self- existing and divorced from the First Being, each creature is cut off from hating Him.

italian: Resta, se dividendo bene stimo, che ’l mal che s’ama è del prossimo; ed esso amor nasce in tre modi in vostro limo.
english: Thus, if I have distinguished properly, ill love must mean to wish one’s neighbor ill; and this love’s born in three ways in your clay.

italian: È chi, per esser suo vicin soppresso, spera eccellenza, e sol per questo brama ch’el sia di sua grandezza in basso messo;
english: There’s he who, through abasement of another, hopes for supremacy; he only longs to see his neighbor’s excellence cast down.

italian: è chi podere, grazia, onore e fama teme di perder perch’ altri sormonti, onde s’attrista sì che ’l contrario ama;
english: Then there is one who, when he is outdone, fears his own loss of fame, power, honor, favor; his sadness loves misfortune for his neighbor.

italian: ed è chi per ingiuria par ch’aonti, sì che si fa de la vendetta ghiotto, e tal convien che ’l male altrui impronti.
english: And there is he who, over injury received, resentful, for revenge grows greedy and, angrily, seeks out another’s harm.

italian: Questo triforme amor qua giù di sotto si piange: or vo’ che tu de l’altro intende, che corre al ben con ordine corrotto.
english: This threefold love is expiated here below; now I would have you understand the love that seeks the good distortedly.

italian: Ciascun confusamente un bene apprende nel qual si queti l’animo, e disira; per che di giugner lui ciascun contende.
english: Each apprehends confusedly a Good in which the mind may rest, and longs for It; and, thus, all strive to reach that Good; but if

italian: Se lento amore a lui veder vi tira o a lui acquistar, questa cornice, dopo giusto penter, ve ne martira.
english: the love that urges you to know It or to reach that Good is lax, this terrace, after a just repentance, punishes for that.

italian: Altro ben è che non fa l’uom felice; non è felicità, non è la buona essenza, d’ogne ben frutto e radice.
english: There is a different good, which does not make men glad; it is not happiness, is not true essence, fruit and root of every good.

italian: L’amor ch’ad esso troppo s’abbandona, di sovr’ a noi si piange per tre cerchi; ma come tripartito si ragiona,
english: The love that—profligately—yields to that is wept on in three terraces above us; but I’ll not say what three shapes that loves takes—

italian: tacciolo, acciò che tu per te ne cerchi».
english: may you seek those distinctions for yourself.”

italian: ﻿Posto avea fine al suo ragionamento l’alto dottore, e attento guardava ne la mia vista s’io parea contento;
english: The subtle teacher had completed his discourse to me; attentively he watched my eyes to see if I seemed satisfied.

italian: e io, cui nova sete ancor frugava, di fuor tacea, e dentro dicea: ‘Forse lo troppo dimandar ch’io fo li grava’.
english: And I, still goaded by new thirst, was silent without, although within I said: “Perhaps I have displeased him with too many questions.”

italian: Ma quel padre verace, che s’accorse del timido voler che non s’apriva, parlando, di parlare ardir mi porse.
english: But that true father, who had recognized the timid want I would not tell aloud, by speaking, gave me courage to speak out.

italian: Ond’ io: «Maestro, il mio veder s’avviva sì nel tuo lume, ch’io discerno chiaro quanto la tua ragion parta o descriva.
english: At which I said: “Master, my sight is so illumined by your light—I recognize all that your words declare or analyze.

italian: Però ti prego, dolce padre caro, che mi dimostri amore, a cui reduci ogne buono operare e ’l suo contraro».
english: Therefore, I pray you, gentle father dear, to teach me what love is: you have reduced to love both each good and its opposite.”

italian: «Drizza», disse, «ver’ me l’agute luci de lo ’ntelletto, e fieti manifesto l’error de’ ciechi che si fanno duci.
english: He said: “Direct your intellect’s sharp eyes toward me, and let the error of the blind who’d serve as guides be evident to you.

italian: L’animo, ch’è creato ad amar presto, ad ogne cosa è mobile che piace, tosto che dal piacere in atto è desto.
english: The soul, which is created quick to love, responds to everything that pleases, just as soon as beauty wakens it to act.
