italian: Vostra apprensiva da esser verace tragge intenzione, e dentro a voi la spiega, sì che l’animo ad essa volger face;
english: Your apprehension draws an image from a real object and expands upon that object until soul has turned toward it;

italian: e se, rivolto, inver’ di lei si piega, quel piegare è amor, quell’ è natura che per piacer di novo in voi si lega.
english: and if, so turned, the soul tends steadfastly, then that propensity is love—it’s nature that joins the soul in you, anew, through beauty.

italian: Poi, come ’l foco movesi in altura per la sua forma ch’è nata a salire là dove più in sua matera dura,
english: Then, just as flames ascend because the form of fire was fashioned to fly upward, toward the stuff of its own sphere, where it lasts longest,

italian: così l’animo preso entra in disire, ch’è moto spiritale, e mai non posa fin che la cosa amata il fa gioire.
english: so does the soul, when seized, move into longing, a motion of the spirit, never resting till the beloved thing has made it joyous.

italian: Or ti puote apparer quant’ è nascosa la veritate a la gente ch’avvera ciascun amore in sé laudabil cosa;
english: Now you can plainly see how deeply hidden truth is from scrutinists who would insist that every love is, in itself, praiseworthy;

italian: però che forse appar la sua matera sempre esser buona, ma non ciascun segno è buono, ancor che buona sia la cera».
english: and they are led to error by the matter of love, because it may seem—always—good; but not each seal is fine, although the wax is.”

italian: «Le tue parole e ’l mio seguace ingegno», rispuos’ io lui, «m’hanno amor discoverto, ma ciò m’ha fatto di dubbiar più pregno;
english: “Your speech and my own wit that followed it,” I answered him, “have shown me what love is; but that has filled me with still greater doubt;

italian: ché, s’amore è di fuori a noi offerto e l’anima non va con altro piede, se dritta o torta va, non è suo merto».
english: for if love’s offered to us from without and is the only foot with which soul walks, soul—going straight or crooked—has no merit.”

italian: Ed elli a me: «Quanto ragion qui vede, dir ti poss’ io; da indi in là t’aspetta pur a Beatrice, ch’è opra di fede.
english: And he to me: “What reason can see here, I can impart; past that, for truth of faith, it’s Beatrice alone you must await.

italian: Ogne forma sustanzïal, che setta è da matera ed è con lei unita, specifica vertute ha in sé colletta,
english: Every substantial form, at once distinct from matter and conjoined to it, ingathers the force that is distinctively its own,

italian: la qual sanza operar non è sentita, né si dimostra mai che per effetto, come per verdi fronde in pianta vita.
english: a force unknown to us until it acts— it’s never shown except in its effects, just as green boughs display the life in plants.

italian: Però, là onde vegna lo ’ntelletto de le prime notizie, omo non sape, e de’ primi appetibili l’affetto,
english: And thus man does not know the source of his intelligence of primal notions and his tending toward desire’s primal objects:

italian: che sono in voi sì come studio in ape di far lo mele; e questa prima voglia merto di lode o di biasmo non cape.
english: both are in you just as in bees there is the honey-making urge; such primal will deserves no praise, and it deserves no blame.

italian: Or perché a questa ogn’ altra si raccoglia, innata v’è la virtù che consiglia, e de l’assenso de’ tener la soglia.
english: Now, that all other longings may conform to this first will, there is in you, inborn, the power that counsels, keeper of the threshold

italian: Quest’ è ’l principio là onde si piglia ragion di meritare in voi, secondo che buoni e rei amori accoglie e viglia.
english: of your assent: this is the principle on which your merit may be judged, for it garners and winnows good and evil longings.

italian: Color che ragionando andaro al fondo, s’accorser d’esta innata libertate; però moralità lasciaro al mondo.
english: Those reasoners who reached the roots of things learned of this inborn freedom; the bequest that, thus, they left unto the world is ethics.

italian: Onde, poniam che di necessitate surga ogne amor che dentro a voi s’accende, di ritenerlo è in voi la podestate.
english: Even if we allow necessity as source for every love that flames in you, the power to curb that love is still your own.

italian: La nobile virtù Beatrice intende per lo libero arbitrio, e però guarda che l’abbi a mente, s’a parlar ten prende».
english: This noble power is what Beatrice means by free will; therefore, remember it, if she should ever speak of it to you.”

italian: La luna, quasi a mezza notte tarda, facea le stelle a noi parer più rade, fatta com’ un secchion che tuttor arda;
english: The moon, with midnight now behind us, made the stars seem scarcer to us; it was shaped just like a copper basin, gleaming, new;

italian: e correa contro ’l ciel per quelle strade che ’l sole infiamma allor che quel da Roma tra ’ Sardi e ’ Corsi il vede quando cade.
english: and counter course, it crossed those paths the sun ignites when those in Rome can see it set between the Corsicans and the Sardinians.

italian: E quell’ ombra gentil per cui si noma Pietola più che villa mantoana, del mio carcar diposta avea la soma;
english: That gracious shade for whom Pietola won more renown than any Mantuan town, had freed me from the weight of doubt I bore;

italian: per ch’io, che la ragione aperta e piana sovra le mie quistioni avea ricolta, stava com’ om che sonnolento vana.
english: so that I, having harvested his clear and open answers to my questions, stood like one who, nearing sleep, has random visions.

italian: Ma questa sonnolenza mi fu tolta subitamente da gente che dopo le nostre spalle a noi era già volta.
english: But readiness for sleep was suddenly taken from me by people who, behind our backs, already turned in our direction.

italian: E quale Ismeno già vide e Asopo lungo di sè di notte furia e calca, pur che i Teban di Bacco avesser uopo,
english: Just as—of old—Ismenus and Asopus, at night, along their banks, saw crowds and clamor whenever Thebans had to summon Bacchus,

italian: cotal per quel giron suo passo falca, per quel ch’io vidi di color, venendo, cui buon volere e giusto amor cavalca.
english: such was the arching crowd that curved around that circle, driven on, as I made out, by righteous will as well as by just love.

italian: Tosto fur sovr’ a noi, perché correndo si movea tutta quella turba magna; e due dinanzi gridavan piangendo:
english: Soon all that mighty throng drew near us, for they ran and ran; and two, in front of them, who wept, were crying: “In her journey, Mary

italian: «Maria corse con fretta a la montagna; e Cesare, per soggiogare Ilerda, punse Marsilia e poi corse in Ispagna».
english: made haste to reach the mountain, and, in order to conquer Lerida, first Caesar thrust against Marseilles, and then to Spain he rushed.”

italian: «Ratto, ratto, che ’l tempo non si perda per poco amor», gridavan li altri appresso, «che studio di ben far grazia rinverda».
english: Following them, the others cried: “Quick, quick, lest time be lost through insufficient love; where urge for good is keen, grace finds new green.”

italian: «O gente in cui fervore aguto adesso ricompie forse negligenza e indugio da voi per tepidezza in ben far messo,
english: “O people in whom eager fervor now may compensate for sloth and negligence you showed in doing good half-heartedly,

italian: questi che vive, e certo i’ non vi bugio, vuole andar sù, pur che ’l sol ne riluca; però ne dite ond’ è presso il pertugio».
english: he—who’s alive, and surely I don’t lie to you—would climb above as soon as he has seen the sun shed light on us again;

italian: Parole furon queste del mio duca; e un di quelli spirti disse: «Vieni di retro a noi, e troverai la buca.
english: then, tell us where the passage lies at hand.” My guide said this. One of the souls replied: “Come, follow us, and you will find the gap.

italian: Noi siam di voglia a muoverci sì pieni, che restar non potem; però perdona, se villania nostra giustizia tieni.
english: We are so fully anxious to advance— we cannot halt; and do forgive us, should you take our penance for discourtesy.

italian: Io fui abate in San Zeno a Verona sotto lo ’mperio del buon Barbarossa, di cui dolente ancor Milan ragiona.
english: I was St. Zeno’s abbot in Verona under the rule of valiant Barbarossa, of whom Milan still speaks with so much sorrow.

italian: E tale ha già l’un piè dentro la fossa, che tosto piangerà quel monastero, e tristo fia d’avere avuta possa;
english: And there is one with one foot in the grave, who soon will weep over that monastery, lamenting that he once had power there,

italian: perché suo figlio, mal del corpo intero, e de la mente peggio, e che mal nacque, ha posto in loco di suo pastor vero».
english: because, in place of its true shepherd, he put one who was unsound of body and, still more, of mind, and born in sin—his son.

italian: Io non so se più disse o s’ei si tacque, tant’ era già di là da noi trascorso; ma questo intesi, e ritener mi piacque.
english: I don’t know if he said more or was silent— he had already raced so far beyond us; but I heard this much and was pleased to hear it.

italian: E quei che m’era ad ogne uopo soccorso disse: «Volgiti qua: vedine due venir dando a l’accidïa di morso».
english: And he who was my help in every need said: “Turn around: see those two coming—they whose words mock sloth.” And I heard those two say

italian: Di retro a tutti dicean: «Prima fue morta la gente a cui il mar s’aperse, che vedesse Iordan le rede sue.
english: behind all of the rest: “The ones for whom the sea parted were dead before the Jordan saw those who had inherited its lands;

italian: E quella che l’affanno non sofferse fino a la fine col figlio d’Anchise, sé stessa a vita sanza gloria offerse».
english: and those who did not suffer trials until the end together with Anchises’ son gave themselves up to life without renown.”

italian: Poi quando fuor da noi tanto divise quell’ ombre, che veder più non potiersi, novo pensiero dentro a me si mise,
english: Then, when those shades were so far off from us that seeing them became impossible, a new thought rose inside of me and, from

italian: del qual più altri nacquero e diversi; e tanto d’uno in altro vaneggiai, che li occhi per vaghezza ricopersi,
english: that thought, still others—many and diverse— were born: I was so drawn from random thought to thought that, wandering in mind, I shut

italian: e ’l pensamento in sogno trasmutai.
english: my eyes, transforming thought on thought to dream.

italian: Ne l’ora che non può ’l calor dïurno intepidar più ’l freddo de la luna, vinto da terra, e talor da Saturno
english: In that hour when the heat of day, defeated by Earth and, sometimes, Saturn, can no longer warm up the moon—sent cold, when geomancers

italian: —quando i geomanti lor Maggior Fortuna veggiono in orïente, innanzi a l’alba, surger per via che poco le sta bruna—,
english: can, in the east, see their Fortuna major rising before the dawn along a path that will be darkened for it only briefly—

italian: mi venne in sogno una femmina balba, ne li occhi guercia, e sovra i piè distorta, con le man monche, e di colore scialba.
english: a stammering woman came to me in dream: her eyes askew, and crooked on her feet, her hands were crippled, her complexion sallow.

italian: Io la mirava; e come ’l sol conforta le fredde membra che la notte aggrava, così lo sguardo mio le facea scorta
english: I looked at her; and just as sun revives cold limbs that night made numb, so did my gaze loosen her tongue and then, in little time,

italian: la lingua, e poscia tutta la drizzava in poco d’ora, e lo smarrito volto, com’ amor vuol, così le colorava.
english: set her contorted limbs in perfect order; and, with the coloring that love prefers, my eyes transformed the wanness of her features.

italian: Poi ch’ell’ avea ’l parlar così disciolto, cominciava a cantar sì, che con pena da lei avrei mio intento rivolto.
english: And when her speech had been set free, then she began to sing so, that it would have been most difficult for me to turn aside.

italian: «Io son», cantava, «io son dolce serena, che ’ marinari in mezzo mar dismago; tanto son di piacere a sentir piena!
english: “I am,” she sang, “I am the pleasing siren, who in midsea leads mariners astray— there is so much delight in hearing me.

italian: Io volsi Ulisse del suo cammin vago al canto mio; e qual meco s’ausa, rado sen parte; sì tutto l’appago!».
english: I turned aside Ulysses, although he had longed to journey; who grows used to me seldom departs—I satisfy him so.”

italian: Ancor non era sua bocca richiusa, quand’ una donna apparve santa e presta lunghesso me per far colei confusa.
english: Her lips were not yet done when, there beside me, a woman showed herself, alert and saintly, to cast the siren into much confusion.

italian: «O Virgilio, Virgilio, chi è questa?», fieramente dicea; ed el venìa con li occhi fitti pur in quella onesta.
english: “O Virgil, Virgil, tell me: who is this?” she asked most scornfully; and he came forward, his eyes intent upon that honest one.

italian: L’altra prendea, e dinanzi l’apria fendendo i drappi, e mostravami ’l ventre; quel mi svegliò col puzzo che n’uscia.
english: He seized the other, baring her in front, tearing her clothes, and showing me her belly; the stench that came from there awakened me.

italian: Io mossi li occhi, e ’l buon maestro: «Almen tre voci t’ho messe!», dicea, «Surgi e vieni; troviam l’aperta per la qual tu entre».
english: I moved my eyes, and my good master cried: “At least three times I’ve called you. Rise and come: let’s find the opening where you may enter.”

italian: Sù mi levai, e tutti eran già pieni de l’alto dì i giron del sacro monte, e andavam col sol novo a le reni.
english: I rose; the daylight had already filled the circles of the sacred mountain—we were journeying with new sun at our back.

italian: Seguendo lui, portava la mia fronte come colui che l’ha di pensier carca, che fa di sé un mezzo arco di ponte;
english: I followed him, bearing my brow like one whose thoughts have weighed him down, who bends as if he were the semiarch that forms a bridge,

italian: quand’ io udi’ «Venite; qui si varca» parlare in modo soave e benigno, qual non si sente in questa mortal marca.
english: and then I heard: “Draw near; the pass is here,” said in a manner so benign and gentle as, in our mortal land, one cannot hear.

italian: Con l’ali aperte, che parean di cigno, volseci in sù colui che sì parlonne tra due pareti del duro macigno.
english: He who addressed us so had open wings, white as a swan’s; and he directed us upward, between two walls of the hard rock.

italian: Mosse le penne poi e ventilonne, ‘Qui lugent’ affermando esser beati, ch’avran di consolar l’anime donne.
english: And then he moved his plumes and, fanning us, affirmed that those “Qui lugent” would be blessed— their souls would be possessed of consolation.

italian: «Che hai che pur inver’ la terra guati?», la guida mia incominciò a dirmi, poco amendue da l’angel sormontati.
english: “What makes you keep your eyes upon the ground?” my guide began to say to me when both of us had climbed a little, past the angel.

italian: E io: «Con tanta sospeccion fa irmi novella visïon ch’a sé mi piega, sì ch’io non posso dal pensar partirmi».
english: And I: “What makes me move with such misgiving is a new vision: it has so beguiled me that I cannot relinquish thoughts of it.”

italian: «Vedesti», disse, «quell’antica strega che sola sovr’ a noi omai si piagne; vedesti come l’uom da lei si slega.
english: “The one you saw,” he said, “that ancient witch— for her alone one must atone above; you saw how man can free himself from her.

italian: Bastiti, e batti a terra le calcagne; li occhi rivolgi al logoro che gira lo rege etterno con le rote magne».
english: Let that suffice, and hurry on your way; fasten your eyes upon the lure that’s spun by the eternal King with His great spheres.”

italian: Quale ’l falcon, che prima a’ pié si mira, indi si volge al grido e si protende per lo disio del pasto che là il tira,
english: Just like a falcon, who at first looks down, then, when the falconer has called, bends forward, craving the food that’s ready for him there,

italian: tal mi fec’ io; e tal, quanto si fende la roccia per dar via a chi va suso, n’andai infin dove ’l cerchiar si prende.
english: so l became—and so remained until, through the cleft rock that lets one climb above, I reached the point at which the circle starts.

italian: Com’ io nel quinto giro fui dischiuso, vidi gente per esso che piangea, giacendo a terra tutta volta in giuso.
english: When I was in the clearing, the fifth level, my eyes discovered people there who wept, lying upon the ground, all turned face down.

italian: ‘Adhaesit pavimento anima mea’ sentia dir lor con sì alti sospiri, che la parola a pena s’intendea.
english: “Adhaesit pavimento anima mea,” I heard them say with sighs so deep that it was hard to comprehend the words they spoke.

italian: «O eletti di Dio, li cui soffriri e giustizia e speranza fa men duri, drizzate noi verso li alti saliri».
english: “O God’s elect, whose sufferings both hope and justice make less difficult, direct us to the stairway meant for our ascent.”

italian: «Se voi venite dal giacer sicuri, e volete trovar la via più tosto, le vostre destre sien sempre di fori».
english: “If you come here but do not need to be prostrate, and you would find the path most quickly, then keep your right hand always to the outside.”

italian: Così pregò ’l poeta, e sì risposto poco dinanzi a noi ne fu; per ch’io nel parlare avvisai l’altro nascosto,
english: So did the poet ask, so did reply come from a little way ahead; and I, hearing that voice reply, learned what was hidden.

italian: e volsi li occhi a li occhi al segnor mio: ond’ elli m’assentì con lieto cenno ciò che chiedea la vista del disio.
english: I turned my eyes to find my master’s eyes; at this, with a glad sign, he ratified what I had asked for with my eager eyes.

italian: Poi ch’io potei di me fare a mio senno, trassimi sovra quella creatura le cui parole pria notar mi fenno,
english: When, free to do as I had wanted to, I moved ahead and bent over that soul whose words—before—had made me notice him,

italian: dicendo: «Spirto in cui pianger matura quel sanza ’l quale a Dio tornar non pòssi, sosta un poco per me tua maggior cura.
english: saying: “Spirit, within whom weeping ripens that without which there’s no return to God, suspend awhile—for me—your greater care.

italian: Chi fosti e perché vòlti avete i dossi al sù, mi dì, e se vuo’ ch’io t’impetri cosa di là ond’ io vivendo mossi».
english: Tell me: Who were you? And why are your backs turned up? And there—where I, alive, set out— would you have me beseech some good for you?”

italian: Ed elli a me: «Perché i nostri diretri rivolga il cielo a sé, saprai; ma prima scias quod ego fui successor Petri.
english: And he to me: “Why Heaven turns our backs against itself, you are to know; but first scias quod ego fui successor Petri.

italian: Intra Sïestri e Chiaveri s’adima una fiumana bella, e del suo nome lo titol del mio sangue fa sua cima.
english: Between Sestri and Chiavari descends a handsome river; and its name is set upon the upper portion of my crest.

italian: Un mese e poco più prova’ io come pesa il gran manto a chi dal fango il guarda, che piuma sembran tutte l’altre some.
english: For one month and a little more I learned how the great mantle weighs on him who’d keep it out of the mire—all other weights seem feathers.

italian: La mia conversïone, omè!, fu tarda; ma, come fatto fui roman pastore, così scopersi la vita bugiarda.
english: Alas, how tardy my conversion was! But when I had been named the Roman shepherd, then I discovered the deceit of life.

italian: Vidi che lì non s’acquetava il core, né più salir potiesi in quella vita; per che di questa in me s’accese amore.
english: I saw that there the heart was not at rest, nor could I, in that life, ascend more high; so that, in me, love for this life was kindled.

italian: Fino a quel punto misera e partita da Dio anima fui, del tutto avara; or, come vedi, qui ne son punita.
english: Until that point I was a squalid soul, from God divided, wholly avaricious; now, as you see, I’m punished here for that.

italian: Quel ch’avarizia fa, qui si dichiara in purgazion de l’anime converse; e nulla pena il monte ha più amara.
english: What avarice enacts is here declared in the purgation of converted souls; the mountain has no punishment more bitter.

italian: Sì come l’occhio nostro non s’aderse in alto, fisso a le cose terrene, così giustizia qui a terra il merse.
english: Just as we did not lift our eyes on high but set our sight on earthly things instead, so justice here impels our eyes toward earth.

italian: Come avarizia spense a ciascun bene lo nostro amore, onde operar perdési, così giustizia qui stretti ne tene,
english: As avarice annulled in us the love of any other good, and thus we lost our chance for righteous works, so justice here

italian: ne’ piedi e ne le man legati e presi; e quanto fia piacer del giusto Sire, tanto staremo immobili e distesi».
english: fetters our hands and feet and holds us captive; and for as long as it may please our just Lord, here we’ll be outstretched and motionless.”

italian: Io m’era inginocchiato e volea dire; ma com’ io cominciai ed el s’accorse, solo ascoltando, del mio reverire,
english: I’d kneeled, wishing to speak: but just as I began—and through my voice alone—he sensed that I had meant to do him reverence.

italian: «Qual cagion», disse, «in giù così ti torse?». E io a lui: «Per vostra dignitate mia coscïenza dritto mi rimorse».
english: “What reason makes you bend your body so?” he said. And I to him: “Your dignity made conscience sting me as I stood erect.”

italian: «Drizza le gambe, lèvati sù, frate!», rispuose; «non errar: conservo sono teco e con li altri ad una podestate.
english: “Brother, straighten your legs; rise up!” he answered. “Don’t be mistaken; I, with you and others, am but a fellow—servant of one Power.

italian: Se mai quel santo evangelico suono che dice ‘Neque nubent’ intendesti, ben puoi veder perch’ io così ragiono.
english: If you have ever understood the holy sound of the Gospel that says ‘Neque nubent,’ then you will see why I have spoken so.

italian: Vattene omai: non vo’ che più t’arresti; ché la tua stanza mio pianger disagia, col qual maturo ciò che tu dicesti.
english: Now go your way: I’d not have you stop longer; your staying here disturbs my lamentations, the tears that help me ripen what you mentioned.

italian: Nepote ho io di là c’ha nome Alagia, buona da sé, pur che la nostra casa non faccia lei per essempro malvagia;
english: Beyond, I have a niece whose name’s Alagia; she in herself is good, as long as our house, by example, brings her not to evil;

italian: e questa sola di là m’è rimasa».
english: and she alone is left to me beyond.”

italian: Contra miglior voler voler mal pugna; onde contra ’l piacer mio, per piacerli, trassi de l’acqua non sazia la spugna.
english: Against a better will, the will fights weakly; therefore, to please him, though against my pleasure, I drew my unquenched sponge out of the water.

italian: Mossimi; e ’l duca mio si mosse per li luoghi spediti pur lungo la roccia, come si va per muro stretto a’ merli;
english: I moved on, and my guide moved through the un- encumbered space, hugging the rock, as one walks on a wall, close to the battlements;

italian: ché la gente che fonde a goccia a goccia per li occhi il mal che tutto ’l mondo occupa, da l’altra parte in fuor troppo s’approccia.
english: for those whose eyes would melt down, drop by drop, the evil that possesses all the world, were too close to the edge, on the far side.

italian: Maladetta sie tu, antica lupa, che più che tutte l’altre bestie hai preda per la tua fame sanza fine cupa!
english: May you be damned, o ancient wolf, whose power can claim more prey than all the other beasts — your hungering is deep and never-ending!

italian: O ciel, nel cui girar par che si creda le condizion di qua giù trasmutarsi, quando verrà per cui questa disceda?
english: O heavens, through whose revolutions many think things on earth are changed, when will he come — the one whose works will drive that wolf away?

italian: Noi andavam con passi lenti e scarsi, e io attento a l’ombre, ch’i’ sentia pietosamente piangere e lagnarsi;
english: Our steps were short and slow as we moved on; I was attentive to the shades; I heard the sorrow in their tears and lamentations.

italian: e per ventura udi’ «Dolce Maria!» dinanzi a noi chiamar così nel pianto come fa donna che in parturir sia;
english: Then I, by chance, heard one ahead of us crying in his lament, “Sweet Mary,” as a woman would outcry in labor pains.

italian: e seguitar: «Povera fosti tanto, quanto veder si può per quello ospizio dove sponesti il tuo portato santo».
english: And he continued: “In that hostel where you had set down your holy burden, there one can discover just how poor you were.”

italian: Seguentemente intesi: «O buon Fabrizio, con povertà volesti anzi virtute che gran ricchezza posseder con vizio».
english: Following this I heard: “O good Fabricius, you chose, as your possessions, indigence with virtue rather than much wealth with vice.”

italian: Queste parole m’eran sì piaciute, ch’io mi trassi oltre per aver contezza di quello spirto onde parean venute.
english: These words had been so pleasing to me — I moved forward, so that I might come to know the spirit from whom they had seemed to come.

italian: Esso parlava ancor de la larghezza che fece Niccolò a le pulcelle, per condurre ad onor lor giovinezza.
english: He kept on speaking, telling the largesse of Nicholas — the gifts he gave the maidens so that they might be honorably wed.

italian: «O anima che tanto ben favelle, dimmi chi fosti», dissi, «e perché sola tu queste degne lode rinovelle.
english: “O soul who speaks of so much righteousness, do tell me who you were,” I said, “and why just you alone renew these seemly praises.

italian: Non fia sanza mercé la tua parola, s’io ritorno a compiér lo cammin corto di quella vita ch’al termine vola».
english: Your speaking to me will not go unthanked when I return to finish the short span of that life which now hurries toward its end.”

italian: Ed elli: «Io ti dirò, non per conforto ch’io attenda di là, ma perché tanta grazia in te luce prima che sie morto.
english: And he: “I’ll tell you — not because I hope for solace from your world, but for such grace as shines in you before your death’s arrived.

italian: Io fui radice de la mala pianta che la terra cristiana tutta aduggia, sì che buon frutto rado se ne schianta.
english: I was the root of the obnoxious plant that overshadows all the Christian lands, so that fine fruit can rarely rise from them.

italian: Ma se Doagio, Lilla, Guanto e Bruggia potesser, tosto ne saria vendetta; e io la cheggio a lui che tutto giuggia.
english: But if Douai and Lille and Bruges and Ghent had power, they would soon take vengeance on it; and this I beg of Him who judges all.

italian: Chiamato fui di là Ugo Ciappetta; di me son nati i Filippi e i Luigi per cui novellamente è Francia retta.
english: The name I bore beyond was Hugh Capet: of me were born the Louises and Philips by whom France has been ruled most recently.

italian: Figliuol fu’ io d’un beccaio di Parigi: quando li regi antichi venner meno tutti, fuor ch’un renduto in panni bigi,
english: I was the son of a Parisian butcher. When all the line of ancient kings was done and only one — a monk in gray — survived,

italian: trova’mi stretto ne le mani il freno del governo del regno, e tanta possa di nuovo acquisto, e sì d’amici pieno,
english: I found the reins that ruled the kingdom tight within my hands, and I held so much new- gained power and possessed so many friends

italian: ch’a la corona vedova promossa la testa di mio figlio fu, dal quale cominciar di costor le sacrate ossa.
english: that, to the widowed crown, my own son’s head was elevated, and from him began the consecrated bones of all those kings.

italian: Mentre che la gran dota provenzale al sangue mio non tolse la vergogna, poco valea, ma pur non facea male.
english: Until the giant dowry of Provence removed all sense of shame within my house, my line was not worth much, but did no wrong.

italian: Lì cominciò con forza e con menzogna la sua rapina; e poscia, per ammenda, Pontì e Normandia prese e Guascogna.
english: There its rapine began with lies and force; and then it seized — that it might make amends — Ponthieu and Normandy and Gascony.

italian: Carlo venne in Italia e, per ammenda, vittima fé di Curradino; e poi ripinse al ciel Tommaso, per ammenda.
english: Charles came to Italy and, for amends, made Conradin a victim, and then thrust back Thomas into Heaven, for amends.

italian: Tempo vegg’ io, non molto dopo ancoi, che tragge un altro Carlo fuor di Francia, per far conoscer meglio e sé e ’ suoi.
english: I see a time — not too far off — in which another Charles advances out of France to make himself and his descendants famous.

italian: Sanz’ arme n’esce e solo con la lancia con la qual giostrò Giuda, e quella ponta sì, ch’a Fiorenza fa scoppiar la pancia.
english: He does not carry weapons when he comes, only the lance that Judas tilted; this he couches so — he twists the paunch of Florence.

italian: Quindi non terra, ma peccato e onta guadagnerà, per sé tanto più grave, quanto più lieve simil danno conta.
english: From this he’ll gain not land, just shame and sin, which will be all the heavier for him as he would reckon lightly such disgrace.

italian: L’altro, che già uscì preso di nave, veggio vender sua figlia e patteggiarne come fanno i corsar de l’altre schiave.
english: The other, who once left his ship as prisoner — I see him sell his daughter, bargaining as pirates haggle over female slaves.

italian: O avarizia, che puoi tu più farne, poscia c’ha’ il mio sangue a te sì tratto, che non si cura de la propria carne?
english: O avarice, my house is now your captive: it traffics in the flesh of its own children — what more is left for you to do to us?

italian: Perché men paia il mal futuro e ’l fatto, veggio in Alagna intrar lo fiordaliso, e nel vicario suo Cristo esser catto.
english: That past and future evil may seem less, I see the fleur-de-lis enter Anagni and, in His vicar, Christ made prisoner.

italian: Veggiolo un’altra volta esser deriso; veggio rinovellar l’aceto e ’l fiele, e tra vivi ladroni esser anciso.
english: I see Him mocked a second time; I see the vinegar and gall renewed — and He is slain between two thieves who’re still alive.

italian: Veggio il novo Pilato sì crudele, che ciò nol sazia, ma sanza decreto portar nel Tempio le cupide vele.
english: And I see the new Pilate, one so cruel that, still not sated, he, without decree, carries his greedy sails into the Temple.

italian: O Segnor mio, quando sarò io lieto a veder la vendetta che, nascosa, fa dolce l’ira tua nel tuo secreto?
english: O You, my Lord, when will You let me be happy on seeing vengeance that, concealed, makes sweet Your anger in Your secrecy?

italian: Ciò ch’io dicea di quell’ unica sposa de lo Spirito Santo e che ti fece verso me volger per alcuna chiosa,
english: What I have said about the only bride the Holy Ghost has known, the words that made you turn to me for commentary — these

italian: tanto è risposto a tutte nostre prece quanto ’l dì dura; ma com’ el s’annotta, contrario suon prendemo in quella vece.
english: words serve as answer to our prayers as long as it is day; but when night falls, then we recite examples that are contrary.

italian: Noi repetiam Pigmalïon allotta, cui traditore e ladro e paricida fece la voglia sua de l’oro ghiotta;
english: Then we tell over how Pygmalion, out of his greedy lust for gold, became a thief and traitor and a parricide;

italian: e la miseria de l’avaro Mida, che seguì a la sua dimanda gorda, per la qual sempre convien che si rida.
english: the wretchedness of avaricious Midas, resulting from his ravenous request, the consequence that always makes men laugh;

italian: Del folle Acàn ciascun poi si ricorda, come furò le spoglie, sì che l’ira di Iosüè qui par ch’ancor lo morda.
english: and each of us recalls the foolish Achan — how he had robbed the spoils, so that the anger of Joshua still seems to sting him here.

italian: Indi accusiam col marito Saffira; lodiam i calci ch’ebbe Elïodoro; e in infamia tutto ’l monte gira
english: Then we accuse Sapphira and her husband; we praise the kicks Heliodorus suffered; and Polymnestor, who killed Polydorus,

italian: Polinestòr ch’ancise Polidoro; ultimamente ci si grida: “Crasso, dilci, che ’l sai: di che sapore è l’oro?”.
english: resounds, in infamy, round all this mountain; and finally, what we cry here is: ‘Crassus, tell us, because you know: How does gold taste?’

italian: Talor parla l’uno alto e l’altro basso, secondo l’affezion ch’ad ir ci sprona ora a maggiore e ora a minor passo:
english: At times one speaks aloud, another low, according to the sentiment that goads us now to be more swift and now more slow:

italian: però al ben che ’l dì ci si ragiona, dianzi non era io sol; ma qui da presso non alzava la voce altra persona».
english: thus, I was not alone in speaking of the good we cite by day, but here nearby no other spirit raised his voice as high.”

italian: Noi eravam partiti già da esso, e brigavam di soverchiar la strada tanto quanto al poder n’era permesso,
english: We had already taken leave of him and were already struggling to advance along that road as far as we were able,

italian: quand’ io senti’, come cosa che cada, tremar lo monte; onde mi prese un gelo qual prender suol colui ch’a morte vada.
english: when I could feel the mountain tremble like a falling thing; at which a chill seized me as cold grips one who goes to meet his death.

italian: Certo non si scoteo sì forte Delo, pria che Latona in lei facesse ’l nido a parturir li due occhi del cielo.
english: Delos had surely not been buffeted so hard before Latona planted there the nest in which to bear the sky’s two eyes.

italian: Poi cominciò da tutte parti un grido tal, che ’l maestro inverso me si feo, dicendo: «Non dubbiar, mentr’ io ti guido».
english: Then such a shout rose up on every side that, drawing near to me, my master said: “Don’t be afraid, as long as I’m your guide.”

italian: ‘Glorïa in excelsis ’ tutti ‘Deo’ dicean, per quel ch’io da’ vicin compresi, onde intender lo grido si poteo.
english: “Gloria in excelsis Deo,” they all cried— so did I understand from those nearby, whose shouted words were able to be heard.

italian: No’ istavamo immobili e sospesi come i pastor che prima udir quel canto, fin che ’l tremar cessò ed el compiési.
english: Just like the shepherds who first heard that song, we stood, but did not move, in expectation, until the trembling stopped, the song was done.

italian: Poi ripigliammo nostro cammin santo, guardando l’ombre che giacean per terra, tornate già in su l’usato pianto.
english: Then we took up again our holy path, watching the shades who lay along the ground, who had resumed their customary tears.

italian: Nulla ignoranza mai con tanta guerra mi fé desideroso di sapere, se la memoria mia in ciò non erra,
english: My ignorance has never struggled so, has never made me long so much to know — if memory does not mislead me now —

italian: quanta pareami allor, pensando, avere; né per la fretta dimandare er’ oso, né per me lì potea cosa vedere:
english: as it seemed then to long within my thoughts; nor did I dare to ask — we were so rushed; nor, by myself, could I discern the cause.

italian: così m’andava timido e pensoso.
english: So, timid, pensive, I pursued my way.

italian: ﻿La sete natural che mai non sazia se non con l’acqua onde la femminetta samaritana domandò la grazia,
english: The natural thirst that never can be quenched except by water that gives grace—the draught the simple woman of Samaria sought—

italian: mi travagliava, e pungeami la fretta per la ’mpacciata via dietro al mio duca, e condoleami a la giusta vendetta.
english: tormented me; haste spurred me on the path crowded with souls, behind my guide; and I felt pity, though their pain was justified.

italian: Ed ecco, sì come ne scrive Luca che Cristo apparve a’ due ch’erano in via, già surto fuor de la sepulcral buca,
english: And here—even as Luke records for us that Christ, new—risen from his burial cave, appeared to two along his way—a shade

italian: ci apparve un’ombra, e dietro a noi venìa, dal piè guardando la turba che giace; né ci addemmo di lei, sì parlò pria,
english: appeared; and he advanced behind our backs while we were careful not to trample on the outstretched crowd. We did not notice him

italian: dicendo: «O frati miei, Dio vi dea pace». Noi ci volgemmo sùbiti, e Virgilio rendéli ’l cenno ch’a ciò si conface.
english: until he had addressed us with: “God give you, o my brothers, peace!” We turned at once; then, after offering suitable response,

italian: Poi cominciò: «Nel beato concilio ti ponga in pace la verace corte che me rilega ne l’etterno essilio».
english: Virgil began: “And may that just tribunal which has consigned me to eternal exile place you in peace within the blessed assembly!”

italian: «Come!», diss’ elli, e parte andavam forte: «se voi siete ombre che Dio sù non degni, chi v’ha per la sua scala tanto scorte?».
english: “What!” he exclaimed, as we moved forward quickly. “If God’s not deemed you worthy of ascent, who’s guided you so far along His stairs?”

italian: E ’l dottor mio: «Se tu riguardi a’ segni che questi porta e che l’angel profila, ben vedrai che coi buon convien ch’e’ regni.
english: “If you observe the signs the angel traced upon this man,” my teacher said, “you’ll see plainly—he’s meant to reign with all the righteous;

italian: Ma perché lei che dì e notte fila non li avea tratta ancora la conocchia che Cloto impone a ciascuno e compila,
english: but since she who spins night and day had not yet spun the spool that Clotho sets upon the distaff and adjusts for everyone,

italian: l’anima sua, ch’è tua e mia serocchia, venendo sù, non potea venir sola, però ch’al nostro modo non adocchia.
english: his soul, the sister of your soul and mine, in its ascent, could not—alone—have climbed here, for it does not see the way we see.

italian: Ond’ io fui tratto fuor de l’ampia gola d’inferno per mostrarli, e mosterrolli oltre, quanto ’l potrà menar mia scola.
english: Therefore, I was brought forth from Hell’s broad jaws to guide him in his going; I shall lead him just as far as where I teach can reach.

italian: Ma dimmi, se tu sai, perché tai crolli diè dianzi ’l monte, e perché tutto ad una parve gridare infino a’ suoi piè molli».
english: But tell me, if you can, why, just before, the mountain shook and shouted, all of it— for so it seemed—down to its sea—bathed shore.”

italian: Sì mi diè, dimandando, per la cruna del mio disio, che pur con la speranza si fece la mia sete men digiuna.
english: His question threaded so the needle’s eye of my desire that just the hope alone of knowing left my thirst more satisfied.

italian: Quei cominciò: «Cosa non è che sanza ordine senta la religïone de la montagna, o che sia fuor d’usanza.
english: That other shade began: “The sanctity of these slopes does not suffer anything that’s without order or uncustomary.

italian: Libero è qui da ogne alterazione: di quel che ’l ciel da sé in sé riceve esser ci puote, e non d’altro, cagione.
english: This place is free from every perturbation: what heaven from itself and in itself receives may serve as cause here—no thing else.

italian: Per che non pioggia, non grando, non neve, non rugiada, non brina più sù cade che la scaletta di tre gradi breve;
english: Therefore, no rain, no hail, no snow, no dew, no hoarfrost falls here any higher than the stairs of entry with their three brief steps;

italian: nuvole spesse non paion né rade, né coruscar, né figlia di Taumante, che di là cangia sovente contrade;
english: neither thick clouds nor thin appear, nor flash of lightning; Thaumas’ daughter, who so often shifts places in your world, is absent here.

italian: secco vapor non surge più avante ch’al sommo d’i tre gradi ch’io parlai, dov’ ha ’l vicario di Pietro le piante.
english: Dry vapor cannot climb up any higher than to the top of the three steps of which I spoke—where Peter’s vicar plants his feet.

italian: Trema forse più giù poco o assai; ma per vento che ’n terra si nasconda, non so come, qua sù non tremò mai.
english: Below that point, there may be small or ample tremors; but here above, I know not why, no wind concealed in earth has ever caused

italian: Tremaci quando alcuna anima monda sentesi, sì che surga o che si mova per salir sù; e tal grido seconda.
english: a tremor; for it only trembles here when some soul feels it’s cleansed, so that it rises or stirs to climb on high; and that shout follows.

italian: De la mondizia sol voler fa prova, che, tutto libero a mutar convento, l’alma sorprende, e di voler le giova.
english: The will alone is proof of purity and, fully free, surprises soul into a change of dwelling place—effectively.

italian: Prima vuol ben, ma non lascia il talento che divina giustizia, contra voglia, come fu al peccar, pone al tormento.
english: Soul had the will to climb before, but that will was opposed by longing to do penance (as once, to sin), instilled by divine justice.

italian: E io, che son giaciuto a questa doglia cinquecent’ anni e più, pur mo sentii libera volontà di miglior soglia:
english: And I, who have lain in this suffering five hundred years and more, just now have felt my free will for a better threshold: thus,

italian: però sentisti il tremoto e li pii spiriti per lo monte render lode a quel Segnor, che tosto sù li ’nvii».
english: you heard the earthquake and the pious spirits throughout the mountain as they praised the Lord— and may He send them speedily upward.”

italian: Così ne disse; e però ch’el si gode tanto del ber quant’ è grande la sete, non saprei dir quant’ el mi fece prode.
english: So did he speak to us; and just as joy is greater when we quench a greater thirst, the joy he brought cannot be told in words.

italian: E ’l savio duca: «Omai veggio la rete che qui vi ’mpiglia e come si scalappia, perché ci trema e di che congaudete.
english: And my wise guide: “I now can see the net impeding you, how one slips through, and why it quakes here, and what makes you all rejoice.

italian: Ora chi fosti, piacciati ch’io sappia, e perché tanti secoli giaciuto qui se’, ne le parole tue mi cappia».
english: And now may it please you to tell me who you were, and in your words may I find why you’ve lain here for so many centuries.”

italian: «Nel tempo che ’l buon Tito, con l’aiuto del sommo rege, vendicò le fóra ond’ uscì ’l sangue per Giuda venduto,
english: “In that age when the worthy Titus, with help from the Highest King, avenged the wounds from which the blood that Judas sold had flowed,

italian: col nome che più dura e più onora era io di là», rispuose quello spirto, «famoso assai, ma non con fede ancora.
english: I had sufficient fame beyond,” that spirit replied; “I bore the name that lasts the longest and honors most—but faith was not yet mine.

italian: Tanto fu dolce mio vocale spirto, che, tolosano, a sé mi trasse Roma, dove mertai le tempie ornar di mirto.
english: So gentle was the spirit of my verse that Rome drew me, son of Toulouse, to her, and there my brow deserved a crown of myrtle.

italian: Stazio la gente ancor di là mi noma: cantai di Tebe, e poi del grande Achille; ma caddi in via con la seconda soma.
english: On earth my name is still remembered—Statius: I sang of Thebes and then of great Achilles; I fell along the way of that last labor.

italian: Al mio ardor fuor seme le faville, che mi scaldar, de la divina fiamma onde sono allumati più di mille;
english: The sparks that warmed me, the seeds of my ardor, were from the holy fire—the same that gave more than a thousand poets light and flame.

italian: de l’Eneïda dico, la qual mamma fummi, e fummi nutrice, poetando: sanz’ essa non fermai peso di dramma.
english: I speak of the Aeneid; when I wrote verse, it was mother to me, it was nurse; my work, without it, would not weigh an ounce.

italian: E per esser vivuto di là quando visse Virgilio, assentirei un sole più che non deggio al mio uscir di bando».
english: And to have lived on earth when Virgil lived— for that I would extend by one more year the time I owe before my exile’s end.”

italian: Volser Virgilio a me queste parole con viso che, tacendo, disse ‘Taci’; ma non può tutto la virtù che vuole;
english: These words made Virgil turn to me, and as he turned, his face, through silence, said: “Be still” (and yet the power of will cannot do all,

italian: ché riso e pianto son tanto seguaci a la passion di che ciascun si spicca, che men seguon voler ne’ più veraci.
english: for tears and smiles are both so faithful to the feelings that have prompted them that true feeling escapes the will that would subdue).

italian: Io pur sorrisi come l’uom ch’ammicca; per che l’ombra si tacque, e riguardommi ne li occhi ove ’l sembiante più si ficca;

english: This was the reason that first prompted them to speak to me. Among themselves they said: “He does not seem to have a fictive body.”

english: “O you who move behind the others not because of sloth but reverence perhaps, give me who burn in thirst and fire your answer.

english: thirsts for cool water. Tell us how you can— as if you’re not yet caught within death’s net— make of yourself a wall against the sun.”

english: Thus one of them had spoken to me; I should now have answered clearly, had I not been fixed on something strangely evident;

italian: ché per lo mezzo del cammino acceso venne gente col viso incontro a questa, la qual mi fece a rimirar sospeso.
english: for in the middle of the burning path, came people moving opposite to these— and I, since they moved left, stared in suspense.

english: There, on all sides, I can see every shade move quickly to embrace another shade, content—they did not pause—with their brief greeting,

english: No sooner is their friendly greeting done than each shade tries to outcry all the rest even before he starts to move ahead,

italian: la nova gente: «Soddoma e Gomorra»; e l’altra: «Ne la vacca entra Pasife, perché ’l torello a sua lussuria corra».
english: the new group shouting: “Sodom and Gomorrah”; the other: “That the bull may hurry toward her lust, Pasiphae hides in the cow.”

italian: Poi, come grue ch’a le montagne Rife volasser parte, e parte inver’ l’arene, queste del gel, quelle del sole schife,
english: Then, just like cranes, of whom a part, to flee the sun, fly north to Riphean mountains, while the rest, to flee the frost, fly toward the sands,

italian: l’una gente sen va, l’altra sen vene; e tornan, lagrimando, a’ primi canti e al gridar che più lor si convene;
english: one group moves with—the other opposite—us; and they return with tears to their first chants and to the shout appropriate to each.

italian: e raccostansi a me, come davanti, essi medesmi che m’avean pregato, attenti ad ascoltar ne’ lor sembianti.
english: And those who had entreated me came close again, in the same way they’d done before; their faces showed how keen they were to listen.

italian: Io, che due volte avea visto lor grato, incominciai: «O anime sicure d’aver, quando che sia, di pace stato,
english: I, seeing their desire once again, began: “O souls who can be sure of gaining the state of peace, whenever that may be,

italian: non son rimase acerbe né mature le membra mie di là, ma son qui meco col sangue suo e con le sue giunture.
english: my limbs—mature or green—have not been left within the world beyond; they’re here with me, together with their blood and with their bones.

italian: Quinci sù vo per non esser più cieco; donna è di sopra che m’acquista grazia, per che ‘l mortal per vostro mondo reco.
english: That I be blind no longer, through this place I pass; above, a lady has gained grace for me; therefore, I bear my mortal body

italian: Ma se la vostra maggior voglia sazia tosto divegna, sì che ‘l ciel v’alberghi ch’è pien d’amore e più ampio si spazia,
english: across your world. So may your deepest longing soon be appeased and you be lodged within the heaven that’s most full of love, most spacious,

italian: ditemi, acciò ch’ancor carte ne verghi, chi siete voi, e chi è quella turba che se ne va di retro a’ vostri terghi».
english: please tell me, so that I may yet transcribe it upon my pages, who you are, and what crowd moves in the direction opposite.”

italian: Non altrimenti stupido si turba lo montanaro, e rimirando ammuta, quando rozzo e salvatico s’inurba,
english: Each shade displayed no less astonishment or less confusion than a mountaineer, who, even as he stares about, falls silent

italian: che ciascun’ ombra fece in sua paruta; ma poi che furon di stupore scarche, lo qual ne li alti cuor tosto s’attuta,
english: when, rough and rustic, he comes to the city; but when they’d set aside astonishment— that’s soon subdued in noble hearts—he who

english: had questioned me before, began again: “Blessed are you who would, in order to die better, store experience of our lands!

italian: La gente che non vien con noi, offese di ciò per che già Cesar, trïunfando, “Regina” contra sé chiamar s’intese:
english: The people moving opposite us shared the sin for which once, while in triumph, Caesar heard ‘Queen’ called out against him; that is why,

italian: però si parton “Soddoma” gridando, rimproverando a sé, com’ hai udito, e aiutan l’arsura vergognando.
english: as they move off from us, they cry out ‘Sodom,’ reproaching their own selves, as you have heard, and through their shame abet the fire’s work.

italian: Nostro peccato fu ermafrodito; ma perché non servammo umana legge, seguendo come bestie l’appetito,
english: Our sin was with the other sex; but since we did not keep the bounds of human law, but served our appetites like beasts, when we

italian: in obbrobrio di noi, per noi si legge, quando partinci, il nome di colei che s’imbestiò ne le ’mbestiate schegge.
english: part from the other ranks, we then repeat, to our disgrace, the name of one who, in the bestial planks, became herself a beast.

italian: Or sai nostri atti e di che fummo rei: se forse a nome vuo’ saper chi semo, tempo non è di dire, e non saprei.
english: You now know why we act so, and you know what our sins were; if you would know our names, time is too short, and I don’t know them all.

italian: Farotti ben di me volere scemo: son Guido Guinizzelli, e già mi purgo per ben dolermi prima ch’a lo stremo».
english: But with regard to me, I’ll satisfy your wish to know: I’m Guido Guinizzelli, purged here because I grieved before my end.”

italian: Quali ne la tristizia di Ligurgo si fer due figli a riveder la madre, tal mi fec’ io, ma non a tanto insurgo,
english: As, after the sad raging of Lycurgus, two sons, finding their mother, had embraced her, so I desired to do—but dared not to—

italian: quand’ io odo nomar sé stesso il padre mio e de li altri miei miglior che mai rime d’amor usar dolci e leggiadre;
english: when I heard him declare his name: the father of me and of the others—those, my betters— who ever used sweet, gracious rhymes of love.

italian: e sanza udire e dir pensoso andai lunga fïata rimirando lui, né, per lo foco, in là più m’appressai.
english: And without hearing, speaking, pensive, I walked on, still gazing at him, a long time, prevented by the fire from drawing closer.

italian: Poi che di riguardar pasciuto fui, tutto m’offersi pronto al suo servigio con l’affermar che fa credere altrui.
english: When I had fed my sight on him, I offered myself—with such a pledge that others must believe—completely ready for his service.

italian: Ed elli a me: «Tu lasci tal vestigio, per quel ch’i’ odo, in me, e tanto chiaro, che Letè nol può tòrre né far bigio.
english: And he to me: “Because of what I hear, you leave a trace within me—one so clear, Lethe itself can’t blur or cancel it.

italian: Ma se le tue parole or ver giuraro, dimmi che è cagion per che dimostri nel dire e nel guardar d’avermi caro».
english: But if your words have now sworn truthfully, do tell me why it is that you have shown in speech and gaze that I am dear to you.”

italian: E io a lui: «Li dolci detti vostri, che, quanto durerà l’uso moderno, faranno cari ancora i loro incostri».
english: And I to him: “It’s your sweet lines that, for as long as modern usage lasts, will still make dear their very inks.” “Brother,” he said,

english: all those who wrote their poems of love or prose romances—let the stupid ones contend, who think that from Limoges there came the best.

italian: A voce più ch’al ver drizzan li volti, e così ferman sua oppinïone prima ch’arte o ragion per lor s’ascolti.
english: They credit rumor rather than the truth, allowing their opinion to be set before they hear what art or reason says.

italian: Così fer molti antichi di Guittone, di grido in grido pur lui dando pregio, fin che l’ha vinto il ver con più persone.
english: So, many of our fathers once persisted, voice after voice, in giving to Guittone the prize—but then, with most, the truth prevailed.

italian: Or se tu hai sì ampio privilegio, che licito ti sia l’andare al chiostro nel quale è Cristo abate del collegio,
english: Now if you are so amply privileged that you will be admitted to the cloister where Christ is abbot of the college, then

italian: falli per me un dir d’un paternostro, quanto bisogna a noi di questo mondo, dove poter peccar non è più nostro».
english: pray say, for me, to Him, a Paternoster— that is, as much of it as those in this place need, since we have lost the power to sin.”

italian: Poi, forse per dar luogo altrui secondo che presso avea, disparve per lo foco, come per l’acqua il pesce andando al fondo.
english: Then, to make place, perhaps, for those behind him, he disappeared into the fire, just as a fish, through water, plunges toward the bottom.

italian: Io mi fei al mostrato innanzi un poco, e dissi ch’al suo nome il mio disire apparecchiava grazïoso loco.
english: Saying that my desire was making ready a place of welcome for his name, I moved ahead a little, toward the one who had

english: been pointed out to me. And he spoke freely: “So does your courteous request please me— I neither could nor would conceal myself

italian: Ieu sui Arnaut, que plor e vau cantan; consiros vei la passada folor, e vei jausen lo joi qu’ esper, denan.
english: from you. I am Arnaut, who, going, weep and sing; with grief, I see my former folly; with joy, I see the hoped—for day draw near.

italian: Ara vos prec, per aquella valor que vos guida al som de l’escalina, sovenha vos a temps de ma dolor!».
english: Now, by the Power that conducts you to the summit of the stairway, I pray you: remember, at time opportune, my pain!”

italian: Poi s’ascose nel foco che li affina.
english: Then, in the fire that refines, he hid.

italian: Sì come quando i primi raggi vibra là dove il suo fattor lo sangue sparse, cadendo Ibero sotto l’alta Libra,
english: Just as, there where its Maker shed His blood, the sun shed its first rays, and Ebro lay beneath high Libra, and the ninth hour’s rays

english: were scorching Ganges’ waves; so here, the sun stood at the point of day’s departure when God’s angel—happy—showed himself to us.

english: He stood along the edge, beyond the flames, singing “Beati mundo corde” in a voice that had more life than ours can claim.

italian: Poscia «Più non si va, se pria non morde, anime sante, il foco: intrate in esso, e al cantar di là non siate sorde»,
english: Then: “Holy souls, you cannot move ahead unless the fire has stung you first: enter the flames, and don’t be deaf to song you’ll hear

english: beyond,” he said when we were close to him; and when I heard him say this, I became like one who has been laid within the grave.

italian: In su le man commesse mi protesi, guardando il foco e imaginando forte umani corpi già veduti accesi.
english: I joined my hands and stretched them out to fend the flames, watching the fire, imagining clearly the human bodies I’d once seen

italian: Volsersi verso me le buone scorte; e Virgilio mi disse: «Figliuol mio, qui può esser tormento, ma non morte.
english: burning. My gentle escorts turned to me, and Virgil said: “My son, though there may be suffering here, there is no death. Remember,

italian: Ricorditi, ricorditi! E se io sovresso Gerïon ti guidai salvo, che farò ora presso più a Dio?
english: remember! If I guided you to safety even upon the back of Geryon, then now, closer to God, what shall I do?

english: Be sure: although you were to spend a full one thousand years within this fire’s center, your head would not be balder by one hair.

english: And if you think I am deceiving you, draw closer to the flames, let your own hands try out, within the fire, your clothing’s hem—

english: put down, by now put down, your every fear; turn toward the fire, and enter, confident!” But I was stubborn, set against my conscience.

english: As, at the name of Thisbe, Pyramus, about to die, opened his eyes, and saw her (when then the mulberry became bloodred),

english: so, when my stubbornness had softened, I, hearing the name that’s always flowering within my mind, turned to my knowing guide.

english: Then he, ahead of me, entered the fire; and he asked Statius, who had walked between us before, dividing us, to go behind.

english: No sooner was I in that fire than I’d have thrown myself in molten glass to find coolness—because those flames were so intense.

english: My gentle father, who would comfort me, kept talking, as we walked, of Beatrice, saying: “I seem to see her eyes already.”

italian: Guidavaci una voce che cantava di là; e noi, attenti pur a lei, venimmo fuor là ove si montava.
english: A voice that sang beyond us was our guide; and we, attentive to that voice, emerged just at the point where it began to climb.

italian: ‘Venite, benedicti Patris mei’, sonò dentro a un lume che lì era, tal che mi vinse e guardar nol potei.
english: “Venite, benedicti Patris mei,” it sang within a light that overcame me: I could not look at such intensity.

english: And we had only tried a few steps when I and my sages sensed the sun had set because the shadow I had cast was spent.

english: each of us made one of those stairs his bed: the nature of the mountain had so weakened our power and desire to climb ahead.

italian: Quali si stanno ruminando manse le capre, state rapide e proterve sovra le cime avante che sien pranse,

italian: e quale il mandrïan che fori alberga, lungo il pecuglio suo queto pernotta, guardando perché fiera non lo sperga;
english: or like the herdsman in the open fields, spending the night beside his quiet flock, watching to see that no beast drives them off;

italian: tali eravamo tutti e tre allotta, io come capra, ed ei come pastori, fasciati quinci e quindi d’alta grotta.
english: such were all three of us at that point—they were like the herdsmen, I was like the goat; upon each side of us, high rock walls rose.

italian: Poco parer potea lì del di fori; ma, per quel poco, vedea io le stelle di lor solere e più chiare e maggiori.
english: From there, one saw but little of the sky, but in that little, I could see the stars brighter and larger than they usually are.

italian: Sì ruminando e sì mirando in quelle, mi prese il sonno; il sonno che sovente, anzi che ’l fatto sia, sa le novelle.
english: But while I watched the stars, in reverie, sleep overcame me—sleep, which often sees, before it happens, what is yet to be.

italian: Ne l’ora, credo, che de l’orïente prima raggiò nel monte Citerea, che di foco d’amor par sempre ardente,
english: It was the hour, I think, when Cytherea, who always seems aflame with fires of love, first shines upon the mountains from the east,

italian: giovane e bella in sogno mi parea donna vedere andar per una landa cogliendo fiori; e cantando dicea:
english: that, in my dream, I seemed to see a woman both young and fair; along a plain she gathered flowers, and even as she sang, she said:

italian: «Sappia qualunque il mio nome dimanda ch’i’ mi son Lia, e vo movendo intorno le belle mani a farmi una ghirlanda.
english: “Whoever asks my name, know that I’m Leah, and I apply my lovely hands to fashion a garland of the flowers I have gathered.

italian: Per piacermi a lo specchio, qui m’addorno; ma mia suora Rachel mai non si smaga dal suo miraglio, e siede tutto giorno.
english: To find delight within this mirror I adorn myself; whereas my sister Rachel never deserts her mirror; there she sits

english: all day; she longs to see her fair eyes gazing, as I, to see my hands adorning, long: she is content with seeing, I with labor.”

italian: le tenebre fuggian da tutti lati, e ’l sonno mio con esse; ond’ io leva’mi, veggendo i gran maestri già levati.
english: the shadows fled upon all sides; my sleep fled with them; and at this, I woke and saw that the great teachers had already risen.

italian: «Quel dolce pome che per tanti rami cercando va la cura de’ mortali, oggi porrà in pace le tue fami».
english: “Today your hungerings will find their peace through that sweet fruit the care of mortals seeks among so many branches.” This, the speech,

english: When all the staircase lay beneath us and we’d reached the highest step, then Virgil set his eyes insistently on me and said:
