italian: Tratto t’ho qui con ingegno e con arte; lo tuo piacere omai prendi per duce; fuor se’ de l’erte vie, fuor se’ de l’arte.
english: I’ve brought you here through intellect and art; from now on, let your pleasure be your guide; you’re past the steep and past the narrow paths.

italian: Vedi lo sol che ’n fronte ti riluce; vedi l’erbette, i fiori e li arbuscelli che qui la terra sol da sé produce.
english: Look at the sun that shines upon your brow; look at the grasses, flowers, and the shrubs born here, spontaneously, of the earth.

italian: Mentre che vegnan lieti li occhi belli che, lagrimando, a te venir mi fenno, seder ti puoi e puoi andar tra elli.
english: Among them, you can rest or walk until the coming of the glad and lovely eyes— those eyes that, weeping, sent me to your side.

italian: Non aspettar mio dir più né mio cenno; libero, dritto e sano è tuo arbitrio, e fallo fora non fare a suo senno:
english: Await no further word or sign from me: your will is free, erect, and whole—to act against that will would be to err: therefore

italian: per ch’io te sovra te corono e mitrio».
english: I crown and miter you over yourself.”

italian: Vago già di cercar dentro e dintorno la divina foresta spessa e viva, ch’a li occhi temperava il novo giorno,
english: Now keen to search within, to search around that forest—dense, alive with green, divine— which tempered the new day before my eyes,

italian: sanza più aspettar, lasciai la riva, prendendo la campagna lento lento su per lo suol che d’ogne parte auliva.
english: without delay, I left behind the rise and took the plain, advancing slowly, slowly across the ground where every part was fragrant.

italian: Un’aura dolce, sanza mutamento avere in sé, mi feria per la fronte non di più colpo che soave vento;
english: A gentle breeze, which did not seem to vary within itself, was striking at my brow but with no greater force than a kind wind’s,

italian: per cui le fronde, tremolando, pronte tutte quante piegavano a la parte u’ la prim’ ombra gitta il santo monte;
english: a wind that made the trembling boughs—they all bent eagerly—incline in the direction of morning shadows from the holy mountain;

italian: non però dal loro esser dritto sparte tanto, che li augelletti per le cime lasciasser d’operare ogne lor arte;
english: but they were not deflected with such force as to disturb the little birds upon the branches in the practice of their arts;

italian: ma con piena letizia l’ore prime, cantando, ricevieno intra le foglie, che tenevan bordone a le sue rime,
english: for to the leaves, with song, birds welcomed those first hours of the morning joyously, and leaves supplied the burden to their rhymes—

italian: tal qual di ramo in ramo si raccoglie per la pineta in su ’l lito di Chiassi, quand’ Ëolo scilocco fuor discioglie.
english: just like the wind that sounds from branch to branch along the shore of Classe, through the pines when Aeolus has set Sirocco loose.

italian: Già m’avean trasportato i lenti passi dentro a la selva antica tanto, ch’io non potea rivedere ond’ io mi ’ntrassi;
english: Now, though my steps were slow, I’d gone so far into the ancient forest that I could no longer see where I had made my entry;

italian: ed ecco più andar mi tolse un rio, che ’nver’ sinistra con sue picciole onde piegava l’erba che ’n sua ripa uscìo.
english: and there I came upon a stream that blocked the path of my advance; its little waves bent to the left the grass along its banks.

italian: Tutte l’acque che son di qua più monde, parrieno avere in sé mistura alcuna verso di quella, che nulla nasconde,
english: All of the purest waters here on earth, when matched against that stream, would seem to be touched by impurity; it hides no thing—

italian: avvegna che si mova bruna bruna sotto l’ombra perpetüa, che mai raggiar non lascia sole ivi né luna.
english: that stream—although it moves, dark, dark, beneath the never—ending shadows, which allow no ray of sun or moon to reach those waters.

italian: Coi piè ristetti e con li occhi passai di là dal fiumicello, per mirare la gran varïazion d’i freschi mai;
english: I halted, and I set my eyes upon the farther bank, to look at the abundant variety of newly—flowered boughs;

italian: e là m’apparve, sì com’ elli appare subitamente cosa che disvia per maraviglia tutto altro pensare,
english: and there, just like a thing that, in appearing most suddenly, repels all other thoughts, so great is the astonishment it brings,

italian: una donna soletta che si gia e cantando e scegliendo fior da fiore ond’ era pinta tutta la sua via.
english: I saw a solitary woman moving, singing, and gathering up flower on flower— the flowers that colored all of her pathway.

italian: «Deh, bella donna, che a’ raggi d’amore ti scaldi, s’i’ vo’ credere a’ sembianti che soglion esser testimon del core,
english: “I pray you, lovely lady, you who warm yourself with rays of love, if I may trust your looks—which often evidence the heart—

italian: vegnati in voglia di trarreti avanti», diss’ io a lei, «verso questa rivera, tanto ch’io possa intender che tu canti.
english: may it please you,” I asked of her, “to move ahead and closer to this river, so that I may understand what you are singing.

italian: Tu mi fai rimembrar dove e qual era Proserpina nel tempo che perdette la madre lei, ed ella primavera».
english: You have reminded me of where and what— just when her mother was deprived of her and she deprived of spring—Proserpina was.”

italian: Come si volge, con le piante strette a terra e intra sé, donna che balli, e piede innanzi piede a pena mette,
english: As, when she turns, a woman, dancing, keeps her soles close to the ground and to each other and scarcely lets one foot precede the other,

italian: volsesi in su i vermigli e in su i gialli fioretti verso me, non altrimenti che vergine che li occhi onesti avvalli;
english: so did she turn, upon the little red and yellow flowers, to me, no differently than would a virgin, lowering chaste eyes.

italian: e fece i prieghi miei esser contenti, sì appressando sé, che ’l dolce suono veniva a me co’ suoi intendimenti.
english: I had beseeched, and I was satisfied, for she approached so close that the sweet sound that reached me then became intelligible.

italian: Tosto che fu là dove l’erbe sono bagnate già da l’onde del bel fiume, di levar li occhi suoi mi fece dono.
english: No sooner had she reached the point where that fair river’s waves could barely bathe the grass, than she gave me this gift: lifting her eyes.

italian: Non credo che splendesse tanto lume sotto le ciglia a Venere, trafitta dal figlio fuor di tutto suo costume.
english: I do not think a light so bright had shone beneath the lids of Venus when her son pierced her in extraordinary fashion.

italian: Ella ridea da l’altra riva dritta, trattando più color con le sue mani, che l’alta terra sanza seme gitta.
english: Erect, along the farther bank, she smiled, her hands entwining varicolored flowers, which that high land, needing no seed, engenders.

italian: Tre passi ci facea il fiume lontani; ma Elesponto, là ’ve passò Serse, ancora freno a tutti orgogli umani,
english: The river kept us just three steps apart; but even Hellespont, where Xerxes crossed— a case that still curbs all men’s arrogance—

italian: più odio da Leandro non sofferse per mareggiare intra Sesto e Abido, che quel da me perch’ allor non s’aperse.
english: did not provoke more hatred in Leander when rough seas ran from Abydos to Sestos, than hatred I bestowed upon that river

italian: «Voi siete nuovi, e forse perch’ io rido», cominciò ella, «in questo luogo eletto a l’umana natura per suo nido,
english: when it refused to open. She began: “You are new here and may—because I smile in this place, chosen to be mankind’s nest—

italian: maravigliando tienvi alcun sospetto; ma luce rende il salmo Delectasti , che puote disnebbiar vostro intelletto.
english: wonder, perplexed, unable to detect the cause; but light to clear your intellect is in the psalm beginning ‘Delectasti.’

italian: E tu che se’ dinanzi e mi pregasti, dì s’altro vuoli udir; ch’i’ venni presta ad ogne tua question tanto che basti».
english: And you, who have stepped forward, who beseeched me, tell me if you’d hear more; I have come ready for all your questions till you’re satisfied.”

italian: «L’acqua», diss’ io, «e ’l suon de la foresta impugnan dentro a me novella fede di cosa ch’io udi’ contraria a questa».
english: I said: “The water and the murmuring forest contend, in me, against the recent credence I gave to words denying their existence.”

italian: Ond’ ella: «Io dicerò come procede per sua cagion ciò ch’ammirar ti face, e purgherò la nebbia che ti fiede.
english: At this, she said: “I’ll tell you how the source of your amazement has its special cause; I’ll clear the cloud that’s left you so distraught.

italian: Lo sommo Ben, che solo esso a sé piace, fé l’uom buono e a bene, e questo loco diede per arr’ a lui d’etterna pace.
english: The Highest Good, whose sole joy is Himself, made man to be—and to enact—good; He gave man this place as pledge of endless peace.

italian: Per sua difalta qui dimorò poco; per sua difalta in pianto e in affanno cambiò onesto riso e dolce gioco.
english: Man’s fault made brief his stay here; and man’s fault made him exchange frank laughter and sweet sport for lamentation and for anxiousness.

italian: Perché ’l turbar che sotto da sé fanno l’essalazion de l’acqua e de la terra, che quanto posson dietro al calor vanno,
english: Below this mountain, land and water vapors, which follow heat as far as they are able, produce their perturbations; to prevent

italian: a l’uomo non facesse alcuna guerra, questo monte salìo verso ’l ciel tanto, e libero n’è d’indi ove si serra.
english: them from molesting man placed here, this mountain rose up this close to Heaven; from the point where its gate locks, it’s free of such disturbance.

italian: Or perché in circuito tutto quanto l’aere si volge con la prima volta, se non li è rotto il cerchio d’alcun canto,
english: Now, since all of the atmosphere revolves within a circle, moved by the first circling, unless its round is broken at some point,

italian: in questa altezza ch’è tutta disciolta ne l’aere vivo, tal moto percuote, e fa sonar la selva perch’ è folta;
english: against this height, which stands completely free within the living air, that motion strikes; and since these woods are dense, they echo it.

italian: e la percossa pianta tanto puote, che de la sua virtute l’aura impregna e quella poi, girando, intorno scuote;
english: And when a plant is struck, its power is such that it impregnates air with seeding force; the air, revolving, casts this seed abroad;

italian: e l’altra terra, secondo ch’è degna per sé e per suo ciel, concepe e figlia di diverse virtù diverse legna.
english: the other hemisphere, depending on the nature of its land and sky, conceives and bears, from diverse powers, diverse trees.

italian: Non parrebbe di là poi maraviglia, udito questo, quando alcuna pianta sanza seme palese vi s’appiglia.
english: If what I’ve said were known, you would not need to be amazed on earth when growing things take root but have no seed that can be seen.

italian: E saper dei che la campagna santa dove tu se’, d’ogne semenza è piena, e frutto ha in sé che di là non si schianta.
english: And you must know: the holy plain on which you find yourself is full of every seed; and it has fruit that—there—cannot be gathered.

italian: L’acqua che vedi non surge di vena che ristori vapor che gel converta, come fiume ch’acquista e perde lena;
english: The water that you see does not spring from a vein that vapor—cold—condensed—restores, like rivers that acquire or lose their force;

italian: ma esce di fontana salda e certa, che tanto dal voler di Dio riprende, quant’ ella versa da due parti aperta.
english: it issues from a pure and changeless fountain, which by the will of God regains as much as, on two sides, it pours and it divides.

italian: Da questa parte con virtù discende che toglie altrui memoria del peccato; da l’altra d’ogne ben fatto la rende.
english: On this side it descends with power to end one’s memory of sin; and on the other, it can restore recall of each good deed.

italian: Quinci Letè; così da l’altro lato Eünoè si chiama, e non adopra se quinci e quindi pria non è gustato:
english: To one side, it is Lethe; on the other, Eunoe; neither stream is efficacious unless the other’s waters have been tasted:

italian: a tutti altri sapori esto è di sopra. E avvegna ch’assai possa esser sazia la sete tua perch’ io più non ti scuopra,
english: their savor is above all other sweetness. Although your thirst might well be satisfied even if I revealed no more to you,

italian: darotti un corollario ancor per grazia; né credo che ’l mio dir ti sia men caro, se oltre promession teco si spazia.
english: I’ll give you freely, too, a corollary; nor do I think my words will be less welcome to you if they extend beyond my promise.

italian: Quelli ch’anticamente poetaro l’età de l’oro e suo stato felice, forse in Parnaso esto loco sognaro.
english: Those ancients who in poetry presented the golden age, who sang its happy state, perhaps, in their Parnassus, dreamt this place.

italian: Qui fu innocente l’umana radice; qui primavera sempre e ogne frutto; nettare è questo di che ciascun dice».
english: Here, mankind’s root was innocent; and here were every fruit and never—ending spring; these streams—the nectar of which poets sing.”

italian: Io mi rivolsi ’n dietro allora tutto a’ miei poeti, e vidi che con riso udito avëan l’ultimo costrutto;
english: Then I turned round completely, and I faced my poets; I could see that they had heard with smiles this final corollary spoken;

italian: poi a la bella donna torna’ il viso.
english: that done, my eyes returned to the fair woman.

italian: Cantando come donna innamorata, continüò col fin di sue parole: ‘Beati quorum tecta sunt peccata!’.
english: Her words were done, but without interruption she sang—like an enamored woman—thus: “Beati quorum tecta sunt peccata!”

italian: E come ninfe che si givan sole per le salvatiche ombre, disïando qual di veder, qual di fuggir lo sole,
english: And just as nymphs who used to walk alone among the woodland shadows, some desiring to see and some to flee the sun, so she

italian: allor si mosse contra ’l fiume, andando su per la riva; e io pari di lei, picciol passo con picciol seguitando.
english: moved countercurrent as she walked along the riverbank; and following her short footsteps with my own steps, I matched her pace.

italian: Non eran cento tra ’ suoi passi e ’ miei, quando le ripe igualmente dier volta, per modo ch’a levante mi rendei.
english: Her steps and mine together did not sum one hundred when the banks, still parallel, so curved about that I was facing east.

italian: Né ancor fu così nostra via molta, quando la donna tutta a me si torse, dicendo: «Frate mio, guarda e ascolta».
english: Nor had we gone much farther on that path when she turned fully round toward me and said: “My brother, look and listen”; and I saw

italian: Ed ecco un lustro sùbito trascorse da tutte parti per la gran foresta, tal che di balenar mi mise in forse.
english: a sudden radiance that swept across the mighty forest on all sides—and I was wondering if lightning had not struck.

italian: Ma perché ’l balenar, come vien, resta, e quel, durando, più e più splendeva, nel mio pensier dicea: ‘Che cosa è questa?’.
english: But since, when lightning strikes, it stops at once, while that light, lingering, increased its force, within my mind I asked: “What thing is this?”

italian: E una melodia dolce correva per l’aere luminoso; onde buon zelo mi fé riprender l’ardimento d’Eva,
english: And through the incandescent air there ran sweet melody; at which, just indignation made me rebuke the arrogance of Eve

italian: che là dove ubidia la terra e ’l cielo, femmina, sola e pur testé formata, non sofferse di star sotto alcun velo;
english: because, where earth and heaven were obedient, a solitary woman, just created, found any veil at all beyond endurance;

italian: sotto ’l qual se divota fosse stata, avrei quelle ineffabili delizie sentite prima e più lunga fïata.
english: if she had been devout beneath her veil, I should have savored those ineffable delights before, and for a longer time.

italian: Mentr’ io m’andava tra tante primizie de l’etterno piacer tutto sospeso, e disïoso ancora a più letizie,
english: While I moved on, completely rapt, among so many first fruits of eternal pleasure, and longing for still greater joys, the air

italian: dinanzi a noi, tal quale un foco acceso, ci si fé l’aere sotto i verdi rami; e ’l dolce suon per canti era già inteso.
english: before us altered underneath the green branches, becoming like an ardent fire, and now the sweet sound was distinctly song.

italian: O sacrosante Vergini, se fami, freddi o vigilie mai per voi soffersi, cagion mi sprona ch’io mercé vi chiami.
english: O Virgins, sacrosanct, if I have ever, for your sake, suffered vigils, cold, and hunger, great need makes me entreat my recompense.

italian: Or convien che Elicona per me versi, e Uranìe m’aiuti col suo coro forti cose a pensar mettere in versi.
english: Now Helicon must pour its fountains for me, Urania must help me with her choir to put in verses things hard to conceive.

italian: Poco più oltre, sette alberi d’oro falsava nel parere il lungo tratto del mezzo ch’era ancor tra noi e loro;
english: Not far beyond, we made out seven trees of gold, though the long stretch of air between those trees and us had falsified their semblance;

italian: ma quand’ i’ fui sì presso di lor fatto, che l’obietto comun, che ’l senso inganna, non perdea per distanza alcun suo atto,
english: but when I’d drawn so close that things perceived through mingled senses, which delude, did not, now they were nearer, lose their real features,

italian: la virtù ch’a ragion discorso ammanna, sì com’ elli eran candelabri apprese, e ne le voci del cantare ‘Osanna’ .
english: the power that offers reason matter judged those trees to be—what they were—candelabra, and what those voices sang to be “Hosanna.”

italian: Di sopra fiammeggiava il bello arnese più chiaro assai che luna per sereno di mezza notte nel suo mezzo mese.
english: The upper part of those fair candles flamed more radiantly than the midmonth moon shines at midnight in an untroubled sky.

italian: Io mi rivolsi d’ammirazion pieno al buon Virgilio, ed esso mi rispuose con vista carca di stupor non meno.
english: Full of astonishment, I turned to my good Virgil; but he only answered me with eyes that were no less amazed than mine.

italian: Indi rendei l’aspetto a l’alte cose che si movieno incontr’ a noi sì tardi, che foran vinte da novelle spose.
english: Then I looked at the extraordinary things that were moving toward us—but so slowly that even brides just wed would move more quickly.

italian: La donna mi sgridò: «Perché pur ardi sì ne l’affetto de le vive luci, e ciò che vien di retro a lor non guardi?».
english: The woman chided me: “Why are you only so eager to behold the living lights and not in seeing what comes after them?”

italian: Genti vid’ io allor, come a lor duci, venire appresso, vestite di bianco; e tal candor di qua già mai non fuci.
english: Then I saw people following those candles, as if behind their guides, and they wore white— whiteness that, in this world, has never been.

italian: L’acqua imprendëa dal sinistro fianco, e rendea me la mia sinistra costa, s’io riguardava in lei, come specchio anco.
english: The water, to my left, reflected flames, and it reflected, too, my left—hand side if I gazed into it, as in a mirror.

italian: Quand’ io da la mia riva ebbi tal posta, che solo il fiume mi facea distante, per veder meglio ai passi diedi sosta,
english: When I was at a point along my shore where all that sundered me from them was water, I stayed my steps in order to see better,

italian: e vidi le fiammelle andar davante, lasciando dietro a sé l’aere dipinto, e di tratti pennelli avean sembiante;
english: and I could see the candle flames move forward, leaving the air behind them colored like the strokes a painter’s brush might have described,

italian: sì che lì sopra rimanea distinto di sette liste, tutte in quei colori onde fa l’arco il Sole e Delia il cinto.
english: so that the air above that retinue was streaked with seven bands in every hue of which the rainbow’s made and Delia’s girdle.

italian: Questi ostendali in dietro eran maggiori che la mia vista; e, quanto a mio avviso, diece passi distavan quei di fori.
english: These pennants stretched far back, beyond my vision; as for the width they filled, I judged the distance between the outer ones to be ten paces.

italian: Sotto così bel ciel com’ io diviso, ventiquattro seniori, a due a due, coronati venien di fiordaliso.
english: Beneath the handsome sky I have described, twenty—four elders moved on, two by two, and they had wreaths of lilies on their heads.

italian: Tutti cantavan: « Benedicta tue ne le figlie d’Adamo, e benedette sieno in etterno le bellezze tue!».
english: And all were singing: “You, among the daughters of Adam, benedicta are; and may your beauties blessed be eternally.”

italian: Poscia che i fiori e l’altre fresche erbette a rimpetto di me da l’altra sponda libere fuor da quelle genti elette,
english: After the flowers and the other fresh plants facing me, along the farther shore, had seen those chosen people disappear,

italian: sì come luce luce in ciel seconda, vennero appresso lor quattro animali, coronati ciascun di verde fronda.
english: then—as in heaven, star will follow star— the elders gone, four animals came on; and each of them had green leaves as his crown;

italian: Ognuno era pennuto di sei ali; le penne piene d’occhi; e li occhi d’Argo, se fosser vivi, sarebber cotali.
english: each had six wings as plumage, and those plumes were full of eyes; they would be very like the eyes of Argus, were his eyes alive.

italian: A descriver lor forme più non spargo rime, lettor; ch’altra spesa mi strigne, tanto ch’a questa non posso esser largo;
english: Reader, I am not squandering more rhymes in order to describe their forms; since I must spend elsewhere, I can’t be lavish here;

italian: ma leggi Ezechïel, che li dipigne come li vide da la fredda parte venir con vento e con nube e con igne;
english: but read Ezekiel, for he has drawn those animals approaching from the north; with wings and cloud and fire, he painted them.

italian: e quali i troverai ne le sue carte, tali eran quivi, salvo ch’a le penne Giovanni è meco e da lui si diparte.
english: And just as you will find them in his pages, such were they here, except that John’s with me as to their wings; with him, John disagrees.

italian: Lo spazio dentro a lor quattro contenne un carro, in su due rote, trïunfale, ch’al collo d’un grifon tirato venne.
english: The space between the four of them contained a chariot—triumphal—on two wheels, tied to a griffin’s neck and drawn by him.

italian: Esso tendeva in sù l’una e l’altra ale tra la mezzana e le tre e tre liste, sì ch’a nulla, fendendo, facea male.
english: His wings, stretched upward, framed the middle band with three bands on each outer side, so that, though he cleaved air, he left the bands intact.

italian: Tanto salivan che non eran viste; le membra d’oro avea quant’ era uccello, e bianche l’altre, di vermiglio miste.
english: His wings—so high that they were lost to sight; his limbs were gold as far as he was bird; the rest of him was white mixed with bloodred.

italian: Non che Roma di carro così bello rallegrasse Affricano, o vero Augusto, ma quel del Sol saria pover con ello;
english: Not only did no chariot so handsome gladden Rome’s Africanus or Augustus himself—even the Sun’s own cannot match it;

italian: quel del Sol che, svïando, fu combusto per l’orazion de la Terra devota, quando fu Giove arcanamente giusto.
english: the Sun’s—which, gone astray, was burnt to cinders because Earth offered up her pious prayers, when Jove, in ways not known to us, was just.

italian: Tre donne in giro da la destra rota venian danzando; l’una tanto rossa ch’a pena fora dentro al foco nota;
english: Three circling women, then advancing, danced: at the right wheel; the first of them, so red that even in a flame she’d not be noted;

italian: l’altr’ era come se le carni e l’ossa fossero state di smeraldo fatte; la terza parea neve testé mossa;
english: the second seemed as if her flesh and bone were fashioned out of emerald; the third seemed to be newly fallen snow. And now

italian: e or parëan da la bianca tratte, or da la rossa; e dal canto di questa l’altre toglien l’andare e tarde e ratte.
english: the white one seemed to lead them, now the red; and from the way in which the leader chanted, the others took their pace, now slow, now rapid.

italian: Da la sinistra quattro facean festa, in porpore vestite, dietro al modo d’una di lor ch’avea tre occhi in testa.
english: Upon the left, four other women, dressed in crimson, danced, depending on the cadence of one of them, with three eyes in her head.

italian: Appresso tutto il pertrattato nodo vidi due vecchi in abito dispari, ma pari in atto e onesto e sodo.
english: Behind all of the group I have described I saw two elders, different in their dress but like in manner—grave and decorous.

italian: L’un si mostrava alcun de’ famigliari di quel sommo Ipocràte che natura a li animali fé ch’ell’ ha più cari;
english: The first seemed to be one of the disciples of great Hippocrates, whom nature made for those who are her dearest living beings;

italian: mostrava l’altro la contraria cura con una spada lucida e aguta, tal che di qua dal rio mi fé paura.
english: the other showed an opposite concern— his sword was bright and sharp, and even on this near side of the river, I felt fear.

italian: Poi vidi quattro in umile paruta; e di retro da tutti un vecchio solo venir, dormendo, con la faccia arguta.
english: Then I saw four of humble aspect; and, when all the rest had passed, a lone old man, his features keen, advanced, as if in sleep.

italian: E questi sette col primaio stuolo erano abitüati, ma di gigli dintorno al capo non facëan brolo,
english: The clothes these seven wore were like the elders’ in the first file, except that these had no garlands of lilies round their brow; instead,

italian: anzi di rose e d’altri fior vermigli; giurato avria poco lontano aspetto che tutti ardesser di sopra da’ cigli.
english: roses and other red flowers wreathed their heads; one seeing them less closely would have sworn that all of them had flames above their eyebrows.

italian: E quando il carro a me fu a rimpetto, un tuon s’udì, e quelle genti degne parvero aver l’andar più interdetto,
english: And when the chariot stood facing me, I heard a bolt of thunder; and it seemed to block the path of that good company,
