english: not speak; for nearing its desired end, our intellect sinks into an abyss so deep that memory fails to follow it.

italian: Veramente quant’ io del regno santo ne la mia mente potei far tesoro, sarà ora materia del mio canto.
english: Nevertheless, as much as I, within my mind, could treasure of the holy kingdom shall now become the matter of my song.

italian: O buono Appollo, a l’ultimo lavoro fammi del tuo valor sì fatto vaso, come dimandi a dar l’amato alloro.
english: O good Apollo, for this final task make me the vessel of your excellence, what you, to merit your loved laurel, ask.

italian: Infino a qui l’un giogo di Parnaso assai mi fu; ma or con amendue m’è uopo intrar ne l’aringo rimaso.
english: Until this point, one of Parnassus’ peaks sufficed for me; but now I face the test, the agon that is left; I need both crests.

italian: Entra nel petto mio, e spira tue sì come quando Marsïa traesti de la vagina de le membra sue.
english: Enter into my breast; within me breathe the very power you made manifest when you drew Marsyas out from his limbs’ sheath.

italian: O divina virtù, se mi ti presti tanto che l’ombra del beato regno segnata nel mio capo io manifesti,
english: O godly force, if you so lend yourself to me, that I might show the shadow of the blessed realm inscribed within my mind,

italian: vedra’mi al piè del tuo diletto legno venire, e coronarmi de le foglie che la materia e tu mi farai degno.
english: then you would see me underneath the tree you love; there I shall take as crown the leaves of which my theme and you shall make me worthy.

italian: Sì rade volte, padre, se ne coglie per trïunfare o cesare o poeta, colpa e vergogna de l’umane voglie,
english: So seldom, father, are those garlands gathered for triumph of a ruler or a poet— a sign of fault or shame in human wills—

italian: che parturir letizia in su la lieta delfica deïtà dovria la fronda peneia, quando alcun di sé asseta.
english: that when Peneian branches can incite someone to long and thirst for them, delight must fill the happy Delphic deity.

italian: Poca favilla gran fiamma seconda: forse di retro a me con miglior voci si pregherà perché Cirra risponda.
english: Great fire can follow a small spark: there may be better voices after me to pray to Cyrrha’s god for aid—that he may answer.

italian: Surge ai mortali per diverse foci la lucerna del mondo; ma da quella che quattro cerchi giugne con tre croci,
english: The lantern of the world approaches mortals by varied paths; but on that way which links four circles with three crosses, it emerges

italian: con miglior corso e con migliore stella esce congiunta, e la mondana cera più a suo modo tempera e suggella.
english: joined to a better constellation and along a better course, and it can temper and stamp the world’s wax more in its own manner.

italian: Fatto avea di là mane e di qua sera tal foce, e quasi tutto era là bianco quello emisperio, e l’altra parte nera,
english: Its entry from that point of the horizon brought morning there and evening here; almost all of that hemisphere was white—while ours

italian: quando Beatrice in sul sinistro fianco vidi rivolta e riguardar nel sole: aquila sì non li s’affisse unquanco.
english: was dark—when I saw Beatrice turn round and left, that she might see the sun; no eagle has ever stared so steadily at it.

italian: E sì come secondo raggio suole uscir del primo e risalire in suso, pur come pelegrin che tornar vuole,
english: And as a second ray will issue from the first and reascend, much like a pilgrim who seeks his home again, so on her action,

italian: così de l’atto suo, per li occhi infuso ne l’imagine mia, il mio si fece, e fissi li occhi al sole oltre nostr’ uso.
english: fed by my eyes to my imagination, my action drew, and on the sun I set my sight more than we usually do.

italian: Molto è licito là, che qui non lece a le nostre virtù, mercé del loco fatto per proprio de l’umana spece.
english: More is permitted to our powers there than is permitted here, by virtue of that place, made for mankind as its true home.

italian: Io nol soffersi molto, né sì poco, ch’io nol vedessi sfavillar dintorno, com’ ferro che bogliente esce del foco;
english: I did not bear it long, but not so briefly as not to see it sparkling round about, like molten iron emerging from the fire;

italian: e di sùbito parve giorno a giorno essere aggiunto, come quei che puote avesse il ciel d’un altro sole addorno.
english: and suddenly it seemed that day had been added to day, as if the One who can had graced the heavens with a second sun.

italian: Beatrice tutta ne l’etterne rote fissa con li occhi stava; e io in lei le luci fissi, di là sù rimote.
english: The eyes of Beatrice were all intent on the eternal circles; from the sun, I turned aside; I set my eyes on her.

italian: Nel suo aspetto tal dentro mi fei, qual si fé Glauco nel gustar de l’erba che ’l fé consorto in mar de li altri dèi.
english: In watching her, within me I was changed as Glaucus changed, tasting the herb that made him a companion of the other sea gods.

italian: Trasumanar significar per verba non si poria; però l’essemplo basti a cui esperïenza grazia serba.
english: Passing beyond the human cannot be worded; let Glaucus serve as simile— until grace grant you the experience.

italian: S’i’ era sol di me quel che creasti novellamente, amor che ’l ciel governi, tu ’l sai, che col tuo lume mi levasti.
english: Whether I only was the part of me that You created last, You—governing the heavens—know: it was Your light that raised me.

italian: Quando la rota che tu sempiterni desiderato, a sé mi fece atteso con l’armonia che temperi e discerni,
english: When that wheel which You make eternal through the heavens’ longing for You drew me with the harmony You temper and distinguish,

italian: parvemi tanto allor del cielo acceso de la fiamma del sol, che pioggia o fiume lago non fece alcun tanto disteso.
english: the fire of the sun then seemed to me to kindle so much of the sky, that rain or river never formed so broad a lake.

italian: La novità del suono e ’l grande lume di lor cagion m’accesero un disio mai non sentito di cotanto acume.
english: The newness of the sound and the great light incited me to learn their cause—I was more keen than I had ever been before.

italian: Ond’ ella, che vedea me sì com’ io, a quïetarmi l’animo commosso, pria ch’io a dimandar, la bocca aprio,
english: And she who read me as I read myself, to quiet the commotion in my mind, opened her lips before I opened mine

italian: e cominciò: «Tu stesso ti fai grosso col falso imaginar, sì che non vedi ciò che vedresti se l’avessi scosso.
english: to ask, and she began: “You make yourself obtuse with false imagining; you can not see what you would see if you dispelled it.

italian: Tu non se’ in terra, sì come tu credi; ma folgore, fuggendo il proprio sito, non corse come tu ch’ad esso riedi».
english: You are not on the earth as you believe; but lightning, flying from its own abode, is less swift than you are, returning home.”

italian: S’io fui del primo dubbio disvestito per le sorrise parolette brevi, dentro ad un nuovo più fu’ inretito,
english: While I was freed from my first doubt by these brief words she smiled to me, I was yet caught in new perplexity. I said: “I was

italian: e dissi: «Già contento requïevi di grande ammirazion; ma ora ammiro com’ io trascenda questi corpi levi».
english: content already; after such great wonder, I rested. But again I wonder how my body rises past these lighter bodies.”

italian: Ond’ ella, appresso d’un pïo sospiro, li occhi drizzò ver’ me con quel sembiante che madre fa sovra figlio deliro,
english: At which, after a sigh of pity, she settled her eyes on me with the same look a mother casts upon a raving child,

italian: e cominciò: «Le cose tutte quante hanno ordine tra loro, e questo è forma che l’universo a Dio fa simigliante.
english: and she began: “All things, among themselves, possess an order; and this order is the form that makes the universe like God.

italian: Qui veggion l’alte creature l’orma de l’etterno valore, il qual è fine al quale è fatta la toccata norma.
english: Here do the higher beings see the imprint of the Eternal Worth, which is the end to which the pattern I have mentioned tends.

italian: Ne l’ordine ch’io dico sono accline tutte nature, per diverse sorti, più al principio loro e men vicine;
english: Within that order, every nature has its bent, according to a different station, nearer or less near to its origin.

italian: onde si muovono a diversi porti per lo gran mar de l’essere, e ciascuna con istinto a lei dato che la porti.
english: Therefore, these natures move to different ports across the mighty sea of being, each given the impulse that will bear it on.

italian: Questi ne porta il foco inver’ la luna; questi ne’ cor mortali è permotore; questi la terra in sé stringe e aduna;
english: This impulse carries fire to the moon; this is the motive force in mortal creatures; this binds the earth together, makes it one.

italian: né pur le creature che son fore d’intelligenza quest’ arco saetta ma quelle c’hanno intelletto e amore.
english: Not only does the shaft shot from this bow strike creatures lacking intellect, but those who have intelligence, and who can love.

italian: La provedenza, che cotanto assetta, del suo lume fa ’l ciel sempre quïeto nel qual si volge quel c’ha maggior fretta;
english: The Providence that has arrayed all this forever quiets—with Its light—that heaven in which the swiftest of the spheres revolves;

italian: e ora lì, come a sito decreto, cen porta la virtù di quella corda che ciò che scocca drizza in segno lieto.
english: to there, as toward a destined place, we now are carried by the power of the bow that always aims its shaft at a glad mark.

italian: Vero è che, come forma non s’accorda molte fïate a l’intenzion de l’arte, perch’ a risponder la materia è sorda,
english: Yet it is true that, even as a shape may, often, not accord with art’s intent, since matter may be unresponsive, deaf,

italian: così da questo corso si diparte talor la creatura, c’ha podere di piegar, così pinta, in altra parte;
english: so, from this course, the creature strays at times because he has the power, once impelled, to swerve elsewhere; as lightning from a cloud

italian: e sì come veder si può cadere foco di nube, sì l’impeto primo l’atterra torto da falso piacere.
english: is seen to fall, so does the first impulse, when man has been diverted by false pleasure, turn him toward earth. You should—if I am right—

italian: Non dei più ammirar, se bene stimo, lo tuo salir, se non come d’un rivo se d’alto monte scende giuso ad imo.
english: not feel more marvel at your climbing than you would were you considering a stream that from a mountain’s height falls to its base.

italian: Maraviglia sarebbe in te se, privo d’impedimento, giù ti fossi assiso, com’ a terra quïete in foco vivo».
english: It would be cause for wonder in you if, no longer hindered, you remained below, as if, on earth, a living flame stood still.”

italian: Quinci rivolse inver’ lo cielo il viso.
english: Then she again turned her gaze heavenward.

italian: ﻿O voi che siete in piccioletta barca, desiderosi d’ascoltar, seguiti dietro al mio legno che cantando varca,
english: O you who are within your little bark, eager to listen, following behind my ship that, singing, crosses to deep seas,

italian: tornate a riveder li vostri liti: non vi mettete in pelago, ché forse, perdendo me, rimarreste smarriti.
english: turn back to see your shores again: do not attempt to sail the seas I sail; you may, by losing sight of me, be left astray.

italian: L’acqua ch’io prendo già mai non si corse; Minerva spira, e conducemi Appollo, e nove Muse mi dimostran l’Orse.
english: The waves I take were never sailed before; Minerva breathes, Apollo pilots me, and the nine Muses show to me the Bears.

italian: Voialtri pochi che drizzaste il collo per tempo al pan de li angeli, del quale vivesi qui ma non sen vien satollo,
english: You other few who turned your minds in time unto the bread of angels, which provides men here with life—but hungering for more—

italian: metter potete ben per l’alto sale vostro navigio, servando mio solco dinanzi a l’acqua che ritorna equale.
english: you may indeed commit your vessel to the deep salt-sea, keeping your course within my wake, ahead of where waves smooth again.

italian: Que’ glorïosi che passaro al Colco non s’ammiraron come voi farete, quando Iasón vider fatto bifolco.
english: Those men of glory, those who crossed to Colchis, when they saw Jason turn into a ploughman were less amazed than you will be amazed.

italian: La concreata e perpetüa sete del deïforme regno cen portava veloci quasi come ’l ciel vedete.
english: The thirst that is innate and everlasting— thirst for the godly realm—bore us away as swiftly as the heavens that you see.

italian: Beatrice in suso, e io in lei guardava; e forse in tanto in quanto un quadrel posa e vola e da la noce si dischiava,
english: Beatrice gazed upward. I watched her. But in a span perhaps no longer than an arrow takes to strike, to fly, to leave

italian: giunto mi vidi ove mirabil cosa mi torse il viso a sé; e però quella cui non potea mia cura essere ascosa,
english: the bow, I reached a place where I could see that something wonderful drew me; and she from whom my need could not be hidden, turned

italian: volta ver’ me, sì lieta come bella, «Drizza la mente in Dio grata», mi disse, «che n’ha congiunti con la prima stella».
english: to me (her gladness matched her loveliness): “Direct your mind to God in gratefulness,” she said; “He has brought us to the first star.”

italian: Parev’ a me che nube ne coprisse lucida, spessa, solida e pulita, quasi adamante che lo sol ferisse.
english: It seemed to me that we were covered by a brilliant, solid, dense, and stainless cloud, much like a diamond that the sun has struck.

italian: Per entro sé l’etterna margarita ne ricevette, com’ acqua recepe raggio di luce permanendo unita.
english: Into itself, the everlasting pearl received us, just as water will accept a ray of light and yet remain intact.

italian: S’io era corpo, e qui non si concepe com’ una dimensione altra patio, ch’esser convien se corpo in corpo repe,
english: If I was body (and on earth we can not see how things material can share one space—the case, when body enters body),

italian: accender ne dovria più il disio di veder quella essenza in che si vede come nostra natura e Dio s’unio.
english: then should our longing be still more inflamed to see that Essence in which we discern how God and human nature were made one.

italian: Lì si vedrà ciò che tenem per fede, non dimostrato, ma fia per sé noto a guisa del ver primo che l’uom crede.
english: What we hold here by faith, shall there be seen, not demonstrated but directly known, even as the first truth that man believes.

italian: Io rispuosi: «Madonna, sì devoto com’ esser posso più, ringrazio lui lo qual dal mortal mondo m’ha remoto.
english: I answered: “With the most devotion I can summon, I thank Him who has brought me far from the mortal world. But now tell me:

italian: Ma ditemi: che son li segni bui di questo corpo, che là giuso in terra fan di Cain favoleggiare altrui?».
english: what are the dark marks on this planet’s body that there below, on earth, have made men tell the tale of Cain?” She smiled somewhat, and then

italian: Ella sorrise alquanto, e poi «S’elli erra l’oppinïon», mi disse, «d’i mortali dove chiave di senso non diserra,
english: she said: “If the opinion mortals hold falls into error when the senses’ key cannot unlock the truth, you should not be

italian: certo non ti dovrien punger li strali d’ammirazione omai, poi dietro ai sensi vedi che la ragione ha corte l’ali.
english: struck by the arrows of amazement once you recognize that reason, even when supported by the senses, has short wings.

italian: Ma dimmi quel che tu da te ne pensi». E io: «Ciò che n’appar qua sù diverso credo che fanno i corpi rari e densi».
english: But tell me what you think of it yourself.” And I: “What seems to us diverse up here is caused—I think—by matter dense and rare.”

italian: Ed ella: «Certo assai vedrai sommerso nel falso il creder tuo, se bene ascolti l’argomentar ch’io li farò avverso.
english: And she: “You certainly will see that your belief is deeply sunk in error if you listen carefully as I rebut it.

italian: La spera ottava vi dimostra molti lumi, li quali e nel quale e nel quanto notar si posson di diversi volti.
english: The eighth sphere offers many lights to you, and you can tell that they, in quality and size, are stars with different visages.

italian: Se raro e denso ciò facesser tanto, una sola virtù sarebbe in tutti, più e men distributa e altrettanto.
english: If rarity and density alone caused this, then all the stars would share one power distributed in lesser, greater, or

italian: Virtù diverse esser convegnon frutti di princìpi formali, e quei, for ch’uno, seguiterieno a tua ragion distrutti.
english: in equal force. But different powers must be fruits of different formal principles; were you correct, one only would be left,

italian: Ancor, se raro fosse di quel bruno cagion che tu dimandi, o d’oltre in parte fora di sua materia sì digiuno
english: the rest, destroyed. And more, were rarity the cause of the dim spots you question, then in part this planet would lack matter through

italian: esto pianeto, o, sì come comparte lo grasso e ’l magro un corpo, così questo nel suo volume cangerebbe carte.
english: and through, or else as, in a body, lean and fat can alternate, so would this planet alternate the pages in its volume.

italian: Se ’l primo fosse, fora manifesto ne l’eclissi del sol, per trasparere lo lume come in altro raro ingesto.
english: To validate the first case, in the sun’s eclipse, the light would have to show through, just as when it crosses matter that is slender.

italian: Questo non è: però è da vedere de l’altro; e s’elli avvien ch’io l’altro cassi, falsificato fia lo tuo parere.
english: This is not so; therefore we must consider the latter case—if I annul that too, then your opinion surely is confuted.

italian: S’elli è che questo raro non trapassi, esser conviene un termine da onde lo suo contrario più passar non lassi;
english: If rarity does not run through and through the moon, then there must be a limit where thickness does not allow the light to pass;

italian: e indi l’altrui raggio si rifonde così come color torna per vetro lo qual di retro a sé piombo nasconde.
english: from there, the rays of sun would be thrown back, just as, from glass that hides lead at its back, a ray of colored light returns, reflected.

italian: Or dirai tu ch’el si dimostra tetro ivi lo raggio più che in altre parti, per esser lì refratto più a retro.
english: Now you will say that where a ray has been reflected from a section farther back, that ray will show itself to be more dim.

italian: Da questa instanza può deliberarti esperïenza, se già mai la provi, ch’esser suol fonte ai rivi di vostr’ arti.
english: Yet an experiment, were you to try it, could free you from your cavil—and the source of your arts’ course springs from experiment.

italian: Tre specchi prenderai; e i due rimovi da te d’un modo, e l’altro, più rimosso, tr’ambo li primi li occhi tuoi ritrovi.
english: Taking three mirrors, place a pair of them at equal distance from you; set the third midway between those two, but farther back.

italian: Rivolto ad essi, fa che dopo il dosso ti stea un lume che i tre specchi accenda e torni a te da tutti ripercosso.
english: Then, turning toward them, at your back have placed a light that kindles those three mirrors and returns to you, reflected by them all.

italian: Ben che nel quanto tanto non si stenda la vista più lontana, lì vedrai come convien ch’igualmente risplenda.
english: Although the image in the farthest glass will be of lesser size, there you will see that it must match the brightness of the rest.

italian: Or, come ai colpi de li caldi rai de la neve riman nudo il suggetto e dal colore e dal freddo primai,
english: Now, just as the sub-matter of the snow, beneath the blows of the warm rays, is stripped of both its former color and its cold,

italian: così rimaso te ne l’intelletto voglio informar di luce sì vivace, che ti tremolerà nel suo aspetto.
english: so is your mind left bare of error; I would offer now to you a new form, light so living that it trembles in your sight.

italian: Dentro dal ciel de la divina pace si gira un corpo ne la cui virtute l’esser di tutto suo contento giace.
english: Within the heaven of the godly peace revolves a body in whose power lies the being of all things that it enfolds.

italian: Lo ciel seguente, c’ha tante vedute, quell’ esser parte per diverse essenze, da lui distratte e da lui contenute.
english: The sphere that follows, where so much is shown, to varied essences bestows that being, to stars distinct and yet contained in it.

italian: Li altri giron per varie differenze le distinzion che dentro da sé hanno dispongono a lor fini e lor semenze.
english: The other spheres, in ways diverse, direct the diverse powers they possess, so that these forces can bear fruit, attain their aims.

italian: Questi organi del mondo così vanno, come tu vedi omai, di grado in grado, che di sù prendono e di sotto fanno.
english: So do these organs of the universe proceed, as you now see, from stage to stage, receiving from above and acting downward.

italian: Riguarda bene omai sì com’ io vado per questo loco al vero che disiri, sì che poi sappi sol tener lo guado.
english: Now do attend to how I pass by way of reason to the truth you want that—then— you may learn how to cross the ford alone.

italian: Lo moto e la virtù d’i santi giri, come dal fabbro l’arte del martello, da’ beati motor convien che spiri;
english: The force and motion of the holy spheres must be inspired by the blessed movers, just as the smith imparts the hammer’s art;

italian: e ’l ciel cui tanti lumi fanno bello, de la mente profonda che lui volve prende l’image e fassene suggello.
english: and so, from the deep Mind that makes it wheel, the sphere that many lights adorn receives that stamp of which it then becomes the seal.

italian: E come l’alma dentro a vostra polve per differenti membra e conformate a diverse potenze si risolve,
english: And as the soul within your dust is shared by different organs, each most suited to a different potency, so does that Mind

italian: così l’intelligenza sua bontate multiplicata per le stelle spiega, girando sé sovra sua unitate.
english: unfold and multiply its bounty through the varied heavens, though that Intellect itself revolves upon its unity.

italian: Virtù diversa fa diversa lega col prezïoso corpo ch’ella avviva, nel qual, sì come vita in voi, si lega.
english: With the dear body that it quickens and with which, as life in you, it too is bound, each different power forms a different compound.

italian: Per la natura lieta onde deriva, la virtù mista per lo corpo luce come letizia per pupilla viva.
english: Because of the glad nature of its source, the power mingled with a sphere shines forth, as gladness, through the living pupil, shines.

italian: Da essa vien ciò che da luce a luce par differente, non da denso e raro; essa è formal principio che produce,
english: From this, and not from matter rare or dense, derive the differences from light to light; this is the forming principle, producing,

italian: conforme a sua bontà, lo turbo e ’l chiaro».
english: conforming with its worth, the dark, the bright.”

italian: Quel sol che pria d’amor mi scaldò ’l petto, di bella verità m’avea scoverto, provando e riprovando, il dolce aspetto;
english: That sun which first had warmed my breast with love had now revealed to me, confuting, proving, the gentle face of truth, its loveliness;

italian: e io, per confessar corretto e certo me stesso, tanto quanto si convenne leva’ il capo a proferer più erto;
english: and I, in order to declare myself corrected and convinced, lifted my head as high as my confessional required.

italian: ma visïone apparve che ritenne a sé me tanto stretto, per vedersi, che di mia confession non mi sovvenne.
english: But a new vision showed itself to me; the grip in which it held me was so fast that I did not remember to confess.

italian: Quali per vetri trasparenti e tersi, o ver per acque nitide e tranquille, non sì profonde che i fondi sien persi,
english: Just as, returning through transparent, clean glass, or through waters calm and crystalline (so shallow that they scarcely can reflect),

italian: tornan d’i nostri visi le postille debili sì, che perla in bianca fronte non vien men forte a le nostre pupille;
english: the mirrored image of our faces meets our pupils with no greater force than that a pearl has when displayed on a white forehead—

italian: tali vid’ io più facce a parlar pronte; per ch’io dentro a l’error contrario corsi a quel ch’accese amor tra l’omo e ’l fonte.
english: so faint, the many faces I saw keen to speak; thus, my mistake was contrary to that which led the man to love the fountain.

italian: Sùbito sì com’ io di lor m’accorsi, quelle stimando specchiati sembianti, per veder di cui fosser, li occhi torsi;
english: As soon as I had noticed them, thinking that what I saw were merely mirrorings, I turned around to see who they might be;

italian: e nulla vidi, e ritorsili avanti dritti nel lume de la dolce guida, che, sorridendo, ardea ne li occhi santi.
english: and I saw nothing; and I let my sight turn back to meet the light of my dear guide, who, as she smiled, glowed in her holy eyes.

italian: «Non ti maravigliar perch’ io sorrida», mi disse, «appresso il tuo püeril coto, poi sopra ’l vero ancor lo piè non fida,
english: “There is no need to wonder if I smile,” she said, “because you reason like a child; your steps do not yet rest upon the truth;

italian: ma te rivolve, come suole, a vòto: vere sustanze son ciò che tu vedi, qui rilegate per manco di voto.
english: your mind misguides you into emptiness: what you are seeing are true substances, placed here because their vows were not fulfilled.

italian: Però parla con esse e odi e credi; ché la verace luce che le appaga da sé non lascia lor torcer li piedi».
english: Thus, speak and listen; trust what they will say: the truthful light in which they find their peace will not allow their steps to turn astray.”

italian: E io a l’ombra che parea più vaga di ragionar, drizza’mi, e cominciai, quasi com’ uom cui troppa voglia smaga:
english: Then I turned to the shade that seemed most anxious to speak, and I began as would a man bewildered by desire too intense:

italian: «O ben creato spirito, che a’ rai di vita etterna la dolcezza senti che, non gustata, non s’intende mai,
english: “O spirit born to goodness, you who feel, beneath the rays of the eternal life, that sweetness which cannot be known unless

italian: grazïoso mi fia se mi contenti del nome tuo e de la vostra sorte». Ond’ ella, pronta e con occhi ridenti:
english: it is experienced, it would be gracious of you to let me know your name and fate.” At this, unhesitant, with smiling eyes:

italian: «La nostra carità non serra porte a giusta voglia, se non come quella che vuol simile a sé tutta sua corte.
english: “Our charity will never lock its gates against just will; our love is like the Love that would have all Its court be like Itself.

italian: I’ fui nel mondo vergine sorella; e se la mente tua ben sé riguarda, non mi ti celerà l’esser più bella,
english: Within the world I was a nun, a virgin; and if your mind attends and recollects, my greater beauty here will not conceal me,

italian: ma riconoscerai ch’i’ son Piccarda, che, posta qui con questi altri beati, beata sono in la spera più tarda.
english: and you will recognize me as Piccarda, who, placed here with the other blessed ones, am blessed within the slowest of the spheres.

italian: Li nostri affetti, che solo infiammati son nel piacer de lo Spirito Santo, letizian del suo ordine formati.
english: Our sentiments, which only serve the flame that is the pleasure of the Holy Ghost, delight in their conforming to His order.

italian: E questa sorte che par giù cotanto, però n’è data, perché fuor negletti li nostri voti, e vòti in alcun canto».
english: And we are to be found within a sphere this low, because we have neglected vows, so that in some respect we were deficient.”

italian: Ond’ io a lei: «Ne’ mirabili aspetti vostri risplende non so che divino che vi trasmuta da’ primi concetti:
english: And I to her: “Within your wonderful semblance there is something divine that glows, transforming the appearance you once showed:

italian: però non fui a rimembrar festino; ma or m’aiuta ciò che tu mi dici, sì che raffigurar m’è più latino.
english: therefore, my recognizing you was slow; but what you now have told me is of help; I can identify you much more clearly.

italian: Ma dimmi: voi che siete qui felici, disiderate voi più alto loco per più vedere e per più farvi amici?».
english: But tell me: though you’re happy here, do you desire a higher place in order to see more and to be still more close to Him?”

italian: Con quelle altr’ ombre pria sorrise un poco; da indi mi rispuose tanto lieta, ch’arder parea d’amor nel primo foco:
english: Together with her fellow shades she smiled at first; then she replied to me with such gladness, like one who burns with love’s first flame:

italian: «Frate, la nostra volontà quïeta virtù di carità, che fa volerne sol quel ch’avemo, e d’altro non ci asseta.
english: “Brother, the power of love appeases our will so—we only long for what we have; we do not thirst for greater blessedness.

italian: Se disïassimo esser più superne, foran discordi li nostri disiri dal voler di colui che qui ne cerne;
english: Should we desire a higher sphere than ours, then our desires would be discordant with the will of Him who has assigned us here,

italian: che vedrai non capere in questi giri, s’essere in carità è qui necesse , e se la sua natura ben rimiri.
english: but you’ll see no such discord in these spheres; to live in love is—here—necessity, if you think on love’s nature carefully.

italian: Anzi è formale ad esto beato esse tenersi dentro a la divina voglia, per ch’una fansi nostre voglie stesse;
english: The essence of this blessed life consists in keeping to the boundaries of God’s will, through which our wills become one single will;

italian: sì che, come noi sem di soglia in soglia per questo regno, a tutto il regno piace com’ a lo re che ’n suo voler ne ’nvoglia.
english: so that, as we are ranged from step to step throughout this kingdom, all this kingdom wills that which will please the King whose will is rule.

italian: E ’n la sua volontade è nostra pace: ell’ è quel mare al qual tutto si move ciò ch’ella crïa o che natura face».
english: And in His will there is our peace: that sea to which all beings move—the beings He creates or nature makes—such is His will.”

italian: Chiaro mi fu allor come ogne dove in cielo è paradiso, etsi la grazia del sommo ben d’un modo non vi piove.
english: Then it was clear to me how every place in Heaven is in Paradise, though grace does not rain equally from the High Good.

italian: Ma sì com’ elli avvien, s’un cibo sazia e d’un altro rimane ancor la gola, che quel si chere e di quel si ringrazia,
english: But just as, when our hunger has been sated with one food, we still long to taste the other— while thankful for the first, we crave the latter—

italian: così fec’ io con atto e con parola, per apprender da lei qual fu la tela onde non trasse infino a co la spuola.
english: so was I in my words and in my gestures, asking to learn from her what was the web of which her shuttle had not reached the end.

italian: «Perfetta vita e alto merto inciela donna più sù», mi disse, «a la cui norma nel vostro mondo giù si veste e vela,
english: “A perfect life,” she said, “and her high merit enheaven, up above, a woman whose rule governs those who, in your world, would wear

italian: perché fino al morir si vegghi e dorma con quello sposo ch’ogne voto accetta che caritate a suo piacer conforma.
english: nuns’ dress and veil, so that, until their death, they wake and sleep with that Spouse who accepts all vows that love conforms unto His pleasure.

italian: Dal mondo, per seguirla, giovinetta fuggi’mi, e nel suo abito mi chiusi e promisi la via de la sua setta.
english: Still young, I fled the world to follow her; and, in her order’s habit, I enclosed myself and promised my life to her rule.

italian: Uomini poi, a mal più ch’a bene usi, fuor mi rapiron de la dolce chiostra: Iddio si sa qual poi mia vita fusi.
english: Then men more used to malice than to good took me—violently—from my sweet cloister: God knows what, after that, my life became.

italian: E quest’ altro splendor che ti si mostra da la mia destra parte e che s’accende di tutto il lume de la spera nostra,
english: This other radiance that shows itself to you at my right hand, a brightness kindled by all the light that fills our heaven—she

italian: ciò ch’io dico di me, di sé intende; sorella fu, e così le fu tolta di capo l’ombra de le sacre bende.
english: has understood what I have said: she was a sister, and from her head, too, by force, the shadow of the sacred veil was taken.

italian: Ma poi che pur al mondo fu rivolta contra suo grado e contra buona usanza, non fu dal vel del cor già mai disciolta.
english: But though she had been turned back to the world against her will, against all honest practice, the veil upon her heart was never loosed.

italian: Quest’ è la luce de la gran Costanza che del secondo vento di Soave generò ’l terzo e l’ultima possanza».
english: This is the splendor of the great Costanza, who from the Swabians’ second gust engendered the one who was their third and final power.”

italian: Così parlommi, e poi cominciò ‘Ave, Maria’ cantando, e cantando vanio come per acqua cupa cosa grave.
english: This said, she then began to sing “Ave Maria” and, while singing, vanished as a weighty thing will vanish in deep water.

italian: La vista mia, che tanto lei seguio quanto possibil fu, poi che la perse, volsesi al segno di maggior disio,
english: My sight, which followed her as long as it was able to, once she was out of view, returned to where its greater longing lay,

italian: e a Beatrice tutta si converse; ma quella folgorò nel mïo sguardo sì che da prima il viso non sofferse;
english: and it was wholly bent on Beatrice; but she then struck my eyes with so much brightness that I, at first, could not withstand her force;

italian: e ciò mi fece a dimandar più tardo.
english: and that made me delay my questioning.

italian: Intra due cibi, distanti e moventi d’un modo, prima si morria di fame, che liber’ omo l’un recasse ai denti;
english: Before a man bit into one of two foods equally removed and tempting, he would die of hunger if his choice were free;

italian: sì si starebbe un agno intra due brame di fieri lupi, igualmente temendo; sì si starebbe un cane intra due dame:
english: so would a lamb stand motionless between the cravings of two savage wolves, in fear of both; so would a dog between two deer;

italian: per che, s’i’ mi tacea, me non riprendo, da li miei dubbi d’un modo sospinto, poi ch’era necessario, né commendo.
english: thus, I need neither blame nor praise myself when both my doubts compelled me equally: what kept me silent was necessity.

italian: Io mi tacea, ma ’l mio disir dipinto m’era nel viso, e ’l dimandar con ello, più caldo assai che per parlar distinto.
english: I did not speak, but in my face were seen longing and questioning, more ardent than if spoken words had made them evident.

italian: Fé sì Beatrice qual fé Danïello, Nabuccodonosor levando d’ira, che l’avea fatto ingiustamente fello;
english: Then Beatrice did just as Daniel did, when he appeased Nebuchadnezzar’s anger, the rage that made the king unjustly fierce.

italian: e disse: «Io veggio ben come ti tira uno e altro disio, sì che tua cura sé stessa lega sì che fuor non spira.
english: She said: “I see how both desires draw you, so that your anxiousness to know is self- entangled and cannot express itself.

italian: Tu argomenti: “Se ’l buon voler dura, la vïolenza altrui per qual ragione di meritar mi scema la misura?”.
english: You reason: ‘If my will to good persists, why should the violence of others cause the measure of my merit to be less?’

italian: Ancor di dubitar ti dà cagione parer tornarsi l’anime a le stelle, secondo la sentenza di Platone.
english: And you are also led to doubt because the doctrine Plato taught would find support by souls’ appearing to return to the stars.

italian: Queste son le question che nel tuo velle pontano igualmente; e però pria tratterò quella che più ha di felle.
english: These are the questions that, within your will, press equally for answers; therefore, I shall treat the most insidious question first.

italian: D’i Serafin colui che più s’india, Moïsè, Samuel, e quel Giovanni che prender vuoli, io dico, non Maria,
english: Neither the Seraph closest unto God, nor Moses, Samuel, nor either John— whichever one you will—nor Mary has,

italian: non hanno in altro cielo i loro scanni che questi spirti che mo t’appariro, né hanno a l’esser lor più o meno anni;
english: I say, their place in any other heaven than that which houses those souls you just saw, nor will their blessedness last any longer.

italian: ma tutti fanno bello il primo giro, e differentemente han dolce vita per sentir più e men l’etterno spiro.
english: But all those souls grace the Empyrean; and each of them has gentle life—though some sense the Eternal Spirit more, some less.

italian: Qui si mostraro, non perché sortita sia questa spera lor, ma per far segno de la celestïal c’ha men salita.
english: They showed themselves to you here not because this is their sphere, but as a sign for you that in the Empyrean their place is lowest.

italian: Così parlar conviensi al vostro ingegno, però che solo da sensato apprende ciò che fa poscia d’intelletto degno.
english: Such signs are suited to your mind, since from the senses only can it apprehend what then becomes fit for the intellect.

italian: Per questo la Scrittura condescende a vostra facultate, e piedi e mano attribuisce a Dio e altro intende;
english: And this is why the Bible condescends to human powers, assigning feet and hands to God, but meaning something else instead.

italian: e Santa Chiesa con aspetto umano Gabrïel e Michel vi rappresenta, e l’altro che Tobia rifece sano.
english: And Gabriel and Michael and the angel who healed the eyes of Tobit are portrayed by Holy Church with human visages.

italian: Quel che Timeo de l’anime argomenta non è simile a ciò che qui si vede, però che, come dice, par che senta.
english: That which Timaeus said in reasoning of souls does not describe what you have seen, since it would seem that as he speaks he thinks.

italian: Dice che l’alma a la sua stella riede, credendo quella quindi esser decisa quando natura per forma la diede;
english: He says the soul returns to that same star from which—so he believes—it had been taken when nature sent that soul as form to body;

italian: e forse sua sentenza è d’altra guisa che la voce non suona, ed esser puote con intenzion da non esser derisa.
english: but his opinion is, perhaps, to be taken in other guise than his words speak, intending something not to be derided.

italian: S’elli intende tornare a queste ruote l’onor de la influenza e ’l biasmo, forse in alcun vero suo arco percuote.
english: If to these spheres he wanted to attribute honor and blame for what they influence, perhaps his arrow reaches something true.

italian: Questo principio, male inteso, torse già tutto il mondo quasi, sì che Giove, Mercurio e Marte a nominar trascorse.
english: This principle, ill-understood, misled almost all of the world once, so that Jove and Mercury and Mars gave names to stars.

italian: L’altra dubitazion che ti commove ha men velen, però che sua malizia non ti poria menar da me altrove.
english: The other doubt that agitates you is less poisonous; for its insidiousness is not such as to lead you far from me.

italian: Parere ingiusta la nostra giustizia ne li occhi d’i mortali, è argomento di fede e non d’eretica nequizia.
english: To mortal eyes our justice seems unjust; that this is so, should serve as evidence for faith—not heresy’s depravity.

italian: Ma perché puote vostro accorgimento ben penetrare a questa veritate, come disiri, ti farò contento.
english: But that your intellect may penetrate more carefully into your other query, I shall—as you desire—explain it clearly.

italian: Se vïolenza è quando quel che pate nïente conferisce a quel che sforza, non fuor quest’ alme per essa scusate:
english: If violence means that the one who suffers has not abetted force in any way, then there is no excuse these souls can claim:

italian: ché volontà, se non vuol, non s’ammorza, ma fa come natura face in foco, se mille volte vïolenza il torza.
english: for will, if it resists, is never spent, but acts as nature acts when fire ascends, though force—a thousand times—tries to compel.

italian: Per che, s’ella si piega assai o poco, segue la forza; e così queste fero possendo rifuggir nel santo loco.
english: So that, when will has yielded much or little, it has abetted force—as these souls did: they could have fled back to their holy shelter.

italian: Se fosse stato lor volere intero, come tenne Lorenzo in su la grada, e fece Muzio a la sua man severo,
english: Had their will been as whole as that which held Lawrence fast to the grate and that which made of Mucius one who judged his own hand, then

italian: così l’avria ripinte per la strada ond’ eran tratte, come fuoro sciolte; ma così salda voglia è troppo rada.
english: once freed, they would have willed to find the faith from which they had been dragged; but it is all too seldom that a will is so intact.

italian: E per queste parole, se ricolte l’hai come dei, è l’argomento casso che t’avria fatto noia ancor più volte.
english: And through these words, if you have grasped their bent, you can eliminate the argument that would have troubled you again—and often.

italian: Ma or ti s’attraversa un altro passo dinanzi a li occhi, tal che per te stesso non usciresti: pria saresti lasso.
english: But now another obstacle obstructs your sight; you cannot overcome it by yourself—it is too wearying to try.

italian: Io t’ho per certo ne la mente messo ch’alma beata non poria mentire, però ch’è sempre al primo vero appresso;
english: I’ve set it in your mind as something certain that souls in blessedness can never lie, since they are always near the Primal Truth.

italian: e poi potesti da Piccarda udire che l’affezion del vel Costanza tenne; sì ch’ella par qui meco contradire.
english: But from Piccarda you were also able to hear how Constance kept her love of the veil: and here Piccarda seems to contradict me.

italian: Molte fïate già, frate, addivenne che, per fuggir periglio, contra grato si fé di quel che far non si convenne;
english: Before this—brother—it has often happened that, to flee menace, men unwillingly did what should not be done; so did Alcmaeon,

italian: come Almeone, che, di ciò pregato dal padre suo, la propria madre spense, per non perder pietà si fé spietato.
english: to meet the wishes of his father, kill his mother—not to fail in filial piety, he acted ruthlessly.

italian: A questo punto voglio che tu pense che la forza al voler si mischia, e fanno sì che scusar non si posson l’offense.
english: At that point—I would have you see—the forces to which one yielded mingles with one’s will; and no excuse can pardon their joint act.

italian: Voglia assoluta non consente al danno; ma consentevi in tanto in quanto teme, se si ritrae, cadere in più affanno.
english: Absolute will does not concur in wrong; but the contingent will, through fear that its resistance might bring greater harm, consents.

italian: Però, quando Piccarda quello spreme, de la voglia assoluta intende, e io de l’altra; sì che ver diciamo insieme».
english: Therefore, Piccarda means the absolute will when she speaks, and I the relative; so that the two of us have spoken truth.”

italian: Cotal fu l’ondeggiar del santo rio ch’uscì del fonte ond’ ogne ver deriva; tal puose in pace uno e altro disio.
english: Such was the rippling of the holy stream issuing from the fountain from which springs all truth: it set to rest both of my longings.

italian: «O amanza del primo amante, o diva», diss’ io appresso, «il cui parlar m’inonda e scalda sì, che più e più m’avviva,
english: Then I said: “O beloved of the First Lover, o you—divine—whose speech so floods and warms me that I feel more and more life,

italian: non è l’affezion mia tanto profonda, che basti a render voi grazia per grazia; ma quei che vede e puote a ciò risponda.
english: however deep my gratefulness, it can not match your grace with grace enough; but He who sees and can—may He grant recompense.

italian: Io veggio ben che già mai non si sazia nostro intelletto, se ’l ver non lo illustra di fuor dal qual nessun vero si spazia.
english: I now see well: we cannot satisfy our mind unless it is enlightened by the truth beyond whose boundary no truth lies.

italian: Posasi in esso, come fera in lustra, tosto che giunto l’ha; e giugner puollo: se non, ciascun disio sarebbe frustra.
english: Mind, reaching that truth, rests within it as a beast within its lair; mind can attain that truth—if not, all our desires were vain.

italian: Nasce per quello, a guisa di rampollo, a piè del vero il dubbio; ed è natura ch’al sommo pinge noi di collo in collo.
english: Therefore, our doubting blossoms like a shoot out from the root of truth; this natural urge spurs us toward the peak, from height to height.

italian: Questo m’invita, questo m’assicura con reverenza, donna, a dimandarvi d’un’altra verità che m’è oscura.
english: Lady, my knowing why we doubt, invites, sustains, my reverent asking you about another truth that is obscure to me.

italian: Io vo’ saper se l’uom può sodisfarvi ai voti manchi sì con altri beni, ch’a la vostra statera non sien parvi».
english: I want to know if, in your eyes, one can amend for unkept vows with other acts— good works your balance will not find too scant.”

italian: Beatrice mi guardò con li occhi pieni di faville d’amor così divini, che, vinta, mia virtute diè le reni,
english: Then Beatrice looked at me with eyes so full of sparks of love, eyes so divine that my own force of sight was overcome, took flight,

italian: e quasi mi perdei con li occhi chini.
english: and, eyes downcast, I almost lost my senses.

italian: ﻿«S’io ti fiammeggio nel caldo d’amore di là dal modo che ’n terra si vede, sì che del viso tuo vinco il valore,
english: “If in the fire of love I seem to flame beyond the measure visible on earth, so that I overcome your vision’s force,

italian: non ti maravigliar, ché ciò procede da perfetto veder, che, come apprende, così nel bene appreso move il piede.
english: you need not wonder; I am so because of my perfected vision—as I grasp the good, so I approach the good in act.

italian: Io veggio ben sì come già resplende ne l’intelletto tuo l’etterna luce, che, vista, sola e sempre amore accende;
english: Indeed I see that in your intellect now shines the never-ending light; once seen, that light, alone and always, kindles love;

italian: e s’altra cosa vostro amor seduce, non è se non di quella alcun vestigio, mal conosciuto, che quivi traluce.
english: and if a lesser thing allure your love, it is a vestige of that light which—though imperfectly—gleams through that lesser thing.

italian: Tu vuo’ saper se con altro servigio, per manco voto, si può render tanto che l’anima sicuri di letigio».
english: You wish to know if, through a righteous act, one can repair a promise unfulfilled, so that the soul and God are reconciled.”

italian: Sì cominciò Beatrice questo canto; e sì com’ uom che suo parlar non spezza, continüò così ’l processo santo:
english: So Beatrice began this canto, and as one who does not interrupt her speech, so did her holy reasoning proceed:

italian: «Lo maggior don che Dio per sua larghezza fesse creando, e a la sua bontate più conformato, e quel ch’e’ più apprezza,
english: “The greatest gift the magnanimity of God, as He created, gave, the gift most suited to His goodness, gift that He

italian: fu de la volontà la libertate; di che le creature intelligenti, e tutte e sole, fuoro e son dotate.
english: most prizes, was the freedom of the will; those beings that have intellect—all these and none but these—received and do receive

italian: Or ti parrà, se tu quinci argomenti, l’alto valor del voto, s’è sì fatto che Dio consenta quando tu consenti;
english: this gift: thus you may draw, as consequence, the high worth of a vow, when what is pledged with your consent encounters God’s consent;

italian: ché, nel fermar tra Dio e l’omo il patto, vittima fassi di questo tesoro, tal quale io dico; e fassi col suo atto.
english: for when a pact is drawn between a man and God, then through free will, a man gives up what I have called his treasure, his free will.

italian: Dunque che render puossi per ristoro? Se credi bene usar quel c’hai offerto, di maltolletto vuo’ far buon lavoro.
english: What, then, can be a fitting compensation? To use again what you had offered, would mean seeking to do good with ill-got gains.

italian: Tu se’ omai del maggior punto certo; ma perché Santa Chiesa in ciò dispensa, che par contra lo ver ch’i’ t’ho scoverto,
english: By now you understand the major point; but since the Holy Church gives dispensations— which seems in contrast with the truth I stated—

italian: convienti ancor sedere un poco a mensa, però che ’l cibo rigido c’hai preso, richiede ancora aiuto a tua dispensa.
english: you need to sit at table somewhat longer: the food that you have taken was tough food— it still needs help, if you are to digest it.

italian: Apri la mente a quel ch’io ti paleso e fermalvi entro; ché non fa scïenza, sanza lo ritenere, avere inteso.
english: Open your mind to what I shall disclose, and hold it fast within you; he who hears, but does not hold what he has heard, learns nothing.

italian: Due cose si convegnono a l’essenza di questo sacrificio: l’una è quella di che si fa; l’altr’ è la convenenza.
english: Two things are of the essence when one vows a sacrifice: the matter of the pledge and then the formal compact one accepts.

italian: Quest’ ultima già mai non si cancella se non servata; e intorno di lei sì preciso di sopra si favella:
english: This last can never be annulled until the compact is fulfilled: it is of this that I have spoken to you so precisely.

italian: però necessitato fu a li Ebrei pur l’offerere, ancor ch’alcuna offerta sì permutasse, come saver dei.
english: Therefore, the Hebrews found it necessary to bring their offerings, although—as you must know—some of their offerings might be altered.

italian: L’altra, che per materia t’è aperta, puote ben esser tal, che non si falla se con altra materia si converta.
english: As for the matter of the vow—discussed above—it may be such that if one shifts to other matter, one commits no sin.

italian: Ma non trasmuti carco a la sua spalla per suo arbitrio alcun, sanza la volta e de la chiave bianca e de la gialla;
english: But let none shift the burden on his shoulder through his own judgment, without waiting for the turning of the white and yellow keys;

italian: e ogne permutanza credi stolta, se la cosa dimessa in la sorpresa come ’l quattro nel sei non è raccolta.
english: and let him see that any change is senseless, unless the thing one sets aside can be contained in one’s new weight, as four in six.

italian: Però qualunque cosa tanto pesa per suo valor che tragga ogne bilancia, sodisfar non si può con altra spesa.
english: Thus, when the matter of a vow has so much weight and worth that it tips every scale, no other weight can serve as substitute.

italian: Non prendan li mortali il voto a ciancia; siate fedeli, e a ciò far non bieci, come Ieptè a la sua prima mancia;
english: Let mortals never take a vow in jest; be faithful and yet circumspect, not rash as Jephthah was, in offering his first gift;

italian: cui più si convenia dicer ‘Mal feci’, che, servando, far peggio; e così stolto ritrovar puoi il gran duca de’ Greci,
english: he should have said, ‘I did amiss,’ and not done worse by keeping faith. And you can find that same stupidity in the Greeks’ chief—

italian: onde pianse Efigènia il suo bel volto, e fé pianger di sé i folli e i savi ch’udir parlar di così fatto cólto.
english: when her fair face made Iphigenia grieve and made the wise and made the foolish weep for her when they heard tell of such a rite.

italian: Siate, Cristiani, a muovervi più gravi: non siate come penna ad ogne vento, e non crediate ch’ogne acqua vi lavi.
english: Christians, proceed with greater gravity: do not be like a feather at each wind, nor think that all immersions wash you clean.

italian: Avete il novo e ’l vecchio Testamento, e ’l pastor de la Chiesa che vi guida; questo vi basti a vostro salvamento.
english: You have both Testaments, the Old and New, you have the shepherd of the Church to guide you; you need no more than this for your salvation.

italian: Se mala cupidigia altro vi grida, uomini siate, e non pecore matte, sì che ’l Giudeo di voi tra voi non rida!
english: If evil greed would summon you elsewhere, be men, and not like sheep gone mad, so that the Jew who lives among you not deride you!

italian: Non fate com’ agnel che lascia il latte de la sua madre, e semplice e lascivo seco medesmo a suo piacer combatte!».
english: Do not act like the foolish, wanton lamb that leaves its mother’s milk and, heedless, wants to war against—and harm—its very self!”

italian: Così Beatrice a me com’ ïo scrivo; poi si rivolse tutta disïante a quella parte ove ’l mondo è più vivo.
english: These words of Beatrice I here transcribe; and then she turned—her longing at the full— to where the world is more alive with light.

italian: Lo suo tacere e ’l trasmutar sembiante puoser silenzio al mio cupido ingegno, che già nuove questioni avea davante;
english: Her silence and the change in her appearance imposed a silence on my avid mind, which now was ready to address new questions;

italian: e sì come saetta che nel segno percuote pria che sia la corda queta, così corremmo nel secondo regno.
english: and even as an arrow that has struck the mark before the bow-cord comes to rest, so did we race to reach the second realm.

italian: Quivi la donna mia vid’ io sì lieta, come nel lume di quel ciel si mise, che più lucente se ne fé ’l pianeta.
english: When she had passed into that heaven’s light, I saw my lady filled with so much gladness that, at her joy, the planet grew more bright.

italian: E se la stella si cambiò e rise, qual mi fec’ io che pur da mia natura trasmutabile son per tutte guise!
english: And if the planet changed and smiled, what then did I—who by my very nature am given to every sort of change—become?

italian: Come ’n peschiera ch’è tranquilla e pura traggonsi i pesci a ciò che vien di fori per modo che lo stimin lor pastura,
english: As in a fish-pool that is calm and clear, the fish draw close to anything that nears from outside, if it seems to be their fare,

italian: sì vid’ io ben più di mille splendori trarsi ver’ noi, e in ciascun s’udia: «Ecco chi crescerà li nostri amori».
english: such were the far more than a thousand splendors I saw approaching us, and each declared: “Here now is one who will increase our loves.”

italian: E sì come ciascuno a noi venìa, vedeasi l’ombra piena di letizia nel folgór chiaro che di lei uscia.
english: And even as each shade approached, one saw, because of the bright radiance it sent forth, the joyousness with which that shade was filled.

italian: Pensa, lettor, se quel che qui s’inizia non procedesse, come tu avresti di più savere angosciosa carizia;
english: Consider, reader, what your misery and need to know still more would be if, at this point, what I began did not go on;

italian: e per te vederai come da questi m’era in disio d’udir lor condizioni, sì come a li occhi mi fur manifesti.
english: and you will—unassisted—feel how I longed so to hear those shades narrate their state as soon as they appeared before my eyes.

italian: «O bene nato a cui veder li troni del trïunfo etternal concede grazia prima che la milizia s’abbandoni,
english: “O you born unto gladness, whom God’s grace allows to see the thrones of the eternal triumph before your war of life is ended,

italian: del lume che per tutto il ciel si spazia noi semo accesi; e però, se disii di noi chiarirti, a tuo piacer ti sazia».
english: the light that kindles us is that same light which spreads through all of heaven; thus, if you would know us, sate yourself as you may please.”

italian: Così da un di quelli spirti pii detto mi fu; e da Beatrice: «Dì, dì sicuramente, e credi come a dii».
english: So did one of those pious spirits speak to me. And Beatrice then urged: “Speak, speak confidently; trust them as you trust gods.”

italian: «Io veggio ben sì come tu t’annidi nel proprio lume, e che de li occhi il traggi, perch’ e’ corusca sì come tu ridi;
english: “I see—plainly—how you have nested in your own light; see—you draw it from your eyes— because it glistens even as you smile;

italian: ma non so chi tu se’, né perché aggi, anima degna, il grado de la spera che si vela a’ mortai con altrui raggi».
english: but I do not know who you are or why, good soul, your rank is in a sphere concealed from mortals by another planet’s rays.”

italian: Questo diss’ io diritto a la lumera che pria m’avea parlato; ond’ ella fessi lucente più assai di quel ch’ell’ era.
english: I said this as I stood turned toward the light that first addressed me; and at this, it glowed more radiantly than it had before.

italian: Sì come il sol che si cela elli stessi per troppa luce, come ’l caldo ha róse le temperanze d’i vapori spessi,
english: Just as the sun, when heat has worn away thick mists that moderate its rays, conceals itself from sight through an excess of light,

italian: per più letizia sì mi si nascose dentro al suo raggio la figura santa; e così chiusa chiusa mi rispuose
english: so did that holy form, through excess gladness, conceal himself from me within his rays; and so concealed, concealed, he answered me

italian: nel modo che ’l seguente canto canta.
english: even as the next canto is to sing.

italian: ﻿«Poscia che Costantin l’aquila volse contr’ al corso del ciel, ch’ella seguio dietro a l’antico che Lavina tolse,
english: “After Constantine had turned the Eagle counter to heaven’s course, the course it took behind the ancient one who wed Lavinia,

italian: cento e cent’ anni e più l’uccel di Dio ne lo stremo d’Europa si ritenne, vicino a’ monti de’ quai prima uscìo;
english: one hundred and one hundred years and more, the bird of God remained near Europe’s borders, close to the peaks from which it first emerged;

italian: e sotto l’ombra de le sacre penne governò ’l mondo lì di mano in mano, e, sì cangiando, in su la mia pervenne.
english: beneath the shadow of the sacred wings, it ruled the world, from hand to hand, until that governing—changing—became my task.

italian: Cesare fui e son Iustinïano, che, per voler del primo amor ch’i’ sento, d’entro le leggi trassi il troppo e ’l vano.
english: Caesar I was and am Justinian, who, through the will of Primal Love I feel, removed the vain and needless from the laws.

italian: E prima ch’io a l’ovra fossi attento, una natura in Cristo esser, non piùe, credea, e di tal fede era contento;
english: Before I grew attentive to this labor, I held that but one nature—and no more— was Christ’s—and in that faith, I was content;

italian: ma ’l benedetto Agapito, che fue sommo pastore, a la fede sincera mi dirizzò con le parole sue.
english: but then the blessed Agapetus, he who was chief shepherd, with his words turned me to that faith which has truth and purity.

italian: Io li credetti; e ciò che ’n sua fede era, vegg’ io or chiaro sì, come tu vedi ogni contradizione e falsa e vera.
english: I did believe him, and now clearly see his faith, as you with contradictories can see that one is true and one is false.

italian: Tosto che con la Chiesa mossi i piedi, a Dio per grazia piacque di spirarmi l’alto lavoro, e tutto ’n lui mi diedi;
english: As soon as my steps shared the Church’s path, God, of His grace, inspired my high task as pleased Him. I was fully drawn to that.

italian: e al mio Belisar commendai l’armi, cui la destra del ciel fu sì congiunta, che segno fu ch’i’ dovessi posarmi.
english: Entrusting to my Belisarius my arms, I found a sign for me to rest from war: Heaven’s right hand so favored him.

italian: Or qui a la question prima s’appunta la mia risposta; ma sua condizione mi stringe a seguitare alcuna giunta,
english: My answer to the question you first asked ends here, and yet the nature of this answer leads me to add a sequel, so that you

italian: perché tu veggi con quanta ragione si move contr’ al sacrosanto segno e chi ’l s’appropria e chi a lui s’oppone.
english: may see with how much reason they attack the sacred standard—those who seem to act on its behalf and those opposing it.

italian: Vedi quanta virtù l’ha fatto degno di reverenza; e cominciò da l’ora che Pallante morì per darli regno.
english: See what great virtue made that Eagle worthy of reverence, beginning from that hour when Pallas died that it might gain a kingdom.

italian: Tu sai ch’el fece in Alba sua dimora per trecento anni e oltre, infino al fine che i tre a’ tre pugnar per lui ancora.
english: You know that for three hundred years and more, it lived in Alba, until, at the end, three still fought three, contending for that standard.

italian: E sai ch’el fé dal mal de le Sabine al dolor di Lucrezia in sette regi, vincendo intorno le genti vicine.
english: You know how, under seven kings, it conquered its neighbors—in the era reaching from wronged Sabine women to Lucrece’s grief—

italian: Sai quel ch’el fé portato da li egregi Romani incontro a Brenno, incontro a Pirro, incontro a li altri principi e collegi;
english: and what it did when carried by courageous Romans, who hurried to encounter Brennus, Pyrrhus, and other principates and cities.

italian: onde Torquato e Quinzio, che dal cirro negletto fu nomato, i Deci e ’ Fabi ebber la fama che volontier mirro.
english: Through this, Torquatus, Quinctius (who is named for his disheveled hair), the Decii, and Fabii gained the fame I gladly honor.

italian: Esso atterrò l’orgoglio de li Aràbi che di retro ad Anibale passaro l’alpestre rocce, Po, di che tu labi.
english: That standard brought the pride of Arabs low when they had followed Hannibal across those Alpine rocks from which, Po, you descend.

italian: Sott’ esso giovanetti trïunfaro Scipïone e Pompeo; e a quel colle sotto ’l qual tu nascesti parve amaro.
english: Beneath that standard, Scipio, Pompey— though young—triumphed; and to that hill beneath which you were born, that standard seemed most harsh.

italian: Poi, presso al tempo che tutto ’l ciel volle redur lo mondo a suo modo sereno, Cesare per voler di Roma il tolle.
english: Then, near the time when Heaven wished to bring all of the world to Heaven’s way—serene— Caesar, as Rome had willed, took up that standard.

italian: E quel che fé da Varo infino a Reno, Isara vide ed Era e vide Senna e ogne valle onde Rodano è pieno.
english: And what it did from Var to Rhine was seen by the Isere, Saone, and Seine and all the valley—floors whose rivers feed the Rhone.

italian: Quel che fé poi ch’elli uscì di Ravenna e saltò Rubicon, fu di tal volo, che nol seguiteria lingua né penna.
english: And what it did, once it had left Ravenna and leaped the Rubicon, was such a flight as neither tongue nor writing can describe.

italian: Inver’ la Spagna rivolse lo stuolo, poi ver’ Durazzo, e Farsalia percosse sì ch’al Nil caldo si sentì del duolo.
english: That standard led the legions on to Spain, then toward Durazzo, and it struck Pharsalia so hard that the warm Nile could feel that hurt.

italian: Antandro e Simeonta, onde si mosse, rivide e là dov’ Ettore si cuba; e mal per Tolomeo poscia si scosse.
english: It saw again its source, Antandros and Simois, and the place where Hector lies; then roused itself—the worse for Ptolemy.

italian: Da indi scese folgorando a Iuba; onde si volse nel vostro occidente, ove sentia la pompeana tuba.
english: From Egypt, lightning-like, it fell on Juba; and then it hurried to the west of you, where it could hear the trumpet of Pompey.

italian: Di quel che fé col baiulo seguente, Bruto con Cassio ne l’inferno latra, e Modena e Perugia fu dolente.
english: Because of what that standard did, with him who bore it next, Brutus and Cassius howl in Hell, and grief seized Modena, Perugia.

italian: Piangene ancor la trista Cleopatra, che, fuggendoli innanzi, dal colubro la morte prese subitana e atra.
english: Because of it, sad Cleopatra weeps still; as she fled that standard, from the asp she drew a sudden and atrocious death.

italian: Con costui corse infino al lito rubro; con costui puose il mondo in tanta pace, che fu serrato a Giano il suo delubro.
english: And, with that very bearer, it then reached the Red Sea shore: with him, that emblem brought the world such peace that Janus’ shrine was shut.

italian: Ma ciò che ’l segno che parlar mi face fatto avea prima e poi era fatturo per lo regno mortal ch’a lui soggiace,
english: But what the standard that has made me speak had done before or then was yet to do throughout the mortal realm where it holds rule,

italian: diventa in apparenza poco e scuro, se in mano al terzo Cesare si mira con occhio chiaro e con affetto puro;
english: comes to seem faint and insignificant if one, with clear sight and pure sentiment, sees what it did in the third Caesar’s hand;

italian: ché la viva giustizia che mi spira, li concedette, in mano a quel ch’i’ dico, gloria di far vendetta a la sua ira.
english: for the true Justice that inspires me granted to it—in that next Caesar’s hand— the glory of avenging His own wrath.

italian: Or qui t’ammira in ciò ch’io ti replìco: poscia con Tito a far vendetta corse de la vendetta del peccato antico.
english: Now marvel here at what I show to you: with Titus—afterward—it hurried toward avenging vengeance for the ancient sin.

italian: E quando il dente longobardo morse la Santa Chiesa, sotto le sue ali Carlo Magno, vincendo, la soccorse.
english: And when the Lombard tooth bit Holy Church, then Charlemagne, under the Eagle’s wings, through victories he gained, brought help to her.

italian: Omai puoi giudicar di quei cotali ch’io accusai di sopra e di lor falli, che son cagion di tutti vostri mali.
english: Now you can judge those I condemned above, and judge how such men have offended, have become the origin of all your evils.

italian: L’uno al pubblico segno i gigli gialli oppone, e l’altro appropria quello a parte, sì ch’è forte a veder chi più si falli.
english: For some oppose the universal emblem with yellow lilies; others claim that emblem for party: it is hard to see who is worse.

italian: Faccian li Ghibellin, faccian lor arte sott’ altro segno, ché mal segue quello sempre chi la giustizia e lui diparte;
english: Let Ghibellines pursue their undertakings beneath another sign, for those who sever this sign and justice are bad followers.

italian: e non l’abbatta esto Carlo novello coi Guelfi suoi, ma tema de li artigli ch’a più alto leon trasser lo vello.
english: And let not this new Charles strike at it with his Guelphs—but let him fear the claws that stripped a more courageous lion of its hide.

italian: Molte fïate già pianser li figli per la colpa del padre, e non si creda che Dio trasmuti l’armi per suoi gigli!
english: The sons have often wept for a father’s fault; and let this son not think that God will change the emblem of His force for Charles’s lilies.

italian: Questa picciola stella si correda d’i buoni spirti che son stati attivi perché onore e fama li succeda:
english: This little planet is adorned with spirits whose acts were righteous, but who acted for the honor and the fame that they would gain:

italian: e quando li disiri poggian quivi, sì disvïando, pur convien che i raggi del vero amore in sù poggin men vivi.
english: and when desires tend toward earthly ends, then, so deflected, rays of the true love mount toward the life above with lesser force.

italian: Ma nel commensurar d’i nostri gaggi col merto è parte di nostra letizia, perché non li vedem minor né maggi.
english: But part of our delight is measuring rewards against our merit, and we see that our rewards are neither less nor more.

italian: Quindi addolcisce la viva giustizia in noi l’affetto sì, che non si puote torcer già mai ad alcuna nequizia.
english: Thus does the Living Justice make so sweet the sentiments in us, that we are free of any turning toward iniquity.

italian: Diverse voci fanno dolci note; così diversi scanni in nostra vita rendon dolce armonia tra queste rote.
english: Differing voices join to sound sweet music; so do the different orders in our life render sweet harmony among these spheres.

italian: E dentro a la presente margarita luce la luce di Romeo, di cui fu l’ovra grande e bella mal gradita.
english: And in this very pearl there also shines the light of Romeo, of one whose acts, though great and noble, met ungratefulness.

italian: Ma i Provenzai che fecer contra lui non hanno riso; e però mal cammina qual si fa danno del ben fare altrui.
english: And yet those Provencals who schemed against him had little chance to laugh, for he who finds harm to himself in others’ righteous acts

italian: Quattro figlie ebbe, e ciascuna reina, Ramondo Beringhiere, e ciò li fece Romeo, persona umìle e peregrina.
english: takes the wrong path. Of Raymond Berenger’s four daughters, each became a queen—and this, poor and a stranger, Romeo accomplished.

italian: E poi il mosser le parole biece a dimandar ragione a questo giusto, che li assegnò sette e cinque per diece,
english: Then Berenger was moved by vicious tongues to ask this just man for accounting—one who, given ten, gave Raymond five and seven.

italian: indi partissi povero e vetusto; e se ’l mondo sapesse il cor ch’elli ebbe mendicando sua vita a frusto a frusto,
english: And Romeo, the poor, the old, departed; and were the world to know the heart he had while begging, crust by crust, for his life-bread,

italian: assai lo loda, e più lo loderebbe».
english: it—though it praise him now—would praise him more.”

italian: «Osanna, sanctus Deus sabaòth, superillustrans claritate tua felices ignes horum malacòth!» .
english: “Hosanna, sanctus Deus sabaoth, superillustrans claritate tua felices ignes horum malacoth!”

italian: Così, volgendosi a la nota sua, fu viso a me cantare essa sustanza, sopra la qual doppio lume s’addua;
english: Thus, even as he wheeled to his own music, I saw that substance sing, that spirit-flame above whom double lights were twinned; and he

italian: ed essa e l’altre mossero a sua danza, e quasi velocissime faville mi si velar di sùbita distanza.
english: and his companions moved within their dance, and as if they were swiftest sparks, they sped out of my sight because of sudden distance.

italian: Io dubitava e dicea ‘Dille, dille!’ fra me, ‘dille’ dicea, ‘a la mia donna che mi diseta con le dolci stille’.
english: I was perplexed, and to myself, I said: “Tell her! Tell her! Tell her, the lady who can slake my thirst with her sweet drops”; and yet

italian: Ma quella reverenza che s’indonna di tutto me, pur per Be e per ice , mi richinava come l’uom ch’assonna.
english: the reverence that possesses all of me, even on hearing only Be and ice, had bowed my head—I seemed a man asleep.

italian: Poco sofferse me cotal Beatrice e cominciò, raggiandomi d’un riso tal, che nel foco faria l’uom felice:
english: But Beatrice soon ended that; for she began to smile at me so brightly that, even in fire, a man would still feel glad.

italian: «Secondo mio infallibile avviso, come giusta vendetta giustamente punita fosse, t’ha in pensier miso;
english: “According to my never-erring judgment, the question that perplexes you is how just vengeance can deserve just punishment;

italian: ma io ti solverò tosto la mente; e tu ascolta, ché le mie parole di gran sentenza ti faran presente.
english: but I shall quickly free your mind from doubt; and listen carefully; the words I speak will bring the gift of a great truth in reach.

italian: Per non soffrire a la virtù che vole freno a suo prode, quell’ uom che non nacque, dannando sé, dannò tutta sua prole;
english: Since he could not endure the helpful curb on his willpower, the man who was not born, damning himself, damned all his progeny.

italian: onde l’umana specie inferma giacque giù per secoli molti in grande errore, fin ch’al Verbo di Dio discender piacque
english: For this, mankind lay sick, in the abyss of a great error, for long centuries, until the Word of God willed to descend

italian: u’ la natura, che dal suo fattore s’era allungata, unì a sé in persona con l’atto sol del suo etterno amore.
english: to where the nature that was sundered from its Maker was united to His person by the sole act of His eternal Love.

italian: Or drizza il viso a quel ch’or si ragiona: questa natura al suo fattore unita, qual fu creata, fu sincera e buona;
english: Now set your sight on what derives from that. This nature, thus united to its Maker, was good and pure, even as when created;

italian: ma per sé stessa pur fu ella sbandita di paradiso, però che si torse da via di verità e da sua vita.
english: but in itself, this nature had been banished from paradise, because it turned aside from its own path, from truth, from its own life.

italian: La pena dunque che la croce porse s’a la natura assunta si misura, nulla già mai sì giustamente morse;
english: Thus, if the penalty the Cross inflicted is measured by the nature He assumed, no one has ever been so justly stung;

italian: e così nulla fu di tanta ingiura, guardando a la persona che sofferse, in che era contratta tal natura.
english: yet none was ever done so great a wrong, if we regard the Person made to suffer, He who had gathered in Himself that nature.

italian: Però d’un atto uscir cose diverse: ch’a Dio e a’ Giudei piacque una morte; per lei tremò la terra e ’l ciel s’aperse.
english: Thus, from one action, issued differing things: God and the Jews were pleased by one same death; earth trembled for that death and Heaven opened.

italian: Non ti dee oramai parer più forte, quando si dice che giusta vendetta poscia vengiata fu da giusta corte.
english: You need no longer find it difficult to understand when it is said that just vengeance was then avenged by a just court.

italian: Ma io veggi’ or la tua mente ristretta di pensiero in pensier dentro ad un nodo, del qual con gran disio solver s’aspetta.
english: But I now see your understanding tangled by thought on thought into a knot, from which, with much desire, your mind awaits release.

italian: Tu dici: “Ben discerno ciò ch’i’ odo; ma perché Dio volesse, m’è occulto, a nostra redenzion pur questo modo”.
english: You say: ‘What I have heard is clear to me; but this is hidden from me—why God willed precisely this pathway for our redemption.’

italian: Questo decreto, frate, sta sepulto a li occhi di ciascuno il cui ingegno ne la fiamma d’amor non è adulto.
english: Brother, this ordinance is buried from the eyes of everyone whose intellect has not matured within the flame of love.

italian: Veramente, però ch’a questo segno molto si mira e poco si discerne, dirò perché tal modo fu più degno.
english: Nevertheless, since there is much attempting to find this point, but little understanding, I shall tell why that way was the most fitting.

italian: La divina bontà, che da sé sperne ogne livore, ardendo in sé, sfavilla sì che dispiega le bellezze etterne.
english: The Godly Goodness that has banished every envy from Its own Self, burns in Itself; and sparkling so, It shows eternal beauties.

italian: Ciò che da lei sanza mezzo distilla non ha poi fine, perché non si move la sua imprenta quand’ ella sigilla.
english: All that derives directly from this Goodness is everlasting, since the seal of Goodness impresses an imprint that never alters.

italian: Ciò che da essa sanza mezzo piove libero è tutto, perché non soggiace a la virtute de le cose nove.
english: Whatever rains from It immediately is fully free, for it is not constrained by any influence of other things.

italian: Più l’è conforme, e però più le piace; ché l’ardor santo ch’ogne cosa raggia, ne la più somigliante è più vivace.
english: Even as it conforms to that Goodness, so does it please It more; the Sacred Ardor that gleams in all things is most bright within

italian: Di tutte queste dote s’avvantaggia l’umana creatura, e s’una manca, di sua nobilità convien che caggia.
english: those things most like Itself. The human being has all these gifts, but if it loses one, then its nobility has been undone.

italian: Solo il peccato è quel che la disfranca e falla dissimìle al sommo bene, per che del lume suo poco s’imbianca;
english: Only man’s sin annuls man’s liberty, makes him unlike the Highest Good, so that, in him, the brightness of Its light is dimmed;

italian: e in sua dignità mai non rivene, se non rïempie, dove colpa vòta, contra mal dilettar con giuste pene.
english: and man cannot regain his dignity unless, where sin left emptiness, man fills that void with just amends for evil pleasure.

italian: Vostra natura, quando peccò tota nel seme suo, da queste dignitadi, come di paradiso, fu remota;
english: For when your nature sinned so totally within its seed, then, from these dignities, just as from Paradise, that nature parted;

italian: né ricovrar potiensi, se tu badi ben sottilmente, per alcuna via, sanza passar per un di questi guadi:
english: and they could never be regained—if you consider carefully—by any way that did not pass across one of these fords:

italian: o che Dio solo per sua cortesia dimesso avesse, o che l’uom per sé isso avesse sodisfatto a sua follia.
english: either through nothing other than His mercy, God had to pardon man, or of himself man had to proffer payment for his folly.

italian: Ficca mo l’occhio per entro l’abisso de l’etterno consiglio, quanto puoi al mio parlar distrettamente fisso.
english: Now fix your eyes on the profundity of the Eternal Counsel; heed as closely as you are able to, my reasoning.

english: Winds, seen or unseen, never have descended so swiftly from cold clouds as not to seem impeded, slow, to any who had seen

english: His niggard nature is descended from one who was generous; and he needs soldiers who are not bent on filling up their coffers.

italian: Lo ben che tutto il regno che tu scandi volge e contenta, fa esser virtute sua provedenza in questi corpi grandi.

italian: E non pur le nature provedute sono in la mente ch’è da sé perfetta, ma esse insieme con la lor salute:

italian: per che quantunque quest’ arco saetta disposto cade a proveduto fine, sì come cosa in suo segno diretta.
english: and thus, whatever this bow shoots must fall according to a providential end, just like a shaft directed to its target.
