english: The other joy, already known to me as precious, then appeared before my eyes like a pure ruby struck by the sun’s rays.

italian: Qui si rimira ne l’arte ch’addorna cotanto affetto, e discernesi ’l bene per che ’l mondo di sù quel di giù torna.
english: For here we contemplate the art adorned by such great love, and we discern the good through which the world above forms that below.

italian: Ma perché tutte le tue voglie piene ten porti che son nate in questa spera, proceder ancor oltre mi convene.
english: But so that all your longings born within this sphere may be completely satisfied when you bear them away, I must continue.

italian: Tu vuo’ saper chi è in questa lumera che qui appresso me così scintilla come raggio di sole in acqua mera.
english: You wish to know what spirit is within the light that here beside me sparkles so, as would a ray of sun in limpid water.

italian: Or sappi che là entro si tranquilla Raab; e a nostr’ ordine congiunta, di lei nel sommo grado si sigilla.
english: Know then that Rahab lives serenely in that light, and since her presence joins our order, she seals that order in the highest rank.

italian: Da questo cielo, in cui l’ombra s’appunta che ’l vostro mondo face, pria ch’altr’ alma del trïunfo di Cristo fu assunta.
english: This heaven, where the shadow cast by earth comes to a point, had Rahab as the first soul to be taken up when Christ triumphed.

italian: Ben si convenne lei lasciar per palma in alcun cielo de l’alta vittoria che s’acquistò con l’una e l’altra palma,
english: And it was right to leave her in this heaven as trophy of the lofty victory that Christ won, palm on palm, upon the cross,

italian: perch’ ella favorò la prima gloria di Iosüè in su la Terra Santa, che poco tocca al papa la memoria.
english: for she had favored the initial glory of Joshua within the Holy Land which seldom touches the Pope’s memory.

italian: La tua città, che di colui è pianta che pria volse le spalle al suo fattore e di cui è la ’nvidia tanto pianta,
english: Your city, which was planted by that one who was the first to turn against his Maker, the one whose envy cost us many tears

italian: produce e spande il maladetto fiore c’ha disvïate le pecore e li agni, però che fatto ha lupo del pastore.
english: produces and distributes the damned flower that turns both sheep and lambs from the true course, for of the shepherd it has made a wolf.

italian: Per questo l’Evangelio e i dottor magni son derelitti, e solo ai Decretali si studia, sì che pare a’ lor vivagni.
english: For this the Gospel and the great Church Fathers are set aside and only the Decretals are studied as their margins clearly show.

italian: A questo intende il papa e ’ cardinali; non vanno i lor pensieri a Nazarette, là dove Gabrïello aperse l’ali.
english: On these the pope and cardinals are intent. Their thoughts are never bent on Nazareth, where Gabriel’s open wings were reverent.

italian: Ma Vaticano e l’altre parti elette di Roma che son state cimitero a la milizia che Pietro seguette,
english: And yet the hill of Vatican as well as other noble parts of Rome that were the cemetery for Peter’s soldiery

italian: tosto libere fien de l’avoltero».
english: will soon be freed from priests’ adultery.

italian: ﻿Guardando nel suo Figlio con l’Amore che l’uno e l’altro etternalmente spira, lo primo e ineffabile Valore
english: Gazing upon His Son with that Love which One and the Other breathe eternally, the Power—first and inexpressible—

italian: quanto per mente e per loco si gira con tant’ ordine fé, ch’esser non puote sanza gustar di lui chi ciò rimira.
english: made everything that wheels through mind and space so orderly that one who contemplates that harmony cannot but taste of Him.

italian: Leva dunque, lettore, a l’alte rote meco la vista, dritto a quella parte dove l’un moto e l’altro si percuote;
english: Then, reader, lift your eyes with me to see the high wheels; gaze directly at that part where the one motion strikes against the other;

italian: e lì comincia a vagheggiar ne l’arte di quel maestro che dentro a sé l’ama, tanto che mai da lei l’occhio non parte.
english: and there begin to look with longing at that Master’s art, which in Himself he loves so much that his eye never parts from it.

italian: Vedi come da indi si dirama l’oblico cerchio che i pianeti porta, per sodisfare al mondo che li chiama.
english: See there the circle branching from that cross—point obliquely: zodiac to bear the planets that satisfy the world in need of them.

italian: Che se la strada lor non fosse torta, molta virtù nel ciel sarebbe in vano, e quasi ogne potenza qua giù morta;
english: For if the planets’ path were not aslant, much of the heavens’ virtue would be wasted and almost every power on earth be dead;

italian: e se dal dritto più o men lontano fosse ’l partire, assai sarebbe manco e giù e sù de l’ordine mondano.
english: and if the zodiac swerved more or less far from the straight course, then earth’s harmony would be defective in both hemispheres.

italian: Or ti riman, lettor, sovra ’l tuo banco, dietro pensando a ciò che si preliba, s’esser vuoi lieto assai prima che stanco.
english: Now, reader, do not leave your bench, but stay to think on that of which you have foretaste; you will have much delight before you tire.

italian: Messo t’ho innanzi: omai per te ti ciba; ché a sé torce tutta la mia cura quella materia ond’ io son fatto scriba.
english: I have prepared your fare; now feed yourself, because that matter of which I am made the scribe calls all my care unto itself.

italian: Lo ministro maggior de la natura, che del valor del ciel lo mondo imprenta e col suo lume il tempo ne misura,
english: The greatest minister of nature—he who imprints earth with heaven’s worth and, with his light, provides the measurement for time—

italian: con quella parte che sù si rammenta congiunto, si girava per le spire in che più tosto ognora s’appresenta;
english: since he was in conjunction with the part I noted, now was wheeling through the spirals where he appears more early every day.

italian: e io era con lui; ma del salire non m’accors’ io, se non com’ uom s’accorge, anzi ’l primo pensier, del suo venire.
english: And I was with him, but no more aware of the ascent than one can be aware of any sudden thought before it starts.

italian: È Bëatrice quella che sì scorge di bene in meglio, sì subitamente che l’atto suo per tempo non si sporge.
english: The one who guides me so from good to better is Beatrice, and on our path her acts have so much swiftness that they span no time.

italian: Quant’ esser convenia da sé lucente quel ch’era dentro al sol dov’ io entra’mi, non per color, ma per lume parvente!
english: How bright within themselves must be the lights I saw on entering the Sun, for they were known to me by splendor, not by color!

italian: Perch’ io lo ’ngegno e l’arte e l’uso chiami, sì nol direi che mai s’imaginasse; ma creder puossi e di veder si brami.
english: Though I should call on talent, craft, and practice, my telling cannot help them be imagined; but you can trust—and may you long to see it.

italian: E se le fantasie nostre son basse a tanta altezza, non è maraviglia; ché sopra ’l sol non fu occhio ch’andasse.
english: And if our fantasies fall short before such heights, there is no need to wonder; for no eye has seen light brighter than the Sun’s.

italian: Tal era quivi la quarta famiglia de l’alto Padre, che sempre la sazia, mostrando come spira e come figlia.
english: Such was the sphere of His fourth family, whom the High Father always satisfies, showing how He engenders and breathes forth.

italian: E Bëatrice cominciò: «Ringrazia, ringrazia il Sol de li angeli, ch’a questo sensibil t’ha levato per sua grazia».
english: And Beatrice began: “Give thanks, give thanks to Him, the angels’ Sun, who, through His grace, has lifted you to this embodied sun.”

italian: Cor di mortal non fu mai sì digesto a divozione e a rendersi a Dio con tutto ’l suo gradir cotanto presto,
english: No mortal heart was ever so disposed to worship, or so quick to yield itself to God with all its gratefulness, as I

italian: come a quelle parole mi fec’ io; e sì tutto ’l mio amore in lui si mise, che Bëatrice eclissò ne l’oblio.
english: was when I heard those words, and all my love was so intent on Him that Beatrice was then eclipsed within forgetfulness.

italian: Non le dispiacque; ma sì se ne rise, che lo splendor de li occhi suoi ridenti mia mente unita in più cose divise.
english: And she was not displeased, but smiled at this, so that the splendor of her smiling eyes divided my rapt mind between two objects.

italian: Io vidi più folgór vivi e vincenti far di noi centro e di sé far corona, più dolci in voce che in vista lucenti:
english: And I saw many lights, alive, most bright; we formed the center, they became a crown, their voices even sweeter than their splendor:

italian: così cinger la figlia di Latona vedem talvolta, quando l’aere è pregno, sì che ritenga il fil che fa la zona.
english: just so, at times, we see Latona’s daughter circled when saturated air holds fast the thread that forms the girdle of her halo.

italian: Ne la corte del cielo, ond’ io rivegno, si trovan molte gioie care e belle tanto che non si posson trar del regno;
english: In Heaven’s court, from which I have returned, one finds so many fair and precious gems that are not to be taken from that kingdom:

italian: e ’l canto di quei lumi era di quelle; chi non s’impenna sì che là sù voli, dal muto aspetti quindi le novelle.
english: one of those gems, the song those splendors sang. He who does not take wings to reach that realm, may wait for tidings of it from the mute.

italian: Poi, sì cantando, quelli ardenti soli si fuor girati intorno a noi tre volte, come stelle vicine a’ fermi poli,
english: After those ardent suns, while singing so, had wheeled three times around us, even as stars that are close to the fixed poles, they seemed

italian: donne mi parver, non da ballo sciolte, ma che s’arrestin tacite, ascoltando fin che le nove note hanno ricolte.
english: to me like women who, though not released from dancing, pause in silence, listening until new notes invite to new dancing.

italian: E dentro a l’un senti’ cominciar: «Quando lo raggio de la grazia, onde s’accende verace amore e che poi cresce amando,
english: And from within one light I heard begin: “Because the ray of grace, from which true love is kindled first and then, in loving, grows,

italian: multiplicato in te tanto resplende, che ti conduce su per quella scala u’ sanza risalir nessun discende;
english: shines with such splendor, multiplied, in you, that it has led you up the stair that none descends who will not climb that stair again,

italian: qual ti negasse il vin de la sua fiala per la tua sete, in libertà non fora se non com’ acqua ch’al mar non si cala.
english: whoever would refuse to quench your thirst with wine from his flask, would be no more free than water that does not flow toward the sea.

italian: Tu vuo’ saper di quai piante s’infiora questa ghirlanda che ’ntorno vagheggia la bella donna ch’al ciel t’avvalora.
english: You want to know what plants bloom in this garland that, circling, contemplates with love the fair lady who strengthens your ascent to heaven.

italian: Io fui de li agni de la santa greggia che Domenico mena per cammino u’ ben s’impingua se non si vaneggia.
english: I was a lamb among the holy flock that Dominic leads on the path where one may fatten well if one does not stray off.

italian: Questi che m’è a destra più vicino, frate e maestro fummi, ed esso Alberto è di Cologna, e io Thomas d’Aquino.
english: He who is nearest on my right was both my brother and my teacher: from Cologne, Albert, and I am Thomas of Aquino.

italian: Se sì di tutti li altri esser vuo’ certo, di retro al mio parlar ten vien col viso girando su per lo beato serto.
english: If you would know who all the others are, then even as I speak let your eyes follow, making their way around the holy wreath.

italian: Quell’ altro fiammeggiare esce del riso di Grazïan, che l’uno e l’altro foro aiutò sì che piace in paradiso.
english: That next flame issues from the smile of Gratian, who served one and the other court of law so well that his work pleases Paradise.

italian: L’altro ch’appresso addorna il nostro coro, quel Pietro fu che con la poverella offerse a Santa Chiesa suo tesoro.
english: That other, who adorns our choir next— he was that Peter who, like the poor widow, offered his treasure to the Holy Church.

italian: La quinta luce, ch’è tra noi più bella, spira di tale amor, che tutto ’l mondo là giù ne gola di saper novella:
english: The fifth light, and the fairest light among us, breathes forth such love that all the world below hungers for tidings of it; in that flame

italian: entro v’è l’alta mente u’ sì profondo saver fu messo, che, se ’l vero è vero, a veder tanto non surse il secondo.
english: there is the lofty mind where such profound wisdom was placed that, if the truth be true, no other ever rose with so much vision.

italian: Appresso vedi il lume di quel cero che giù in carne più a dentro vide l’angelica natura e ’l ministero.
english: Next you can see the radiance of that candle which, in the flesh, below, beheld most deeply the angels’ nature and their ministry.

italian: Ne l’altra piccioletta luce ride quello avvocato de’ tempi cristiani del cui latino Augustin si provide.
english: Within the other little light there smiles that champion of the Christian centuries whose narrative was used by Augustine.

italian: Or se tu l’occhio de la mente trani di luce in luce dietro a le mie lode, già de l’ottava con sete rimani.
english: Now, if your mind’s eye, following my praising, was drawn from light to light, you must already be thirsting for the eighth: within that light,

italian: Per vedere ogne ben dentro vi gode l’anima santa che ’l mondo fallace fa manifesto a chi di lei ben ode.
english: because he saw the Greatest Good, rejoices the blessed soul who makes the world’s deceit most plain to all who hear him carefully.

italian: Lo corpo ond’ ella fu cacciata giace giuso in Cieldauro; ed essa da martiro e da essilio venne a questa pace.
english: The flesh from which his soul was banished lies below, within Cieldauro, and he came from martyrdom and exile to this peace.

italian: Vedi oltre fiammeggiar l’ardente spiro d’Isidoro, di Beda e di Riccardo, che a considerar fu più che viro.
english: Beyond, you see, flaming, the ardent spirits of Isidore and Bede and Richard—he whose meditation made him more than man.

italian: Questi onde a me ritorna il tuo riguardo, è ’l lume d’uno spirto che ’n pensieri gravi a morir li parve venir tardo:
english: This light from whom your gaze returns to me contains a spirit whose oppressive thoughts made him see death as coming much too slowly:

italian: essa è la luce etterna di Sigieri, che, leggendo nel Vico de li Strami, silogizzò invidïosi veri».
english: it is the everlasting light of Siger, who when he lectured in the Street of Straw demonstrated truths that earned him envy.”

italian: Indi, come orologio che ne chiami ne l’ora che la sposa di Dio surge a mattinar lo sposo perché l’ami,
english: Then, like a clock that calls us at the hour in which the Bride of God, on waking, sings matins to her Bridegroom, encouraging

italian: che l’una parte e l’altra tira e urge, tin tin sonando con sì dolce nota, che ’l ben disposto spirto d’amor turge;
english: His love (when each clock—part both drives and draws), chiming the sounds with notes so sweet that those with spirit well—disposed feel their love grow;

italian: così vid’ ïo la gloriosa rota muoversi e render voce a voce in tempra e in dolcezza ch’esser non pò nota
english: so did I see the wheel that moved in glory go round and render voice to voice with such sweetness and such accord that they can not

italian: se non colà dove gioir s’insempra.
english: be known except where joy is everlasting

italian: O insensata cura de’ mortali, quanto son difettivi silogismi quei che ti fanno in basso batter l’ali!
english: O senseless cares of mortals, how deceiving are syllogistic reasonings that bring your wings to flight so low, to earthly things!

italian: Chi dietro a iura e chi ad amforismi sen giva, e chi seguendo sacerdozio, e chi regnar per forza o per sofismi,
english: One studied law and one the Aphorisms of the physicians; one was set on priesthood and one, through force or fraud, on rulership;

italian: e chi rubare e chi civil negozio, chi nel diletto de la carne involto s’affaticava e chi si dava a l’ozio,
english: one meant to plunder, one to politick; one labored, tangled in delights of flesh, and one was fully bent on indolence;

italian: quando, da tutte queste cose sciolto, con Bëatrice m’era suso in cielo cotanto glorïosamente accolto.
english: while I, delivered from our servitude to all these things, was in the height of heaven with Beatrice, so gloriously welcomed.

italian: Poi che ciascuno fu tornato ne lo punto del cerchio in che avanti s’era, fermossi, come a candellier candelo.
english: After each of those spirits had returned to that place in the ring where it had been, it halted, like a candle in its stand.

italian: E io senti’ dentro a quella lumera che pria m’avea parlato, sorridendo incominciar, faccendosi più mera:
english: And from within the splendor that had spoken to me before, I heard him, as he smiled— become more radiant, more pure—begin:

italian: «Così com’ io del suo raggio resplendo, sì, riguardando ne la luce etterna, li tuoi pensieri onde cagioni apprendo.
english: “Even as I grow bright within Its rays, so, as I gaze at the Eternal Light, I can perceive your thoughts and see their cause.

italian: Tu dubbi, e hai voler che si ricerna in sì aperta e ’n sì distesa lingua lo dicer mio, ch’al tuo sentir si sterna,
english: You are in doubt; you want an explanation in language that is open and expanded, so clear that it contents your understanding

italian: ove dinanzi dissi: “U’ ben s’impingua”, e là u’ dissi: “Non nacque il secondo”; e qui è uopo che ben si distingua.
english: of two points: where I said, ‘They fatten well,’ and where I said, ‘No other ever rose’— and here one has to make a clear distinction.

italian: La provedenza, che governa il mondo con quel consiglio nel quale ogne aspetto creato è vinto pria che vada al fondo,
english: The Providence that rules the world with wisdom so fathomless that creatures’ intellects are vanquished and can never probe its depth,

italian: però che andasse ver’ lo suo diletto la sposa di colui ch’ad alte grida disposò lei col sangue benedetto,
english: so that the Bride of Him who, with loud cries, had wed her with His blessed blood, might meet her Love with more fidelity and more

italian: in sé sicura e anche a lui più fida, due principi ordinò in suo favore, che quinci e quindi le fosser per guida.
english: assurance in herself, on her behalf commanded that there be two princes, one on this side, one on that side, as her guides.

italian: L’un fu tutto serafico in ardore; l’altro per sapïenza in terra fue di cherubica luce uno splendore.
english: One prince was all seraphic in his ardor; the other, for his wisdom, had possessed the splendor of cherubic light on earth.

italian: De l’un dirò, però che d’amendue si dice l’un pregiando, qual ch’om prende, perch’ ad un fine fur l’opere sue.
english: I shall devote my tale to one, because in praising either prince one praises both: the labors of the two were toward one goal.

italian: Intra Tupino e l’acqua che discende del colle eletto dal beato Ubaldo, fertile costa d’alto monte pende,
english: Between Topino’s stream and that which flows down from the hill the blessed Ubaldo chose, from a high peak there hangs a fertile slope;

italian: onde Perugia sente freddo e caldo da Porta Sole; e di rietro le piange per grave giogo Nocera con Gualdo.
english: from there Perugia feels both heat and cold at Porta Sole, while behind it sorrow Nocera and Gualdo under their hard yoke.

italian: Di questa costa, là dov’ ella frange più sua rattezza, nacque al mondo un sole, come fa questo talvolta di Gange.
english: From this hillside, where it abates its rise, a sun was born into the world, much like this sun when it is climbing from the Ganges.

italian: Però chi d’esso loco fa parole, non dica Ascesi, ché direbbe corto, ma Orïente, se proprio dir vuole.
english: Therefore let him who names this site not say Ascesi, which would be to say too little, but Orient, if he would name it rightly.

italian: Non era ancor molto lontan da l’orto, ch’el cominciò a far sentir la terra de la sua gran virtute alcun conforto;
english: That sun was not yet very distant from his rising, when he caused the earth to take some comfort from his mighty influence;

italian: ché per tal donna, giovinetto, in guerra del padre corse, a cui, come a la morte, la porta del piacer nessun diserra;
english: for even as a youth, he ran to war against his father, on behalf of her— the lady unto whom, just as to death,

italian: e dinanzi a la sua spirital corte et coram patre le si fece unito; poscia di dì in dì l’amò più forte.
english: none willingly unlocks the door; before his spiritual court et coram patre, he wed her; day by day he loved her more.

italian: Questa, privata del primo marito, millecent’ anni e più dispetta e scura fino a costui si stette sanza invito;
english: She was bereft of her first husband; scorned, obscure, for some eleven hundred years, until that sun came, she had had no suitor.

italian: né valse udir che la trovò sicura con Amiclate, al suon de la sua voce, colui ch’a tutto ’l mondo fé paura;
english: Nor did it help her when men heard that he who made earth tremble found her unafraid— serene, with Amyclas—when he addressed her;

italian: né valse esser costante né feroce, sì che, dove Maria rimase giuso, ella con Cristo pianse in su la croce.
english: nor did her constancy and courage help when she, even when Mary stayed below, suffered with Christ upon the cross. But so

italian: Ma perch’ io non proceda troppo chiuso, Francesco e Povertà per questi amanti prendi oramai nel mio parlar diffuso.
english: that I not tell my tale too darkly, you may now take Francis and take Poverty to be the lovers meant in my recounting.

italian: La lor concordia e i lor lieti sembianti, amore e maraviglia e dolce sguardo facieno esser cagion di pensier santi;
english: Their harmony and their glad looks, their love and wonder and their gentle contemplation, served others as a source of holy thoughts;

italian: tanto che ’l venerabile Bernardo si scalzò prima, e dietro a tanta pace corse e, correndo, li parve esser tardo.
english: so much so, that the venerable Bernard went barefoot first; he hurried toward such peace; and though he ran, he thought his pace too slow.

italian: Oh ignota ricchezza! oh ben ferace! Scalzasi Egidio, scalzasi Silvestro dietro a lo sposo, sì la sposa piace.
english: O wealth unknown! O good that is so fruitful! Egidius goes barefoot, and Sylvester, behind the groom—the bride delights them so.

italian: Indi sen va quel padre e quel maestro con la sua donna e con quella famiglia che già legava l’umile capestro.
english: Then Francis—father, master—goes his way with both his lady and his family, the lowly cord already round their waists.

italian: Né li gravò viltà di cuor le ciglia per esser fi’ di Pietro Bernardone, né per parer dispetto a maraviglia;
english: Nor did he lower his eyes in shame because he was the son of Pietro Bernardone, nor for the scorn and wonder he aroused;

italian: ma regalmente sua dura intenzione ad Innocenzio aperse, e da lui ebbe primo sigillo a sua religïone.
english: but like a sovereign, he disclosed in full— to Innocent—the sternness of his rule; from him he had the first seal of his order.

italian: Poi che la gente poverella crebbe dietro a costui, la cui mirabil vita meglio in gloria del ciel si canterebbe,
english: And after many of the poor had followed Francis, whose wondrous life were better sung by glory’s choir in the Empyrean,

italian: di seconda corona redimita fu per Onorio da l’Etterno Spiro la santa voglia d’esto archimandrita.
english: the sacred purpose of this chief of shepherds was then encircled with a second crown by the Eternal Spirit through Honorius.

italian: E poi che, per la sete del martiro, ne la presenza del Soldan superba predicò Cristo e li altri che ’l seguiro,
english: And after, in his thirst for martyrdom, within the presence of the haughty Sultan, he preached of Christ and those who followed Him.

italian: e per trovare a conversione acerba troppo la gente e per non stare indarno, redissi al frutto de l’italica erba,
english: But, finding hearers who were too unripe to be converted, he—not wasting time— returned to harvest the Italian fields;

italian: nel crudo sasso intra Tevero e Arno da Cristo prese l’ultimo sigillo, che le sue membra due anni portarno.
english: there, on the naked crag between the Arno and Tiber, he received the final seal from Christ; and this, his limbs bore for two years.

italian: Quando a colui ch’a tanto ben sortillo piacque di trarlo suso a la mercede ch’el meritò nel suo farsi pusillo,
english: When He who destined Francis to such goodness was pleased to draw him up to the reward that he had won through his humility,

italian: a’ frati suoi, sì com’ a giuste rede, raccomandò la donna sua più cara, e comandò che l’amassero a fede;
english: then to his brothers, as to rightful heirs, Francis commended his most precious lady, and he bade them to love her faithfully;

italian: e del suo grembo l’anima preclara mover si volle, tornando al suo regno, e al suo corpo non volle altra bara.
english: and when, returning to its kingdom, his bright soul wanted to set forth from her bosom, it, for its body, asked no other bier.

italian: Pensa oramai qual fu colui che degno collega fu a mantener la barca di Pietro in alto mar per dritto segno;
english: Consider now that man who was a colleague worthy of Francis; with him, in high seas, he kept the bark of Peter on true course.

italian: e questo fu il nostro patrïarca; per che qual segue lui, com’ el comanda, discerner puoi che buone merce carca.
english: Such was our patriarch; thus you can see that those who follow him as he commands, as cargo carry worthy merchandise.

italian: Ma ’l suo pecuglio di nova vivanda è fatto ghiotto, sì ch’esser non puote che per diversi salti non si spanda;
english: But now his flock is grown so greedy for new nourishment that it must wander far, in search of strange and distant grazing lands;

italian: e quanto le sue pecore remote e vagabunde più da esso vanno, più tornano a l’ovil di latte vòte.
