italian: «A costui fa mestieri, e nol vi dice né con la voce né pensando ancora, d’un altro vero andare a la radice.
english: “He does not tell you of it—not with speech nor in his thoughts as yet—but this man needs to reach the root of still another truth.

italian: Diteli se la luce onde s’infiora vostra sustanza, rimarrà con voi etternalmente sì com’ ell’ è ora;
english: Do tell him if that light with which your soul blossoms will stay with you eternally even as it is now; and if it stays,

italian: e se rimane, dite come, poi che sarete visibili rifatti, esser porà ch’al veder non vi nòi».
english: do tell him how, when you are once again made visible, it will be possible for you to see such light and not be harmed.”

italian: Come, da più letizia pinti e tratti, a la fïata quei che vanno a rota levan la voce e rallegrano li atti,
english: As dancers in a ring, when drawn and driven by greater gladness, lift at times their voices and dance their dance with more exuberance,

italian: così, a l’orazion pronta e divota, li santi cerchi mostrar nova gioia nel torneare e ne la mira nota.
english: so, when they heard that prompt, devout request, the blessed circles showed new joyousness in wheeling dance and in amazing song.

italian: Qual si lamenta perché qui si moia per viver colà sù, non vide quive lo refrigerio de l’etterna ploia.
english: Whoever weeps because on earth we die that we may live on high, has never seen eternal showers that bring refreshment there.

italian: Quell’ uno e due e tre che sempre vive e regna sempre in tre e ’n due e ’n uno, non circunscritto, e tutto circunscrive,
english: That One and Two and Three who ever lives and ever reigns in Three and Two and One, not circumscribed and circumscribing all,

italian: tre volte era cantato da ciascuno di quelli spirti con tal melodia, ch’ad ogne merto saria giusto muno.
english: was sung three times by each and all those souls with such a melody that it would be appropriate reward for every merit.

italian: E io udi’ ne la luce più dia del minor cerchio una voce modesta, forse qual fu da l’angelo a Maria,
english: And I could hear within the smaller circle’s divinest light a modest voice (perhaps much like the angel’s voice in speech to Mary)

italian: risponder: «Quanto fia lunga la festa di paradiso, tanto il nostro amore si raggerà dintorno cotal vesta.
english: reply: “As long as the festivity of Paradise shall be, so long shall our love radiate around us such a garment.

italian: La sua chiarezza séguita l’ardore; l’ardor la visïone, e quella è tanta, quant’ ha di grazia sovra suo valore.
english: Its brightness takes its measure from our ardor, our ardor from our vision, which is measured by what grace each receives beyond his merit.

italian: Come la carne glorïosa e santa fia rivestita, la nostra persona più grata fia per esser tutta quanta;
english: When, glorified and sanctified, the flesh is once again our dress, our persons shall, in being all complete, please all the more;

italian: per che s’accrescerà ciò che ne dona di gratüito lume il sommo bene, lume ch’a lui veder ne condiziona;
english: therefore, whatever light gratuitous the Highest Good gives us will be enhanced— the light that will allow us to see Him;

italian: onde la visïon crescer convene, crescer l’ardor che di quella s’accende, crescer lo raggio che da esso vene.
english: that light will cause our vision to increase, the ardor vision kindles to increase, the brightness born of ardor to increase.

italian: Ma sì come carbon che fiamma rende, e per vivo candor quella soverchia, sì che la sua parvenza si difende;
english: Yet even as a coal engenders flame, but with intenser glow outshines it, so that in that flame the coal persists, it shows,

italian: così questo folgór che già ne cerchia fia vinto in apparenza da la carne che tutto dì la terra ricoperchia;
english: so will the brightness that envelops us be then surpassed in visibility by reborn flesh, which earth now covers up.

italian: né potrà tanta luce affaticarne: ché li organi del corpo saran forti a tutto ciò che potrà dilettarne».
english: Nor will we tire when faced with such bright light, for then the body’s organs will have force enough for all in which we can delight.”

italian: Tanto mi parver sùbiti e accorti e l’uno e l’altro coro a dicer «Amme!», che ben mostrar disio d’i corpi morti:
english: One and the other choir seemed to me so quick and keen to say “Amen” that they showed clearly how they longed for their dead bodies—

italian: forse non pur per lor, ma per le mamme, per li padri e per li altri che fuor cari anzi che fosser sempiterne fiamme.
english: not only for themselves, perhaps, but for their mothers, fathers, and for others dear to them before they were eternal flames.

italian: Ed ecco intorno, di chiarezza pari, nascere un lustro sopra quel che v’era, per guisa d’orizzonte che rischiari.
english: And—look!—beyond the light already there, an added luster rose around those rings, even as a horizon brightening.

italian: E sì come al salir di prima sera comincian per lo ciel nove parvenze, sì che la vista pare e non par vera,
english: And even as, at the approach of evening, new lights begin to show along the sky, so that the sight seems and does not seem real,

italian: parvemi lì novelle sussistenze cominciare a vedere, e fare un giro di fuor da l’altre due circunferenze.
english: it seemed to me that I began to see new spirits there, forming a ring beyond the choirs with their two circumferences.

italian: Oh vero sfavillar del Santo Spiro! come si fece sùbito e candente a li occhi miei che, vinti, nol soffriro!
english: O the true sparkling of the Holy Ghost— how rapid and how radiant before my eyes that, overcome, could not sustain it!

italian: Ma Bëatrice sì bella e ridente mi si mostrò, che tra quelle vedute si vuol lasciar che non seguir la mente.
english: But, smiling, Beatrice then showed to me such loveliness—it must be left among the visions that take flight from memory.

italian: Quindi ripreser li occhi miei virtute a rilevarsi; e vidimi translato sol con mia donna in più alta salute.
english: From this my eyes regained the strength to look above again; I saw myself translated to higher blessedness, alone with my

italian: Ben m’accors’ io ch’io era più levato, per l’affocato riso de la stella, che mi parea più roggio che l’usato.
english: lady; and I was sure that I had risen because the smiling star was red as fire— beyond the customary red of Mars.

italian: Con tutto ’l core e con quella favella ch’è una in tutti, a Dio feci olocausto, qual conveniesi a la grazia novella.
english: With all my heart and in that language which is one for all, for this new grace I gave to God my holocaust, appropriate.

italian: E non er’ anco del mio petto essausto l’ardor del sacrificio, ch’io conobbi esso litare stato accetto e fausto;
english: Though in my breast that burning sacrifice was not completed yet, I was aware that it had been accepted and auspicious;

italian: ché con tanto lucore e tanto robbi m’apparvero splendor dentro a due raggi, ch’io dissi: «O Elïòs che sì li addobbi!».
english: for splendors, in two rays, appeared to me, so radiant and fiery that I said: “O Helios, you who adorn them thus!”

italian: Come distinta da minori e maggi lumi biancheggia tra ’ poli del mondo Galassia sì, che fa dubbiar ben saggi;
english: As, graced with lesser and with larger lights between the poles of the world, the Galaxy gleams so that even sages are perplexed;

italian: sì costellati facean nel profondo Marte quei raggi il venerabil segno che fan giunture di quadranti in tondo.
english: so, constellated in the depth of Mars, those rays described the venerable sign a circle’s quadrants form where they are joined.

italian: Qui vince la memoria mia lo ’ngegno; ché quella croce lampeggiava Cristo, sì ch’io non so trovare essempro degno;
english: And here my memory defeats my wit: Christ’s flaming from that cross was such that I can find no fit similitude for it.

italian: ma chi prende sua croce e segue Cristo, ancor mi scuserà di quel ch’io lasso, vedendo in quell’ albor balenar Cristo.
english: But he who takes his cross and follows Christ will pardon me again for my omission— my seeing Christ flash forth undid my force.

italian: Di corno in corno e tra la cima e ’l basso si movien lumi, scintillando forte nel congiugnersi insieme e nel trapasso:
english: Lights moved along that cross from horn to horn and from the summit to the base, and as they met and passed, they sparkled, radiant:

italian: così si veggion qui diritte e torte, veloci e tarde, rinovando vista, le minuzie d’i corpi, lunghe e corte,
english: so, straight and slant and quick and slow, one sees on earth the particles of bodies, long and short, in shifting shapes, that move along

italian: moversi per lo raggio onde si lista talvolta l’ombra che, per sua difesa, la gente con ingegno e arte acquista.
english: the ray of light that sometimes streaks across the shade that men devise with skill and art to serve as their defense against the sun.

italian: E come giga e arpa, in tempra tesa di molte corde, fa dolce tintinno a tal da cui la nota non è intesa,
english: And just as harp and viol, whose many chords are tempered, taut, produce sweet harmony although each single note is not distinct,

italian: così da’ lumi che lì m’apparinno s’accogliea per la croce una melode che mi rapiva, sanza intender l’inno.
english: so, from the lights that then appeared to me, out from that cross there spread a melody that held me rapt, although I could not tell

italian: Ben m’accors’ io ch’elli era d’alte lode, però ch’a me venìa «Resurgi» e «Vinci» come a colui che non intende e ode.
english: what hymn it was. I knew it sang high praise, since I heard “Rise” and “Conquer,” but I was as one who hears but cannot seize the sense.

italian: Ïo m’innamorava tanto quinci, che ’nfino a lì non fu alcuna cosa che mi legasse con sì dolci vinci.
english: Yet I was so enchanted by the sound that until then no thing had ever bound me with such gentle bonds. My words may seem

italian: Forse la mia parola par troppo osa, posponendo il piacer de li occhi belli, ne’ quai mirando mio disio ha posa;
english: presumptuous, as though I dared to deem a lesser thing the lovely eyes that bring to my desire, as it gazes, peace.

italian: ma chi s’avvede che i vivi suggelli d’ogne bellezza più fanno più suso, e ch’io non m’era lì rivolto a quelli,
english: But he who notes that, in ascent, her eyes— all beauty’s living seals—gain force, and notes that I had not yet turned to them in Mars,

italian: escusar puommi di quel ch’io m’accuso per escusarmi, e vedermi dir vero: ché ’l piacer santo non è qui dischiuso,
english: can then excuse me—just as I accuse myself, thus to excuse myself—and see that I speak truly: here her holy beauty

italian: perché si fa, montando, più sincero.
english: is not denied—ascent makes it more perfect.

italian: Benigna volontade in che si liqua sempre l’amor che drittamente spira, come cupidità fa ne la iniqua,
english: Generous will—in which is manifest always the love that breathes toward righteousness, as in contorted will is greediness—

italian: silenzio puose a quella dolce lira, e fece quïetar le sante corde che la destra del cielo allenta e tira.
english: imposing silence on that gentle lyre, brought quiet to the consecrated chords that Heaven’s right hand slackens and draws taut.

italian: Come saranno a’ giusti preghi sorde quelle sustanze che, per darmi voglia ch’io le pregassi, a tacer fur concorde?
english: Can souls who prompted me to pray to them, by falling silent all in unison, be deaf to men’s just prayers? Then he may grieve

italian: Bene è che sanza termine si doglia chi, per amor di cosa che non duri etternalmente, quello amor si spoglia.
english: indeed and endlessly—the man who leaves behind such love and turns instead to seek things that do not endure eternally.

italian: Quale per li seren tranquilli e puri discorre ad ora ad or sùbito foco, movendo li occhi che stavan sicuri,
english: As, through the pure and tranquil skies of night, at times a sudden fire shoots, and moves eyes that were motionless—a fire that seems

italian: e pare stella che tramuti loco, se non che da la parte ond’ e’ s’accende nulla sen perde, ed esso dura poco:
english: a star that shifts its place, except that in that portion of the heavens where it flared, nothing is lost, and its own course is short—

italian: tale dal corno che ’n destro si stende a piè di quella croce corse un astro de la costellazion che lì resplende;
english: so, from the horn that stretches on the right, down to the foot of that cross, a star ran out of the constellation glowing there;

italian: né si partì la gemma dal suo nastro, ma per la lista radïal trascorse, che parve foco dietro ad alabastro.
english: nor did that gem desert the cross’s track, but coursed along the radii, and seemed just like a flame that alabaster screens.

italian: Sì pïa l’ombra d’Anchise si porse, se fede merta nostra maggior musa, quando in Eliso del figlio s’accorse.
english: With such affection did Anchises’ shade reach out (if we may trust our greatest muse) when in Elysium he saw his son.

italian: «O sanguis meus, o superinfusa gratïa Deï, sicut tibi cui bis unquam celi ianüa reclusa?».
english: “O blood of mine—o the celestial grace bestowed beyond all measure—unto whom as unto you was Heaven’s gate twice opened?”

italian: Così quel lume: ond’ io m’attesi a lui; poscia rivolsi a la mia donna il viso, e quinci e quindi stupefatto fui;
english: That light said this; at which, I stared at him. Then, looking back to see my lady, I, on this side and on that, was stupefied;

italian: ché dentro a li occhi suoi ardeva un riso tal, ch’io pensai co’ miei toccar lo fondo de la mia gloria e del mio paradiso.
english: for in the smile that glowed within her eyes, I thought that I—with mine—had touched the height of both my blessedness and paradise.

italian: Indi, a udire e a veder giocondo, giunse lo spirto al suo principio cose, ch’io non lo ’ntesi, sì parlò profondo;
english: Then—and he was a joy to hear and see— that spirit added to his first words things that were too deep to meet my understanding.

italian: né per elezïon mi si nascose, ma per necessità, ché ’l suo concetto al segno d’i mortal si soprapuose.
english: Not that he chose to hide his sense from me; necessity compelled him; he conceived beyond the mark a mortal mind can reach.

italian: E quando l’arco de l’ardente affetto fu sì sfogato, che ’l parlar discese inver’ lo segno del nostro intelletto,
english: And when his bow of burning sympathy was slack enough to let his speech descend to meet the limit of our intellect,

italian: la prima cosa che per me s’intese, «Benedetto sia tu», fu, «trino e uno, che nel mio seme se’ tanto cortese!».
english: these were the first words where I caught the sense: “Blessed be you, both Three and One, who show such favor to my seed.” And he continued:

italian: E seguì: «Grato e lontano digiuno, tratto leggendo del magno volume du’ non si muta mai bianco né bruno,
english: “The long and happy hungering I drew from reading that great volume where both black and white are never changed, you—son—have now

italian: solvuto hai, figlio, dentro a questo lume in ch’io ti parlo, mercè di colei ch’a l’alto volo ti vestì le piume.
english: appeased within this light in which I speak to you; for this, I owe my gratitude to her who gave you wings for your high flight.

italian: Tu credi che a me tuo pensier mei da quel ch’è primo, così come raia da l’un, se si conosce, il cinque e ’l sei;
english: You think your thoughts flow into me from Him who is the First—as from the number one, the five and six derive, if one is known—

italian: e però ch’io mi sia e perch’ io paia più gaudïoso a te, non mi domandi, che alcun altro in questa turba gaia.
english: and so you do not ask me who I am and why I seem more joyous to you than all other spirits in this festive throng.

italian: Tu credi ’l vero; ché i minori e ’ grandi di questa vita miran ne lo speglio in che, prima che pensi, il pensier pandi;
english: Your thought is true, for both the small and great of this life gaze into that mirror where, before you think, your thoughts have been displayed.

italian: ma perché ’l sacro amore in che io veglio con perpetüa vista e che m’asseta di dolce disïar, s’adempia meglio,
english: But that the sacred love in which I keep my vigil with unending watchfulness, the love that makes me thirst with sweet desire,

italian: la voce tua sicura, balda e lieta suoni la volontà, suoni ’l disio, a che la mia risposta è già decreta!».
english: be better satisfied, let your voice—bold, assured, and glad—proclaim your will and longing, to which my answer is decreed already.”

italian: Io mi volsi a Beatrice, e quella udio pria ch’io parlassi, e arrisemi un cenno che fece crescer l’ali al voler mio.
english: I turned to Beatrice, but she heard me before I spoke; her smile to me was signal that made the wings of my desire grow.

italian: Poi cominciai così: «L’affetto e ’l senno, come la prima equalità v’apparse, d’un peso per ciascun di voi si fenno,
english: Then I began: “As soon as you beheld the First Equality, both intellect and love weighed equally for each of you,

italian: però che ’l sol che v’allumò e arse, col caldo e con la luce è sì iguali, che tutte simiglianze sono scarse.
english: because the Sun that brought you light and heat possesses heat and light so equally that no thing matches His equality;

italian: Ma voglia e argomento ne’ mortali, per la cagion ch’a voi è manifesta, diversamente son pennuti in ali;
english: whereas in mortals, word and sentiment— to you, the cause of this is evident— are wings whose featherings are disparate.

italian: ond’ io, che son mortal, mi sento in questa disagguaglianza, e però non ringrazio se non col core a la paterna festa.
english: I—mortal—feel this inequality; thus, it is only with my heart that I can offer thanks for your paternal greeting.

italian: Ben supplico io a te, vivo topazio che questa gioia prezïosa ingemmi, perché mi facci del tuo nome sazio».
english: Indeed I do beseech you, living topaz, set in this precious jewel as a gem: fulfill my longing—let me know your name.”

italian: «O fronda mia in che io compiacemmi pur aspettando, io fui la tua radice»: cotal principio, rispondendo, femmi.
english: “O you, my branch in whom I took delight even awaiting you, I am your root,” so he, in his reply to me, began,

italian: Poscia mi disse: «Quel da cui si dice tua cognazione e che cent’ anni e piùe girato ha ’l monte in la prima cornice,
english: then said:”The man who gave your family its name, who for a century and more has circled the first ledge of Purgatory,

italian: mio figlio fu e tuo bisavol fue: ben si convien che la lunga fatica tu li raccorci con l’opere tue.
english: was son to me and was your great-grandfather; it is indeed appropriate for you to shorten his long toil with your good works.

italian: Fiorenza dentro da la cerchia antica, ond’ ella toglie ancora e terza e nona, si stava in pace, sobria e pudica.
english: Florence, within her ancient ring of walls— that ring from which she still draws tierce and nones— sober and chaste, lived in tranquillity.

italian: Non avea catenella, non corona, non gonne contigiate, non cintura che fosse a veder più che la persona.
english: No necklace and no coronal were there, and no embroidered gowns; there was no girdle that caught the eye more than the one who wore it.

italian: Non faceva, nascendo, ancor paura la figlia al padre, che ’l tempo e la dote non fuggien quinci e quindi la misura.
english: No daughter’s birth brought fear unto her father, for age and dowry then did not imbalance— to this side and to that—the proper measure.

italian: Non avea case di famiglia vòte; non v’era giunto ancor Sardanapalo a mostrar ciò che ’n camera si puote.
english: There were no families that bore no children; and Sardanapalus was still a stranger— not come as yet to teach in the bedchamber.

italian: Non era vinto ancora Montemalo dal vostro Uccellatoio, che, com’ è vinto nel montar sù, così sarà nel calo.
english: Not yet had your Uccellatoio’s rise outdone the rise of Monte Mario, which, too, will be outdone in its decline.

italian: Bellincion Berti vid’ io andar cinto di cuoio e d’osso, e venir da lo specchio la donna sua sanza ’l viso dipinto;
english: I saw Bellincione Berti girt with leather and with bone, and saw his wife come from her mirror with her face unpainted.

italian: e vidi quel d’i Nerli e quel del Vecchio esser contenti a la pelle scoperta, e le sue donne al fuso e al pennecchio.
english: I saw dei Nerli and del Vecchio content to wear their suits of unlined skins, and saw their wives at spindle and at spool.

italian: Oh fortunate! ciascuna era certa de la sua sepultura, e ancor nulla era per Francia nel letto diserta.
english: O happy wives! Each one was sure of her own burial place, and none—for France’s sake— as yet was left deserted in her bed.

italian: L’una vegghiava a studio de la culla, e, consolando, usava l’idïoma che prima i padri e le madri trastulla;
english: One woman watched with loving care the cradle and, as she soothed her infant, used the way of speech with which fathers and mothers play;

italian: l’altra, traendo a la rocca la chioma, favoleggiava con la sua famiglia d’i Troiani, di Fiesole e di Roma.
english: another, as she drew threads from the distaff, would tell, among her household, tales of Trojans, and tales of Fiesole, and tales of Rome.

italian: Saria tenuta allor tal maraviglia una Cianghella, un Lapo Salterello, qual or saria Cincinnato e Corniglia.
english: A Lapo Salterello, a Cianghella, would then have stirred as much dismay as now a Cincinnatus and Cornelia would.

italian: A così riposato, a così bello viver di cittadini, a così fida cittadinanza, a così dolce ostello,
english: To such a life—so tranquil and so lovely— of citizens in true community, into so sweet a dwelling place did Mary,

italian: Maria mi diè, chiamata in alte grida; e ne l’antico vostro Batisteo insieme fui cristiano e Cacciaguida.
english: invoked in pains of birth, deliver me; and I, within your ancient Baptistery, at once became Christian and Cacciaguida.

italian: Moronto fu mio frate ed Eliseo; mia donna venne a me di val di Pado, e quindi il sopranome tuo si feo.
english: Moronto was my brother, and Eliseo; my wife came from the valley of the Po— the surname that you bear was brought by her.

italian: Poi seguitai lo ’mperador Currado; ed el mi cinse de la sua milizia, tanto per bene ovrar li venni in grado.
english: In later years I served the Emperor Conrad—and my good works so gained his favor that he gave me the girdle of his knighthood.

italian: Dietro li andai incontro a la nequizia di quella legge il cui popolo usurpa, per colpa d’i pastor, vostra giustizia.
english: I followed him to war against the evil of that law whose adherents have usurped— this, through your Pastors’ fault—your just possessions.

italian: Quivi fu’ io da quella gente turpa disviluppato dal mondo fallace, lo cui amor molt’ anime deturpa;
english: There, by that execrable race, I was set free from fetters of the erring world, the love of which defiles so many souls.

italian: e venni dal martiro a questa pace».
english: From martyrdom I came unto this peace.”

italian: O poca nostra nobiltà di sangue, se glorïar di te la gente fai qua giù dove l’affetto nostro langue,
english: If here below, where sentiment is far too weak to withstand error, I should see men glorying in you, nobility

italian: mirabil cosa non mi sarà mai: ché là dove appetito non si torce, dico nel cielo, io me ne gloriai.
english: of blood—a meager thing!—I should not wonder, for even where desire is not awry, I mean in Heaven, I too felt such pride.

italian: Ben se’ tu manto che tosto raccorce: sì che, se non s’appon di dì in die, lo tempo va dintorno con le force.
english: You are indeed a cloak that soon wears out, so that if, day by day, we add no patch, then circling time will trim you with its shears.

italian: Dal ‘voi’ che prima a Roma s’offerie, in che la sua famiglia men persevra, ricominciaron le parole mie;
english: My speech began again with you, the word that Rome was the first city to allow, although her people seldom speak it now;

italian: onde Beatrice, ch’era un poco scevra, ridendo, parve quella che tossio al primo fallo scritto di Ginevra.
english: at this word, Beatrice, somewhat apart, smiling, seemed like the woman who had coughed— so goes the tale—at Guinevere’s first fault.

italian: Io cominciai: «Voi siete il padre mio; voi mi date a parlar tutta baldezza; voi mi levate sì, ch’i’ son più ch’io.
english: So did my speech begin: “You are my father; you hearten me to speak with confidence; you raise me so that I am more than I.

italian: Per tanti rivi s’empie d’allegrezza la mente mia, che di sé fa letizia perché può sostener che non si spezza.
english: So many streams have filled my mind with gladness— so many, and such gladness, that mind must rejoice that it can bear this and not burst.

italian: Ditemi dunque, cara mia primizia, quai fuor li vostri antichi e quai fuor li anni che si segnaro in vostra püerizia;
english: Then tell me, founder of my family, who were your ancestors and, in your boyhood, what were the years the records registered;

italian: ditemi de l’ovil di San Giovanni quanto era allora, e chi eran le genti tra esso degne di più alti scanni».
english: and tell me of the sheepfold of St. John— how numerous it was, who in that flock were worthy of the highest offices.”

italian: Come s’avviva a lo spirar d’i venti carbone in fiamma, così vid’ io quella luce risplendere a’ miei blandimenti;
english: As at the breathing of the winds, a coal will quicken into flame, so I saw that light glow at words that were affectionate;

italian: e come a li occhi miei si fé più bella, così con voce più dolce e soave, ma non con questa moderna favella,
english: and as, before my eyes, it grew more fair, so, with a voice more gentle and more sweet— not in our modern speech—it said to me:

italian: dissemi: «Da quel dì che fu detto ‘ Ave ’ al parto in che mia madre, ch’è or santa, s’allevïò di me ond’ era grave,
english: “Down from that day when Ave was pronounced, until my mother (blessed now), by giving birth, eased the burden borne in bearing me,

italian: al suo Leon cinquecento cinquanta e trenta fiate venne questo foco a rinfiammarsi sotto la sua pianta.
english: this fire of Mars had come five-hundred-fifty and thirty more times to its Lion—there to be rekindled underneath its paw.

italian: Li antichi miei e io nacqui nel loco dove si truova pria l’ultimo sesto da quei che corre il vostro annüal gioco.
english: My ancestors and I were born just where the runner in your yearly games first comes upon the boundary of the final ward.

italian: Basti d’i miei maggiori udirne questo: chi ei si fosser e onde venner quivi, più è tacer che ragionare onesto.
english: That is enough concerning my forebears: what were their names, from where they came—of that, silence, not speech, is more appropriate.

italian: Tutti color ch’a quel tempo eran ivi da poter arme tra Marte e ’l Batista, eran il quinto di quei ch’or son vivi.
english: All those who, at that time, between the Baptist and Mars, were capable of bearing arms, numbered one fifth of those who live there now.

italian: Ma la cittadinanza, ch’è or mista di Campi, di Certaldo e di Fegghine, pura vediesi ne l’ultimo artista.
english: But then the citizens, now mixed with Campi, with the Certaldo, and with the Figline, were pure down to the humblest artisan.

italian: Oh quanto fora meglio esser vicine quelle genti ch’io dico, e al Galluzzo e a Trespiano aver vostro confine,
english: Oh, it would be far better if you had those whom I mention as your neighbors (and your boundaries at Galuzzo and Trespiano),

italian: che averle dentro e sostener lo puzzo del villan d’Aguglion, di quel da Signa, che già per barattare ha l’occhio aguzzo!
english: than to have them within, to bear the stench of Aguglione’s wretch and Signa’s wretch, whose sharp eyes now on barratry are set.

italian: Se la gente ch’al mondo più traligna non fosse stata a Cesare noverca, ma come madre a suo figlio benigna,
english: If those who, in the world, go most astray had not seen Caesar with stepmothers’ eyes, but, like a mother to her son, been kind,

italian: tal fatto è fiorentino e cambia e merca, che si sarebbe vòlto a Simifonti, là dove andava l’avolo a la cerca;
english: then one who has become a Florentine trader and money changer would have stayed in Semifonte, where his fathers peddled,

italian: sariesi Montemurlo ancor de’ Conti; sarieno i Cerchi nel piovier d’Acone, e forse in Valdigrieve i Buondelmonti.
english: the Counts would still be lords of Montemurlo, the Cerchi would be in Acone’s parish, perhaps the Buondelmonti in Valdigreve.

italian: Sempre la confusion de le persone principio fu del mal de la cittade, come del vostro il cibo che s’appone;
english: The mingling of the populations led to evil in the city, even as food piled on food destroys the body’s health;

italian: e cieco toro più avaccio cade che cieco agnello; e molte volte taglia più e meglio una che le cinque spade.
english: the blind bull falls more quickly, more headlong, than does the blind lamb; and the one blade can often cut more and better than five swords.

italian: Se tu riguardi Luni e Orbisaglia come sono ite, e come se ne vanno di retro ad esse Chiusi e Sinigaglia,
english: Consider Luni, Urbisaglia, how they went to ruin (Sinigaglia follows, and Chiusi, too, will soon have vanished); then,

italian: udir come le schiatte si disfanno non ti parrà nova cosa né forte, poscia che le cittadi termine hanno.
english: if you should hear of families undone, you will find nothing strange or difficult in that—since even cities meet their end.

italian: Le vostre cose tutte hanno lor morte, sì come voi; ma celasi in alcuna che dura molto, e le vite son corte.
english: All things that you possess, possess their death, just as you do; but in some things that last long, death can hide from you whose lives are short.

italian: E come ’l volger del ciel de la luna cuopre e discuopre i liti sanza posa, così fa di Fiorenza la Fortuna:
english: And even as the heaven of the moon, revolving, respiteless, conceals and then reveals the shores, so Fortune does with Florence;

italian: per che non dee parer mirabil cosa ciò ch’io dirò de li alti Fiorentini onde è la fama nel tempo nascosa.
english: therefore, there is no cause for wonder in what I shall tell of noble Florentines, of those whose reputations time has hidden.

italian: Io vidi li Ughi e vidi i Catellini, Filippi, Greci, Ormanni e Alberichi, già nel calare, illustri cittadini;
english: I saw the Ughi, saw the Catellini, Filippi, Greci, Ormanni, Alberichi, famed citizens already in decline,

italian: e vidi così grandi come antichi, con quel de la Sannella, quel de l’Arca, e Soldanieri e Ardinghi e Bostichi.
english: and saw, as great as they were venerable, dell’Arca with della Sannella, and Ardinghi, Soldanieri, and Bostichi.

italian: Sovra la porta ch’al presente è carca di nova fellonia di tanto peso che tosto fia iattura de la barca,
english: Nearby the gate that now is burdened with new treachery that weighs so heavily that it will bring the vessel to shipwreck,

italian: erano i Ravignani, ond’ è disceso il conte Guido e qualunque del nome de l’alto Bellincione ha poscia preso.
english: there were the Ravignani, from whose line Count Guido comes and all who—since—derive their name from the illustrious Bellincione.

italian: Quel de la Pressa sapeva già come regger si vuole, e avea Galigaio dorata in casa sua già l’elsa e ’l pome.
english: And della Pressa knew already how to rule; and Galigaio, in his house, already had the gilded hilt and pommel.

italian: Grand’ era già la colonna del Vaio, Sacchetti, Giuochi, Fifanti e Barucci e Galli e quei ch’arrossan per lo staio.
english: The stripe of Vair had mightiness already, as did the Giuochi, Galli, and Barucci, Fifanti, and Sacchetti, and those who

italian: Lo ceppo di che nacquero i Calfucci era già grande, e già eran tratti a le curule Sizii e Arrigucci.
english: blush for the bushel; and the stock from which spring the Calfucci was already mighty, and Sizzi and Arrigucci were already

italian: Oh quali io vidi quei che son disfatti per lor superbia! e le palle de l’oro fiorian Fiorenza in tutt’ i suoi gran fatti.
english: raised to high office. Oh, how great were those I saw—whom pride laid low! And the gold balls, in all of her great actions, flowered Florence.

italian: Così facieno i padri di coloro che, sempre che la vostra chiesa vaca, si fanno grassi stando a consistoro.
english: Such were the ancestors of those who now, whenever bishops’ sees are vacant, grow fat as they sit in church consistories.

italian: L’oltracotata schiatta che s’indraca dietro a chi fugge, e a chi mostra ’l dente o ver la borsa, com’ agnel si placa,
english: The breed—so arrogant and dragonlike in chasing him who flees, but lamblike, meek to him who shows his teeth or else his purse—

italian: già venìa sù, ma di picciola gente; sì che non piacque ad Ubertin Donato che poï il suocero il fé lor parente.
english: was on the rise already, but of stock so mean that Ubertin Donato, when his father-in-law made him kin to them,

italian: Già era ’l Caponsacco nel mercato disceso giù da Fiesole, e già era buon cittadino Giuda e Infangato.
english: was scarcely pleased. Already Caponsacco had come from Fiesole down to the market; already citizens of note were Giuda

italian: Io dirò cosa incredibile e vera: nel picciol cerchio s’entrava per porta che si nomava da quei de la Pera.
english: and Infangato. I shall tell a thing incredible and true: the gateway through the inner walls was named for the della Pera.

italian: Ciascun che de la bella insegna porta del gran barone il cui nome e ’l cui pregio la festa di Tommaso riconforta,
english: All those whose arms bear part of the fair ensign of the great baron—he whose memory and worth are honored on the feast of Thomas—

italian: da esso ebbe milizia e privilegio; avvegna che con popol si rauni oggi colui che la fascia col fregio.
english: received knighthood and privilege from him, though he whose coat of arms has fringed that ensign has taken sides now with the populace.

italian: Già eran Gualterotti e Importuni; e ancor saria Borgo più quïeto, se di novi vicin fosser digiuni.
english: The Gualterotti and the Importuni were there already; were the Borgo spared new neighbors, it would still be tranquil there.

italian: La casa di che nacque il vostro fleto, per lo giusto disdegno che v’ha morti e puose fine al vostro viver lieto,
english: The house of Amidei, with which your sorrows began—by reason of its just resentment, which ruined you and ended years of gladness—

italian: era onorata, essa e suoi consorti: o Buondelmonte, quanto mal fuggisti le nozze süe per li altrui conforti!
english: was honored then, as were its close companions. O Buondelmonte, through another’s counsel, you fled your wedding pledge, and brought such evil!

italian: Molti sarebber lieti, che son tristi, se Dio t’avesse conceduto ad Ema la prima volta ch’a città venisti.
english: Many would now rejoice, who still lament, if when you first approached the city, God had given you unto the river Ema!

italian: Ma conveniesi a quella pietra scema che guarda ’l ponte, che Fiorenza fesse vittima ne la sua pace postrema.
english: But Florence, in her final peace, was fated to offer up—unto that mutilated stone guardian upon her bridge—a victim.

italian: Con queste genti, e con altre con esse, vid’ io Fiorenza in sì fatto riposo, che non avea cagione onde piangesse.
english: These were the families, and others with them: the Florence that I saw—in such repose that there was nothing to have caused her sorrow.

italian: Con queste genti vid’io glorïoso e giusto il popol suo, tanto che ’l giglio non era ad asta mai posto a ritroso,
english: These were the families: with them I saw her people so acclaimed and just, that on her staff the lily never was reversed,

italian: né per divisïon fatto vermiglio».
english: nor was it made bloodred by factious hatred.”

italian: ﻿Qual venne a Climenè, per accertarsi di ciò ch’avëa incontro a sé udito, quei ch’ancor fa li padri ai figli scarsi;
english: Like Phaethon (one who still makes fathers wary of sons) when he had heard insinuations, and he, to be assured, came to Clymene,

italian: tal era io, e tal era sentito e da Beatrice e da la santa lampa che pria per me avea mutato sito.
english: such was I and such was I seen to be by Beatrice and by the holy lamp that—earlier—had shifted place for me.

italian: Per che mia donna «Manda fuor la vampa del tuo disio», mi disse, «sì ch’ella esca segnata bene de la interna stampa:
english: Therefore my lady said to me: “Display the flame of your desire, that it may be seen well-stamped with your internal seal,

italian: non perché nostra conoscenza cresca per tuo parlare, ma perché t’ausi a dir la sete, sì che l’uom ti mesca».
english: not that we need to know what you’d reveal, but that you learn the way that would disclose your thirst, and you be quenched by what we pour.”

italian: «O cara piota mia che sì t’insusi, che, come veggion le terrene menti non capere in trïangol due ottusi,
english: “O my dear root, who, since you rise so high, can see the Point in which all times are present— for just as earthly minds are able to

italian: così vedi le cose contingenti anzi che sieno in sé, mirando il punto a cui tutti li tempi son presenti;
english: see that two obtuse angles cannot be contained in a triangle, you can see contingent things before they come to be—

italian: mentre ch’io era a Virgilio congiunto su per lo monte che l’anime cura e discendendo nel mondo defunto,
english: while I was in the company of Virgil, both on the mountain that heals souls and when descending to the dead world, what I heard

italian: dette mi fuor di mia vita futura parole gravi, avvegna ch’io mi senta ben tetragono ai colpi di ventura;
english: about my future life were grievous words— although, against the blows of chance I feel myself as firmly planted as a cube.

italian: per che la voglia mia saria contenta d’intender qual fortuna mi s’appressa: ché saetta previsa vien più lenta».
english: Thus my desire would be appeased if I might know what fortune is approaching me: the arrow one foresees arrives more gently.”

italian: Così diss’ io a quella luce stessa che pria m’avea parlato; e come volle Beatrice, fu la mia voglia confessa.
english: So did I speak to the same living light that spoke to me before; as Beatrice had wished, what was my wish was now confessed.

italian: Né per ambage, in che la gente folle già s’inviscava pria che fosse anciso l’Agnel di Dio che le peccata tolle,
english: Not with the maze of words that used to snare the fools upon this earth before the Lamb of God who takes away our sins was slain,

italian: ma per chiare parole e con preciso latin rispuose quello amor paterno, chiuso e parvente del suo proprio riso:
english: but with words plain and unambiguous, that loving father, hidden, yet revealed by his own smile, replied: “Contingency,

italian: «La contingenza, che fuor del quaderno de la vostra matera non si stende, tutta è dipinta nel cospetto etterno;
english: while not extending past the book in which your world of matter has been writ, is yet in the Eternal Vision all depicted

italian: necessità però quindi non prende se non come dal viso in che si specchia nave che per torrente giù discende.
english: (but this does not imply necessity, just as a ship that sails downstream is not determined by the eye that watches it).

italian: Da indi, sì come viene ad orecchia dolce armonia da organo, mi viene a vista il tempo che ti s’apparecchia.
english: And from that Vision—just as from an organ the ear receives a gentle harmony— what time prepares for you appears to me.

italian: Qual si partio Ipolito d’Atene per la spietata e perfida noverca, tal di Fiorenza partir ti convene.
english: Hippolytus was forced to leave his Athens because of his stepmother, faithless, fierce; and so must you depart from Florence: this

italian: Questo si vuole e questo già si cerca, e tosto verrà fatto a chi ciò pensa là dove Cristo tutto dì si merca.
english: is willed already, sought for, soon to be accomplished by the one who plans and plots where—every day—Christ is both sold and bought.

italian: La colpa seguirà la parte offensa in grido, come suol; ma la vendetta fia testimonio al ver che la dispensa.
english: The blame, as usual, will be cried out against the injured party; but just vengeance will serve as witness to the truth that wields it.

italian: Tu lascerai ogne cosa diletta più caramente; e questo è quello strale che l’arco de lo essilio pria saetta.
english: You shall leave everything you love most dearly: this is the arrow that the bow of exile shoots first. You are to know the bitter taste

italian: Tu proverai sì come sa di sale lo pane altrui, e come è duro calle lo scendere e ’l salir per l’altrui scale.
english: of others’ bread, how salt it is, and know how hard a path it is for one who goes descending and ascending others’ stairs.

italian: E quel che più ti graverà le spalle, sarà la compagnia malvagia e scempia con la qual tu cadrai in questa valle;
english: And what will be most hard for you to bear will be the scheming, senseless company that is to share your fall into this valley;

italian: che tutta ingrata, tutta matta ed empia si farà contr’ a te; ma, poco appresso, ella, non tu, n’avrà rossa la tempia.
english: against you they will be insane, completely ungrateful and profane; and yet, soon after, not you but they will have their brows bloodred.

italian: Di sua bestialitate il suo processo farà la prova; sì ch’a te fia bello averti fatta parte per te stesso.
english: Of their insensate acts, the proof will be in the effects; and thus, your honor will be best kept if your party is your self.

italian: Lo primo tuo refugio e ’l primo ostello sarà la cortesia del gran Lombardo che ’n su la scala porta il santo uccello;
english: Your first refuge and your first inn shall be the courtesy of the great Lombard, he who on the ladder bears the sacred bird;

italian: ch’in te avrà sì benigno riguardo, che del fare e del chieder, tra voi due, fia primo quel che tra li altri è più tardo.
english: and so benign will be his care for you that, with you two, in giving and in asking, that shall be first which is, with others, last.

italian: Con lui vedrai colui che ’mpresso fue, nascendo, sì da questa stella forte, che notabili fier l’opere sue.
english: You shall—beside him—see one who, at birth, had so received the seal of this strong star that what he does will be remarkable.

italian: Non se ne son le genti ancora accorte per la novella età, ché pur nove anni son queste rote intorno di lui torte;
english: People have yet to notice him because he is a boy—for nine years and no more have these spheres wheeled around him—but before

italian: ma pria che ’l Guasco l’alto Arrigo inganni, parran faville de la sua virtute in non curar d’argento né d’affanni.
english: the Gascon gulls the noble Henry, some sparks will have marked the virtue of the Lombard: hard labor and his disregard for silver.

italian: Le sue magnificenze conosciute saranno ancora, sì che ’ suoi nemici non ne potran tener le lingue mute.
english: His generosity is yet to be so notable that even enemies will never hope to treat it silently.

italian: A lui t’aspetta e a’ suoi benefici; per lui fia trasmutata molta gente, cambiando condizion ricchi e mendici;
english: Put trust in him and in his benefits: his gifts will bring much metamorphosis— rich men and beggars will exchange their states.

italian: e portera’ne scritto ne la mente di lui, e nol dirai»; e disse cose incredibili a quei che fier presente.
english: What I tell you about him you will bear inscribed within your mind—but hide it there”; and he told things beyond belief even

italian: Poi giunse: «Figlio, queste son le chiose di quel che ti fu detto; ecco le ’nsidie che dietro a pochi giri son nascose.
english: for those who will yet see them. Then he added: “Son, these are glosses of what you had heard; these are the snares that hide beneath brief years.

italian: Non vo’ però ch’a’ tuoi vicini invidie, poscia che s’infutura la tua vita vie più là che ’l punir di lor perfidie».
english: Yet I’d not have you envying your neighbors; your life will long outlast the punishment that is to fall upon their treacheries.”

italian: Poi che, tacendo, si mostrò spedita l’anima santa di metter la trama in quella tela ch’io le porsi ordita,
english: After that holy soul had, with his silence, showed he was freed from putting in the woof across the web whose warp I set for him,

italian: io cominciai, come colui che brama, dubitando, consiglio da persona che vede e vuol dirittamente e ama:
english: I like a man who, doubting, craves for counsel from one who sees and rightly wills and loves, replied to him: “I clearly see, my father,

italian: «Ben veggio, padre mio, sì come sprona lo tempo verso me, per colpo darmi tal, ch’è più grave a chi più s’abbandona;
english: how time is hurrying toward me in order to deal me such a blow as would be most grievous for him who is not set for it;

italian: per che di provedenza è buon ch’io m’armi, sì che, se loco m’è tolto più caro, io non perdessi li altri per miei carmi.
english: thus, it is right to arm myself with foresight, that if I lose the place most dear, I may not lose the rest through what my poems say.

italian: Giù per lo mondo sanza fine amaro, e per lo monte del cui bel cacume li occhi de la mia donna mi levaro,
english: Down in the world of endless bitterness, and on the mountain from whose lovely peak I was drawn upward by my lady’s eyes,

italian: e poscia per lo ciel, di lume in lume, ho io appreso quel che s’io ridico, a molti fia sapor di forte agrume;
english: and afterward, from light to light in Heaven, I learned that which, if I retell it, must for many have a taste too sharp, too harsh;

italian: e s’io al vero son timido amico, temo di perder viver tra coloro che questo tempo chiameranno antico».
english: yet if I am a timid friend of truth, I fear that I may lose my life among those who will call this present, ancient times.”

italian: La luce in che rideva il mio tesoro ch’io trovai lì, si fé prima corusca, quale a raggio di sole specchio d’oro;
english: The light in which there smiled the treasure I had found within it, first began to dazzle, as would a golden mirror in the sun,

italian: indi rispuose: «Coscïenza fusca o de la propria o de l’altrui vergogna pur sentirà la tua parola brusca.
english: then it replied: “A conscience that is dark— either through its or through another’s shame— indeed will find that what you speak is harsh.

italian: Ma nondimen, rimossa ogne menzogna, tutta tua visïon fa manifesta; e lascia pur grattar dov’ è la rogna.
english: Nevertheless, all falsehood set aside, let all that you have seen be manifest, and let them scratch wherever it may itch.

italian: Ché se la voce tua sarà molesta nel primo gusto, vital nodrimento lascerà poi, quando sarà digesta.
english: For if, at the first taste, your words molest, they will, when they have been digested, end as living nourishment. As does the wind,

italian: Questo tuo grido farà come vento, che le più alte cime più percuote; e ciò non fa d’onor poco argomento.
english: so shall your outcry do—the wind that sends its roughest blows against the highest peaks; that is no little cause for claiming honor.

italian: Però ti son mostrate in queste rote, nel monte e ne la valle dolorosa pur l’anime che son di fama note,
english: Therefore, within these spheres, upon the mountain, and in the dismal valley, you were shown only those souls that unto fame are known—

italian: che l’animo di quel ch’ode, non posa né ferma fede per essempro ch’aia la sua radice incognita e ascosa,
english: because the mind of one who hears will not put doubt to rest, put trust in you, if given examples with their roots unknown and hidden,

italian: né per altro argomento che non paia».
english: or arguments too dim, too unapparent.”

italian: Già si godeva solo del suo verbo quello specchio beato, e io gustava lo mio, temprando col dolce l’acerbo;
english: By now that blessed mirror was delighting in its own inner words; I, tasting mine, was tempering the bitter with the sweet.

italian: e quella donna ch’a Dio mi menava disse: «Muta pensier; pensa ch’i’ sono presso a colui ch’ogne torto disgrava».
english: But she, the lady leading me to God, said: “Shift your thoughts: remember—I am close to Him who lightens every unjust hurt.”

italian: Io mi rivolsi a l’amoroso suono del mio conforto; e qual io allor vidi ne li occhi santi amor, qui l’abbandono:
english: Hearing the loving sound my solace spoke, I turned. But here I have to leave untold what love I saw within her holy eyes,

italian: non perch’ io pur del mio parlar diffidi, ma per la mente che non può redire sovra sé tanto, s’altri non la guidi.
english: not just because I do not trust my speech, but, too, because recall cannot retrieve that much, unless Another is its guide.

italian: Tanto poss’ io di quel punto ridire, che, rimirando lei, lo mio affetto libero fu da ogne altro disire,
english: This only—of that moment—can I tell: that even as I gazed at her, my soul was free from any other need as long

italian: fin che ’l piacere etterno, che diretto raggiava in Bëatrice, dal bel viso mi contentava col secondo aspetto.
english: as the Eternal Loveliness that shone on Beatrice directly, from her eyes, contented me with the reflected light.

italian: Vincendo me col lume d’un sorriso, ella mi disse: «Volgiti e ascolta; ché non pur ne’ miei occhi è paradiso».
english: But, conquering my will with her smile’s splendor, she told me: “Turn to him and listen—for not only in my eyes is Paradise.”

italian: Come si vede qui alcuna volta l’affetto ne la vista, s’elli è tanto, che da lui sia tutta l’anima tolta,
english: As, here on earth, at times our sentiment, if it be passionate enough to take the soul entirely, shows in the face,

italian: così nel fiammeggiar del folgór santo, a ch’io mi volsi, conobbi la voglia in lui di ragionarmi ancora alquanto.
english: so, in the flaming of the holy fire to which I turned, I saw that he desired some further words with me. And he began:

italian: El cominciò: «In questa quinta soglia de l’albero che vive de la cima e frutta sempre e mai non perde foglia,
english: “In this fifth resting place, upon the tree that grows down from its crown and endlessly bears fruit and never loses any leaves,

italian: spiriti son beati, che giù, prima che venissero al ciel, fuor di gran voce, sì ch’ogne musa ne sarebbe opima.
english: are blessed souls that, down below, before they came to heaven, were so notable that any poem would be enriched by them.

italian: Però mira ne’ corni de la croce: quello ch’io nomerò, lì farà l’atto che fa in nube il suo foco veloce».
english: Therefore look at the cross, along its horns: those whom I name will race as swiftly as, within a cloud, its rapid lightnings flash.”

italian: Io vidi per la croce un lume tratto dal nomar Iosuè, com’ el si feo; né mi fu noto il dir prima che ’l fatto.
english: Then, just as soon as Joshua was named, I saw a splendor thrust along the cross, nor did I note the name before the act.

italian: E al nome de l’alto Macabeo vidi moversi un altro roteando, e letizia era ferza del paleo.
english: And at the name of noble Maccabeus, I saw another flame wheel round itself, and gladness was the whip that spurred that top.

italian: Così per Carlo Magno e per Orlando due ne seguì lo mio attento sguardo, com’ occhio segue suo falcon volando.
english: So, too, for Charlemagne and Roland—my attentive eye held fast to that pair like a falconer who tracks his falcon’s flight.

italian: Poscia trasse Guiglielmo e Rinoardo e ’l duca Gottifredi la mia vista per quella croce, e Ruberto Guiscardo.
english: The next to draw my eyes along that cross were William and Renouard and, too, Duke Godfrey and Robert Guiscard. Then, when he had left me

italian: Indi, tra l’altre luci mota e mista, mostrommi l’alma che m’avea parlato qual era tra i cantor del cielo artista.
english: and mingled with the other lights, the soul who had addressed me showed his artistry, singing among the singers in that sphere.

italian: Io mi rivolsi dal mio destro lato per vedere in Beatrice il mio dovere, o per parlare o per atto, segnato;
english: I turned to my right side to see if I might see if Beatrice had signified by word or gesture what I was to do

italian: e vidi le sue luci tanto mere, tanto gioconde, che la sua sembianza vinceva li altri e l’ultimo solere.
english: and saw such purity within her eyes, such joy, that her appearance now surpassed its guise at other times, even the last.

italian: E come, per sentir più dilettanza bene operando, l’uom di giorno in giorno s’accorge che la sua virtute avanza,
english: And as, by feeling greater joyousness in doing good, a man becomes aware that day by day his virtue is advancing,

italian: sì m’accors’ io che ’l mio girare intorno col cielo insieme avea cresciuto l’arco, veggendo quel miracol più addorno.
english: so I became aware that my revolving with heaven had increased its arc—by seeing that miracle becoming still more brilliant.

italian: E qual è ’l trasmutare in picciol varco di tempo in bianca donna, quando ’l volto suo si discarchi di vergogna il carco,
english: And like the rapid change that one can see in a pale woman’s face when it has freed itself from bearing bashful modesty,

italian: tal fu ne li occhi miei, quando fui vòlto, per lo candor de la temprata stella sesta, che dentro a sé m’avea ricolto.
english: such change I, turning, saw: the red of Mars was gone—and now the temperate sixth star’s white heaven welcomed me into itself.

italian: Io vidi in quella giovïal facella lo sfavillar de l’amor che lì era segnare a li occhi miei nostra favella.
english: I saw within that torch of Jupiter the sparkling of the love that it contained design before my eyes the signs we speak.

italian: E come augelli surti di rivera, quasi congratulando a lor pasture, fanno di sé or tonda or altra schiera,
english: And just as birds that rise from riverbanks, as if rejoicing after feeding there, will form a round flock or another shape,

italian: sì dentro ai lumi sante creature volitando cantavano, e faciensi or D , or I , or L in sue figure.
english: so, in their lights, the saintly beings sang and, in their flight, the figures that they spelled were now a D, now I, and now an L.

italian: Prima, cantando, a sua nota moviensi; poi, diventando l’un di questi segni, un poco s’arrestavano e taciensi.
english: First, they moved to the rhythm of their song; then, after they had finished forming one letter, they halted for a while, in silence.

italian: O diva Pegasëa che li ’ngegni fai glorïosi e rendili longevi, ed essi teco le cittadi e ’ regni,
english: O godly Pegasea, you who give to genius glory and long life, as it, through you, gives these to kingdoms and to cities,

italian: illustrami di te, sì ch’io rilevi le lor figure com’ io l’ho concette: paia tua possa in questi versi brevi!
english: give me your light that I may emphasize these signs as I inscribed them in my mind: your power—may it appear in these brief lines!

italian: Mostrarsi dunque in cinque volte sette vocali e consonanti; e io notai le parti sì, come mi parver dette.
english: Those blessed spirits took the shape of five times seven vowels and consonants, and I noted the parts as they were spelled for me.

italian: ‘DILIGITE IUSTITIAM’ , primai fur verbo e nome di tutto ’l dipinto; ‘QUI IUDICATIS TERRAM’ , fur sezzai.
english: DILIGITE IUSTITIAM were the verb and noun that first appeared in that depiction; QUI IUDICATIS TERRAM followed after.

italian: Poscia ne l’emme del vocabol quinto rimasero ordinate; sì che Giove pareva argento lì d’oro distinto.
english: Then, having formed the M of the fifth word, those spirits kept their order; Jupiter’s silver, at that point, seemed embossed with gold.

italian: E vidi scendere altre luci dove era il colmo de l’emme, e lì quetarsi cantando, credo, il ben ch’a sé le move.
english: And I saw other lights descending on the apex of the M and, settling, singing— I think—the Good that draws them to Itself.

italian: Poi, come nel percuoter d’i ciocchi arsi surgono innumerabili faville, onde li stolti sogliono agurarsi,
english: Then, as innumerable sparks rise up when one strikes burning logs (and in those sparks fools have a way of reading auguries),

italian: resurger parver quindi più di mille luci e salir, qual assai e qual poco, sì come ’l sol che l’accende sortille;
english: from that M seemed to surge more than a thousand lights; and they climbed, some high, some low, just as the Sun that kindles them assigned positions.

italian: e quïetata ciascuna in suo loco, la testa e ’l collo d’un’aguglia vidi rappresentare a quel distinto foco.
english: With each light settled quietly in place, I saw that the array of fire had shaped the image of an eagle’s head and neck.

italian: Quei che dipinge lì, non ha chi ’l guidi; ma esso guida, e da lui si rammenta quella virtù ch’è forma per li nidi.
english: He who paints there has no one as His guide: He guides Himself; in Him we recognize the shaping force that flows from nest to nest.

italian: L’altra bëatitudo, che contenta pareva prima d’ingigliarsi a l’emme, con poco moto seguitò la ’mprenta.
english: The other lights, who were, it seemed, content at first to form a lily on the M, moving a little, formed the eagle’s frame.

italian: O dolce stella, quali e quante gemme mi dimostraro che nostra giustizia effetto sia del ciel che tu ingemme!
english: O gentle star, what—and how many—gems made plain to me that justice here on earth depends upon the heaven you engem!

italian: Per ch’io prego la mente in che s’inizia tuo moto e tua virtute, che rimiri ond’ esce il fummo che ’l tuo raggio vizia;
english: Therefore I pray the Mind in which begin your motion and your force, to watch that place which has produced the smoke that dims your rays,

italian: sì ch’un’altra fïata omai s’adiri del comperare e vender dentro al templo che si murò di segni e di martìri.
english: that once again His anger fall upon those who would buy and sell within that temple whose walls were built by miracles and martyrs.

italian: O milizia del ciel cu’ io contemplo, adora per color che sono in terra tutti svïati dietro al malo essemplo!
english: O hosts of Heaven whom I contemplate, for all who, led by bad example, stray within the life they live on earth, do pray!

italian: Già si solea con le spade far guerra; ma or si fa togliendo or qui or quivi lo pan che ’l pïo Padre a nessun serra.
english: Men once were used to waging war with swords; now war means seizing here and there the bread the tender Father would deny to none.

italian: Ma tu che sol per cancellare scrivi, pensa che Pietro e Paulo, che moriro per la vigna che guasti, ancor son vivi.
english: But you who only write to then erase, remember this: Peter and Paul, who died to save the vines you spoil, are still alive.

italian: Ben puoi tu dire: «I’ ho fermo ’l disiro sì a colui che volle viver solo e che per salti fu tratto al martiro,
english: Well may you say:”My longing is so bent on him who chose the solitary life and for a dance was dragged to martyrdom—

italian: ch’io non conosco il pescator né Polo».
english: I do not know the Fisherman or Paul.”

italian: Parea dinanzi a me con l’ali aperte la bella image che nel dolce frui liete facevan l’anime conserte;
english: The handsome image those united souls, happy within their blessedness, were shaping, appeared before me now with open wings.

italian: parea ciascuna rubinetto in cui raggio di sole ardesse sì acceso, che ne’ miei occhi rifrangesse lui.
english: Each soul seemed like a ruby—one in which a ray of sun burned so, that in my eyes, it was the total sun that seemed reflected.

italian: E quel che mi convien ritrar testeso, non portò voce mai, né scrisse incostro, né fu per fantasia già mai compreso;
english: And what I now must tell has never been reported by a voice, inscribed by ink, never conceived by the imagination;

italian: ch’io vidi e anche udi’ parlar lo rostro, e sonar ne la voce e «io» e «mio», quand’ era nel concetto e ‘noi’ e ‘nostro’.
english: for I did see the beak, did hear it speak and utter with its voice both I and mine when we and ours were what, in thought, was meant.

italian: E cominciò: «Per esser giusto e pio son io qui essaltato a quella gloria che non si lascia vincere a disio;
english: And it began: “Because I was both just and merciful, I am exalted here to glory no desire can surpass;

italian: e in terra lasciai la mia memoria sì fatta, che le genti lì malvage commendan lei, ma non seguon la storia».
english: the memory I left on earth is such that even the malicious praise it there, although they do not follow its example.”

italian: Così un sol calor di molte brage si fa sentir, come di molti amori usciva solo un suon di quella image.
english: Thus one sole warmth is felt from many embers, even as from a multitude of loves one voice alone rose from the Eagle’s image.

italian: Ond’ io appresso: «O perpetüi fiori de l’etterna letizia, che pur uno parer mi fate tutti vostri odori,
english: To which I said: “O everlasting flowers of the eternal gladness, who make all your fragrances appear to me as one,

italian: solvetemi, spirando, il gran digiuno che lungamente m’ha tenuto in fame, non trovandoli in terra cibo alcuno.
english: do let your breath deliver me from that great fast which kept me hungering so long, not finding any food for it on earth.

italian: Ben so io che, se ’n cielo altro reame la divina giustizia fa suo specchio, che ’l vostro non l’apprende con velame.
english: I know indeed that, though God’s Justice has another realm in Heaven as Its mirror, you here do not perceive it through a veil.

italian: Sapete come attento io m’apparecchio ad ascoltar; sapete qual è quello dubbio che m’è digiun cotanto vecchio».
english: You know how keenly I prepare myself to listen, and you know what is that doubt which caused so old a hungering in me.”

italian: Quasi falcone ch’esce del cappello, move la testa e con l’ali si plaude, voglia mostrando e faccendosi bello,
english: Just like a falcon set free from its hood, which moves its head and flaps its wings, displaying its eagerness and proud appearance, so

italian: vid’ io farsi quel segno, che di laude de la divina grazia era contesto, con canti quai si sa chi là sù gaude.
english: I saw that ensign do, that Eagle woven of praises of God’s grace, accompanied by songs whose sense those up above enjoy.

italian: Poi cominciò: «Colui che volse il sesto a lo stremo del mondo, e dentro ad esso distinse tanto occulto e manifesto,
english: Then it began: “The One who turned His compass to mark the world’s confines, and in them set so many things concealed and things revealed,

italian: non poté suo valor sì fare impresso in tutto l’universo, che ’l suo verbo non rimanesse in infinito eccesso.
english: could not imprint His Power into all the universe without His Word remaining in infinite excess of such a vessel.

italian: E ciò fa certo che ’l primo superbo, che fu la somma d’ogne creatura, per non aspettar lume, cadde acerbo;
english: In proof of this, the first proud being, he who was the highest of all creatures, fell— unripe because he did not wait for light.

italian: e quinci appar ch’ogne minor natura è corto recettacolo a quel bene che non ha fine e sé con sé misura.
english: Thus it is clear that every lesser nature is—all the more—too meager a container for endless Good, which is Its own sole measure.

italian: Dunque vostra veduta, che convene esser alcun de’ raggi de la mente di che tutte le cose son ripiene,
english: In consequence of this, your vision—which must be a ray of that Intelligence with which all beings are infused—cannot

italian: non pò da sua natura esser possente tanto, che suo principio discerna molto di là da quel che l’è parvente.
english: of its own nature find sufficient force to see into its origin beyond what God himself makes manifest to man;

italian: Però ne la giustizia sempiterna la vista che riceve il vostro mondo, com’ occhio per lo mare, entro s’interna;
english: therefore, the vision that your world receives can penetrate into Eternal Justice no more than eye can penetrate the sea;

italian: che, ben che da la proda veggia il fondo, in pelago nol vede; e nondimeno èli, ma cela lui l’esser profondo.
english: for though, near shore, sight reaches the sea floor, you cannot reach it in the open sea; yet it is there, but hidden by the deep.

italian: Lume non è, se non vien dal sereno che non si turba mai; anzi è tenèbra od ombra de la carne o suo veleno.
english: Only the light that shines from the clear heaven can never be obscured—all else is darkness or shadow of the flesh or fleshly poison.

italian: Assai t’è mo aperta la latebra che t’ascondeva la giustizia viva, di che facei question cotanto crebra;
english: Now is the hiding place of living Justice laid open to you—where it had been hidden while you addressed it with insistent questions.

italian: ché tu dicevi: “Un uom nasce a la riva de l’Indo, e quivi non è chi ragioni di Cristo né chi legga né chi scriva;
english: For you would say: ‘A man is born along the shoreline of the Indus River; none is there to speak or teach or write of Christ.

italian: e tutti suoi voleri e atti buoni sono, quanto ragione umana vede, sanza peccato in vita o in sermoni.
english: And he, as far as human reason sees, in all he seeks and all he does is good: there is no sin within his life or speech.

italian: Muore non battezzato e sanza fede: ov’ è questa giustizia che ’l condanna? ov’ è la colpa sua, se ei non crede?”.
english: And that man dies unbaptized, without faith. Where is this justice then that would condemn him? Where is his sin if he does not believe?’

italian: Or tu chi se’, che vuo’ sedere a scranna, per giudicar di lungi mille miglia con la veduta corta d’una spanna?
english: Now who are you to sit upon the bench, to judge events a thousand miles away, when your own vision spans so brief a space?

italian: Certo a colui che meco s’assottiglia, se la Scrittura sovra voi non fosse, da dubitar sarebbe a maraviglia.
english: Of course, for him who would be subtle with me, were there no Scriptures to instruct you, then there would be place for an array of questions.

italian: Oh terreni animali! oh menti grosse! La prima volontà, ch’è da sé buona, da sé, ch’è sommo ben, mai non si mosse.
english: O earthly animals, o minds obtuse! The Primal Will, which of Itself is good, from the Supreme Good—Its Self—never moved.

italian: Cotanto è giusto quanto a lei consuona: nullo creato bene a sé la tira, ma essa, radïando, lui cagiona».
english: So much is just as does accord with It; and so, created good can draw It to itself—but It, rayed forth, causes such goods.”

italian: Quale sovresso il nido si rigira poi c’ha pasciuti la cicogna i figli, e come quel ch’è pasto la rimira;
english: Just as, above the nest, the stork will circle when she has fed her fledglings, and as he whom she has fed looks up at her, so did

italian: cotal si fece, e sì leväi i cigli, la benedetta imagine, che l’ali movea sospinte da tanti consigli.
english: the blessed image do, and so did I, the fledgling, while the Eagle moved its wings, spurred on by many wills in unison.

italian: Roteando cantava, e dicea: «Quali son le mie note a te, che non le ’ntendi, tal è il giudicio etterno a voi mortali».
english: Wheeling, the Eagle sang, then said: “Even as are my songs to you—past understanding— such is Eternal Judgment to you mortals.”

italian: Poi si quetaro quei lucenti incendi de lo Spirito Santo ancor nel segno che fé i Romani al mondo reverendi,
english: After the Holy Ghost’s bright flames fell silent while still within the sign that made the Romans revered throughout the world, again the Eagle

italian: esso ricominciò: «A questo regno non salì mai chi non credette ’n Cristo, né pria né poi ch’el si chiavasse al legno.
english: began: “No one without belief in Christ has ever risen to this kingdom—either before or after He was crucified.

italian: Ma vedi: molti gridan “Cristo, Cristo!”, che saranno in giudicio assai men prope a lui, che tal che non conosce Cristo;
english: But there are many who now cry ‘Christ! Christ!’ who at the Final Judgment shall be far less close to Him than one who knows not Christ;

italian: e tai Cristian dannerà l’Etïòpe, quando si partiranno i due collegi, l’uno in etterno ricco e l’altro inòpe.
english: the Ethiopian will shame such Christians when the two companies are separated, the one forever rich, the other poor.

italian: Che poran dir li Perse a’ vostri regi, come vedranno quel volume aperto nel qual si scrivon tutti suoi dispregi?
english: What shall the Persians, when they come to see that open volume in which they shall read the misdeeds of your rulers, say to them?

italian: Lì si vedrà, tra l’opere d’Alberto, quella che tosto moverà la penna, per che ’l regno di Praga fia diserto.
english: There one shall see, among the deeds of Albert, that which is soon to set the pen in motion, his making of a desert of Prague’s kingdom.

italian: Lì si vedrà il duol che sovra Senna induce, falseggiando la moneta, quel che morrà di colpo di cotenna.
english: There one shall see the grief inflicted on the Seine by him who falsifies his coins, one who shall die beneath a wild boar’s blow.

italian: Lì si vedrà la superbia ch’asseta, che fa lo Scotto e l’Inghilese folle, sì che non può soffrir dentro a sua meta.
english: There one shall see the thirst of arrogance that drives the Scot and Englishman insane— unable to remain within their borders.

italian: Vedrassi la lussuria e ’l viver molle di quel di Spagna e di quel di Boemme, che mai valor non conobbe né volle.
english: That book will show the life of Lechery and ease the Spaniard led—and the Bohemian, who never knew and never wished for valor.

italian: Vedrassi al Ciotto di Ierusalemme segnata con un i la sua bontate, quando ’l contrario segnerà un emme.
english: That book will show the Cripple of Jerusalem— his good deeds labeled with an I alone, whereas his evils will be under M.

italian: Vedrassi l’avarizia e la viltate di quei che guarda l’isola del foco, ove Anchise finì la lunga etate;
english: That book will show the greed and cowardice of him who oversees the Isle of Fire, on which Anchises ended his long life;

italian: e a dare ad intender quanto è poco, la sua scrittura fian lettere mozze, che noteranno molto in parvo loco.
english: and to make plain his paltriness, the letters that register his deeds will be contracted, to note much pettiness in little space.

italian: E parranno a ciascun l’opere sozze del barba e del fratel, che tanto egregia nazione e due corone han fatte bozze.
english: And all shall see the filthiness of both his uncle and his brother, who dishonored a family so famous—and two crowns.

italian: E quel di Portogallo e di Norvegia lì si conosceranno, e quel di Rascia che male ha visto il conio di Vinegia.
english: And he of Portugal and he of Norway shall be known in that book, and he of Rascia, who saw—unluckily—the coin of Venice.

italian: Oh beata Ungheria, se non si lascia più malmenare! e beata Navarra, se s’armasse del monte che la fascia!
english: O happy Hungary, if she would let herself be wronged no more! Happy Navarre, if mountains that surround her served as armor!

italian: E creder de’ ciascun che già, per arra di questo, Niccosïa e Famagosta per la lor bestia si lamenti e garra,
english: And if Navarre needs token of her future, now Nicosia and Famagosta offer— as men must see—lament and anger over

italian: che dal fianco de l’altre non si scosta».
english: their own beast, with his place beside the others.”

italian: Quando colui che tutto ’l mondo alluma de l’emisperio nostro sì discende, che ’l giorno d’ogne parte si consuma,
english: When he who graces all the world with light has sunk so far below our hemisphere that on all sides the day is spent, the sky,

italian: lo ciel, che sol di lui prima s’accende, subitamente si rifà parvente per molte luci, in che una risplende;
english: which had been lit before by him alone, immediately shows itself again with many lights reflecting one same source,

italian: e questo atto del ciel mi venne a mente, come ’l segno del mondo e de’ suoi duci nel benedetto rostro fu tacente;
english: and I remembered this celestial course when, in the blessed beak, the emblem of the world and of its guardians fell silent;

italian: però che tutte quelle vive luci, vie più lucendo, cominciaron canti da mia memoria labili e caduci.
english: for then all of those living lights grew more resplendent, but the songs that they began were labile—they escape my memory.

italian: O dolce amor che di riso t’ammanti, quanto parevi ardente in que’ flailli, ch’avieno spirto sol di pensier santi!
english: O gentle love that wears a smile as mantle, how ardent was your image in those torches filled only with the breath of holy thoughts!

italian: Poscia che i cari e lucidi lapilli ond’ io vidi ingemmato il sesto lume puoser silenzio a li angelici squilli,
english: After the precious, gleaming jewels with which the sixth of Heaven’s heavens was engemmed had ended their angelic song in silence,

italian: udir mi parve un mormorar di fiume che scende chiaro giù di pietra in pietra, mostrando l’ubertà del suo cacume.
english: I seemed to hear the murmur of a torrent that, limpid, falls from rock to rock, whose flow shows the abundance of its mountain source.

italian: E come suono al collo de la cetra prende sua forma, e sì com’ al pertugio de la sampogna vento che penètra,
english: Even as sound takes shape at the lute’s neck, and even as the wind that penetrates the blow-hole of the bagpipe, so—with no

italian: così, rimosso d’aspettare indugio, quel mormorar de l’aguglia salissi su per lo collo, come fosse bugio.
english: delay—that murmur of the Eagle rose straight up, directly through its neck as if its neck were hollow; and that murmuring

italian: Fecesi voce quivi, e quindi uscissi per lo suo becco in forma di parole, quali aspettava il core ov’ io le scrissi.
english: became a voice that issued from its beak, taking the shape of words desired by my heart—and that is where they were transcribed.

italian: «La parte in me che vede e pate il sole ne l’aguglie mortali», incominciommi, «or fisamente riguardar si vole,
english: “Now you must watch—and steadily—that part of me that can, in mortal eagles, see and suffer the sun’s force,” it then began

italian: perché d’i fuochi ond’ io figura fommi, quelli onde l’occhio in testa mi scintilla, e’ di tutti lor gradi son li sommi.
english: to say to me, “because, of all the flames from which I shape my form, those six with which the eye in my head glows hold highest rank.

italian: Colui che luce in mezzo per pupilla, fu il cantor de lo Spirito Santo, che l’arca traslatò di villa in villa:
english: He who gleams in the center, my eye’s pupil— he was the singer of the Holy Spirit, who bore the ark from one town to another;

italian: ora conosce il merto del suo canto, in quanto effetto fu del suo consiglio, per lo remunerar ch’è altrettanto.
english: now he has learned the merit will can earn— his song had not been spurred by grace alone, but his own will, in part, had urged him on.

italian: Dei cinque che mi fan cerchio per ciglio, colui che più al becco mi s’accosta, la vedovella consolò del figlio:
english: Of those five flames that, arching, form my brow, he who is nearest to my beak is one who comforted the widow for her son;

italian: ora conosce quanto caro costa non seguir Cristo, per l’esperïenza di questa dolce vita e de l’opposta.
english: now he has learned the price one pays for not following Christ, through his experience of this sweet life and of its opposite.

italian: E quel che segue in la circunferenza di che ragiono, per l’arco superno, morte indugiò per vera penitenza:
english: And he whose place is next on the circumference of which I speak, along the upward arc, delayed his death through truthful penitence;

italian: ora conosce che ’l giudicio etterno non si trasmuta, quando degno preco fa crastino là giù de l’odïerno.
english: now he has learned that the eternal judgment remains unchanged, though worthy prayer below makes what falls due today take place tomorrow.

italian: L’altro che segue, con le leggi e meco, sotto buona intenzion che fé mal frutto, per cedere al pastor si fece greco:
english: The next who follows—one whose good intention bore evil fruit—to give place to the Shepherd, with both the laws and me, made himself Greek;

italian: ora conosce come il mal dedutto dal suo bene operar non li è nocivo, avvegna che sia ’l mondo indi distrutto.
english: now he has learned that, even though the world be ruined by the evil that derives from his good act, that evil does not harm him.

italian: E quel che vedi ne l’arco declivo, Guiglielmo fu, cui quella terra plora che piagne Carlo e Federigo vivo:
english: He whom you see—along the downward arc— was William, and the land that mourns his death, for living Charles and Frederick, now laments;

italian: ora conosce come s’innamora lo ciel del giusto rege, e al sembiante del suo fulgore il fa vedere ancora.
