italian: La carne d’i mortali è tanto blanda, che giù non basta buon cominciamento dal nascer de la quercia al far la ghianda.
english: The flesh of mortals yields so easily— on earth a good beginning does not run from when the oak is born until the acorn.

italian: Pier cominciò sanz’ oro e sanz’ argento, e io con orazione e con digiuno, e Francesco umilmente il suo convento;
english: Peter began with neither gold nor silver, and I with prayer and fasting, and when Francis began his fellowship, he did it humbly;

italian: e se guardi ’l principio di ciascuno, poscia riguardi là dov’ è trascorso, tu vederai del bianco fatto bruno.
english: if you observe the starting point of each, and look again to see where it has strayed, then you will see how white has gone to gray.

italian: Veramente Iordan vòlto retrorso più fu, e ’l mar fuggir, quando Dio volse, mirabile a veder che qui ’l soccorso».
english: And yet, the Jordan in retreat, the sea in flight when God had willed it so, were sights more wonderful than His help here will be.”

italian: Così mi disse, e indi si raccolse al suo collegio, e ’l collegio si strinse; poi, come turbo, in sù tutto s’avvolse.
english: So did he speak to me, and he drew back to join his company, which closed, compact; then, like a whirlwind, upward, all were swept.

italian: La dolce donna dietro a lor mi pinse con un sol cenno su per quella scala, sì sua virtù la mia natura vinse;
english: The gentle lady—simply with a sign— impelled me after them and up that ladder, so did her power overcome my nature;

italian: né mai qua giù dove si monta e cala naturalmente, fu sì ratto moto ch’agguagliar si potesse a la mia ala.
english: and never here below, where our ascent and descent follow nature’s law, was there motion as swift as mine when I took wing.

italian: S’io torni mai, lettore, a quel divoto trïunfo per lo quale io piango spesso le mie peccata e ’l petto mi percuoto,
english: So, reader, may I once again return to those triumphant ranks—an end for which I often beat my breast, weep for my sins—

italian: tu non avresti in tanto tratto e messo nel foco il dito, in quant’ io vidi ’l segno che segue il Tauro e fui dentro da esso.
english: more quickly than your finger can withdraw from flame and be thrust into it, I saw, and was within, the sign that follows Taurus.

italian: O glorïose stelle, o lume pregno di gran virtù, dal quale io riconosco tutto, qual che si sia, il mio ingegno,
english: O stars of glory, constellation steeped in mighty force, all of my genius— whatever be its worth—has you as source:

italian: con voi nasceva e s’ascondeva vosco quelli ch’è padre d’ogne mortal vita, quand’ io senti’ di prima l’aere tosco;
english: with you was born and under you was hidden he who is father of all mortal lives, when I first felt the air of Tuscany;

italian: e poi, quando mi fu grazia largita d’entrar ne l’alta rota che vi gira, la vostra regïon mi fu sortita.
english: and then, when grace was granted me to enter the high wheel that impels your revolutions, your region was my fated point of entry.

italian: A voi divotamente ora sospira l’anima mia, per acquistar virtute al passo forte che a sé la tira.
english: To you my soul now sighs devotedly, that it may gain the force for this attempt, hard trial that now demands its every strength.

italian: «Tu se’ sì presso a l’ultima salute», cominciò Bëatrice, «che tu dei aver le luci tue chiare e acute;

english: you enter farther, do look downward, see what I have set beneath your feet already: much of the world is there. If you see that,

english: your heart may then present itself with all the joy it can to the triumphant throng that comes in gladness through this ether’s rounds.”

italian: Col viso ritornai per tutte quante le sette spere, e vidi questo globo tal, ch’io sorrisi del suo vil sembiante;
english: My eyes returned through all the seven spheres and saw this globe in such a way that I smiled at its scrawny image: I approve

italian: e quel consiglio per migliore approbo che l’ha per meno; e chi ad altro pensa chiamar si puote veramente probo.
english: that judgment as the best, which holds this earth to be the least; and he whose thoughts are set elsewhere, can truly be called virtuous.

italian: Vidi la figlia di Latona incensa sanza quell’ ombra che mi fu cagione per che già la credetti rara e densa.
english: I saw Latona’s daughter radiant, without the shadow that had made me once believe that she contained both rare and dense.

italian: L’aspetto del tuo nato, Iperïone, quivi sostenni, e vidi com’ si move circa e vicino a lui Maia e Dïone.
english: And there, Hyperion, I could sustain the vision of your son, and saw Dione and Maia as they circled nearby him.

italian: Quindi m’apparve il temperar di Giove tra ’l padre e ’l figlio; e quindi mi fu chiaro il varïar che fanno di lor dove;
english: The temperate Jupiter appeared to me between his father and his son; and I saw clearly how they vary their positions.

italian: e tutti e sette mi si dimostraro quanto son grandi e quanto son veloci e come sono in distante riparo.

italian: L’aiuola che ci fa tanto feroci, volgendom’ io con li etterni Gemelli, tutta m’apparve da’ colli a le foci;
english: that so incites our savagery was all— from hills to river mouths—revealed to me while I wheeled with eternal Gemini.

italian: poscia rivolsi li occhi a li occhi belli.
english: My eyes then turned again to the fair eyes.

italian: Come l’augello, intra l’amate fronde, posato al nido de’ suoi dolci nati la notte che le cose ci nasconde,

italian: che, per veder li aspetti disïati e per trovar lo cibo onde li pasca, in che gravi labor li sono aggrati,
english: and, on an open branch, anticipates the time when she can see their longed-for faces and find the food with which to feed them—chore

italian: previene il tempo in su aperta frasca, e con ardente affetto il sole aspetta, fiso guardando pur che l’alba nasca;
english: that pleases her, however hard her labors— as she awaits the sun with warm affection, steadfastly watching for the dawn to break:

italian: così la donna mïa stava eretta e attenta, rivolta inver’ la plaga sotto la quale il sol mostra men fretta:

english: as I saw her in longing and suspense, I grew to be as one who, while he wants what is not his, is satisfied with hope.

italian: Ma poco fu tra uno e altro quando, del mio attender, dico, e del vedere lo ciel venir più e più rischiarando;
english: But time between one and the other when was brief—I mean the whens of waiting and of seeing heaven grow more radiant.

italian: e Bëatrice disse: «Ecco le schiere del trïunfo di Cristo e tutto ’l frutto ricolto del girar di queste spere!».
english: And Beatrice said: “There you see the troops of the triumphant Christ—and all the fruits ingathered from the turning of these spheres!”

italian: Pariemi che ’l suo viso ardesse tutto, e li occhi avea di letizia sì pieni, che passarmen convien sanza costrutto.
english: It seemed to me her face was all aflame, and there was so much gladness in her eyes— I am compelled to leave it undescribed.

italian: Quale ne’ plenilunïi sereni Trivïa ride tra le ninfe etterne che dipingon lo ciel per tutti i seni,

english: and through its living light the glowing Substance appeared to me with such intensity— my vision lacked the power to sustain it.

english: This is the Wisdom and the Potency that opened roads between the earth and Heaven, the paths for which desire had long since waited.”

english: when I heard what she offered me, deserving of so much gratitude that it can never be canceled from the book that tells the past.

italian: e così, figurando il paradiso, convien saltar lo sacrato poema, come chi trova suo cammin riciso.
english: And thus, in representing Paradise, the sacred poem has to leap across, as does a man who finds his path cut off.

italian: Ma chi pensasse il ponderoso tema e l’omero mortal che se ne carca, nol biasmerebbe se sott’ esso trema:
english: But he who thinks upon the weighty theme, and on the mortal shoulder bearing it, will lay no blame if, burdened so, I tremble:

italian: non è pareggio da picciola barca quel che fendendo va l’ardita prora, né da nocchier ch’a sé medesmo parca.
english: this is no crossing for a little bark— the sea that my audacious prow now cleaves— nor for a helmsman who would spare himself.

italian: «Perché la faccia mia sì t’innamora, che tu non ti rivolgi al bel giardino che sotto i raggi di Cristo s’infiora?
english: “Why are you so enraptured by my face as to deny your eyes the sight of that fair garden blossoming beneath Christ’s rays?

italian: Quivi è la rosa in che ’l verbo divino carne si fece; quivi son li gigli al cui odor si prese il buon cammino».
english: The Rose in which the Word of God became flesh grows within that garden; there the lilies whose fragrance let men find the righteous way.”

italian: Così Beatrice; e io, che a’ suoi consigli tutto era pronto, ancora mi rendei a la battaglia de’ debili cigli.
english: Thus Beatrice, and I—completely ready to do what she might counsel—once again took up the battle of my feeble brows.

english: Under a ray of sun that, limpid, streams down from a broken cloud, my eyes have seen, while shade was shielding them, a flowered meadow;

english: so I saw many troops of splendors here lit from above by burning rays of light, but where those rays began was not in sight.

italian: O benigna vertù che sì li ’mprenti, sù t’essaltasti, per largirmi loco a li occhi lì che non t’eran possenti.
english: O kindly Power that imprints them thus, you rose on high to leave space for my eyes— for where I was, they were too weak to see You!

italian: Il nome del bel fior ch’io sempre invoco e mane e sera, tutto mi ristrinse l’animo ad avvisar lo maggior foco;
english: The name of that fair flower which I always invoke, at morning and at evening, drew my mind completely to the greatest flame.

italian: e come ambo le luci mi dipinse il quale e il quanto de la viva stella che là sù vince come qua giù vinse,
english: And when, on both my eye-lights, were depicted the force and nature of the living star that conquers heaven as it conquered earth,

italian: per entro il cielo scese una facella, formata in cerchio a guisa di corona, e cinsela e girossi intorno ad ella.
english: descending through that sky there came a torch, forming a ring that seemed as if a crown: wheeling around her—a revolving garland.

italian: Qualunque melodia più dolce suona qua giù e più a sé l’anima tira, parrebbe nube che squarciata tona,

italian: comparata al sonar di quella lira onde si coronava il bel zaffiro del quale il ciel più chiaro s’inzaffira.
english: if likened to the music of that lyre which sounded from the crown of that fair sapphire, the brightest light that has ensapphired heaven.

italian: «Io sono amore angelico, che giro l’alta letizia che spira del ventre che fu albergo del nostro disiro;
english: “I am angelic love who wheel around that high gladness inspired by the womb that was the dwelling place of our Desire;

italian: e girerommi, donna del ciel, mentre che seguirai tuo figlio, e farai dia più la spera suprema perché lì entre».
english: so shall I circle, Lady of Heaven, until you, following your Son, have made that sphere supreme, still more divine by entering it.”

italian: Così la circulata melodia si sigillava, e tutti li altri lumi facean sonare il nome di Maria.
english: So did the circulating melody, sealing itself, conclude; and all the other lights then resounded with the name of Mary.

italian: Lo real manto di tutti i volumi del mondo, che più ferve e più s’avviva ne l’alito di Dio e nei costumi,
english: The royal cloak of all the wheeling spheres within the universe, the heaven most intense, alive, most burning in the breath

english: from that point where I was; and thus my eyes possessed no power to follow that crowned flame, which mounted upward, following her Son.

italian: ciascun di quei candori in sù si stese con la sua cima, sì che l’alto affetto ch’elli avieno a Maria mi fu palese.
english: each of those blessed splendors stretched its peak upward, so that the deep affection each possessed for Mary was made plain to me.

english: Then they remained within my sight, singing “Regina coeli” with such tenderness that my delight in that has never left me.

italian: Oh quanta è l’ubertà che si soffolce in quelle arche ricchissime che fuoro a seminar qua giù buone bobolce!
english: Oh, in those richest coffers, what abundance is garnered up for those who, while below, on earth, were faithful workers when they sowed!

italian: Quivi si vive e gode del tesoro che s’acquistò piangendo ne lo essilio di Babillòn, ove si lasciò l’oro.
english: Here do they live, delighting in the treasure they earned with tears in Babylonian exile, where they had no concern for gold.

italian: Quivi trïunfa, sotto l’alto Filio di Dio e di Maria, di sua vittoria, e con l’antico e col novo concilio,

english: he who is keeper of the keys of glory.

english: direct your mind to his immense desire, quench him somewhat: you who forever drink from that Source which his thought and longing seek.”

english: “O you who pray to us with such devotion— my holy sister—with your warm affection, you have released me from that lovely sphere.”

english: So, after he had stopped his motion, did the blessed flame breathe forth unto my lady; and what he said I have reported here.

english: But since this realm has gained its citizens through the true faith, it rightly falls to him to speak of faith, that he may glorify it.”

english: Just as the bachelor candidate must arm himself and does not speak until the master submits the question for discussion—not

english: deducing what we can from syllogisms, without our being able to see more: thus faith is also called an evidence.”

english: with such persuasiveness that faith has truth— when set beside that argument, all other demonstrations seem to me obtuse.”

english: the sixth, when the sun shifts to a new quadrant.

english: commanded silence, I then heard: “If I change color, do not be amazed, for as I speak, you will see change in all these flames.

english: He who on earth usurps my place, my place, my place that in the sight of God’s own Son is vacant now, has made my burial ground

english: a sewer of blood, a sewer of stench, so that the perverse one who fell from Heaven, here above, can find contentment there below.”

english: “The Bride of Christ was never nurtured by my blood, and blood of Linus and of Cletus, to be employed in gaining greater riches;

english: but to acquire this life of joyousness, Sixtus and Pius, Urban and Calixtus, after much lamentation, shed their blood.

english: nor did we want my form upon a seal for trafficking in lying privileges— for which I often blush and flash with anger.

english: From here on high one sees rapacious wolves clothed in the cloaks of shepherds. You, the vengeance of God, oh, why do you still lie concealed?

english: The Gascons and the Cahorsines—they both prepare to drink our blood: o good beginning, to what a miserable end you fall!

italian: Ma l’alta provedenza, che con Scipio difese a Roma la gloria del mondo, soccorrà tosto, sì com’ io concipio;
english: But that high Providence which once preserved, with Scipio, the glory of the world for Rome, will soon bring help, as I conceive;

italian: e tu, figliuol, che per lo mortal pondo ancor giù tornerai, apri la bocca, e non asconder quel ch’io non ascondo».
english: and you, my son, who through your mortal weight will yet return below, speak plainly there, and do not hide that which I do not hide.”

italian: Sì come di vapor gelati fiocca in giuso l’aere nostro, quando ’l corno de la capra del ciel col sol si tocca,
english: As, when the horn of heaven’s Goat abuts the sun, our sky flakes frozen vapors downward, so did I see that ether there adorned;

english: for from that sphere, triumphant vapors now were flaking up to the Empyrean— returning after dwelling here with us.

italian: Lo viso mio seguiva i suoi sembianti, e seguì fin che ’l mezzo, per lo molto, li tolse il trapassar del più avanti.
english: My sight was following their semblances— until the space between us grew so great as to deny my eyes all farther reach.

italian: Onde la donna, che mi vide assolto de l’attendere in sù, mi disse: «Adima il viso e guarda come tu se’ vòlto».
english: At this, my lady, seeing me set free from gazing upward, told me: “Let your eyes look down and see how far you have revolved.”

english: I should have seen more of this threshing floor but for the motion of the sun beneath my feet: it was a sign and more away.

italian: La mente innamorata, che donnea con la mia donna sempre, di ridure ad essa li occhi più che mai ardea;
english: My mind, enraptured, always longing for my lady gallantly, was burning more than ever for my eyes’ return to her;

italian: e se natura o arte fé pasture da pigliare occhi, per aver la mente, in carne umana o ne le sue pitture,
english: and if—by means of human,flesh or portraits— nature or art has fashioned lures to draw the eye so as to grip the mind, all these

english: would seem nothing if set beside the godly beauty that shone upon me when I turned to see the smiling face of Beatrice.

italian: E la virtù che lo sguardo m’indulse, del bel nido di Leda mi divelse, e nel ciel velocissimo m’impulse.

italian: Ma ella, che vedëa ’l mio disire, incominciò, ridendo tanto lieta, che Dio parea nel suo volto gioire:
english: But she, who saw what my desire was— her smile had so much gladness that within her face there seemed to be God’s joy—began:

italian: «La natura del mondo, che quïeta il mezzo e tutto l’altro intorno move, quinci comincia come da sua meta;
english: “The nature of the universe, which holds the center still and moves all else around it, begins here as if from its turning-post.

italian: e questo cielo non ha altro dove che la mente divina, in che s’accende l’amor che ’l volge e la virtù ch’ei piove.
english: This heaven has no other where than this: the mind of God, in which are kindled both the love that turns it and the force it rains.

italian: Luce e amor d’un cerchio lui comprende, sì come questo li altri; e quel precinto colui che ’l cinge solamente intende.
english: As in a circle, light and love enclose it, as it surrounds the rest—and that enclosing, only He who encloses understands.

italian: Non è suo moto per altro distinto, ma li altri son mensurati da questo, sì come diece da mezzo e da quinto;
english: No other heaven measures this sphere’s motion, but it serves as the measure for the rest, even as half and fifth determine ten;

italian: e come il tempo tegna in cotal testo le sue radici e ne li altri le fronde, omai a te può esser manifesto.
english: and now it can be evident to you how time has roots within this vessel and, within the other vessels, has its leaves.

italian: Ben fiorisce ne li uomini il volere; ma la pioggia continüa converte in bozzacchioni le sosine vere.

italian: Tale, balbuzïendo ancor, digiuna, che poi divora, con la lingua sciolta, qualunque cibo per qualunque luna;

english: and one, while he still lisps, will love and heed his mother, but when he acquires speech more fully, he will long to see her buried.

english: Just so, white skin turns black when it is struck by direct light—the lovely daughter of the one who brings us dawn and leaves us evening.

italian: Tu, perché non ti facci maraviglia, pensa che ’n terra non è chi governi; onde sì svïa l’umana famiglia.

english: and then fine fruit shall follow on the flower.”

english: sparks that were more in number than the sum one reaches doubling in succession each square of a chessboard, one to sixty-four.

english: And she who saw my mind’s perplexities said: “The first circles have displayed to you the Seraphim and Cherubim. They follow

english: the ties of love with such rapidity because they are as like the Point as creatures can be, a power dependent on their vision.

english: the measure of their vision lies in merit, produced by grace and then by will to goodness: and this is the progression, step by step.

italian: L’altro ternaro, che così germoglia in questa primavera sempiterna che notturno Arïete non dispoglia,
english: The second triad—blossoming in this eternal springtime that the nightly Ram does not despoil—perpetually sings

english: ‘Hosanna’ with three melodies that sound in the three ranks of bliss that form this triad; within this hierarchy there are three

english: groups of rejoicing ones within the next triad are wheeling Principalities and the Archangels; last, the playful Angels.

english: These orders all direct—ecstatically— their eyes on high; and downward, they exert such force that all are drawn and draw to God.

english: And Dionysius, with much longing, set himself to contemplate these orders: he named and distinguished them just as I do.

english: When they climbed down into that flowering Rose, from rank to rank, they shared that peace and ardor which they had gained, with wings that fanned their sides.

italian: Né l’interporsi tra ’l disopra e ’l fiore di tanta moltitudine volante impediva la vista e lo splendore:
english: Nor did so vast a throng in flight, although it interposed between the candid Rose and light above, obstruct the sight or splendor,

italian: ché la luce divina è penetrante per l’universo secondo ch’è degno, sì che nulla le puote essere ostante.
english: because the light of God so penetrates the universe according to the worth of every part, that no thing can impede it.

italian: Questo sicuro e gaudïoso regno, frequente in gente antica e in novella, viso e amore avea tutto ad un segno.
english: This confident and joyous kingdom, thronged with people of both new and ancient times, turned all its sight and ardor to one mark.

italian: O trina luce che ’n unica stella scintillando a lor vista, sì li appaga! guarda qua giuso a la nostra procella!
english: O threefold Light that, in a single star sparkling into their eyes, contents them so, look down and see our tempest here below!

italian: Se i barbari, venendo da tal plaga che ciascun giorno d’Elice si cuopra, rotante col suo figlio ond’ ella è vaga,
english: If the Barbarians, when they came from a region that is covered every day by Helice, who wheels with her loved son,

italian: veggendo Roma e l’ardüa sua opra, stupefaciensi, quando Laterano a le cose mortali andò di sopra;
english: were, seeing Rome and her vast works, struck dumb (when, of all mortal things, the Lateran was the most eminent), then what amazement

italian: ïo, che al divino da l’umano, a l’etterno dal tempo era venuto, e di Fiorenza in popol giusto e sano,
english: must have filled me when I to the divine came from the human, to eternity from time, and to a people just and sane

italian: di che stupor dovea esser compiuto! Certo tra esso e ’l gaudio mi facea libito non udire e starmi muto.
english: from Florence came! And certainly, between the wonder and the joy, it must have been welcome to me to hear and speak nothing.

italian: E quasi peregrin che si ricrea nel tempio del suo voto riguardando, e spera già ridir com’ ello stea,
english: And as a pilgrim, in the temple he had vowed to reach, renews himself—he looks and hopes he can describe what it was like—

italian: su per la viva luce passeggiando, menava ïo li occhi per li gradi, mo sù, mo giù e mo recirculando.
english: so did I journey through the living light, guiding my eyes, from rank to rank, along a path now up, now down, now circling round.

italian: Vedëa visi a carità süadi, d’altrui lume fregiati e di suo riso, e atti ornati di tutte onestadi.
english: There I saw faces given up to love— graced with Another’s light and their own smile— and movements graced with every dignity.

italian: La forma general di paradiso già tutta mïo sguardo avea compresa, in nulla parte ancor fermato fiso;
english: By now my gaze had taken in the whole of Paradise—its form in general— but without looking hard at any part;

italian: e volgeami con voglia rïaccesa per domandar la mia donna di cose di che la mente mia era sospesa.
english: and I, my will rekindled, turning toward my lady, was prepared to ask about those matters that inclined my mind to doubt.

italian: Uno intendëa, e altro mi rispuose: credea veder Beatrice e vidi un sene vestito con le genti glorïose.
english: Where I expected her, another answered: I thought I should see Beatrice, and saw an elder dressed like those who are in glory.

italian: Diffuso era per li occhi e per le gene di benigna letizia, in atto pio quale a tenero padre si convene.
english: His gracious gladness filled his eyes, suffused his cheeks; his manner had that kindliness which suits a tender father. “Where is she?”

italian: E «Ov’ è ella?», sùbito diss’ io. Ond’ elli: «A terminar lo tuo disiro mosse Beatrice me del loco mio;
english: I asked him instantly. And he replied: “That all your longings may be satisfied, Beatrice urged me from my place. If you

italian: e se riguardi sù nel terzo giro dal sommo grado, tu la rivedrai nel trono che suoi merti le sortiro».
english: look up and to the circle that is third from that rank which is highest, you will see her on the throne her merits have assigned her.”

italian: Sanza risponder, li occhi sù levai, e vidi lei che si facea corona reflettendo da sé li etterni rai.
english: I, without answering, then looked on high and saw that round her now a crown took shape as she reflected the eternal rays.

italian: Da quella regïon che più sù tona occhio mortale alcun tanto non dista, qualunque in mare più giù s’abbandona,
english: No mortal eye, not even one that plunged into deep seas, would be so distant from that region where the highest thunder forms,

italian: quanto lì da Beatrice la mia vista; ma nulla mi facea, ché süa effige non discendëa a me per mezzo mista.
english: as—there—my sight was far from Beatrice; but distance was no hindrance, for her semblance reached me—undimmed by any thing between.

italian: «O donna in cui la mia speranza vige, e che soffristi per la mia salute in inferno lasciar le tue vestige,
english: “O lady, you in whom my hope gains strength, you who, for my salvation, have allowed your footsteps to be left in Hell, in all

italian: di tante cose quant’ i’ ho vedute, dal tuo podere e da la tua bontate riconosco la grazia e la virtute.
english: the things that I have seen, I recognize the grace and benefit that I, depending upon your power and goodness, have received.

italian: Tu m’hai di servo tratto a libertate per tutte quelle vie, per tutt’ i modi che di ciò fare avei la potestate.
english: You drew me out from slavery to freedom by all those paths, by all those means that were within your power. Do, in me, preserve

italian: La tua magnificenza in me custodi, sì che l’anima mia, che fatt’ hai sana, piacente a te dal corpo si disnodi».
english: your generosity, so that my soul, which you have healed, when it is set loose from my body, be a soul that you will welcome.”

italian: Così orai; e quella, sì lontana come parea, sorrise e riguardommi; poi si tornò a l’etterna fontana.
english: So did I pray. And she, however far away she seemed, smiled, and she looked at me. Then she turned back to the eternal fountain.

italian: E ’l santo sene: «Acciò che tu assommi perfettamente», disse, «il tuo cammino, a che priego e amor santo mandommi,
english: And he, the holy elder, said: “That you may consummate your journey perfectly— for this, both prayer and holy love have sent me

italian: vola con li occhi per questo giardino; ché veder lui t’acconcerà lo sguardo più al montar per lo raggio divino.
english: to help you—let your sight fly round this garden; by gazing so, your vision will be made more ready to ascend through God’s own ray.

italian: E la regina del cielo, ond’ ïo ardo tutto d’amor, ne farà ogne grazia, però ch’i’ sono il suo fedel Bernardo».
english: The Queen of Heaven, for whom I am all aflame with love, will grant us every grace: I am her faithful Bernard.” Just as one

italian: Qual è colui che forse di Croazia viene a veder la Veronica nostra, che per l’antica fame non sen sazia,
english: who, from Croatia perhaps, has come to visit our Veronica—one whose old hunger is not sated, who, as long

italian: ma dice nel pensier, fin che si mostra: ‘Segnor mio Iesù Cristo, Dio verace, or fu sì fatta la sembianza vostra?’;
english: as it is shown, repeats these words in thought: “O my Lord Jesus Christ, true God, was then Your image like the image I see now?”—

italian: tal era io mirando la vivace carità di colui che ’n questo mondo, contemplando, gustò di quella pace.
english: such was I as I watched the living love of him who, in this world, in contemplation, tasted that peace. And he said: “Son of grace,

italian: «Figliuol di grazia, quest’ esser giocondo», cominciò elli, «non ti sarà noto, tenendo li occhi pur qua giù al fondo;
english: you will not come to know this joyous state if your eyes only look down at the base; but look upon the circles, look at those

italian: ma guarda i cerchi infino al più remoto, tanto che veggi seder la regina cui questo regno è suddito e devoto».
english: that sit in a position more remote, until you see upon her seat the Queen to whom this realm is subject and devoted.”

italian: Io levai li occhi; e come da mattina la parte orïental de l’orizzonte soverchia quella dove ’l sol declina,
english: I lifted up my eyes; and as, at morning, the eastern side of the horizon shows more splendor than the side where the sun sets,

italian: così, quasi di valle andando a monte con li occhi, vidi parte ne lo stremo vincer di lume tutta l’altra fronte.
english: so, as if climbing with my eyes from valley to summit, I saw one part of the farthest rank of the Rose more bright than all the rest.

italian: E come quivi ove s’aspetta il temo che mal guidò Fetonte, più s’infiamma, e quinci e quindi il lume si fa scemo,
english: And as, on earth, the point where we await the shaft that Phaethon had misguided glows brightest, while, to each side, the light shades off,

italian: così quella pacifica oriafiamma nel mezzo s’avvivava, e d’ogne parte per igual modo allentava la fiamma;
english: so did the peaceful oriflamme appear brightest at its midpoint, so did its flame, on each side, taper off at equal pace.

italian: e a quel mezzo, con le penne sparte, vid’ io più di mille angeli festanti, ciascun distinto di fulgore e d’arte.
english: I saw, around that midpoint, festive angels— more than a thousand—with their wings outspread; each was distinct in splendor and in skill.

italian: Vidi a lor giochi quivi e a lor canti ridere una bellezza, che letizia era ne li occhi a tutti li altri santi;
english: And there I saw a loveliness that when it smiled at the angelic songs and games made glad the eyes of all the other saints.

italian: e s’io avessi in dir tanta divizia quanta ad imaginar, non ardirei lo minimo tentar di sua delizia.
english: And even if my speech were rich as my imagination is, I should not try to tell the very least of her delights.

italian: Bernardo, come vide li occhi miei nel caldo suo caler fissi e attenti, li suoi con tanto affetto volse a lei,
english: Bernard—when he had seen my eyes intent, fixed on the object of his burning fervor— turned his own eyes to her with such affection

italian: che ’ miei di rimirar fé più ardenti.
english: that he made mine gaze still more ardently.

italian: Affetto al suo piacer, quel contemplante libero officio di dottore assunse, e cominciò queste parole sante:
english: Though he had been absorbed in his delight, that contemplator freely undertook the task of teaching; and his holy words

italian: «La piaga che Maria richiuse e unse, quella ch’è tanto bella da’ suoi piedi è colei che l’aperse e che la punse.
english: began: “The wound that Mary closed and then anointed was the wound that Eve—so lovely at Mary’s feet—had opened and had pierced.

italian: Ne l’ordine che fanno i terzi sedi, siede Rachel di sotto da costei con Bëatrice, sì come tu vedi.
english: Below her, in the seats of the third rank, Rachel and Beatrice, as you see, sit. Sarah, Rebecca, Judith, and the one

italian: Sarra e Rebecca, Iudìt e colei che fu bisava al cantor che per doglia del fallo disse ‘ Miserere mei’ ,
english: who was the great-grandmother of the singer who, as he sorrowed for his sinfulness, cried, ‘Miserere mei’—these you can see

italian: puoi tu veder così di soglia in soglia giù digradar, com’ io ch’a proprio nome vo per la rosa giù di foglia in foglia.
english: from rank to rank as I, in moving through the Rose, from petal unto petal, give to each her name. And from the seventh rank,

italian: E dal settimo grado in giù, sì come infino ad esso, succedono Ebree, dirimendo del fior tutte le chiome;
english: just as they did within the ranks above, the Hebrew women follow—ranging downward— dividing all the tresses of the Rose.

italian: perché, secondo lo sguardo che fée la fede in Cristo, queste sono il muro a che si parton le sacre scalee.
english: They are the wall by which the sacred stairs divide, depending on the view of Christ with which their faith aligned. Upon one side,

italian: Da questa parte onde ’l fiore è maturo di tutte le sue foglie, sono assisi quei che credettero in Cristo venturo;
english: there where the Rose is ripe, with all its petals, are those whose faith was in the Christ to come; and on the other side—that semicircle

italian: da l’altra parte onde sono intercisi di vòti i semicirculi, si stanno quei ch’a Cristo venuto ebber li visi.
english: whose space is broken up by vacant places— sit those whose sight was set upon the Christ who had already come. And just as on

italian: E come quinci il glorïoso scanno de la donna del cielo e li altri scanni di sotto lui cotanta cerna fanno,
english: this side, to serve as such a great partition, there is the throne in glory of the Lady of Heaven and the seats that range below it,

italian: così di contra quel del gran Giovanni, che sempre santo ’l diserto e ’l martiro sofferse, e poi l’inferno da due anni;
english: so, opposite, the seat of the great John— who, always saintly, suffered both the desert and martyrdom, and then two years of Hell—

italian: e sotto lui così cerner sortiro Francesco, Benedetto e Augustino e altri fin qua giù di giro in giro.
english: serves to divide; below him sit, assigned to this partition, Francis, Benedict, and Augustine, and others, rank on rank,

italian: Or mira l’alto proveder divino: ché l’uno e l’altro aspetto de la fede igualmente empierà questo giardino.
english: down to this center of the Rose. Now see how deep is God’s foresight: both aspects of the faith shall fill this garden equally.

italian: E sappi che dal grado in giù che fiede a mezzo il tratto le due discrezioni, per nullo proprio merito si siede,
english: And know that there, below the transverse row that cuts across the two divisions, sit souls who are there for merits not their own,

italian: ma per l’altrui, con certe condizioni: ché tutti questi son spiriti asciolti prima ch’avesser vere elezïoni.
english: but—with certain conditions—others’ merits; for all of these are souls who left their bodies before they had the power of true choice.

italian: Ben te ne puoi accorger per li volti e anche per le voci püerili, se tu li guardi bene e se li ascolti.
english: Indeed, you may perceive this by yourself— their faces, childlike voices, are enough, if you look well at them and hear them sing.

italian: Or dubbi tu e dubitando sili; ma io discioglierò ’l forte legame in che ti stringon li pensier sottili.
english: But now you doubt and, doubting, do not speak; yet I shall loose that knot; I can release you from the bonds of subtle reasoning.

italian: Dentro a l’ampiezza di questo reame casüal punto non puote aver sito, se non come tristizia o sete o fame:
english: Within the ample breadth of this domain, no point can find its place by chance, just as there is no place for sorrow, thirst, or hunger;

italian: ché per etterna legge è stabilito quantunque vedi, sì che giustamente ci si risponde da l’anello al dito;
english: whatever you may see has been ordained by everlasting law, so that the fit of ring and finger here must be exact;

italian: e però questa festinata gente a vera vita non è sine causa intra sé qui più e meno eccellente.
english: and thus these souls who have, precociously, reached the true life do not, among themselves, find places high or low without some cause.

italian: Lo rege per cui questo regno pausa in tanto amore e in tanto diletto, che nulla volontà è di più ausa,
english: The King through whom this kingdom finds content in so much love and so much joyousness that no desire would dare to ask for more,

italian: le menti tutte nel suo lieto aspetto creando, a suo piacer di grazia dota diversamente; e qui basti l’effetto.
english: creating every mind in His glad sight, bestows His grace diversely, at His pleasure— and here the fact alone must be enough.

italian: E ciò espresso e chiaro vi si nota ne la Scrittura santa in quei gemelli che ne la madre ebber l’ira commota.
english: And this is clearly and expressly noted for you in Holy Scripture, in those twins who, in their mother’s womb, were moved to anger.

italian: Però, secondo il color d’i capelli, di cotal grazia l’altissimo lume degnamente convien che s’incappelli.
english: Thus, it is just for the celestial light to grace their heads with a becoming crown, according to the color of their hair.

italian: Dunque, sanza mercé di lor costume, locati son per gradi differenti, sol differendo nel primiero acume.
english: Without, then, any merit in their works, these infants are assigned to different ranks— proclivity at birth, the only difference.

italian: Bastavasi ne’ secoli recenti con l’innocenza, per aver salute, solamente la fede d’i parenti;
english: In early centuries, their parents’ faith alone, and their own innocence, sufficed for the salvation of the children; when

italian: poi che le prime etadi fuor compiute, convenne ai maschi a l’innocenti penne per circuncidere acquistar virtute;
english: those early times had reached completion, then each male child had to find, through circumcision, the power needed by his innocent

italian: ma poi che ’l tempo de la grazia venne, sanza battesmo perfetto di Cristo tale innocenza là giù si ritenne.
english: member; but then the age of grace arrived, and without perfect baptism in Christ, such innocence was kept below, in Limbo.

italian: Riguarda omai ne la faccia che a Cristo più si somiglia, ché la sua chiarezza sola ti può disporre a veder Cristo».
english: Look now upon the face that is most like the face of Christ, for only through its brightness can you prepare your vision to see Him.”

italian: Io vidi sopra lei tanta allegrezza piover, portata ne le menti sante create a trasvolar per quella altezza,
english: I saw such joy rain down upon her, joy carried by holy intellects created to fly at such a height, that all which I

italian: che quantunque io avea visto davante, di tanta ammirazion non mi sospese, né mi mostrò di Dio tanto sembiante;
english: had seen before did not transfix me with amazement so intense, nor show to me a semblance that was so akin to God.

italian: e quello amor che primo lì discese, cantando ‘ Ave, Maria, gratïa plena ’, dinanzi a lei le sue ali distese.
english: And the angelic love who had descended earlier, now spread his wings before her, singing “Ave Maria, gratia plena.”

italian: Rispuose a la divina cantilena da tutte parti la beata corte, sì ch’ogne vista sen fé più serena.
english: On every side, the blessed court replied, singing responses to his godly song, so that each spirit there grew more serene.

italian: «O santo padre, che per me comporte l’esser qua giù, lasciando il dolce loco nel qual tu siedi per etterna sorte,
english: “O holy father—who, for me, endure your being here below, leaving the sweet place where eternal lot assigns your seat—

italian: qual è quell’ angel che con tanto gioco guarda ne li occhi la nostra regina, innamorato sì che par di foco?».
english: who is that angel who with such delight looks into our Queen’s eyes—he who is so enraptured that he seems to be a flame?”

italian: Così ricorsi ancora a la dottrina di colui ch’abbelliva di Maria, come del sole stella mattutina.
english: So, once again, I called upon the teaching of him who drew from Mary beauty, as the morning star draws beauty from the sun.

italian: Ed elli a me: «Baldezza e leggiadria quant’ esser puote in angelo e in alma, tutta è in lui; e sì volem che sia,
english: And he to me: “All of the gallantry and confidence that there can be in angel or blessed soul are found in him, and we

italian: perch’ elli è quelli che portò la palma giuso a Maria, quando ’l Figliuol di Dio carcar si volse de la nostra salma.
english: would have it so, for it was he who carried the palm below to Mary, when God’s Son wanted to bear our flesh as His own burden.

italian: Ma vieni omai con li occhi sì com’ io andrò parlando, e nota i gran patrici di questo imperio giustissimo e pio.
english: But follow with your eyes even as I proceed to speak, and note the great patricians of this most just and merciful empire.

italian: Quei due che seggon là sù più felici per esser propinquissimi ad Agusta, son d’esta rosa quasi due radici:
english: Those two who, there above, are seated, most happy to be so near the Empress, may be likened to the two roots of this Rose:

italian: colui che da sinistra le s’aggiusta è il padre per lo cui ardito gusto l’umana specie tanto amaro gusta;
english: the one who, on her left, sits closest, is the father whose presumptuous tasting caused humankind to taste such bitterness;

italian: dal destro vedi quel padre vetusto di Santa Chiesa a cui Cristo le chiavi raccomandò di questo fior venusto.
english: and on the right, you see that ancient father of Holy Church, into whose care the keys of this fair flower were consigned by Christ.

italian: E quei che vide tutti i tempi gravi, pria che morisse, de la bella sposa che s’acquistò con la lancia e coi clavi,
english: And he who saw, before he died, all of the troubled era of the lovely Bride— whom lance and nails had won—sits at his side;

italian: siede lungh’ esso, e lungo l’altro posa quel duca sotto cui visse di manna la gente ingrata, mobile e retrosa.
english: and at the side of Adam sits that guide under whose rule the people, thankless, fickle, and stubborn, lived on manna. Facing Peter,

italian: Di contr’ a Pietro vedi sedere Anna, tanto contenta di mirar sua figlia, che non move occhio per cantare osanna;
english: Anna is seated, so content to see her daughter that, as Anna sings hosannas, she does not move her eyes. And opposite

italian: e contro al maggior padre di famiglia siede Lucia, che mosse la tua donna quando chinavi, a rovinar, le ciglia.
english: the greatest father of a family, Lucia sits, she who urged on your lady when you bent your brows downward, to your ruin.

italian: Ma perché ’l tempo fugge che t’assonna, qui farem punto, come buon sartore che com’ elli ha del panno fa la gonna;
english: But time, which brings you sleep, takes flight, and now we shall stop here—even as a good tailor who cuts the garment as his cloth allows—

italian: e drizzeremo li occhi al primo amore, sì che, guardando verso lui, penètri quant’ è possibil per lo suo fulgore.
english: and turn our vision to the Primal Love, that, gazing at Him, you may penetrate— as far as that can be—His radiance.

italian: Veramente, ne forse tu t’arretri movendo l’ali tue, credendo oltrarti, orando grazia conven che s’impetri
english: But lest you now fall back when, even as you move your wings, you think that you advance, imploring grace, through prayer you must beseech

italian: grazia da quella che puote aiutarti; e tu mi seguirai con l’affezione, sì che dal dicer mio lo cor non parti».
english: grace from that one who has the power to help you; and do you follow me with your affection— so may my words and your heart share one way.”

italian: E cominciò questa santa orazione:
english: And he began this holy supplication:

italian: «Vergine Madre, figlia del tuo figlio, umile e alta più che creatura, termine fisso d’etterno consiglio,
english: “Virgin mother, daughter of your Son, more humble and sublime than any creature, fixed goal decreed from all eternity,

italian: tu se’ colei che l’umana natura nobilitasti sì, che ’l suo fattore non disdegnò di farsi sua fattura.
english: you are the one who gave to human nature so much nobility that its Creator did not disdain His being made its creature.

italian: Nel ventre tuo si raccese l’amore, per lo cui caldo ne l’etterna pace così è germinato questo fiore.
english: That love whose warmth allowed this flower to bloom within the everlasting peace—was love rekindled in your womb; for us above,

italian: Qui se’ a noi meridïana face di caritate, e giuso, intra ’ mortali, se’ di speranza fontana vivace.
english: you are the noonday torch of charity, and there below, on earth, among the mortals, you are a living spring of hope. Lady,

italian: Donna, se’ tanto grande e tanto vali, che qual vuol grazia e a te non ricorre, sua disïanza vuol volar sanz’ ali.
english: you are so high, you can so intercede, that he who would have grace but does not seek your aid, may long to fly but has no wings.

italian: La tua benignità non pur soccorre a chi domanda, ma molte fïate liberamente al dimandar precorre.
english: Your loving-kindness does not only answer the one who asks, but it is often ready to answer freely long before the asking.

italian: In te misericordia, in te pietate, in te magnificenza, in te s’aduna quantunque in creatura è di bontate.
english: In you compassion is, in you is pity, in you is generosity, in you is every goodness found in any creature.

italian: Or questi, che da l’infima lacuna de l’universo infin qui ha vedute le vite spiritali ad una ad una,
english: This man—who from the deepest hollow in the universe, up to this height, has seen the lives of spirits, one by one—now pleads

italian: supplica a te, per grazia, di virtute tanto, che possa con li occhi levarsi più alto verso l’ultima salute.
english: with you, through grace, to grant him so much virtue that he may lift his vision higher still— may lift it toward the ultimate salvation.

italian: E io, che mai per mio veder non arsi più ch’i’ fo per lo suo, tutti miei prieghi ti porgo, e priego che non sieno scarsi,
english: And I, who never burned for my own vision more than I burn for his, do offer you all of my prayers—and pray that they may not

italian: perché tu ogne nube li disleghi di sua mortalità co’ prieghi tuoi, sì che ’l sommo piacer li si dispieghi.
english: fall short—that, with your prayers, you may disperse all of the clouds of his mortality so that the Highest Joy be his to see.

italian: Ancor ti priego, regina, che puoi ciò che tu vuoli, che conservi sani, dopo tanto veder, li affetti suoi.
english: This, too, O Queen, who can do what you would, I ask of you: that after such a vision, his sentiments preserve their perseverance.

italian: Vinca tua guardia i movimenti umani: vedi Beatrice con quanti beati per li miei prieghi ti chiudon le mani!».
english: May your protection curb his mortal passions. See Beatrice—how many saints with her! They join my prayers! They clasp their hands to you!”

italian: Li occhi da Dio diletti e venerati, fissi ne l’orator, ne dimostraro quanto i devoti prieghi le son grati;
english: The eyes that are revered and loved by God, now fixed upon the supplicant, showed us how welcome such devotions are to her;

italian: indi a l’etterno lume s’addrizzaro, nel qual non si dee creder che s’invii per creatura l’occhio tanto chiaro.
english: then her eyes turned to the Eternal Light— there, do not think that any creature’s eye can find its way as clearly as her sight.

italian: E io ch’al fine di tutt’ i disii appropinquava, sì com’ io dovea, l’ardor del desiderio in me finii.
english: And I, who now was nearing Him who is the end of all desires, as I ought, lifted my longing to its ardent limit.

italian: Bernardo m’accennava, e sorridea, perch’ io guardassi suso; ma io era già per me stesso tal qual ei volea:
english: Bernard was signaling—he smiled—to me to turn my eyes on high; but I, already was doing what he wanted me to do,

italian: ché la mia vista, venendo sincera, e più e più intrava per lo raggio de l’alta luce che da sé è vera.
english: because my sight, becoming pure, was able to penetrate the ray of Light more deeply— that Light, sublime, which in Itself is true.

italian: Da quinci innanzi il mio veder fu maggio che ’l parlar mostra, ch’a tal vista cede, e cede la memoria a tanto oltraggio.
english: From that point on, what I could see was greater than speech can show: at such a sight, it fails— and memory fails when faced with such excess.

italian: Qual è colüi che sognando vede, che dopo ’l sogno la passione impressa rimane, e l’altro a la mente non riede,
english: As one who sees within a dream, and, later, the passion that had been imprinted stays, but nothing of the rest returns to mind,

italian: cotal son io, ché quasi tutta cessa mia visïone, e ancor mi distilla nel core il dolce che nacque da essa.
english: such am I, for my vision almost fades completely, yet it still distills within my heart the sweetness that was born of it.

italian: Così la neve al sol si disigilla; così al vento ne le foglie levi si perdea la sentenza di Sibilla.
english: So is the snow, beneath the sun, unsealed; and so, on the light leaves, beneath the wind, the oracles the Sibyl wrote were lost.

italian: O somma luce che tanto ti levi da’ concetti mortali, a la mia mente ripresta un poco di quel che parevi,
english: O Highest Light, You, raised so far above the minds of mortals, to my memory give back something of Your epiphany,

italian: e fa la lingua mia tanto possente, ch’una favilla sol de la tua gloria possa lasciare a la futura gente;
english: and make my tongue so powerful that I may leave to people of the future one gleam of the glory that is Yours, for by

italian: ché, per tornare alquanto a mia memoria e per sonare un poco in questi versi, più si conceperà di tua vittoria.
english: returning somewhat to my memory and echoing awhile within these lines, Your victory will be more understood.

italian: Io credo, per l’acume ch’io soffersi del vivo raggio, ch’i’ sarei smarrito, se li occhi miei da lui fossero aversi.
english: The living ray that I endured was so acute that I believe I should have gone astray had my eyes turned away from it.

italian: E’ mi ricorda ch’io fui più ardito per questo a sostener, tanto ch’i’ giunsi l’aspetto mio col valore infinito.
english: I can recall that I, because of this, was bolder in sustaining it until my vision reached the Infinite Goodness.

italian: Oh abbondante grazia ond’ io presunsi ficcar lo viso per la luce etterna, tanto che la veduta vi consunsi!
english: O grace abounding, through which I presumed to set my eyes on the Eternal Light so long that I spent all my sight on it!

italian: Nel suo profondo vidi che s’interna, legato con amore in un volume, ciò che per l’universo si squaderna:
english: In its profundity I saw—ingathered and bound by love into one single volume— what, in the universe, seems separate, scattered:

italian: sustanze e accidenti e lor costume quasi conflati insieme, per tal modo che ciò ch’i’ dico è un semplice lume.
english: substances, accidents, and dispositions as if conjoined—in such a way that what I tell is only rudimentary.

italian: La forma universal di questo nodo credo ch’i’ vidi, perché più di largo, dicendo questo, mi sento ch’i’ godo.
english: I think I saw the universal shape which that knot takes; for, speaking this, I feel a joy that is more ample. That one moment

italian: Un punto solo m’è maggior letargo che venticinque secoli a la ’mpresa che fé Nettuno ammirar l’ombra d’Argo.
english: brings more forgetfulness to me than twenty- five centuries have brought to the endeavor that startled Neptune with the Argo’s shadow!

italian: Così la mente mia, tutta sospesa, mirava fissa, immobile e attenta, e sempre di mirar faceasi accesa.
english: So was my mind—completely rapt, intent, steadfast, and motionless—gazing; and it grew ever more enkindled as it watched.

italian: A quella luce cotal si diventa, che volgersi da lei per altro aspetto è impossibil che mai si consenta;
english: Whoever sees that Light is soon made such that it would be impossible for him to set that Light aside for other sight;

italian: però che ’l ben, ch’è del volere obietto, tutto s’accoglie in lei, e fuor di quella è defettivo ciò ch’è lì perfetto.
english: because the good, the object of the will, is fully gathered in that Light; outside that Light, what there is perfect is defective.

italian: Omai sarà più corta mia favella, pur a quel ch’io ricordo, che d’un fante che bagni ancor la lingua a la mammella.
english: What little I recall is to be told, from this point on, in words more weak than those of one whose infant tongue still bathes at the breast.

italian: Non perché più ch’un semplice sembiante fosse nel vivo lume ch’io mirava, che tal è sempre qual s’era davante;
english: And not because more than one simple semblance was in the Living Light at which I gazed— for It is always what It was before—

italian: ma per la vista che s’avvalorava in me guardando, una sola parvenza, mutandom’ io, a me si travagliava.
english: but through my sight, which as I gazed grew stronger, that sole appearance, even as I altered, seemed to be changing. In the deep and bright

italian: Ne la profonda e chiara sussistenza de l’alto lume parvermi tre giri di tre colori e d’una contenenza;
english: essence of that exalted Light, three circles appeared to me; they had three different colors, but all of them were of the same dimension;

italian: e l’un da l’altro come iri da iri parea reflesso, e ’l terzo parea foco che quinci e quindi igualmente si spiri.
english: one circle seemed reflected by the second, as rainbow is by rainbow, and the third seemed fire breathed equally by those two circles.

italian: Oh quanto è corto il dire e come fioco al mio concetto! e questo, a quel ch’i’ vidi, è tanto, che non basta a dicer ‘poco’.
english: How incomplete is speech, how weak, when set against my thought! And this, to what I saw. is such—to call it little is too much.

italian: O luce etterna che sola in te sidi, sola t’intendi, e da te intelletta e intendente te ami e arridi!
english: Eternal Light, You only dwell within Yourself, and only You know You; Self-knowing, Self-known, You love and smile upon Yourself!

italian: Quella circulazion che sì concetta pareva in te come lume reflesso, da li occhi miei alquanto circunspetta,
english: That circle—which, begotten so, appeared in You as light reflected—when my eyes had watched it with attention for some time,

italian: dentro da sé, del suo colore stesso, mi parve pinta de la nostra effige: per che ’l mio viso in lei tutto era messo.
english: within itself and colored like itself, to me seemed painted with our effigy, so that my sight was set on it completely.

italian: Qual è ’l geomètra che tutto s’affige per misurar lo cerchio, e non ritrova, pensando, quel principio ond’ elli indige,
english: As the geometer intently seeks to square the circle, but he cannot reach, through thought on thought, the principle he needs,

italian: tal era io a quella vista nova: veder voleva come si convenne l’imago al cerchio e come vi s’indova;
english: so I searched that strange sight: I wished to see the way in which our human effigy suited the circle and found place in it—

italian: ma non eran da ciò le proprie penne: se non che la mia mente fu percossa da un fulgore in che sua voglia venne.
english: and my own wings were far too weak for that. But then my mind was struck by light that flashed and, with this light, received what it had asked.

italian: A l’alta fantasia qui mancò possa; ma già volgeva il mio disio e ’l velle , sì come rota ch’igualmente è mossa,
english: Here force failed my high fantasy; but my desire and will were moved already—like a wheel revolving uniformly—by

italian: l’amor che move il sole e l’altre stelle.
english: the Love that moves the sun and the other stars.
